States' procurement portals so that the benefits of MSP procurement reach genuine 
farmers in a transparent manner. In addition, adequate number of procurement centres, 
including direct procurement centres as required, are established by the procurement 
agencies in consultation with the State Governments to improve farmers' access to 
procurement facilities. Further, Cash Credit Limits (CCLs) are made available to the Central 
Nodal Agencies (CNAs) to ensure timely payment of MSP to the farmers. Regular 
awareness and publicity campaigns are undertaken by the Central and State Governments 
and Procurement Agencies to enhance farmers' awareness about MSP procurement 
operations. Initiatives taken by FCI to strengthen procurement process include deployment 
of biometric based procurement system and Integration of Digitized Mandi/Procurement 
centre operation. Further, wide publicity is undertaken through print, electronic and social 
media, public announcements and other communication channels to disseminate 
information regarding procurement schedules, procurement centres and other relevant 
aspects of procurement, thereby enhancing farmers' awareness and access to 
procurement.

LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 2561 
TO BE ANSWERED ON 04.08.2026 
 
 
DEVELOPMENT OF TEXTILE INDUSTRY IN RAJASTHAN 
 
2561#   SHRI HANUMAN BENIWAL: 
 
Will the Minister of TEXTILES वस्त्रमंत्री 
be pleased to state : 
 
(a) details of the schemes being implemented in Rajasthan for the development of the textile 
industry district-wise handlooms, powerlooms, technical textiles and the apparel sector, if so, the 
details thereof;  
(b) the details of the projects approved, fin ancial assistance released and actual expenditure 
incurred under the various schemes of the Government in Rajasthan during the last five years 
and the current year, scheme and year-wise;  
(c) whether the Government is implementing any special scheme for th e modernisation and 
infrastructure development of the major textile clusters in Rajasthan, if so, the details thereof, if 
not, the reasons therefor; and  
(d) the details of the assistance provided to handloom weavers, artisans and micro, small and 
medium enterprises engaged in the textile sector in Rajasthan for skill development, marketing, 
technology upgradation and export promotion during the last five years and the current year? 
 
उत्तर 
ANSWER 
वस्त्र राज् य मंत्री(श्री पबित्र मार्घेररटा) 
THE MINISTER OF STATE FOR TEXTILES  
 (SHRI PABITRA MARGHERITA) 
 
(a) to (d):    The Government of India has implemented various schemes for development of 
textile industry across the country including the state of Rajasthan. The major schemes 
include Scheme for Integrated Textile Park (SITP) for setting up textile parks with state of the 
art infrastructure in textile hubs; Production Linked Incentive (PLI) Scheme focusing on Man-
Made Fibre (MMF) Fabric, MMF Apparel and Technical Textiles to boost large scale 
manufacturing and enhancing competitiveness; National Technical Textiles Mission 
(NTTM) focusing on Research & Innovation in the field of specialty fibres and technical 
textile, indigenous development of machinery and creating human resources with requisit e 
skills; SAMARTH -Scheme for Capacity Building in Textile Sector with the objective of 
providing demand driven, placement oriented, skilling program; Amended Technology 
Upgradation Fund Scheme (ATUFS); National Handloom Development Programme; National 
Handicraft Development Programme; and Comprehensive Handicrafts Cluster Development 
Scheme (CHCDS).  
Under the National Handloom Development Programme and the Raw Material Supply 
Schemes in Handloom sector, financial assistance is provided to eligible handloom  

agencies/workers for raw materials, procurement of upgraded looms & accessories, solar 
lighting units, construction of workshed, product diversification & design innovation, 
technical and common infrastructure, marketing of handloom products in domestic/o verseas 
markets, concessional loans under weavers’ MUDRA scheme and social security etc. The 
following support has been provided to development of handloom sector in Rajasthan during 
the last five years and current year: 
 2 Small Handloom Clusters have been taken up for financial assistance of Rs.2.02 
Crore  giving  benefit to 465 handloom workers.  
 163 weavers have been provided improved looms/accessories.  
 930 handloom workers have been imparted Skill up-gradation training. 
 To enhance productivity, marketing capabilities and facilitate better incomes, 2 
Handloom Producer companies have been formed. 
 268 beneficiaries have been enrolled under Pradhan Mantri Jeevan Jyoti Bima Yojana 
and Pradhan Mantri Suraksha Bima Yojana. 
  2 lakh kg of yarn has been supplied under Transport Subsidy & Price Subsidy. 
Under the National Handicraft Development Programme (NHDP) and Comprehensive 
Handicrafts Cluster Development Scheme (CHCDS) in Handicrafts sector, need based 
financial assistance is provided for end -to-end support to the artisans through marketing 
events, skill development, cluster development, formation of Producer Companies, direct 
benefit to artisans, infrastructural and technology support, research and development support, 
digitization, branding and marketing of handicraft products in domestic & interna tional 
markets etc. which benefit the traditional crafts and increase livelihood opportunities 
throughout the country including  the state of Rajasthan . Under NHDP schemes, 669 such 
programmes have been conducted in the state of Rajasthan and sanctioned Rs . 83.37 crores 
giving benefit to 27287 artisans during F.Y. 2021-22 to 2025-26. 
  
The Ministry is implementing Scheme for Integrated Textile Park (SITP) to provide 
support for setting up textile parks with state of the art infrastructure in textile hubs ac ross the 
country. Under SITP, 3 projects have been sanctioned in Rajasthan. The details are as below-

In order to facilitate the textile industry to meet the required environmental standards and

Amended Technology Upgradation  Fund Scheme (ATUFS) was implemented on pan 
India basis with a view to achieve the vision of generating employment and promoting 
exports by way of technology upgradation in textile sector through “Make in India”. There are

released to these projects during the last 5 years and the current year is as per the table below:

With a view to boost Technical Textiles in the country, National Technical Textiles 
Mission (NTTM) was launched in the year 2020. NTTM is a pan India mission which focuses 
on research & innovation in the field of specialty fibres like Carbon fibre, Aramid fibre, 
Nylon, Composites etc. as well as in different segments of Technical Textiles such as geo 
textiles, agro textiles, medical textiles etc. and indigenous development of machinery; 
promoting aware ness amongst users; enhancing India’s exports of technical textiles; and 
creating human resources with requisite skills. Under NTTM, the following projects have 
been undertaken in the state of Rajasthan: 
i) Research & Development projects: 
a. Development of Ceramic and UHMWPE Textile Based Hybrid Polymer Composite 
Armor 
b. Development of E-glass/Carbon textile reinforced hybrid polymer composites for wind 
turbine Blade application 
c. Development of Energy-Dense All-Carbon Lithium-ion Capacitor from Textile Waste 
derived Carbon Materials 

d. Performance evaluation of selected geotextile-based liner material against seepage loss in 
water conservation system under a wide range of temperature 
  
ii) Start-Up Project: 
a. Development of shrink-resistant, detergent washable, camouflage dyed, far infra-red 
wool clothing for protection in extreme cold conditions through plasma technology with 
enhanced mechanical, comfort and thermal properties 
  
iii) Education Projects:  Education projects have been taken up in MLV Textile and 
Engineering College, Banasthali Vidyapith and BITS Pilani. 
  
The Production Linked Incentive (PLI) Scheme aims to address India’s structural gaps in 
MMF textiles and enhance global competitiveness t hrough scale, technology and value 
addition. Incentives of Rs. 386.30 crore has been released under the scheme across the 
country. Out of the 170 participant companies selected under the scheme, 06 are in Rajasthan. 
  
Under Samarth Scheme, Ministry of Text iles provides demand driven, placement -
oriented skilling programmes to supplement the efforts of the Indian textile industries in 
creating jobs in the organized textile and related sectors, covering the entire value chain of 
textiles. A total of 57,725 ben eficiaries has been trained (passed) under the scheme in the 
State of Rajasthan.

THE MINISTER OF PANCHAYATI RAJ  
 
(SHRI RAJIV RANJAN SINGH ALIAS LALAN SINGH) 
  
(a) & (b) Ministry of Panchayati Raj (MoPR) had implemented Panchayat Empowerment and 
Accountability Incentive Scheme (PEAIS) w.e.f. the year 2011-12. From 2013-14 various 
schemes, including PEAIS, were subsumed in Rajiv Gandhi Panchayat Sashaktikaran Abhiyan 
(RGPSA) scheme which is now revamped as Rashtriya Gram Swaraj Abhiyan (RGSA) scheme. 
Presently, National Panchayat Awards are conferred to Panchayats and other State/Union 
Territory (UT)/District level Institutions under the Incentivization of Panchayats (IoP), a central 
component of RGSA scheme.  
Panchayat, being “Local Self Government”, is a State subject. However, MoPR has been 
implementing the Centrally Sponsored Scheme of RGSA since the financial year 2022-23. The 
main objective of the scheme is to build the capacity of Panchayati Raj institutions (PRIs) by 
creating a learning ecosystem, especially through training for the Elected Representatives (ERs), 
functionaries, and other stakeholders to develop their governance capabilities to function 
effectively, and also by supporting exposure visits, development of training modules and 
materials, etc. Under this scheme, the Ministry has strengthened the capacity of States/UTs, 
including the State of Karnataka, Cuttack and Palghar districts, along with Pali and Dumka Lok 
Sabha Constituency for training and capacity building of elected representatives and Panchayat

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF FISHERIES, ANIMAL HUSBANDRY AND DAIRYING 
DEPARTMENT OF FISHERIES 
 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO - 2565 
ANSWERED ON 04/08/2026 
 
INDIAN SHRIMP EXPORT CONSIGNMENT 
 
2565. DR. T SUMATHY ALIAS THAMIZHACHI THANGAPANDIAN: 
  
Will the MINISTER OF FISHERIES, ANIMAL HUSBANDRY AND DAIRYING be pleased to 
state: 
(a) the total number of Indian shrimp export consignments rejected by major global markets like the 
United States and the European Union due to the presence of banned aquati c veterinary antibiotic 
residues (such as nitrofurans and chloramphenicol) since the implementation of the March 2025 ban, 
along with the details of financial losses incurred by the domestic seafood sector, 
(b) whether the Government has identified the exa ct regulatory loopholes such as the unauthorized 
sale of veterinary-grade drugs in local markets that allow these banned substances to continue entering 
the aquaculture supply chain; 
(c) the details of enforcement actions taken, penalties imposed and inspe ctions carried out by the 
Central and State task forces to crack down on illegal antibiotic use in India's major shrimp producing 
coastal belts, State/district-wise; and 
(d) the concrete steps being taken by the Government to support small-scale shrimp farmers in Tamil 
Nadu with access to affordable, certified antibiotic -free feeds and seed certification programs like 
"SHAPHARI" to restore the global credibility of Indian sea food exports? 
ANSWER 
THE MINISTER OF FISHERIES, ANIMAL HUSBANDRY AND DAIRYING 
(SHRI RAJIV RANJAN SINGH ALIAS LALAN SINGH) 
(a) As informed by the Export Inspection Council (EIC), Department of Commerce, Government of 
India, from March 2025 till date, a total of 35 Indian shrimp export consignments were rejected 
by major importing markets, namely the United States of America (USA), the European Union 
(EU), Japan and Russia, due to the detection of banned antibiotic residues. The details of the 
number, quantity and export value of the rejected shrimp export consignments are given in 
Annexure-I. 
(b) The Government has identified risks arising from the unauthorized sale and misuse of veterinary 
drugs and has strengthened the regulatory framework to prevent the use of banned antibiotics in 
aquaculture. The Coastal Aquaculture Authority (CAA), under the  

 
      Coastal Aquaculture Authority Act, 2005 (as amended in 2023), has expanded the list of prohibited 
substances to 75 antibiotics and other pharmacologically active substances for use in coastal 
aquaculture. The CAA also permits only c ertified aquaculture inputs, prescribes penalties for 
violations under the Act, and issues advisories and notices to stakeholders to promote compliance 
and raise awareness regarding the prohibition on the use of banned antibiotics. 
Further, the Government has undertaken several regulatory measures during 2025 to strengthen 
antibiotic control in aquaculture. The Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, based on the 
recommendations of the Drugs Technical Advisory Board (DTAB), has prohibited the import, 
manufacture, distribution and sale of Chloramphenicol and Nitrofuran for use in food -producing 
animals and has also prohibited the import, manufacture, sale and distribution of 34 specified 
antimicrobial medicinal products for veterinary use. In addition, the Min istry of Commerce and 
Industry, Department of Commerce, has prohibited the use of 37 antimicrobials reserved for 
human use in aquaculture activities relating to shrimp, prawn, fish and fishery products to ensure 
compliance with international food safety requirements. 
(c) The Department of Fisheries, Government of India, has advised all coastal States and Union 
Territories to constitute Antibiotic Task Forces for monitoring the use and supply of banned 
antibiotics across the aquaculture value chain. Accordin gly, the coastal States and Union 
Territories are required to undertake surveillance, inspections, and enforcement actions in 
accordance with the applicable statutory provisions. All coastal States have since constituted 
multidisciplinary Antibiotic Task Forces.  
The Government of India also facilitates inspection and system audits by major importing 
countries to assess the regulatory and monitoring mechanisms in place for the prevention, 
detection and control of banned antibiotic use in aquaculture. In add ition, the Export Inspection 
Council (EIC), Department of Commerce, investigates every reported case of antibiotic -related 
non-compliance to identify the root cause and implements appropriate corrective and preventive 
measures. The EIC has also strengthene d pre -export residue monitoring through stringent 
sampling protocols and 100% testing of consignments for export to sensitive markets such as the 
European Union and Japan. Establishments with repeated antibiotic-related non-compliances are 
subjected to temporary restrictions until satisfactory corrective actions are implemented. 
The Department of Fisheries does not maintain centralized database on the State-wise or district-
wise inspections conducted, enforcement actions taken or penalties imposed by the St ate-level 
Antibiotic Task Forces. The respective State Governments and competent authorities under the 
applicable statutory provisions undertake such enforcement. 

 (d) The Government is implementing several measures to support shrimp farmers, including sma ll-
scale farmers in Tamil Nadu, by improving access to quality aquaculture inputs, strengthening 
disease surveillance and promoting antibiotic-free shrimp production. Under the Pradhan Mantri 
Matsya Sampada Yojana (PMMSY), financial assistance is provided to strengthen seed, nursery, 
and feed infrastructure. In Tamil Nadu, 37 nursery/seed rearing ponds have been approved at a 
total project cost of ₹2.59 crore, one disease diagnostic and quality testing laboratory at a project 
cost of ₹40 lakh, and seven fis h feed mill projects at a total project cost of ₹5.20 crore. These 
interventions are aimed at improving the availability of quality seed and feed and strengthening 
disease surveillance in the State. 
Further, to promote the use of certified antibiotic-free aquaculture inputs, the Coastal Aquaculture 
Authority (CAA) has established a certification mechanism under which manufacturers and 
distributors are issued a Certificate of Compliance for antibiotic -free aquaculture inputs meeting 
the prescribed standards. So far, CAA has certified 10,109 aquaculture input products across ten 
categories, including aquaculture feeds, feed additives, probiotics, immunostimulants, 
disinfectants, chemicals and mineral mixtures, thereby facilitating the availability of quality -
certified, antibiotic-free inputs to shrimp farmers. 
In addition, the Marine Products Export Development Authority (MPEDA) is implementing the 
SHAPHARI certification programme, aligned with FAO guidelines, to promote disease-free and 
antibiotic-free shrimp seed and farm production. Under the programme, 50% of the audit and 
testing cost for hatcheries is borne by MPEDA, while farmers are not required to bear any audit 
or testing charges. At present, 16 hatcheries and 392 hectares of shrimp farms are certified under 
SHAPHARI across the country, of which one hatchery and 83.47 hectares of certified shrimp 
farms are located in Tamil Nadu.

2567. THIRU DAYANIDHI MARAN 
           Will the Minister of COMMERCE AND INDUSTRY (वाणिज्य एवं उद्योग मंत्री ) be 
pleased to state: 
(a) the key outcomes of the visit of Minister of Commerce & Industries to Spain, 
 Belgium and Finland, including agreements on trade, investment and technology, 
 if so, the details thereof;  
(b) whether any investment proposals or technology partnerships were secured for 
 Tamil Nadu in sectors such as automobiles, semiconductors, renewable energy, 
 textiles, electronics and food processing, if so, the details thereof and the 
 achievements of the trip itemised by beneficiary State;  
(c) whether representatives from Tamil Nadu's industries, MSMEs and export bodies 
 were included in the official delegation and if so, the details thereof;  
(d) the steps taken to ensure Tamil Nadu's export -oriented sectors, including 
 textiles, leather, automobiles, engineering goods and IT services, benefit from 
 the India-EU Free Trade Agreement; and  
(e) whether the Government proposes a dedicated mechanism to attract European 
 investments into Tamil Nadu's industrial clusters and if so, the details thereof? 
ANSWER 
 
वाणिज्य और उद्योग मंत्रालय में राज्य मंत्री (श्री णिणिन प्रसाद) 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF COMMERCE AND INDUSTRY 
(SHRI JITIN PRASADA) 
(a) Minister of Commerce & Industry, Shri Piyush Goyal, visited Spain, Belgium and 
Finland from 13 -17 July, 2026 with the objective of strengthening economic 
engagement with Europe, focusing on trade, investment, technology, innovation and 
sustainability. During the visit, discussions were held with the Governments and industry 
representatives of the three countries on enhancing cooperation in areas including 
trade, investment, technology, innovation, resilient sup ply chains, leveraging 
opportunities arising from the India -European Union Free Trade Agreement and the 
implementation of the India -EU FTA. The Minister also co -chaired the 3rd India -EU 
Trade and Technology Council (TTC) Ministerial Meeting held in Brussel s. During the 

2 
 
visit to Finland, two Memoranda of Understanding (MoUs) were signed, namely, an MoU 
between the Confederation of Indian Industry (CII) and Business Finland for commercial 
cooperation, and an MoU between the Confederation of Indian Industry (C II) and the 
Confederation of Finnish Industries (EK) to promote deeper business engagement and 
leverage the India-EU FTA. 
(b) During the visit, discussions were held with Governments and industry 
representatives of Spain, Belgium and Finland on opportunities for investment and 
technology collaboration in sectors including automobiles, semiconductors, renewable 
energy, textiles, electronics, manufacturing, food processing, artificial intelligence and 
digital technologies. The engagements were aimed at facilitating greater investment and 
technology partnerships across India including Tamil Nadu.  
 
(c) Yes, the representatives from T amil Nadu industries were part of the business 
delegations accompanying the Minister of Commerce & Industry during the visits to 
Spain, Belgium and Finland. The business delegations comprised representatives from 
diverse sectors of Indian industry from acr oss the country. The representation from 
Tamil Nadu included sectors such as engineering and manufacturing, healthcare, 
footwear, construction, e-waste recycling, design and education. 
 
(d) The India-EU Free Trade Agreement (FTA) is expected to provide ben efits across 
states including the state of Tamil Nadu in various key sectors such as textiles & 
apparel, leather & footwear, engineering goods and automobiles through preferential 
market access across 97% of EU tariff lines covering more than 99% of India’ s current 
export value. Preferential tariff access is expected to enhance India’s export 
competitiveness, promote value addition and provide opportunities for integration into 
EU value chains, thereby strengthening domestic manufacturing and employment 
particularly in labor -intensive and MSME -driven sectors. In the services sector, India 
has secured commitments across key services subsectors, including IT/ITeS, 
professional services, education and other business services. Indian service providers 
are expect ed to benefit from a stable and predictable regime in the EU market and 
facilitative mobility commitments for professionals, thereby boosting India's services 
exports. 
  
(e) The India-EU FTA provides predictable and preferential market access to European 
companies. This along with regulatory cooperation and policy certainty, is expected to 
enable the development of integrated and trusted supply chains between India and 
Europe, thereby encouraging long-term investments across manufacturing and services 
sectors.

Cooperative Godowns 
  
2568.  Shri Babu Singh Kushwaha: 
Shri Lalji Verma: 
Ms Iqra Choudhary: 
Shri Devesh Shakya: 
             
Will the Minister of COOPERATION (सहकारिता मंत्री) be pleased to state: 
(a) whether the Government has taken cognizance of the reports stating that cooperative godowns 
are being used for illegal storage by private traders instead of farmers and if so, the details 
thereof including such cases in Jaunpur; 
(b) whether the employees of the Primary Agricultural Credit Societies (PACS) have been imparted 
training in modern warehouse management and e -commerce and if so, the details thereof 
particularly for Jaunpur; 
(c) whether the Government is aware that small, marginal, Dalit and backward class farmers of 
Jaunpur , Purvanchal and Bundelkhand and regions of Uttar Pradesh are not getting equal access 
to Government godowns and cold storage facilities and if so, the steps taken in this regard; and 
(d) whether the Government proposes to strengthen the storage capacity, cold chains and mandi 
linkages in Jaunpur and to conduct third-party inspections/audits of these centres and if so, the 
details thereof?  
 
ANSWER 
  
THE MINISTER OF COOPERATION 
सहकारिता मंत्री (SHRI AMIT SHAH) 
(a)       Since the implementation of decentralized grain storage plan in Cooperative Sector from 
31.05.2023, no such report has been received from the State of Uttar Pradesh.   
(b)       In order to ensure proper utilization of the godowns the employees of the PACS/Cooperative 
Societies have been imparted training in modern warehouse management organized by NABARD 
and WDRA in the state of Uttar Pradesh. However, no specific training request on modern warehouse 
management has been received so far from Jaunpur. The state can raise request for conduct of such 
training for their PACS/Cooperative Societies to NABARD and WDRA.   

Page 2 of 2 
 
(c) & (d)         In this regard, no such information/complaint has been received from the state of Uttar 
Pradesh. Decentralized storage plan in cooperative sector entails creation of various agri  
infrastructure including godowns, custom hiring centers, processing units, Fair Price Shops, cold 
storage etc., at Primary Agricultural Credit Societies (PACS)/other cooperative societies level 
through convergence of various existing schemes of the Govern ment of India (GoI), such as, 
Agriculture Infrastructure Fund (AIF), Agricultural Marketing Infrastructure Scheme (AMI), Sub 
Mission on Agricultural Mechanization (SMAM), Pradhan Mantri Formalization of Micro Food 
Processing Enterprises Scheme (PMFME).  
Unnao, Sonbhadra in Purvanchal and Jaunpur, Mahoba, Hamirpur, Banda, Jalaun, and Jhansi in 
Bundelkhand region are listed under Pradhan Mantri Dhan-Dhaanya Krishi Yojana (PMDDKY). The 
decentralised grain storage plan in Cooperative Sector is one of the components of Pradhan Mantri 
Dhan-Dhaanya Krishi Yojana (PMDDKY), complements promoting integrated agricultural 
infrastructure and value addition in rural areas. Under the plan the creation of storage  infrastructure 
at PACS/other cooperative societies, coupled with primary processing and allied facilities, is expected 
to generate substantial employment opportunities. Jaunpur  district can also participate and avail the 
benefit under the decentralized grain storage plan in cooperative sector with the approval of District 
Cooperative Development Committee (DCDC). Under the plan the detailed project report is 
sanctioned by the respective DCCB after scrutinizing all the requisite document and for availing the 
advance subsidy claim the DPR is verified by NABARD through their dedicated portal. After 
completion of the project, physical verification is conducted by respective bank and NABARD.

2569. SHRI E TUKARAM 
         
Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE क ृ िष और िकसान कʞाण मंũी 
be pleased to state: 
(a) whether the Government has reviewed the implementation of PM-AASHA across the 
country to ensure that farmers receive the benefit of Minimum Support Price (MSP) for 
eligible crops;  
 
(b) the details of crops covered, farmers benefited, procurement made and Central 
assistance provided under the scheme during the last three years, including Ballari 
Parliamentary Constituency in Karnataka;  
 
(c) whether the Government has received representations regarding low awareness, limited 
procurement facilities and difficulties faced by farmers in availing the benefits of the Scheme; 
and  
 
(d) whether the Government proposes to expand procurement, strengthen awareness, 
improve implementation and extend the benefits to more farmers, including those in Ballari 
and if so, the details thereof?  
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE FOR AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE  
क ृ िष एवं िकसान कʞाण राǛ मंũी   (SHRI RAMNATH THAKUR) 
 
(a):  The implementation of the Pradhan Mantri Annadata Aay Sanrakshan Abhiyan (PM-
AASHA) is regularly monitored at the National, State and District level. In addition a third-
party evaluation of the Price Support Scheme (PSS) was conducted in 2024 by the National 
Council of Applied Economic Research (NCAER) as part of study commissioned by the 
Development Monitoring and Evaluation Office (DMEO), NITI Aayog. Similarly in 2025-26, 
the Price Deficit Payment Scheme (PDPS) and Market Intervention Scheme (MIS) were 
evaluated by the DMEO, NITI Aayog. The evaluation study of PSS observed that 
procurement at MSP under the Scheme provides remunerative prices to farmers during 
periods of low market prices, helps protect them from distress sales and is positively 
associated with farm income, production and productivity. The evaluation of PDPS assessed 
that the Scheme effectively stabilises prices, enhances farmers' incomes and confidence 
and is a credible and scalable price support mechanism for oilseed crops. The evaluation of 
MIS affirms that the Scheme is delivering on its core intent of protecting farmers from 
distress sales and stabilising incomes in volatile, perishable value chain-most clearly 
through post-harvest loss reduction, stronger bargaining power and recovery of cost of 
cultivation. 
 

(b): The details of crops covered, farmers benefited and procurement made including MSP 
value of the quantity procured under the scheme during the last three years in Karnataka, 
including Ballari Parliamentary Constituency is at Annexure. 
 
(c) & (d): To make MSP procurement more effective, transparent and farmer-friendly, the 
State Governments, in coordination with the Central Nodal Agencies (CNAs), have taken 
several measures across country including Ballari District in Karnataka. Adequate 
procurement centres are opened by the State Governments in consultation with the CNAs 
to facilitate farmers in selling their produce at MSP. Wide publicity is undertaken through 
print, electronic and social media, newspaper advertisements in local languages, farmers' 
meetings, camps/Chaupals and other outreach activities regarding procurement schedules, 
locations of procurement centres and Fair Average Quality (FAQ) parameters to enhance 
farmers' awareness and participation.The procurement process has been digitized through 
dedicated portals such as e-Samridhi and eSamyukti, covering farmer registration, 
procurement operations, quality assessment and Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT) of MSP 
payments. Further the State Governments, in consultation with the CNAs, make necessary 
arrangements for procurement operations, including storage facilities, gunny bags, 
transportation, weighing equipment and quality testing infrastructure. The procurement 
period is generally up to 90 days and may be extended by a further 30 days on the request 
of the concerned State Government, wherever required. To further expand procurement 
outreach, Primary Agricultural Credit Societies (PACS), Farmer Producer Organizations 
(FPOs), Farmer Producer Companies (FPCs) and cooperative societies have been 
associated with procurement operations. In addition, the CNAs have been permitted to 
undertake direct procurement of notified pulses, including Tur, Gram, Masur and Urad, from 
pre-registered farmers through their procurement centres, wherever required

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF COOPERATION 
 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION No. 2570 
TO BE ANSWERED ON  04th AUGUST, 2026 
 
Strengthening of PACS in Eastern Uttar Pradesh 
2570. Shri Shashank Mani: 
Will the Minister of COOPERATION (सहकारिता मंत्री) be pleased to state: 
(a) the number of Primary Agricultural Credit Societies (PACS) in eastern Uttar Pradesh, 
including Deoria, that have been computerised and modernised under the Central Sector 
Scheme during the last three years, district-wise; 
(b) the details of financial assistance released for the modernisation of PACS in the region; 
(c) whether any new multipurpose PACS have been established in the eastern Uttar Pradesh, 
including Deoria; and 
(d) the measures taken to expand the activities of PACS to include storage, dairy, fisheries and 
other rural services? 
 
 
ANSWER 
 
THE MINISTER OF COOPERATION 
सहकारिता मंत्री (SHRI AMIT SHAH) 
 
(a)  As per the National Cooperative Database  (NCD), as on 15.07.2026, there are 8, 044 
functional Primary Agricultural Credit Societies (PACS) in Uttar Pradesh, including 196 
PACS in Deoria District.  
 
The Government launched the Centrally Sponsored Project for Computerization of PACS 
in 2022 to bring all functional PACS onto a common ERP (Enterprise Resource Planning) 
based national software. Under the project, 6,2 57 PACS have been sanctioned for 
computerization in Uttar Pradesh, of which 119 PACS are in Deoria district. So far, 85 
PACS in Deoria district have been onboarded onto the ERP software.  The district wise 
details of PACS computerization in Uttar Pradesh are attached at Annexure-1.  
 
(b) Initially, 63,000 PACS were approved under the Centrally Sponsored Project for 
Computerization of PACS with a financial outlay of ₹2,516 crore. The project has since 
been expanded to cover 79,630 PACS with a revised outlay of ₹2,925.39 crore. Financial 
assistance of ₹68.05 crore has been provided to the State of Uttar Pradesh. This includes 

Page 2 of 8 
 
₹11.28 crore during FY 2022–23, ₹42.30 crore in FY 2023–24, nil in FY 2024–25, ₹4.47 
crore during FY 2025–26, and ₹10.00 crore during FY 2026–27.  
Additionally, as on 30.06.2026, the National Cooperative Development Corporation 
(NCDC) has cumulatively disbursed ₹5,74,090.48 crore for the development of cooperative 
institutions across the country. T he district wise details of disbursement by NCDC during 
last three years in Uttar Pradesh are attached at Annexure-2.  
 
(c) Yes, Sir. As per the National Cooperative Database, as on 15.07.2026, 1,387 new 
multipurpose Primary Agricultural Credit Societies (PACS) have been registered in Uttar 
Pradesh, including Deoria district, since the Government approved the plan on 15.02.2023 
for the establishment of new multipurpose PACS, dairy, and fisheries cooperative societies. 
The district-wise details of the newly registered PACS in Uttar Pradesh are enclosed at 
Annexure-3.  
 
(d) To strengthen PACS, t he Government has circulated Model Bye -laws, enabling them to 
undertake more than 25 business activities and function as multipurpose cooperative 
societies. PACS can now operate as Common Service Centres (CSCs), Pradhan Mantri 
Bharatiya Janaushadhi Kendras ( PMBJKs), Pradhan Mantri Kisan Samriddhi Kendras 
(PMKSKs), LPG distributorships, retail petrol/diesel outlets, and other service centres. 
 
Further, the Government has approved the World’s Largest Grain Storage Plan to create 
warehouses, custom hiring centers, primary processing units and other agri -infrastructure 
for grain storage at PACS level, through convergence of various Government of India 
(GOI) schemes. 
 
These initiatives have strengthened PACS and expanded livelihood opportunities in rural 
areas. They have improved access to institutional credit, enhanced marketing opportunities 
through cooperative institutions, promoted business diversification, generated add itional 
employment and income for farmers, rural youth and women, and improved transparency, 
financial inclusion and service delivery through technology-enabled cooperative societies.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF STEEL 
 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 2571 
FOR ANSWER ON 04.08.2026  
 
STATUS OF STEEL SCRAP RECYCLING POLICY  
 
2571. SHRI SHANKAR LALWANI:  
SHRI ANANTA NAYAK:  
SMT. KAMALJEET SEHRAWAT:  
SMT. MALVIKA DEVI:  
SHRI RAVINDRA SHUKLA ALIAS RAVI KISHAN:  
SHRI SUNIL KUMAR:  
 
Will the Minister of STEEL be pleased to state:  
 
(a) the current status of implementation of the Steel Scrap Recycling Policy in the 
country;  
 
(b) the details of steel scrap recycling capacity created and the quantity of steel scrap 
recycled so far, including the corresponding details for the State of Odisha;  
 
(c) the steps taken to promote organised scrap collection, processing and utilisation 
of recycled steel scrap in steel making to reduce carbon emissions, including initiatives 
undertaken in Odisha and the Keonjhar Lok Sabha Constituency;  
 
(d) the strategy of the Government to develop a robust ecosystem for steel scrap 
recycling, improve resource efficiency and encourage establishment of recycling 
facilities in Odisha, particularly in the Keonjhar Lok Sabha Constituency; and  
 
(e) the manner in which the steel scrap generated from Bokaro Steel Plant and 
Burnpur Steel Plant under Steel Authority of India Limited has been recycled or 
auctioned during the last three years? 
 
ANSWER 
 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE          (SHRI BHUPATHIRAJU SRINIVASA VARMA) 
MINISTRY OF STEEL 
 
(a),(c)&(d): The current status of implementation of Steel Scrap Recycling Policy in 
the country including the steps taken by the Government to promote organized scrap 
collection, processing and utilization of recycled steel scrap in steel making as well as 
develop robust ecosystem for steel scrap recycling to improve resource efficiency and 
reduce carbon emissions in steel sector across the country including Odisha and 
Keonjhar Lok Sabha Constituency are as under: - 
 
(i) The Steel Scrap Recycling Policy, 2019 provides a coordination framework with 
various Ministries to promote recycling of ferrous scrap generated from various 
sources. 
 
Contd…..2/- 
 
 
 

 
::2:: 
 
(ii) The Ministry of Road Transport and Highways (MoRTH) has formulated the 
Vehicle Scrapping Policy that includes a system of incentives/disincentives for 
creation of an ecosystem to phase out older, unfit polluting vehicles. Under the 
policy, MoRTH has issued rules for Registration and Functions of Vehicle 
Scrapping Facility (RVSF), which provides the procedures and infrastructure 
facilities required for de-pollution and dismantling of End-of-Life Vehicles (ELVs) 
for further recovery of metal and other materials under environmental regulations. 
As on 24.07.2026, 151 Registered Vehicle Scrapping Facilities (RVSFs) are 
operational across 23 States/UTs. 
 
(iii) The Government of India has notified the Hazardous and Other Wastes 
(Management and Transboundary Movement) Rules, 2016 to ensure safe 
handling, storage, recycling, utilisation, treatment and disposal of hazardous and 
other wastes in an environmentally safe manner. 
 
(iv) Ministry of Environment, Forest & Climate Change has introduced the 
Environment Protection (End-of-Life Vehicles) Rules, 2025, which establishes a 
framework for managing End-of-Life Vehicles (ELVs) in an environmentally sound 
manner and mandates Extended Producer Responsibility (EPR), requiring vehicle 
producers to meet annual scrapping targets based on the type of vehicle and 
materials recovered. 
 
(v) Recycling of Ships Act, 2019 has been notified by Ministry of Shipping, Ports 
and Waterways with aims to regulate and promote the safe and environmentally 
sound recycling of ships. 
 
(b) During Financial Year 2025-26, total 36 million tonnes ferrous scrap was used 
for production of steel, of which approximately 28 million tonnes scrap generated 
domestically.  The details of Registered Vehicle Scrapping Facilities (RVSFs) across 
the country including Odisha is available on the Ministry of Road Transport and 
Highways’ parivahan portal at the URL given below:  
  
‘https://vscrap.parivahan.gov.in/vehiclescrap/vahan/rvsfdetails.xhtml’. 
 
(e) The manner in which the steel scrap generated from Bokaro Steel Plant and 
Burnpur Steel Plant under Steel Authority of India Limited has been recycled or 
auctioned during the last three years is given below: 
 
Bokaro Steel Plant: Steel scrap generated at Bokaro Steel Plant has been 
systematically recovered, processed and fully recycled and utilized in its Steel Melting 
Shop for steel production. No internally generated steel scrap has been disposed of 
through auction during last three years. 
 
IISCO Steel Plant, Burnpur: Steel scrap generated at IISCO Steel Plant has been 
systematically recovered, processed and managed. The scrap has been primarily 
recycled through the Steel Melting Shop. Surplus or non-utilisable scrap, wherever 
required, has been disposed of through Inter-Plant Transfer or transparent auction 
processes to ensure optimum resource utilization and value realization.

AGRICULTURAL SCHEMES AND DIGITAL INFRASTRUCTURE 
 
2573. SHRI LALJI VERMA: 
 
Will the Minister of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare क ृ िष एवं िकसान कʞाण मंũी 
be pleased to state:  
 
(a) the number of farmers registered under PM-KISAN in Ambedkar Nagar who 
actually received the benefits without any technical glitches during 2025-26 along with 
the number of applications pending due to land records anomalies;  
(b) the details of credit disbursement and availability of fertilizers and seeds in rural 
areas following the computerization of PACS;  
(c) whether the Government have data regarding the number of PACS that have 
actually commenced multipurpose services along with the extent to which small 
farmers of Ambedkar Nagar are able to avail benefits therefrom; and  
(d) whether any review has been conducted regarding the exclusion of marginal 
farmers from these schemes due to lack of digital infrastructure and bureaucratic 
complexities? 
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE FOR AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE 
क ृ िष एवं िकसान कʞाण राǛ मंũी (SHRI RAMNATH THAKUR) 
 
(a):       Government of India has disbursed over ₹ 4.47 lakh Cr. to the beneficiaries 
through 23 installments since inception of the Scheme. The instalment-wise details of 
beneficiaries benefitted in Ambedkar Nagar district of Uttar Pradesh in FY 2025-26 is 
as follows: 
Instalment Beneficiaries 
Benefitted 
Amount Released 
(Rs. Crore) 
20th Instalment (Apr'25 - Jul'25) 3,70,416 79.55 
21st Instalment  (Aug 25-Nov 25) 3,50,285 70.09 
22nd Instalment  (Dec 25-Mar 26) 3,51,145 70.23 
 In the Ambedkar Nagar District of Uttar Pradesh, as on date, there are 2910 
farmers who are not receiving benefits due to non-fulfillment of essential condition 
related to land records. 
(b): The Government is implementing a 100% Centrally Funded Central Sector 
Scheme known as the Modified Interest Subvention Scheme (MISS) across various 
States and UTs in pan India. This scheme aims to provide easy and affordable credit 
to all farmers for meeting their working capital needs of various agriculture and allied 
sector activities up to a loan limit of Rs. 3.00 lakh at an effective interest rate of 4%. 
Interest Subsidies (IS & PRI) amounting to Rs. 18,366.80 Crore have been disbursed 
under MISS during FY 2025–26.  

Before the commencement of each cropping season, Department of Agriculture 
and Farmers Welfare (DA&FW), in consultation with all the State Governments, 
assesses the State-wise & month-wise requirement of fertilizers. On the basis of 
requirement projected by DA&FW, Department of Fertilizers (DoF) allocates adequate 
quantities of fertilizers to States by issuing monthly supply plan and continuously 
monitors the availability. The distribution of fertilizers within the State at district/block 
level is done by the concerned State government.  
In view of above, the availability of fertilizers viz. Urea, DAP, MOP and NPKS 
in the country has remained adequate during the ongoing Kharif 2026 season.  As on 
29.07.2026, the all-India availability of major fertilizers stood at 177.27 LMT of Urea, 
43.03 LMT of DAP, 14.31 LMT of MOP and 88.93 LMT of NPKS.  
Regarding availability of seeds, as reported by the States, 193.24 lakh qtls. 
certified/quality seeds are available against the requirement of 173.25 lakh qtls. during 
the current Kharif, 2026 season across the country.  
 
(c): Primary Agricultural Credit Societies (PACS) primarily cater to the credit and 
other service requirements of rural communities, including a large number of small and 
marginal farmers. With the introduction of the Model Bye-laws, PACS have been 
enabled to diversify their business activities by undertaking more than 25 economic 
activities, including fertilizer distribution, operation of Common Service Centres 
(CSCs), Pradhan Mantri Bhartiya Janaushadhi Kendras (PMBJKs), retail petrol/diesel 
outlets, LPG distributorships, solar roof top installations, custom hiring centres, 
warehousing and other farmer-centric services, thereby enhancing the range of 
services available to their members. As per the information received from the National 
Cooperative Database (NCD), there are 111 functional Primary Agricultural Credit 
Societies (PACS) in Ambedkar Nagar district of Uttar Pradesh. 
 
(d): Periodic meetings are conducted with States/UTs to review the implementation 
of PM-KISAN Scheme including digital infrastructure and bureaucratic complexities. A 
dedicated PM-KISAN portal and mobile app have been developed, offering services 
like self-registration, benefit status tracking, and facial authentication-based e-KYC. 
PM-KISAN Scheme has also been integrated with the Farmer ID which is a single, 
verified identity for every farmer. Common Service Centres (CSCs) have also been on-
boarded to provide services like registration and eKYC. Further, Village Nodal Officers 
(VNOs) also provide the services of eKYC to the farmers.  
 
In order to ensure that no eligible farmer, including marginal farmers, is left out, 
the Government of India undertakes saturation drives in coordination with the 
States/UTs In addition, States/UTs also undertake saturation drives from time to time 
to identify and facilitate the enrolment of eligible farmers completing all mandatory 
conditions under the Scheme.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF AGRICULTURE & FARMERS WELFARE 
DEPARTMENT OF AGRICULTURE & FARMERS WELFARE 
 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 2575 
TO BE ANSWERED ON THE 4TH AUGUST 2026 
 
PROMOTION OF MODERNISATION IN AGRICULTURE 
 
2575. MS. S JOTHIMANI: 
Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE कृ ͪष एवं ͩकसान 
कãयाण मंğी be pleased to state: 
(a) the details of the initiatives taken to promote modernisation in agriculture, 
including mechanization, precision farming and the use of AI; 
(b) the details of the financial and technical support provided to farmers for 
adopting modern agricultural practices; 
(c) the steps taken to improve access to timely credit, efficient irrigation, and 
climate-resilient technologies; and 
(d) whether the Government has collaborated with private sectors or research 
institutions to enhance agricultural productivity and if so, the details thereof? 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE FOR AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE  
कृ ͪष एवं ͩकसान कãयाण राÏय मंğी  (SHRI RAMNATH THAKUR)   
 
(a) &(b): Agriculture is a State subject and Government of India supports the efforts 
of States for modernization in agriculture through appropriate policy measures and 
budgetary allocation under various schemes/ programmes.  
Sub-Mission on Agricultural Mechanization (SMAM) provides financial assistance 
to farmers for purchasing modern agricultural machinery and equipment. This 
centrally sponsored scheme provides financial assistance @ 40-50% of the cost of 
machines to farmers for purchase of agricultural machinery and equipment. It also 
supports the establishment of Custom Hiring Centres (CHCs) with financial 
assistance @ 40% of the project cost for the projects costing up to Rs. 250 lakhs. 
Establishment of Farm Machinery Banks (FMBs) are supported with financial 
assistance @ 80% of the project cost for the projects costing up to Rs. 30 lakhs. 
The financial assistance towards FMBs for the North Eastern States is @ 95% of 
the project cost. Adoption of modern farm machinery, including precision agriculture 
tools, drones and other advanced mechanization technologies and women-friendly 
farm implements are encouraged under SMAM. 
Crop Residue Management (CRM) Scheme is implemented in the State of Punjab, 
Haryana, Uttar Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh and NCT of Delhi to promote sustainable 
crop residue management through the provision of subsidized agricultural 
machinery, establishment of Custom Hiring Centres (CHCs), and other measures 

aimed at reducing stubble burning. Financial assistance @ 50% of the cost of 
machinery is provided to the farmers for purchase of CRM machinery and financial 
assistance @ 80% of the project cost is provided for establishment of CHCs of crop 
residue management machinery. Financial assistance @ 65% on the capital cost 
of machinery costing up to Rs. 1.50 crores is also provided for establishing a robust 
supply chain of paddy straw for various end user industries in biomass power 
generation and biofuel sectors. 
Digital Agriculture Mission (DAM) promotes precision farming, satellite-based crop 
monitoring, and AI-driven advisories for improving productivity and resource 
efficiency. The Mission focuses on building a strong Digital Public Infrastructure 
(DPI) for agriculture, including AgriStack, the Krishi Decision Support System and 
comprehensive soil profile mapping. AgriStack comprises foundational databases 
such as Farmers’ Registry, Geo-referenced Village Maps and Crop Sown Registry, 
enabling timely and reliable crop-related information for farmers. The Mahalanobis 
National Crop Forecast Centre (MNCFC) supports the Mission through satellite-
based crop forecasting under the FASAL project, drought monitoring, and 
technological support to Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana (PMFBY) through 
YES-TECH and digital crop-cutting experiments. The Government is also 
promoting AI and IoT-based solutions for personalized advisories and improved 
farm management. Key initiatives include the AI- powered Kisan e-Mitra chatbot for 
farmer queries and the National Pest Surveillance System, which uses AI/ML tools 
to detect pest infestations and reduce crop losses. 
The Government is implementing various technology-oriented programmes for 
capacity building and skill development of farmers through Farm Machinery 
Training & Testing Institutes (FMTTIs), State Agricultural Universities (SAUs), 
Krishi Vigyan Kendras (KVKs) and other extension institutions for improving 
productivity and income of farmers. As an integral part of various schemes, the 
training programmes include short-term and medium-term practical training 
courses covering scientific and modern technology-based agricultural practices. 
(c): Yes, the Government has taken various initiatives to improve access to 
timely credit, efficient irrigation and climate-resilient technologies. The Kisan Credit 
Card (KCC) Scheme provide timely and affordable institutional credit to farmers for 
crop cultivation, post-harvest expenses and allied activities such as dairy, fisheries, 
and animal husbandry. The scheme enables farmers to access flexible, revolving 
credit through a simplified process, reducing dependence on informal sources of 
finance. The Government is also implementing Central Sector Scheme ‘Modified 
Interest Subvention Scheme (MISS)’ across various States and UTs, which provide 
concessional interest rates on short-term agricultural loans obtained by farmers 
through Kisan Credit Cards (KCC) for their working capital requirements. Under this 
scheme, farmers receive KCC loans at a subsidized interest rate of 7%. To facilitate 
this, an upfront interest subvention of 1.5% is provided to financial institutions. 
Additionally, farmers who repay their loans promptly receive a 3% Prompt 
Repayment Incentive (PRI), effectively reducing the interest rate to 4% per annum. 
The Agriculture Infrastructure Fund (AIF) provides medium-long term debt financing 
facility for investment in viable projects for post-harvest management infrastructure 
and viable farming assets through interest subvention and credit guarantee 
support. The Scheme provides 3% interest subvention and credit guarantee 

support on loans up to ₹2 crore for eligible borrowers, subject to a maximum lending 
rate of 9% per annum. 
Per Drop More Crop (PDMC) scheme promote initiatives towards enhancing water 
use efficiency at farm level through Micro Irrigation and increasing productivity of 
crops and income of farmers through precision water management. Financial 
assistance is provided to farmers @ 55% of the benchmark cost for Small and 
Marginal Farmers and 45% of the benchmark cost for other Farmers, for installation 
of micro-irrigation systems. The scheme also supports activities such as micro-
irrigation demonstrations, capacity building, training, and awareness programmes 
to facilitate adoption of efficient irrigation technologies. 
The National Mission for Sustainable Agriculture (NMSA) implement strategies to 
make Indian agriculture more resilient to the changing climate. Various schemes 
have been integrated under NMSA to deal with the adverse climate situations in 
the agriculture sector. PDMC scheme increases water use efficiency at the farm 
level through micro irrigation technologies i.e. drip and sprinkler irrigation systems. 
Rainfed Area Development (RAD) scheme focuses on Integrated Farming System 
(IFS) for enhancing productivity and minimizing risks associated with climatic 
variability. The Soil Health & Fertility scheme assists states in promoting Integrated 
Nutrient Management through judicious use of chemical fertilizers including 
secondary and micronutrients in conjunction with organic manures & bio-fertilizers 
for improving soil health and its productivity. Mission for Integrated Development of 
Horticulture, Agroforestry & National Bamboo Mission also promote climate 
resilience in agriculture. Further, Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana along with 
weather index based Restructured Weather Based Crop Insurance Scheme 
provide a comprehensive insurance cover against failure of the crop by providing 
financial support to farmers suffering crop loss/damage arising out of unforeseen 
natural calamities and adverse weather incidence.  
Indian Council of Agricultural Research (ICAR) is implementing a project, National 
Innovations in Climate Resilient Agriculture (NICRA) that studies the impact of 
climate change on agriculture including crops, livestock, horticulture and fisheries. 
It also develops and promotes climate resilient technologies to help the regions 
prone to extreme weather conditions. NICRA project creates awareness about 
impact of climate change among farmers. Capacity building programmes are 
conducted to educate the farmers for wider adoption of climate resilient 
technologies. Large scale demonstrations of climate resilient varieties are 
undertaken in farmers’ fields through Krishi Vigyan Kendras (KVKs) under NICRA. 
Farmers are also provided with weather advisories as ICAR in collaboration with 
India Meteorological Department issues Agromet advisories to farmers through 
Gramin Krishi Mausam Seva program.  
 (d): The Government has undertaken various collaborative initiatives with 
private-sector organizations, startups, industry bodies, national and international 
research institutions to enhance agricultural productivity, promote technology 
adoption and improve farmers' income. Public–Private Partnerships (PPPs) have 
been promoted in quality seed production, farm mechanization, precision 
agriculture, irrigation and post-harvest management. Through ICAR, collaborations 
with State Agricultural Universities (SAUs), private seed companies, agri-input 
industries and Farmer Producer Organizations (FPOs) support the development 
and dissemination of high-yielding, climate-resilient crop varieties and sustainable 

farming technologies. Under the Digital Agriculture Mission, partnerships with agri-
tech startups, technology companies and research institutions facilitate the 
deployment of Artificial Intelligence (AI), drones, Internet of Things (IoT), remote 
sensing and digital advisory services. The Government also supports agri-tech 
startups, promotes farm mechanization through partnerships with machinery 
manufacturers, collaborates with international research organizations for climate-
resilient technologies and disseminates innovations through KVKs via 
demonstrations, on-farm trials, training, and extension programmes. The National 
Mission on Edible Oil – Oilseeds (NMEO-OS) and Mission for Aatmanirbharta in 
Pulses promotes technological interventions and innovation by supporting the 
development and dissemination of improved seed varieties, climate-resilient 
technologies, mechanization, digital tools and extension activities. It also 
encourages collaboration with Farmer Producer Organizations (FPOs), 
cooperatives, private seed corporations and other stakeholders for seed 
production, technology dissemination and value chain development, thereby 
leveraging public-private partnerships to enhance technology adoption and 
productivity.

†2576. Shri Sudhakar Singh: 
 
Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE कृ िष एवं िकसान कÐयाण मंýी 
be pleased to state: 
(a) the details of progress made so far in terms of area expansion, productivity 
enhancement, and increase in total domestic production under the "Mission for Atmanirbharta 
in Pulses" implemented in the country for six years, year-wise and State-wise; 
(b) whether it is a fact that under this Mission, special efforts have been made to increase 
the Government procurement of pulses and expand farmers' participation under the Minimum 
Support Price (MSP) framework in the eastern States, including Bihar and if so, the details of 
the progress achieved so far; and 
(c) whether the Government has assessed the regional disparities existing in the 
productivity of pulses across various States and if so, the concrete steps being taken by the 
Government to bridge these gaps and reduce dependency on the import of pulses? 
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE FOR AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE 
 कृ िष एवं िकसान कÐयाण राºय मंýी (SHRI RAMNATH THAKUR) 
(a)    The Government of India has launched the Mission for Aatmanirbharta in Pulses in 
October, 2025. With a financial outlay of ₹11,440 crore, the Mission aims at boosting domestic 
production and achieving self-sufficiency (Aatmanirbharta) in pulses over a six-year period 
from 2025-26 to 2030-31. In India, the production of pulses has increased from 256.83 lakh 
tons during 2024-25 to 274.09 lakh tons during 2025-26. Similarly, the area under pulses has 
increased form 277.20 lakh ha to 286.46 lakh ha and the productivity of pulses has increased 
from 926 kg/ha to 957 kg/ha during the same period. The State-wise area, production and yield 
of pulses during 2024-25 and 2025-26 is at Annexure-I.  
(b)   Under Price Support Scheme (PSS) of Pradhan Mantri Annadata Aay Sanrakshan 
Abhiyan (PM-AASHA), procurement of notified pulses (Arhar, Moong, Urad, Masur & 
Chana) is undertaken on the request of the State Governments at Minimum Support Price 

(MSP) when market prices fall below MSP thus ensuring remunerative prices to the farmers 
for their agricultural produce. To encourage domestic production of pulses, the Government is 
undertaking procurement of Tur, Urad and Masur under the scheme on the request of State 
Government from pre-registered farmers as much as is offered by them through Central Nodal 
Agencies, namely the National Agricultural Cooperative Marketing Federation of India Ltd. 
(NAFED) and the National Cooperative Consumers' Federation of India Limited (NCCF). For 
other pulses, the overall quantity of procurement by Central Government is limited to 25% of 
the production of the particular pulses in the state for the season. The procurement of pulses 
undertaken under PSS during 2025-26 for Eastern States is given at Annexure-II.  
(c)   The productivity of pulses across various States  is influenced by a wide range of 
factors, including soil conditions, level of  irrigation, weather, rainfall , temperature , land-
holding size, types of seeds being used, manure / fertilizer usage, farming practices etc. In order 
to enhance the productivity of pulses, under the Pulses Mission,  assistance is provided to 
farmers through the State Governments for various interventions such as production and 
distribution of newly released, high yielding & climate resilient varieties of seeds, 
demonstration of crop production technologies, seed kit distribution, capacity building and 
strengthening of post-harvest infrastructure. Under the Research & Development component 
of the Mission, financial support is given to promote strategic and adaptive research for 
improving the production and productivity of pulses. 
 In addition  the Indian Council of Agricultural Research (ICAR) is undertaking basic and 
strategic research on pulses crops at the ICAR-Indian Institute of Pulses Research, Kanpur and 
its regional stations .ICAR is also undertaking applied research through All India Coordinated 
Research Project (AICRP) on pulses in collaboration with state agricultural 
universities/research institutes for developing location-specific high yielding varieties and 
matching production technology packages to enhance productivity potential and production of 
pulses. As a result, total 473 high yielding climate resilient varieties of Pulses comprising 118 
of Gram, 66 of Tur (Arhar), 69 of Mung bean, 62 of Urd bean, 50 of Lentil, 39 of Field pea, 29 
of Cowpea, 9 of Horse gram, 9 of Rajmash, 5 of Faba bean, 5 of Cluster bean, 3 of Indian bean, 
5 of Moth bean and 4 of Lathyrus have been notified for cultivation in the country during the 
last 11 years (2014-2025).

during the last three years and if so, the details of projects approved and their present status; 
(b) the details of funds sanctioned, released and utilised under the Mission for Tamil Nadu and the 
details of assistance provided, component-wise;  
(c) whether assistance has been provided for indigenous breed development, artificial insemination,

AGRICULTURAL ROADMAPS BASED ON AGRO-CLIMATIC CONDITIONS 
 
2578. SHRI LAVU SRI KRISHNA DEVARAYALU: 
          SHRI PUTTA MAHESH KUMAR: 
 
Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS’ WELFARE कृͪष एवं ͩकसान 
कãयाण मंğी be pleased to state: 
 
(a) Whether the Government has initiated preparation of State-wise agricultural 
roadmaps based on agro-climatic conditions in consultation with the State 
Governments; 
(b) if so, the details regarding the number of consultations held with the States for 
preparation of such roadmaps, State/UT-wise; 
(c) the number of States that are currently preparing or have initiated preparation of 
such agricultural roadmaps along with the present status thereof; 
(d) the details regarding the financial, technical or institutional assistance provided by 
the Union Government to various States for preparation of these roadmaps; 
(e) the timeline fixed by the Government for preparation and finalization of such State-
wise agricultural roadmaps and commencement of implementation thereof; 
(f) the details regarding the institutional framework and agencies involved in 
preparation of these roadmaps and the mechanism adopted to ensure alignment with 
local agro-climatic conditions, climate resilience and farmer needs; and 
(g) the expected outcomes and targets proposed to be achieved through these 
roadmaps? 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE FOR AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE  
 
क ृ िष एवं िकसान कʞाण राǛ मंũी (SHRI  RAMNATH THAKUR) 
 
 
 
(a) to (g):  As reported by the Indian Council of Agricultural Research (ICAR), 
Agricultural Action Plans have been initiated for the States of Assam, Goa, 
Maharashtra, Uttarakhand, Tamil Nadu, Andhra Pradesh, Andaman & Nicobar 
Islands. Comprehensive consultations have been undertaken with the concerned 
State Governments and other stakeholders for preparation of these agricultural 
Roadmaps.  
  

 
     The Agricultural Roadmap are being prepared collaboratively by ICAR, Department 
of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare, ICAR, ICAR Institutes, State Governments, State 
Agricultural Universities, and experts. The planning is based on agro-climatic regions, 
natural resource endowments, climate resilience, technological interventions and 
farmers' needs. The roadmaps aim to ensure technical validation, alignment with State 
priorities, local agro-climatic conditions, and climate resilience. 
 
        The Roadmap seek enhancement of productivity, profitability and resource-use 
efficiency in agriculture and allied sectors. The agricultural roadmaps is broad policy 
framework based on agro-climatic conditions. States/UTs may refer to these guiding 
principles while formulating annual action plans under various schemes.  The key 
outcomes of Agricultural Roadmap include enhancing farmers’ income, improve self-
sufficiency in agricultural and allied commodities, generate rural employment 
opportunities and ensure sustainable growth of the agriculture sector, while 
addressing local agro-climatic conditions, climate resilience and farmers’ needs.

Will the Minister of FISHERIES, ANIMAL HUSBANDRY AND DAIRYING 
मत्स्यपालन, पशुपालन और डेयरी मंत्री 
be pleased to state: 
 
(a) the current status of the implementation of the National Livestock Mission (NLM) and the 
details of efforts being made by the Government to enhance milk production and productivity, 
State and district -wise including Maharashtra, Lok Sabha Constituency Nabarangpur in Odisha, 
Lok Sabha Constituency Valmiki Nagar in Bihar and Akola district in Maharashtra; 
(b) the details of the progress made so far under the breed improvement, fodder development and 
animal health programmes during the last five years, State/district-wise including Maharashtra and 
Akola district in Maharashtra and Nabarangpur district in Odisha; 
(c) the details of financial assistance provided by the Union Government to States for livestock 
and dairy development and the number of projects sanctioned during the last three years, State -
wise including Maharashtra and Lok Sabha Constituency Jalgaon an d Akola district in 
Maharashtra and Lok Sabha Constituency Nabarangpur in Odisha; 
(d) the details of steps taken by the Government to promote dairy activities, enhance farmer's 
income through dairying livestock development, generate employment, dairy livestock and value 
addition and to achieve self -reliance in milk and livestock product s, State and district -wise 
including Lok Sabha Constituency Nabarangpur and Akola district in Maharashtra; 
(e) whether the Government has any proposals to undertake further initiatives to achieve self -
sufficiency in milk and livestock products and strengthen the livestock sector, if so, the details 
thereof, State-wise including Maharashtra and Lok Sabha Constituency Jalgaon and Akola district; 
(f) whether the Government has taken any measures to strengthen dairy infrastructure, livestock 
disease control, artificial insemination and scientific livestock management, if so, the details 
thereof, State-wise including Lok Sabha Constituency Jalgaon; 

(g) whether the Government has any proposals to strengthen livestock and dairy development 
infrastructure, if so, the details thereof, State -wise including Maharashtra, particularly in Lok 
Sabha Constituency Jalgaon; 
(h) the assessment and impact of the NLM on milk productivity, rural employment and income 
enhancement of livestock farmers; and 
(i) whether the Government has any proposal to strengthen livestock and dairy development 
infrastructure in Maharashtra particularly in Lok Sabha Constituency Jalgaon, if so, the details 
thereof? 
ANSWER 
 
THE MINISTER OF FISHERIES, ANIMAL HUSBANDRY AND DAIRYING 
(SHRI RAJIV RANJAN SINGH ALIAS LALAN SINGH) 
 
(a and b) The National Livestock Mission (NLM) is under implementation in the country.  In order 
to supplement the efforts of the States and Union Territories, the Department of Animal Husbandry 
and Dairying (DAHD), Government of India is implementing Rashtriya Gokul Mission (RGM) 
for enhancement of milk production and productivity for cattle  and buffalo through Nation-wide 
Artificial Insemination Programme  (NAIP), In -Vitro Fertilization (IVF), sex -sorted semen 
technology, strengthening of semen station in the country including all the districts of Maharashtra, 
Odisha and Bihar. 
 
RGM scheme is implemented for breed improvement for cattle and buffalo.  NLM scheme focuses 
on  breed development of sheep, goat, pig, camel, donkey and horses and fodder production. 
Livestock Health and Disease Control Programme  (LHDCP) is implemented for disease control. 
The progress made under RGM, LHDCP and NLM during last five years is as under: 
 
Rashtriya Gokul Mission:  
 
(i) 17.27 crore Artificial Insemination have been performed covering 10.51 crore animals 
and 5.98 crore farmers benefitted across the country under NAIP programme. Number of 
Artificial Insemination conducted in Maharashtra, Odisha and Bihar including Lok S baha 
constituency Nabarangpur , Odisha, Lok Sabha constituency Valmiki Nagar, Bihar and 
Akola District in Maharashtra is at Annexure- I. 47687 Multi -Purpose Artificial 
Insemination Technicians in Rural India (MAITRI’s )  have been trained and inducted in 
the country under the Scheme. The State -wise district -wise details of establishment of 
MAITRIs, including Lok Sabha Constituency Naba rangpur in Odisha, Lok Sabha 
Constituency Valmiki Nagar in Bihar and Aloka district in Maharashtra given under 
Annexure-. I 
 
(ii) Assistance have been provided for establishment of 24 IVF laboratories including 3 
labs in Maharashtra and 2 in Bihar State for promotion of indigenous breeds in the country. 
From these labs 29283 viable embryos have been produced, 17424 embryos trans ferred 
and 2748 calves born. 
 
(iii) Accelerated Breed Improvement programme  using IVF technology is initiated to 
deliver technology at farmers’ doorstep. Incentive at rate Rs 5000/ - assured pregnancy is 
made available to farmers under the component. Under the programme so far 7959 
embryos transferred, 1666 pregnancies established  and 1223 calves born under the 
programme including 1142 females.  
 

(iv) 1.41 crore sex-sorted semen doses have been produced using high genetic merit bulls, 
including bulls from indigenous breeds. 9.71 lakh Artificial Insemination have been 
performed using sex sorted semen and 7.82 lakh farmers benefitted as per data available 
on Bharat Pashudhan. 
(v) 48 semen stations have been sanctioned including 4 semen stations in     Maharashtra 
(Rahuri, Nagpur, Aurangabad & Pune) and one in Bihar (Purnea).  
(vi) 28 heifer rearing centers have been sanctioned in the country, including Munger and 
Dumroan centre in Bihar and one at Kolhapur with capacity of 500 Heifers in Maharashtra.   
 
National Livestock Mission: 
(i) Five regional semen stations for sheep and goat have been approved in the State of West 
Bengal, Andhra Pradesh, Jammu and Kashmir, Assam and Rajasthan.  Six goat semen 
banks for goat have also been approved for the state of Jammu and Kashmir, Meghalaya, 
West Bengal, Assam, Himachal Pradesh and Rajasthan. 6,405 cattle and buffalo Artificial 
Insemination (AI) centers have been upgraded to provide AI services for goat in the 
State/UT of Jammu and Kashmir, Chhattisgarh, West Bengal, Rajasthan, Himachal 
Pradesh and Meghalaya.  Nine pig semen collection and processing laboratories have been 
approved in the State of Sikkim, Meghalaya, Arunachal Pradesh, Manipur, Mizoram, 
Assam and Tamil Nadu. 
(ii) 4084 breed multiplication farms for poultry, sheep, goat, pig, camel, horse and donkey 
have been approved. 
(iii) 1.61 lakh metric ton of quality fodder seed has been produced so far. 
 
   (iv) 204 silage and TMR making units have been approved under NLM -Entrepreneurship 
Development Program (NLM -EDP) with expected capacity of 7.20 lakh metric ton per 
annum. 
 
(vi) three numbers of fodder seed processing and grading units have been approved with 
7000 Metric ton per annum processing capacity.  
 
 Livestock Health and Disease Control Program:

In Jalgaon district:  FMD vaccination 38 Lakhs, Brucellosis vaccination 0.69 Lakhs, CSF 
vaccination 0.14 Lakhs and PPR: 10.82 Lakhs. 
 
(c) Financial assistance is provided to the State Government. Details of financial assistance 
provided to States/UTs under RGM, NLM, National Programme for Dairy Development (NPDD) 
and LHDCP are at Annexure II. No. of projects sanctioned under NPDD, Animal Husbandry 
Infrastructure Development Fund(AHIDF) and NLM -EDP state-wise is at Annexure III. 
   
(d) to (i) Department  of Animal Husbandry and Dairying (DAHD) is implementing National 
Programme for Dairy Development (NPDD) scheme across the country since 2014 -15. NPDD 
scheme is being implemented with the following two components: 
 
Component A  of NPDD focuses on creating and strengthening infrastructure for quality milk 
testing, primary milk procurement and chilling facilities across the country. It also supports the 
development of milk processing and value addition infrastructure in the Hilly Areas, North Eastern 
Region (NER) and Union Territories (UTs). This component is being implemented across the 
country. 
 
Component B of the NPDD scheme, “Dairying through Cooperatives,” aims to increase sale of 
milk and dairy products by increasing farmer’s access to organized market, upgrading dairy 
processing facilities and marketing infrastructure. This component is being implemented  in nine 
States. Maharashtra and Odisha are not covered under Component B of NPDD scheme  
 
Details of financial assistance provided by the Union Government to States and number of projects 
sanctioned during the last three years under NPDD scheme is at Annexure-II & III. 
 
Further, the Department of Animal Husbandry and Dairying is implementing Animal Husbandry 
Infrastructure Development Fund (AHIDF) to incentivize the dairy processing and value addition 
infrastructure, meat processing and value addition, animal feed plant, Technology assisted breed 
multiplication farm, veterinary drugs and vaccine infrastructure, waste to wealth ( agri-waste) and 
primary wool processing infrastructure.  Under the scheme 3% interest subvention is provided on 
the term loan for eight years to Individual, FPO, MSME, Private Companies, Dairy Cooperatives 
and Section 8. The State-wise sanctioned dairy projects are at Annexure - III 
 
The Government of Maharashtra proposes to strengthen livestock and dairy development 
infrastructure through the Mukhyamantri Gramin Pashudhan Udyojakta Yojana, in the State of 
Maharashtra, including Lok Sabha Constituency Jalgaon. 
 
The Government of India has taken various initiative for strengthening dairy infrastructure, 
livestock disease control, artificial insemination and scientific livestock management in the 
country including all Lok Sabha constituency of Maharashtra through i mplementation of the 
following schemes:  
(i) National Programme for Dairy Development and Animal Husbandry Infrastructure 
Development Fund for strengthening dairy infrastructure.  
(ii) Livestock Health and Disease Control Programme for prevention and control diseases in 
livestock  
(iii) Rashtriya Gokul Mission for breed development of cattle and buffalo through Artificial 
Insemination and scientific livestock management.  

(iv) National Livestock Mission for breed development and scientific management of small 
ruminant, camel, horse, donkey and pig. 
 
The NITI Aayog has conducted detailed review of the NLM scheme including the EDP 
component. The evaluation confirms that NLM has enabled progress in breed development, feed 
and fodder security, capacity building, and entrepreneurship promotion. Majority of beneficiaries 
reported improved livestock productivity, increased income, reduced input costs, and stronger 
linkages with veterinary and extension services.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF RURAL DEVELOPMENT

OPERATIONALISATION OF SHE-LEAPS 
 
2580. Shri Yaduveer Wadiyar: 
 
Will the Minister of RURAL DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state: 
 
(a)  whether the Government has operationalised the Self Help 
Entrepreneur-Livelihoods and Enterprise Application for 
Prosperity and Sustainability (SHE-LEAPS) for monitoring 
enterprises established under the Deendayal Antyodaya Yojana-
National Rural Livelihoods Mission (DAY-NRLM), if so, the details 
thereof; 
(b)  the details of SHG enterprises registered on the digital platform, 
State-wise; 
(c)  whether the Government maintains data on enterprise 
continuity, turnover and income generation through SHE-LEAPS, 
if so, the details thereof; 
(d)  the details of SHG enterprises established through Community 
Investment Fund assistance under DAY-NRLM in Karnataka 
during the last three years and the number of SHGs that still 
remain operational at the present; and 
(e)  the measures taken to strengthen the sustainability and market 
competitiveness of SHG enterprises thereof? 
 
ANSWER 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF RURAL DEVELOPMENT 
(DR. CHANDRA SEKHAR PEMMASANI) 
  
(a): The Self-Help Entrepreneur-Livelihoods and Enterprise 
Application for Prosperity and Sustainability (SHE-LEAPS) has been 
operationalized and has the provision for monitoring the enterprises 
on boarded through SHE-LEAPS. The application was launched on 
29th June, 2026 on the occasion of Rashtriya Gramin Vikas 
Sammelan of Ministry of Rural Development. SHE-LEAPS application 
is developed under the LokOS digital platform for capturing 
enterprise-related information of Self Help Group (SHG) 
entrepreneurs under DAY-NRLM. The platform supports onboarding of 

Page 2 of 3 
 
enterprises and captures real-time enterprise data to facilitate 
management and monitoring of enterprises. It is being implemented 
across 34 States and UTs through the State Rural Livelihood Missions 
and in monitoring enterprises and support for planning and decision-
making. 
(b): The State-wise details of SHG enterprises registered on the 
SHE-LEAPS digital platform are given at Annexure-I. 
(c): The SHE-LEAPS digital platform captures the details of 
enterprises promoted under DAY-NRLM. This platform has provision 
to maintain the information relating to annual turnover and 
enterprises continuity for all enterprises indicated in Annexure-I. 
(d): As reported by the Karnataka State Rural Livelihoods Mission 
(KSRLM), the details of SHG enterprises established through 
Community Investment Fund (CIF) assistance under DAY-NRLM in 
Karnataka during the last three years and the number of SHG 
enterprises are as follows:  
Sl no. Year No. of SHG enterprises 
1.   2023-2024 21,438 
2.   2024-2025 27,173  
3.   2025-2026 31,246  
  Total 79,857  
  
(e): The Ministry of Rural Development, under DAY-NRLM, has taken 
several measures to strengthen the sustainability and market 
competitiveness of Self Help Group (SHG) enterprises. The Ministry 
has registered the brands "Saras", "Saras Aajeevika" and "Aajeevika" 
for promotion of SHG products. Twenty-five States have also created 
State-level brands, such as UMED (Maharashtra), Palash and Adiva 
(Jharkhand), Himira (Himachal Pradesh) and Mathi (Tamil Nadu) etc. 
to facilitate the sale of SHG products. Saras Melas are organised at 
the National, Regional, State and District levels to promote SHG 
products, including two National-level Saras Melas, one Food Festival 
and more than 50 State-level Saras Melas annually. A retail outlet, 
Saras Aajeevika Gallery, operates in Central Delhi for the sale of 
curated SHG products, while States also operate retail outlets under 
their respective brands. In addition, the Ministry operates the eSaras 
e-commerce platform for the sale of curated SHG products and has 
entered into partnerships with GeM, ONDC, Amazon, Flipkart, Meesho 
and JioMart to facilitate their wider market access.
