GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF SOCIAL JUSTICE & EMPOWERMENT 
DEPARTMENT OF EMPOWERMENT OF PERSONS WITH DISABILITIES 
(DIVYANGJAN) 
  
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO.2581 
TO BE ANSWERED ON- 04/08.2026 
  
ADIP SCHEME AND RASHTRIYA VAYOSHRI YOJANA 
  
2581. Shri Bhausaheb Rajaram Wakchaure: 
  
Will the Minister of SOCIAL JUSTICE AND EMPOWERMENT be pleased to state: 
  
(a) whether there is a provision for organizing special camps in rural areas for the distribution of 
assistive aids and appliances under the Assistance to Divyangjans for Purchase/Fitting of Aids 
and Appliances (ADIP) scheme and the Rashtriya Vayoshri Yojana (RVY), if so, the details 
thereof; 
  
(b) whether the Government is aware of the large number of Divyangjan and their poor 
economic condition in the Sangamner Taluka of the Shirdi Parliamentary Constituency in 
Ahilyanagar district, if so, the details thereof; 
  
(c) whether there is any proposal to organize a special 'Assistive Aids Distribution Camp' in 
Sangamner through the Artificial Limbs Manufacturing Corporation of India (ALIMCO), if so, 
the details thereof; 
  
(d) whether modern equipments including motorized tricycles (battery-operated tricycles) and 
hearing aids are likely to be provided through the said camp and if so, the details thereof; and 
  
(e) the timeline by which this camp is likely to be organized in Sangamner?  
  
ANSWER 
  
MINISTER OF STATE FOR SOCIAL JUSTICE AND EMPOWERMENT 
(SHRI B. L. VERMA) 
  
(a) Under the Assistance to Persons with Disabilities for Purchase/Fitting of Aids/Appliances 
(ADIP) Scheme which is demand driven, assessment and distribution camps are organised across 
the country, including in rural and remote areas, for providing aids and assistive devices to 
eligible persons with disabilities (Divyangjan). Such camps are organised through the Artificial 

2 
 
Limbs Manufacturing Corporation of India (ALIMCO), a major implementing agency under the 
Scheme, in coordination with the District Administration, generally on the request of Hon'ble 
Members of Parliament, Public Representatives and District Administration. 
(b) Relief to persons with disabilities is primarily a State subject by virtue of Entry 9 in the State 
List of the Constitution of India. The Central Government supplements the efforts of the States 
for the welfare of persons with disabilities through various schemes and programmes. Specific 
information regarding the number of persons with disabilities and their economic condition is not 
maintained by this Department & hence such information regarding Sangamner Taluka of the 
Shirdi Parliamentary Constituency in Ahilyanagar district is not available. 
(c) to (e) With a view to enhancing the outreach and ensuring year-round availability of services 
under the Assistance to Persons with Disabilities for Purchase/Fitting of Aids/Appliances (ADIP) 
Scheme and the Rashtriya Vayoshri Yojana (RVY), the Department of Empowerment of Persons 
with Disabilities (DEPwD), in association with the Artificial Limbs Manufacturing Corporation 
of India (ALIMCO), has opened permanent centres across the country known as Pradhan Mantri 
Divyasha-Vayoshri Kendras (PMD-VKs). 
These walk-in centres provide assessment, fitting and distribution of eligible aids and assistive 
devices, including motorized tricycles, hearing aids, wheelchairs, tricycles and other assistive 
devices, to divyangjan and senior citizens, subject to the provisions and eligibility criteria of the 
respective Schemes. 
So far, 107 PMD-VKs have been opened across the country, including PMD-VK District 
Disability Rehabilitation Centre (DDRC) Ahilyanagar, Maharashtra. Since a permanent PMD-
VK is operational in Ahilyanagar district, the aids and assistive devices are being provided 
through the permanent PMD-VK, thereby ensuring year-round access to eligible beneficiaries.

TO BE ANSWERED ON - 04/08/2026 
   
SPECIAL RECOGNISED INSTITUTIONS FOR THE EDUCATION OF 
DIVYANGJANS 
  
2582 : Shri Tejasvi Surya; 
 
Will the Minister of SOCIAL JUSTICE AND EMPOWERMENT be pleased to state: 
 
(a) the measures taken by the Department of Empowerment of Divyangjans (DEPwD), through 
its National Institutes and Special Recognised Institutions, to improve the quality of education 
for Divyangjans, including educational facilities, assistive devices, scholarships and other 
concessions provided to students; 
 
(b) the number of trained special educators available in the Special Recognised Institutions for 
the Education of Divyangjans in Bengaluru, Chennai, Hyderabad and Mumbai, along with the 
sanctioned and vacant posts, if any; 
 
(c) the measures taken to strengthen infrastructure, assistive technologies, digital learning 
resources and the availability of trained special educators in these institutions; 
 
(d) the proposed steps to be taken by the Government under the “Project 
Formation/Commission" initiative; and  
 
(e) whether the Government proposes to establish additional Special Recognised Institutions 
or upgrade the existing institutions to improve access to quality education for Divyangjans, if 
so, the details thereof? 
  
  
ANSWER 
  
 MINISTER OF STATE FOR SOCIAL JUSTICE AND EMPOWERMENT 
 (SHRI B. L. VERMA) 
  
(a):  National Institutes and their Composite Regional Centres under the Department conducts 
recognized undergraduate, postgraduate, diploma and certificate programmes including for 
Divyangjans. These institutions have undertaken various initiatives to enhance the quality of 
education for Divyangjans, including the development of inclusive and accessible educational 
infrastructure, accessible classrooms, laboratories, clinical facilities, smart classrooms, digital 
libraries, and access to e-books and e-journals. They also conduct skill development 
programmes.  

2 
 
Under ‘Assistance to Persons with Disabilities for Purchase/ Fitting of Aids/ Appliances 
(ADIP) scheme, funds are released including to National Institutes and Artificial Limbs 
Manufacturing Corporation of India (ALIMCO), Kanpur, a CPSE under this Department, for 
providing modern assistive devices to eligible Divyangjans, including students.  
Under the Scholarship Scheme for Students with Disabilities, scholarships are provided under 
six components – Pre-Matric, Post-Matric, Top Class, National Fellowship, National Overseas 
Scholarship and Free Coaching. 
National Institutes functioning under the aegis of the Department of Empowerment of Persons 
with Disabilities also allow waiver of fee to Divyangjans in academic courses etc. 
(b): Total 26 posts are sanctioned in the National Institutes and their CRCs/RCs under the aegis 
of the Department of Empowerment of Persons with Disabilities situated in Bengaluru, 
Chennai, Hyderabad and Mumbai and as on date 24 Special Educators are in position. 
(c) to (e): National Institutes have developed barrier-free infrastructure, smart classrooms, 
resource rooms, therapy units, computer laboratories and accessible digital learning resources 
including e-learning platforms and ICT-enabled tools. 
ALIMCO is promoting advanced assistive technologies through partnerships with premier 
academic institutions, national laboratories, research organisations and start-ups. 
During last five years, the Department has released Rs. 452.38 Crore to National Institutes for 
strengthening their infrastructure and also provided Rs. 544.16 crore towards resources, 
equipment, training and other institutional activities. 
Qualified special educators are recruited as per RCI norms and their capacity is continuously 
enhanced through CRE programmes, Faculty Development Programmes, workshops and 
seminars. 
At present, there is no proposal to establish additional National Institutes. However, 
upgradation of existing institutions is a continuous process and infrastructure, equipment and 
facilities are upgraded as per requirements of National Institutes.

2583. DR. MOHAMMAD JAWED: 
Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE कृ ͪष एवं ͩकसान 
कãयाण मंğी be pleased to state : 
(a) the details of the risks and perils covered under the Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima 
Yojana (PMFBY); 
(b) whether the Government maintains data on crop losses caused by floods and 
river erosion across the country, particularly for Bihar and if so, the details of the 
same for the last three financial years, State/UT-wise; 
(c) whether the Government will furnish the number of crop insurance claims 
received in Bihar due to floods during the last three financial years, along with the 
number of claims settled and the total amount of compensation disbursed, year-wise; 
and 
(d) the measures which the Government has taken to mitigate crop losses caused by 
floods and river erosion and to ensure timely settlement of insurance claims under 
PMFBY ? 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE FOR AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE  
 
कृ ͪष एवं ͩकसान कãयाण राÏय मंğी  (SHRI RAMNATH THAKUR) 
 
(a):  Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana (PMFBY) provides for yield based 
comprehensive risk insurance against crop damage from pre-sowing to post-harvest 
for crops and area notified by the concerned State Government.  The scheme not 
only safeguards crops of farmers against wide spread yield loss due to non-
preventable natural risks/ & extreme climate calamities viz.  flood, inundation, 
landslide, drought, heat waves, hailstorm, cyclone, pests/diseases, natural fire and  
lightening, storm, typhoon, tempest, hurricane, tornado etc.  but also against farm 
level yield loss due to localized risks (hailstorm, landslide, inundation, cloudburst and 
natural fire) and post harvest losses due to cyclone, cyclonic/unseasonal rain and 
hailstorm and  prevented sowing.   

     Whereas weather index based insurance is provided under Restructured Weather 
Based Crop Insurance Scheme (RWBCIS) through scientifically designed term 
sheets. RWBCIS is generally applicable for horticultural crops and provides 
insurance protection to the farmers against adverse weather incidence, such as 
deficit and excess rainfall, high or low temperature, humidity etc., which are deemed 
to impact crop production adversely. It has the advantage to settle claims within the 
shortest possible time. The States/UTs are required to notify crops under RWBCIS. 
(b) :   Such data is not maintained centrally. 
(c) :  The State of Bihar does not implement Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana 
(PMFBY)/ Restructured Weather Based Crop Insurance Scheme (RWBCIS). 
  
However, as informed by the State Government of Bihar, surveys are conducted 
regarding flood-induced crop damage.  Based on the same, compensation is provided

settlement of claims under the PMFBY: 
- Government has undertaken development of National Crop Insurance Portal 
(NCIP) as a single source of data for subsidy payment, dissemination of 
information,  delivery of services including online enrolment of farmers, 
uploading/obtaining individual insured famer’s details and transfer of claim 
amount electronically to the individual farmer’s Bank Account.   

 
- In order to rigorously monitor claim disbursal process, a dedicated module 
namely ‘Digiclaim Module’ has been operationalized for payment of claims 
from Kharif 2022 onwards.  It involves integration of National Crop Insurance 
Portal (NCIP) with Public Finance Management System (PFMS) and 
accounting system of Insurance Companies to provide timely & transparent 
processing of all claims. 
 
- W.e.f. Kharif 2024, in case payment is not made timely by Insurance 
Company, penalty of 12% is auto-calculated and levied through NCIP.    
 
- Delinking of Central Government share of premium subsidy from that of State 
Governments has been implemented so that farmers can get proportionate 
claims relating to the Central Government share.  
 
- 12% penalty is also levied from Kharif 2025 on State Government for delay in 
release of State share of subsidy. 
 
- Opening of ESCROW Account by the State Government concerned for 
deposit of their premium share in advance as per provisions of the scheme 
has been made mandatory w.e.f. Kharif 2025 season for bringing financial 
discipline.   
 
- Also, towards leveraging technology in implementation of the scheme, various 
steps like capturing of yield data/Crop Cutting Experiments (CCEs) data 
through CCE-Agri App & uploading it on the NCIP, allowing insurance 
companies to witness the conduct of CCEs, integration of State land records 
with NCIP and usage of remote sensing based yield estimation through YES-
TECH have already been taken to improve timely settlement of the claims to 
farmers.   
 
- Crop Loss Assessment App (CLAP), developed as a digital mobile application 
to streamline and improve the efficiency of crop loss assessments for 
loacalised calamities/post harvest losses for individual farms and  land parcels 
under PMFBY.  The use of CLAP has been made mandatory for all the 
States/Uts under the scheme.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF PANCHAYATI RAJ 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO.– 2584 
ANSWERED ON- 04.08.2026 
  
OPERATIONALISATION OF THE PANCHAYAT DEVOLUTION INDEX 
  
2584. SMT. POONAMBEN HEMATBHAI MAADAM: 
  
Will the Minister of PANCHAYATI RAJ be pleased to state: 
  
(a) the details of the current status of operationalisation of the Panchayat Devolution Index 
across States and Union Territories; 
 (b) whether the Government has assessed the progress of States under the Index, if so, the 
details of top performing States under the Index; 
 (c) whether the findings of the Index are being utilised for policy formulation and 
capacity  building, if so, the details thereof; and  
(d) whether any incentives have been provided to improve performance under the Index if so, the 
details thereof? 
 
ANSWER  
  
THE MINISTER OF PANCHAYATI RAJ 
 
(SHRI RAJIV RANJAN SINGH) 
  
(a) & (b)  “Panchayat”, being “Local Government”, is a State subject and part of State List of 
Seventh Schedule of the Constitution of India. Panchayats are set up and operate through the 
respective State Panchayati Raj Acts. States have made their own Panchayati Raj Act, subject to 
the provisions of the Constitution.  
  
 However, the Ministry of Panchayati Raj reviews performance of Panchayats, from time 
to time, through studies, review meetings, field visits, video conferencing, Information 
Technology applications etc. 
  
This Ministry has released a report titled “Status of Devolution to Panchayats in States - 
An Indicative Evidence-Based Ranking, 2024” in February 2025 only to assess the effectiveness 
of devolution and the role of local governments in strengthening grassroots democracy of the 
States/UTs. This report presents the Devolution Index, which provides the overall scores and 
ranks for all States/Union Territories covered under Part-IX of the Constitution, based on six 
identified dimensions: Framework, Functions, Finances, Functionaries, Capacity Enhancement, 

2 
 
and Accountability. This report reveals that the extent of devolution has increased from 39.9% to 
43.9% between the period 2013-14 to 2021-22. Ranking of States/UTs, including top performing 
States, in Devolution Index and Sub-indices is attached as Annexure-I. 
  
(c) & (d) Yes, Sir. The Ministry has implemented a Centrally Sponsored Scheme, namely the 
Revamped Rashtriya Gram Swaraj Abhiyan (RGSA), w.e.f. financial year 2022-23, with the 
objective of supporting Panchayati Raj institutions by imparting trainings to Elected 
Representatives and other stakeholders to develop leadership abilities, thereby enabling Gram 
Panchayats to function effectively across all States/UTs. Under the scheme, capacity building 
support is provided to elected representatives, functionaries, and other stakeholders of 
Panchayats under different categories, viz. basic orientation and refresher programmes, thematic 
interventions, specialized trainings and Panchayat Development Plan-related programmes, etc. 
The scheme also supports exposure visits to facilitate experiential learning and replication of best 
practices for strengthening Panchayat governance, as well as development of training modules 
and materials etc.  A total of 1,66,41,509 participants from financial year 2022-23 to 2026-27 (as 
on 10th July, 2026) have been trained under this scheme. 
  
Further, to enhance skills and knowledge, a major step has also been taken to build 
capacity and train elected representatives and functionaries of Panchayats through Institutes of 
excellence such as IIMs/IITs under the Leadership/Management Development Program (MDP).  
  
The Ministry of Panchayati Raj, in collaboration with IIM Ahmedabad, has also 
developed a training module on Own Source Revenue (OSR) to strengthen the financial self-
reliance of Gram Panchayats. The module helps elected representatives and Panchayat 
functionaries understand how OSR is generated through tax and non-tax sources.  
  
Additionally, the Ministry has launched a Specialized Training Module as a part of 
“Shashkta Panchayat Netri Abhiyan” for the capacity building of Women Elected 
Representatives of Panchayati Raj Institutions. The focus of this training module is to build the 
capacity of Women Elected Representatives across different aspects of rural governance and 
enhance their knowledge and practical skills for the effective discharge of roles and 
responsibilities as elected representatives, thereby promoting women-led governance. 
  
This Ministry does not provide any incentive to improve performance under the 
Devolution Index.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF FISHERIES, ANIMAL HUSBANDRY AND DAIRYING 
DEPARTMENT OF FISHERIES 
 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 2585 
ANSWERED ON 04/08/2026 
 
SMALL FISHERMEN IN SUNDARBANS 
2585. SHRI BAPI HALDAR:  
Will the Minister of FISHERIES, ANIMAL HUSBANDRY AND DAIRYING  be 
pleased to state: 
(a) whether the Government is aware that small fishermen in the Sundarbans in West Bengal are 
facing severe livelihood challenges due to the operation of large industrial trawlers engaged in 
destructive bottom trawling, if so, the details thereof; 
(b) whether the Government has assessed the impact of such practices on marine biodiversity, fish 
stocks and the livelihoods of traditional fishing communities in the region, if so, the details thereof; 
(c) the measures taken by the Government to regulate destructive fishing practices, strengthen 
monitoring and ensure sustainable fishing in the Sundarbans and adjoining coastal waters; and 
(d) whether the Government has any proposals to provide special support or protectio n measures 
for traditional and small -scale fishermen in the Lok Sabha Mathurapur Constituency in West 
Bengal, if so, the details thereof? 
 
ANSWER 
THE MINISTER OF FISHERIES, ANIMAL HUSBANDRY AND DAIRYING 
(SHRI RAJIV RANJAN SINGH ALIAS LALAN SINGH) 
(a) to (d): Marine fisheries within territorial waters (up to 12 nautical miles  from the baseline) 
are regulated by the respective Coastal States as per  their Marine Fishing Regulation Acts 
(MFRAs). In several States, including West Bengal, MFRA regulate the operation  of all 
mechanised fishing vessels in inshore areas traditionally used by small‑scale and artisanal fishers. 
Under the West Bengal Marine Fishing Regulation Rules, 1995, operational zones are demarcated 
based on vessel capacity, and mechanised vessels above 30 HP are prohibited from operating within 
Zone A (up to 15 km from the shoreline), which is reserved exclusively for traditional and 
small‑scale fishers. 
In the Exclusive Economic Zone (EEZ), the Government of India is implementing a range of 
conservation and management measures to curb destructive fishing practices and promote 
sustainable fisheries. These include a ban on paired/bull trawling and the use of LED lights in 
fishing, and maritime States/UTs have been advised to enforce similar restrictions within their 
respective territorial waters. A uniform 61‑day annual fishing ban is imposed in the EEZ during  

monsoon season to support fish stock regeneration. Monitoring of fishing activities and vessel 
safety has been strengthened through the national r oll‑out of the Vessel Communication and 
Support System (VCSS) under the Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana (PMMSY), involving 
installation of transponders and use of the Nabhmitra application. Under PMMSY, the Government 
of India is also supporting the fitment of Turtle Excluder Devices (TEDs) in shrimp trawls to protect 
sea turtles. Sea ranching and installation of artificial reefs in coastal areas are also being supported 
under PMMSY to enhance coastal fish stocks for the benefit of fishermen, particularly small‑scale 
fishers. 
The Department of Fisheries, Government of India  has been implementing the Pradhan Mantri 
Matsya Sampada Yojana (PMMSY) since 2020–21. Under PMMSY, the Department of Fisheries, 
Government of India has approved project proposals of West Bengal amounting to ₹546.38 crore, 
including a Central share of ₹223.25 crore. The approval inter alia  includes assistance for 
upgradation and conversion of traditional vessels, and promotion of deep‑sea fishing  vessels. 
Traditional and small‑scale fi shers across all States/UTs, including those in the Mathurapur Lok 
Sabha constituency, are eligible for support under the scheme. The Department of Fisheries, 
Government of India has also approved the modernisation and upgradation of the existing fishing 
harbours at Petuaghat, Shankarpur, Frasergunj and Kakdwip in Medinipur, Purba Medinipur and 
South 24 Parganas, West Bengal, with an investment of ₹65.65 crore, to provide safe and hygienic 
landing facilities for fishermen, including traditional fishers. Add itionally, alternative livelihood 
opportunities such as mariculture, seaweed cultivation, and open‑sea cage culture are being 
promoted to reduce pressure on nearshore fisheries. 
The Indian Council of Agricultural Research (ICAR) has informed that its research institutes and 
centres have been developing and demonstrating need‑based technologies for fish farmers and 
fishermen of West Bengal, including those in the Sundarbans, coveri ng freshwater aquaculture, 
brackishwater aquaculture, pen and cage culture in open‑water bodies, and marine fisheries 
assessment and management. These institutes are also implementing Central Government welfare 
schemes, including the Scheduled Caste Sub‑Pl an (SCSP) and Tribal Sub‑Plan (TSP), to provide 
livelihood support to marginal fishermen and fish farmers in the State, including in the Sundarbans.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF FISHERIES, ANIMAL HUSBANDRY AND DAIRYING 
DEPARTMENT OF FISHERIES 
 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION No. 2587 
ANSWERED ON 04/08/2026 
 
SUSTAINABLE FISHERIES MANAGEMENT 
2587. THIRU D M KATHIR ANAND:  
Will the Minister of FISHERIES, ANIMAL HUSBANDRY AND DAIRYING be pleased to state: 
(a) whether the Government has taken note of reports that the country's fisheries sector is facing mounting 
challenges due to declining marine fish stocks, overfishing, climate change, habitat degradation, marine 
pollution, destructive fishing practices, rising operational costs and increasing livelihood insecurity among 
traditional fishing communities despite the sector's significant contribution to food security, exports and 
employment; 
(b) the assessment of the Government regarding principal factors responsible for the present situation; 
(c) the action taken by the Government to strengthen scientific fisheries management, fish stock 
assessment, habitat restoration, marine conservation and regulation of fishing effort; 
(d) whether additional support is proposed by the Government for small-scale fishermen through climate-
resilient infrastructure, insurance, alternative livelihoods, modern fishing technologies and value -chain 
development; and 
(e) if so, the target fixed by the Government to ensure sustainable fisheries and improve fishermen's 
incomes during the next five years? 
 
ANSWER 
 
 THE MINISTER OF FISHERIES, ANIMAL HUSBANDRY AND DAIRYING 
(SHRI RAJIV RANJAN SINGH ALIAS LALAN SINGH) 
(a) and (b): As per the Marine Fish Stock Status of India (2022)  published by the ICAR‑Central Marine 
Fisheries Research Institute (ICAR‑CMFRI), the marine fish stocks in Indian waters remain in good 
health, with 91.1% of the 135 fish stocks assessed across different regions of the Indian EEZ found to be 
at sustainable levels. Analysis of India’s marine fish landings for 2014 –2023, based on ICAR‑CMFRI’s 
statistically validated scientific sampling programme and average annual growth trends, indicates an 
overall stable trajectory with a marginal increase, with no evidence of sustained decline in marine fish 
production. 
ICAR has further informed that ICAR‑CMFRI undertakes continuous monitoring of fish landings and 
conducts focused research on the biological performance of major commercial and ecologically important 
resources through its research centres and field stations across coastal States/UTs. 

 The Institute also monitors coastal ecosystem health through real‑time surveys. The Fishery Survey of 
India (FSI) similarly monitors the status of marine fishery resources through systematic exploratory 
surveys in the Indian Exclusive Economic Zone (EEZ), generating baseline data on the distribution, 
abundance, and biological characteristics of demersal and oceanic fish stocks to support assessments of 
impacts arising from fishing pressure, climate variability, marine pollution, and habitat degradation. 
The available scientific evidence from the studies by these Institutions indicates that, a lthough, 
environmental stressors such  as increased sea surface temperature have been observed to influence the 
distribution, abundance, and seasonal availability of certain fish species, no direct and conclusive impact 
on overall marine fish production has been established solely due to clima te change, marine pollution, 
coastal erosion, or pollution of inland water bodies. 
(c) to (e): The Department of Fisheries, Government of India, has undertaken comprehensive measures to 
strengthen scientific fisheries management, marine conservation, and the welfare of small -scale fishers. 
Since 2015, the Government has significantly enhanced investment in the sector, allocating ₹39,272 crore 
through flagship initiatives such as the Blue Revolution Scheme, Fisheries and Aquaculture Infrastructure 
Development Fund (FIDF),  the Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana (PMMSY), and the Pradhan 
Mantri Matsya Kisan Samridhi Sah Yojana (PM MKSSY). 
To sustainably harness fisheries resources in the EEZ, regulate fishing effort, and safeguard marine 
biodiversity, the Government has notified the Sustainable Harnessing of Fisheries in the Exclusive 
Economic Zone Rule s, 2025 on 4 November 2025. This landmark framework adopts an ecosystem  
approach and mandates key conservation measures, including uniform ban on fishing during fish breeding 
seasons; enforcement of minimum legal size for fish capture and adoption of bycatch reduction measures; 
strict prohibition of destructive and juvenile fishing practices; promotion of best practices to minimize 
post-harvest losses. 
Under the PMMSY, targeted interventions are implemented to rejuvenate fish stocks and restore marine 
habitats, including extensive sea ranching programmes, installation of artificial reefs, and deployment of 
Turtle Excluder Devices (TEDs) in trawl nets to protect sea turtles. To ensure sustainable fisheries and 
enable small scale fishers to significantly enhan ce incomes, the Schemes of the Department prioritises 
livelihood diversification and reduction of fishing pressure on overexploited inshore waters. Core 
measures include promoting open sea cage culture, seaweed cultivation, ornamental fisheries, and 
induction of modern deep sea fishing vessels. Complementary efforts focus on upgrading fisheries 
infrastructure, climate resilient fishing villages, modern harbours, landing centres, cold chain and market 
linked facilities , providing safety nets such as group ac cident insurance for traditional fishers, and 
strengthening Fisheries Cooperative Societies and FFPOs to expand operations, access deep sea resources, 
and enhance processing and export capabilities.

Will the Minister of HEAVY INDUSTRIES be pleased to state:  
 
(a) the details of number of Electric Bus deployed in Odisha and the country under the PM e - Bus 
Sewa-Payment Security Mechanism Scheme; 
 
(b) the details of status of PLI Scheme for Automobile and Auto Components;  
 
(c) whether the Government is planning to implement FAME-III , as FAME-II has delivered a strong 
improvement in the E-Transportation;  
 
(d) the details of progress and implementation of the SAMARTH Udyog Bharat 4.0; and  
 
(e) whether the Government is going to increase the number of Common Engineering Facility Centres 
and if so, the details thereon? 
 
ANSWER 
THE MINISTER OF STATE FOR HEAVY INDUSTRIES 
(SHRI BHUPATHIRAJU SRINIVASA VARMA) 
 
(a): As on 10.07.2026, the PM-eBus Sewa – Payment Security Mechanism (PSM) Scheme covers 
27,555 e-buses out of the targeted 38,000 e -buses. Of these, 10,000 e -buses are under the PM -eBus 
Sewa Scheme of the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs (MoHUA), 14,000 e-buses are under the 
PM E-DRIVE Scheme of the Ministry of Heavy Industries (MHI), and 3,555 e -buses under various 
State Government/State Transport Undertaking (STU) initiatives. 
 
As on 10.07.2026, a total of 523 e -buses have been deployed across the country under the 
PM-eBus Sewa–PSM Scheme. Further, under the PM-eBus Sewa Scheme of MoHUA covered under

03.08.2026

क ृ िष एवं िकसान कʞाण राǛ मंũी  (SHRI RAMNATH THAKUR) 
 
(a):  As per Agriculture Census 2015-16, there are 1464.54 lakh operational land holdings

(b) & (c):  State-wise and Year-wise details of the number of farmer applications enrolled & 
number of farmer applications paid claims during 2021-22 to 2025-26 under Pradhan 
Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana are given at Annexure. 
 
(d): The PMFBY is demand driven and voluntary for the States/UTs as well as farmers. 
Therefore, State Government and farmers subscribe to the scheme as per their risk 
perception. During 2025-26 (as on 30.06.2026), 1,393 lakh farmer applications, covering 
558 lakh ha. area insured, which is  23.8%  and 7.91% higher respectively, as compared to 
2022-23.    
 
With a view to improve insurance coverage under the scheme, Government is taking 
following steps : 
- AIDE (App for Intermediary Enrolment): A smart-phone App has been designed 
and rolled out in Kharif 2023 for enrolment of farmers at their door-steps through a large 
network of Insurance Intermediaries. It offers a completely paper-less and cash-less 
experience to a farmer. 
- The Government has actively supported the awareness activities being carried out 
by the States, implementing Insurance Companies, financial institutions, and Common 
Service Centres (CSCs) network to disseminate key features of PMFBY amongst 
farmers and members of Panchayati Raj Institutions (PRIs). 

 
- Further, a structured awareness campaign ‘Crop Insurance Week/Fasal Bima 
Saptah’ has been initiated by the Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare since 
Kharif 2021 season onwards to increase the awareness about benefits of the scheme, 
sensitize the stakeholders and to increase overall enrolment of farmers, with special 
focus on identified aspirational/tribal districts. Along with this, ‘Fasal Bima Pathshalas’ 
are also being organized at village/GP level for knowledge building of farmers on 
various aspects of scheme implementation.  
 
- Government had also organized a nationwide Doorstep Crop Insurance 
Policy/receipt Distribution mega drive – ‘Meri Policy Mere Haath’. Hard copies of crop 
insurance policy receipts are distributed to farmers enrolled under PMFBY through 
special camps at gram Panchayat/village level. 
 
- Apart from this, other activities for awareness generation involve the publicity of 
key features and benefits of the scheme through advertisements in leading National and 
local newspapers, airing of audio-visual spots on regional / local channels, distribution 
of IEC material in local languages, dissemination of SMS through Kisan/ National Crop 
Insurance Portal (NCIP) portal and organisation of online workshops of all stakeholders 
including farmers, Panchayat Members, and other key stakeholders.

(a):  National Cooperative Development Corporation (NCDC), a statutory organization 
under the Ministry of Cooperation, promotes, strengthens and develops cooperative sector in

assistance to the cooperative sector under its Corporation-sponsored schemes as well as various

as amended from time to time. In recent years, NCDC has introduced sector -specific schemes 
and focused products to align with the evolving needs of the cooperative sector, with special 
emphasis on new cooperatives, women empowerment, rural healthcare etc. thereby 
strengthening the cooperative infrastructure.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF COMMERCE & INDUSTRY 
DEPARTMENT FOR PROMOTION OF INDUSTRY AND INTERNAL TRADE 
 
LOK SABHA 
 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 2549. 
           TO BE ANSWERED ON TUESDAY, THE 04TH AUGUST, 2026. 
 
IMPLEMENTATION OF ONDC 
 
2549.  SMT. RACHNA BANERJEE: 
 
Will the Minister of COMMERCE AND INDUSTRY be pleased to state: 
वाणिज्य  एवं उद्योग मंत्री 
(a)  the present status of implementation and expansion of the Open Network for 
Digital Commerce (ONDC); 
 
(b)  the number of sellers, traders and MSMEs onboarded on the platform, State -
wise; 
 
(c)  whether the Government has assessed the impact of ONDC on small retailers 
and traditional markets; and 
 
(d)  the measures being taken to improve awareness and participation of small 
traders in the network? 
 
ANSWER 
 
वाणिज्य  एवं उद्योग मंत्रालय में राज्य मंत्री (श्री णिणिन प्रसाद)   
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF COMMERCE & INDUSTRY 
(SHRI JITIN PRASADA) 
 
(a): The Open Network for Digital Commerce (ONDC)  is an open, interoperable 
network that enables buyers and sellers to transact across multiple platforms 
without being tied to any single application. ONDC is a Section 8 (not-for-profit) 
company incorporated under the Companies Act,  2013. It is not a platform, 
application or a marketplace. 
The network has progressively expanded across multiple domains of e -
commerce, including retail (grocery, food & beverage, fashion, electronics, and 
general merchandise), mobility, logistics, financ ial services, and agriculture, 
enabling participation  by a wide spectrum of sellers, including MSMEs, 
farmers, Self-Help Groups (SHGs), weavers, artisans, kirana stores, and 
traditional retailers. 
Since its launch,  a cumulative total of over 500 million orders has been 
transacted on the ONDC network as of July 2026. Over 500 orders per minute 
are processed, reflecting the pace of adoption across this network. 
(b): As ONDC is a network rather than a platform, sellers transact through their 
respective Seller Network Participants and aggregator entities; a single such 
entity may represent multiple MSMEs and small retailers. Crucially, sellers can 
migrate between network participants based on their preferences and the 
oﬀerings provided by Seller Network Participants and aggregator entities, while 
maintaining access to the network-wide consumer base. 

ONDC does not maintain a network-wide, individually attributed count of every 
seller, MSME, and small retailer transacting on the network. At the aggregate 
network level, approximately 2 lakh+ merchants (including SHGs, FPOs, 
MSMEs, sellers, traders etc.) across retail are active on the network, along with 
approximately 10 lakh+ service providers across mobility and logistics are 
associated with the network as of July 2026. 
(c) & (d): ONDC monitors network -level participation and transaction metrics to assess 
the growth and inclusiveness of the network. As of July 2026, approximately 2 
lakh+ merchants across retail—including merchants, SHGs, FPOs, MSMEs, 
sellers, traders and other business entities—are active on the network, of which 
approximately 60% are small sellers. The increasing participation of small 
sellers on the network is indicative of ONDC's role in expanding digital market 
access by enabling sellers to  reach a wider base of buyers through an  open, 
interoperable network, without dependence on any single platform. This 
approach seeks to reduce barriers to digital commerce, including high 
commissions, platform lock -in, and onboarding costs associated with closed 
platforms. 
Following measures have been undertaken to promote awareness, digital 
readiness and participation of small traders on the network: 
i. DigiDukaan, an ONDC initiative for onboarding small kirana and retail 
traders onto the digital commerce net work, is currently operational in 
Hyderabad and Jaipur, with support from a network of distributors and 
wholesalers that provides access through major consumer goods 
companies in Hyderabad and Jaipur. The initiative deploys dedicated field 
resources and digital outreach campaigns for on-the-ground onboarding 
and awareness generation among small traders. 
ii. Under the MSME TEAM Initiative, a sub -component of the World Bank -
supported RAMP programme of the Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium 
Enterprises, a total outlay of Rs. 277.35 crore has been approved for FY 
2024-25 to FY 2026 -27 to facilitate onboarding of micro and small 
enterprises onto ONDC through awareness, capacity-building and training 
activities, with financial assistance extended for onboarding, prod uct 
cataloguing, account management, logistics, and packaging material and 
design, and with 50% of beneficiary MSMEs targeted to be women-owned 
enterprises. 
iii. State-level initiatives are also underway for onboarding local and 
indigenous products, as well as enabling SHGs and cooperatives to sell 
through ONDC. 
iv. ONDC has developed and disseminated training and capacity -building 
programs, including over 3,000 hours of virtual training and 200+ hours of 
technical training through open digital sessions, attended by  over 50,000 
participants. 
v. ONDC publishes Seller Handbooks and Guidebooks to assist first -time 
digital sellers, made available in 14 Indian languages.  
vi. ONDC is working with ecosystem partners such as SIDBI, NABARD, and 
other developmental organizations to onboard SHGs, social-sector sellers 
and micro-entrepreneurs

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF PANCHAYATI RAJ 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 2595 
ANSWERED ON 04/08/2026 
  
REVAMPED RASHTRIYA GRAM SWARAJ ABHIYAN PROJECTS IN ANDHRA 
PRADESH 
2595. DR. GUMMA THANUJA RANI: 
  
Will the Minister of PANCHAYATI RAJ be pleased to state: 
  
(a) whether the Government has reviewed the reasons for non-approval of economic 
development and income generation projects under the Revamped Rashtriya Gram Swaraj 
Abhiyan in Andhra Pradesh, if so, the details thereof; 
(b) whether the Government has received proposals from Andhra Pradesh for rural 
livelihood, tourism, food processing or Self Help Group-based economic development 
projects under the Scheme; and 
(c) if so, the details thereof and if not, the reasons therefor? 
  
ANSWER 
  
THE MINISTER OF PANCHAYATI RAJ 
 (SHRI RAJIV RANJAN SINGH ALIAS LALAN SINGH) 
  
(a) to (c) Panchayat, being a “Local Self Government”, is a State subject and part of the State 
List of the Seventh Schedule of the Constitution of India. Accordingly, strengthening 
Panchayat capacity is primarily the responsibility of States/UTs. However, the Ministry is 
implementing a Centrally Sponsored Scheme, namely the Revamped Rashtriya Gram Swaraj 
Abhiyan (RGSA), w.e.f. financial year 2022-23, with the objective of supporting Panchayati 
Raj institutions (PRIs) by imparting training to Elected Representatives (ERs) and other 
stakeholders to develop leadership abilities, thereby enabling Gram Panchayats to function 
effectively across all States/UTs. 
Under RGSA, Innovative and Economic Development and Income Enhancement is one of 
the components in which GP/cluster of GPs are being funded for micro projects on economic 
development and income enhancement. Financial assistance in the form of viability gap 
funding for micro projects catering to subject areas enlisted in the Eleventh Schedule of the 
Constitution for devolution to Panchayats is provided based on the merit of the proposal and 
its viability and sustainability. 
During FY 2025-26, the State of Andhra Pradesh has submitted 9 projects focused on rural 
livelihood, eco-tourism and Self-Help Groups, under the Innovative and Economic 
Development and Income Enhancement component of RGSA. Out of these, the Ministry has 
sanctioned 4 projects to the State of Andhra Pradesh amounting to Rs.16.50 crore, and the 
remaining 5 projects were deferred due to limited availability of time for implementation. 
The details of these projects may be seen at Annexure-I.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF AGRICULTURE & FARMERS’ WELFARE 
DEPARTMENT OF AGRICULTURE & FARMERS’ WELFARE  
 
LOK SABHA 
 UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 2596 
TO BE ANSWERED ON THE 04th August, 2026 
 
IMPACT OF CLIMATE CHANGE ON AGRICULTURE 
 
 2596. SHRI SHAFI PARAMBIL: 
           SHRI RAJMOHAN UNNITHAN: 
 
Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS’ WELFARE क ृ िष एवं िकसान 
कʞाण मंũी be pleased to state: 
 
(a) whether the Government has undertaken any assessment of the impact of climate 
change, unseasonal rainfall, floods and drought on agricultural production in Keralam 
and other coastal States during the last five years; 
(b) the details of crop losses and financial assistance provided to farmers in the State 
during the said period, crop-wise; 
(c) the funds allocated and released to Keralam under various Central schemes for 
climate resilient agriculture during the last five years; 
(d) the measures taken by the Government to promote climate-resilient farming, crop 
diversification and sustainable agricultural practices in Keralam; 
(e) the measures taken to strengthen scientific support and climate adaptation for 
farmers; and 
(f) Whether the Government proposes any special package or targeted intervention to 
strengthen the resilience and income of farmers in Keralam in view of the State's 
recurring climate-related challenges? 
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE OF AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE  
 
क ृ िष एवं िकसान कʞाण राǛ मंũी (SHRI  RAMNATH THAKUR) 
 
(a) to (c):  The Government, through the Indian Council of Agricultural Research 
(ICAR), is implementing the National Innovations in Climate Resilient Agriculture 
(NICRA) project to assess the impact of climate change and weather aberrations, 
including unseasonal rainfall, floods and drought, on agricultural production in the 
country, including the State of Keralam and other coastal States.  

      As reported by the Government of Keralam, crop losses are assessed based on 
applications under the State Contingency for Natural Calamity Scheme and the State 
Crop Insurance Scheme. From 01.04.2021 to 31.03.2026, 31,281.878 hectares of 
crop area was affected due to natural calamities. 257,214.73 hectares was covered 
under the State Crop Insurance Scheme, for which compensation of ₹122.32 crore 
was disbursed. In addition, Government of India released ₹164.43 crore under the 
Restructured Weather Based Crop Insurance Scheme (RWBCIS) during 2023-2025. 
The crop-wise details are given at Annexure. 
       The Government is implementing various schemes to promote climate-resilient 
agriculture. During the last five years (2021–22 to 2025–26), under the Per Drop More 
Crop (PDMC) scheme, a total amount of ₹97.83 crore was allocated to the State of 
Kerala, against which ₹26.03 crore was released. During the same period, under the 
Rainfed Area Development (RAD) scheme, a total allocation of ₹17.54 crore was 
made, against which ₹6.89 crore was released. Under the Soil Health Card (SHC) 
Scheme, a total of ₹22.65 crore was allocated and ₹6.96 crore was released. Under 
the Paramparagat Krishi Vikas Yojana (PKVY), a total allocation of ₹59.50 crore was 
made, against which ₹33.65 crore was released. Further, under the National Mission 
on Natural Farming (NMNF), a total of ₹5.58 crore was allocated and the entire 
allocated amount was released during the said period. 
(d) to (e):  Indian Council of Agricultural Research (ICAR) is implementing a project- 
National Innovations in Climate Resilient Agriculture (NICRA) in 651 districts that 
studies the impact of climate change on agriculture. It conducts district level risk & 
vulnerability assessment due to climate change including the State of Keralam. Out of 
the 310 districts identified as vulnerable to climate change, 201 districts are 
categorized as 'High' climate-vulnerable and 109 districts as 'Very High' climate-
vulnerable. Of the 109 'Very High' climate-vulnerable districts, 8 districts (Kasaragod, 
Kozhikode, Ernakulam, Kottayam, Alappuzha, Pathanamthitta, Kollam and 
Thiruvananthapuram) are in Keralam. Of the 201 'High' climate-vulnerable districts, 5 
districts (Kannur, Wayanad, Malappuram, Palakkad and Thrissur) are in Keralam. 
District Agriculture Contingency Plans (DACPs) for these 651 districts have been 
prepared to address weather aberrations. Under NICRA location-specific climate 
resilient technologies such as system of rice intensification, aerobic rice, direct seeding 
of rice, in-situ incorporation of rice residues etc. have been demonstrated through 
KVKs in 448 model Climate Resilient Villages. 9 villages are in the State of Keralam. 

     The Government is taking various measures to promote sustainable agricultural 
practices. Per Drop More Crop scheme is implemented to promote water use 
efficiency at the farm level through Micro Irrigation technologies. Rainfed Area 
Development scheme is implemented to promote Integrated Farming System for 
enhancing productivity and minimizing risks associated with climatic variability. The 
Soil Health and Fertility scheme assists states in promoting Integrated Nutrient 
Management through judicious use of fertilizers. The Government is also promoting 
organic farming through Paramparagat Krishi Vikas Yojana and natural farming 
through National Mission on Natural Farming scheme. “Mission for Aatmanirbharta in 
Pulses”, National Mission on Edible Oils – Oilseeds, and National Food Security & 
Nutrition Mission promotes crop diversification.  Mission for Integrated Development 
of Horticulture, Agroforestry & National Bamboo Mission also promote climate 
resilience in agriculture.  
       To strengthen scientific support and climate adaptation, the Government is 
leveraging emerging technologies such as Artificial Intelligence (AI), Internet of Things 
(IoT), and digital platforms to enhance crop productivity and  sustainability, including 
in the State of Kerala. The “Kisan e-Mitra” voice-based AI chatbot, supporting 11 
regional languages, assists farmers with queries related to PM-KISAN and other 
Government programmes. It handles over 20,000 queries daily and has responded to 
more than 95 lakh queries to date. Further, the Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers 
Welfare has launched “Bharat VISTAAR”, an AI-powered multilingual digital platform 
that provides farmers with real-time advisories, access to Government schemes, and 
weather updates through a single interface . The National Pest Surveillance System 
(NPSS) uses AI and Machine Learning technologies for early detection of pest 
infestations, thereby helping farmers reduce climate-induced crop losses. The system 
is currently utilized by over 10,000 extension workers and supports surveillance of 61 
crops and more than 400 pests. AI-based analytics using field photographs and 
satellite imagery are also being deployed for crop-weather matching and monitoring 
of sowing patterns.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF RURAL DEVELOPMENT 
DEPARTMENT OF RURAL DEVELOPMENT 
 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 2597 
  ANSWERED ON 04/08/2026 
 
ALLOCATION OF FUNDS TO KERALA 
 
2597. Shri Rajmohan Unnithan: 
 
Will the Minister of RURAL DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state: 
 
(a)  the details of funds released to Kerala under rural employment 
programmes during the current financial year; 
(b)  whether the Government has reviewed employment generated 
in coastal and backward districts, if so, the details thereof; 
(c)  whether any additional allocation has been considered for 
districts with high unemployment, if so, the details thereof; and 
(d)  the measures taken to ensure timely release of Central 
assistance, State-wise? 
 
ANSWER 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF RURAL DEVELOPMENT 
(SHRI KAMLESH PASWAN)  
 
(a): Consequent upon enactment of Viksit Bharat–Guarantee for 
Rozgar and Aajeevika Mission (Gramin) (VB-G RAM G), Act 2025, the 
new scheme has been operationalized in rural areas of the entire 
country including Kerala with effect from 1st July, 2026. During the 
financial year 2026–27, (as on 29.07.2026), an amount of Rs. 1230.01 
crores has been sanctioned to Kerala under the Mahatma Gandhi 
NREGS. Further an interim allocation of Rs 3136.44 crore have been 
made to the State as Central Share for FY 2026-27 for the period 
between 01.07.2026 to 31.03.2027.  Subsequently, Mother Sanctions 
amounting to Rs. 925.33 crore have been issued as first instalment 
for various component under VB-G RAM G based on the proposal 
received from the State.  
 
(b): The VB-G RAM G which is a demand driven Scheme, provides 
for a statutory guarantee of one hundred and twenty five days of wage 
employment in a financial year to every rural household whose adult 
members volunteer to undertake unskilled manual work. The 
Government monitors the implementation of the Scheme, including 

Page 2 of 4 
 
generation of employment across all rural districts of the country, 
through the Management Information System (MIS).  
 
Employment generation under the Scheme depends on various 
factors such as the demand for work by registered eligible rural 
household, acceptance of the offer of employment made and agro-
climatic conditions etc. Necessary technical and financial support is 
provided to States/UTs to facilitate effective implementation of the 
Scheme across all districts, including coastal and backward 
districts. Through regular review meeting and field visits States are 
sensitized to ensure that no demand for employment remain 
unmet. During the current financial year 2026-27, as on 31.07.2026, 
over 99.90% of the workers have been offered employment against 
demand and 1.66 crore Persondays have been generated in Kerala 
under VB G RAM G and Mahatma Gandhi NREGS. 
 
(c): As per the provisions of Act, funds are allocated by the Central 
Government to States/UTs. The intra-State distribution of funds 
among districts is prerogative of the concerned State/UTs in 
accordance with the provisions of the Scheme notified by them. 
However, it is stated that the VB–G RAM G Act, scheme incorporates 
several structural reforms to address the diverse development needs 
of rural areas. The provision of normative allocation of funds has been 
introduced to ensure equitable distribution of resources among the 
States based on objective development parameters. Further, the 
approved normative allocation is required to be distributed within the 
State in an equitable, need-based and transparent manner across 
districts and Gram Panchayats, taking into consideration the 
categorisation of Gram Panchayats and their assessed infrastructure 
and development needs.  
 
The Scheme also provides for preparation of Viksit Gram 
Panchayat Plans (VGPPs) through an evidence-based, participatory

livelihoods and reducing rural poverty.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF COOPERATION 
 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 2598 
TO BE ANSWERED ON 04th AUGUST, 2026 
 
Fisheries Cooperatives 
 
2598.  Shri Manoj Tiwari: 
Dr. Nishikant Dubey:  
Shri Amar Sharadrao Kale: 
Shri Pradeep Kumar Singh: 
Shri Mukeshkumar Chandrakaant Dalal:  
Shri Vishweshwar Hegde Kageri: 
Shri Ramesh Awasthi:  
Shri Kota Srinivasa Poojary:  
Dr. Hemant Vishnu Savara:  
Shri Jagdambika Pal: 
Shri Trivendra Singh Rawat:  
Shri Bibhu Prasad Tarai:  
Shri Krishna Prasad Tenneti:  
Shri Sunil Kumar: 
Shri Naba Charan Majhi:  
Will the Minister of COOPERATION (सहकारिता मंत्री) be pleased to state: 
(a)  the details of progress made so far towards strengthening Fisheries Cooperative Societies under 
the vision of "Sahkar se Samriddhi" (Prosperity through Cooperation), including details of the 
number of newly formed fisheries cooperative societies along with the number of existing societies 
modernised; 
(b) the current status of the formation of new fisheries cooperative societies and their integration 
with the National Cooperative Database, State -wise including Karnataka, Palghar district in 
Maharashtra and West Champaran district in Bihar; 
(c) the details of financial and technical assistance provided for deep -sea fishing trawlers, cold -
chains, processing units and development of other infrastructural facilities to fisheries cooperative 
societies, State-wise including Palghar district in Maharashtra; 
(d) whether an effective convergence has been established with schemes like 'Pradhan Mantri 
Matsya Sampada Yojana'; and 
(e) if so, the details of achievements and outcomes obtained so far through this convergence?  
 

Page 2 of 5 
 
ANSWER 
 
THE MINISTER OF COOPERATION 
सहकारिता मंत्री (SHRI AMIT SHAH) 
 
(a) to (e) Under the National Plan for formation of new Multipurpose PACS, Dairy and Fishery 
Cooperative Societies to achieve cooperative coverage in every uncovered Panchayat/village over 
a period of five years, effective convergence has been established with the Pradhan Mantri Matsya 
Sampada Yojana (PMMSY). Information relating to Fishery Cooperative Societies, as furnished 
by the States/UTs, is being maintained on the National Cooperative Database for identification of 
uncovered areas, monitoring progress and facil itating implementation of the Plan.  As on 
15.07.2026, a total of 2,356 new Fishery Cooperative Societies (FCSs) have been registered across 
the country under the National Plan approved on 15.02.2023, while 1,700 existing FCSs have been 
strengthened. The current status of the formation of new fisheries cooperative societies, State-wise, 
including Karnataka, Palghar district in Maharashtra and West Champaran district in Bihar is given 
at Annexure -A. 
 
The National Cooperative Database (NCD) is used for identification of uncovered areas and for 
maintaining updated information on cooperative societies. Bihar has completed two -way 
integration of its cooperative database with the NCD, while data relating to  Karnataka and 
Maharashtra are updated on the portal through nodal officers designated by the respective State 
Governments. 
Further, the Department of Fisheries, through NFDB as the nodal agency and in convergence with 
the Ministry of Cooperation, is implementing Pradhan Mantri Matsya Kisan Samridhi Sah-Yojana 
(PM-MKSSY) during 2024–25 to 2028–29 to form 6,000 new multipurpose Fisheries Cooperative 
Societies (FCSs) and strengthen 5,500 existing FCSs across the coun try under the vision of 
"Sahkar se Samriddhi." 
Under the Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana (PMMSY), financial and technical assistance 
is provided to eligible Fisheries Cooperative Societies, FFPOs and other eligible entities for 
establishment of deep-sea fishing vessels/trawlers, cold chain infrastructure, fish processing units, 
hatcheries, integrated aqua parks, integrated fish farming projects and other fisheries 
infrastructure, as per the scheme guidelines. 
So far, six projects of Fisheries Cooperative Societies/FFPOs have been approved under these 
components in the States of Assam, Maharashtra and Uttar Pradesh, involving a total approved 
project cost of Rs1,643.54 lakhs with an eligible subsidy of Rs 410.87  lakh. Of these, subsidy 
amounting to Rs 135.99 lakh has been released to eligible beneficiaries in accordance with the 
prescribed norms. In Maharashtra, three projects with a total approved project cost of Rs 888.78 
lakh and eligible subsidy of Rs 222.19 lakh have been sanctioned, including projects relating to 
integrated deep-sea fishing vessels, cold chain development and freshwater finfish hatchery . No 
project has been sanctioned in Palghar district of Maharashtra under these components as on date. 

Page 3 of 5 
 
Further, Fisheries Cooperative Societies are being supported through gap analysis, preparation of 
Business Development Plans (BDPs), mentoring, capacity building and need -based financial 
assistance under PM-MKSSY, while eligible societies are also availing assistance under PMMSY 
for fisheries infrastructure such as hatcheries, deep -sea fishing vessels, cold chain facilities, fish 
processing and value addition units, and other post -harvest infrastructure. This convergence has 
enhanced institutional capacity, improved access to modern fisheries infrastructure, strengthened 
the business viability of Fisheries Cooperative Societies and contributed to better income and 
livelihood opportunities for fisher communities. 
Department of Fisheries has allocated the task of converting 1,000 existing fisheries cooperative 
societies into Fish Farmer Producer Organizations (FFPOs) to the National Cooperative 
Development Corporation (NCDC). This initiative has an approved outlay of ₹280.65 crore. As of 
May 31, 2026, NCDC has disbursed ₹130 crore to FFPOs and Cluster -Based Business 
Organizations (CBBOs) to facilitate market linkages and processing facilities. Further, the NCDC 
provides long-term and working capital loans specifically for the fisheries sector. In the financial 
year 2025-26, NCDC disbursed ₹319.03 crore specifically for fisheries cooperative activities. 
 
Further, Fisheries cooperative societies are being enabled to act as Bank Mitras of District Central 
Cooperative Banks (DCCBs) and State Cooperative Banks (StCBs). They are being provided with 
Micro-ATMs (supported by NABARD) to provide "doorstep financial  services," enhancing 
transparency and financial inclusion in rural areas. 
 
These measures are intended to strengthen institutional capacity, improve access to infrastructure, 
facilitate processing and marketing, and enhance market linkages for fishers and fisheries 
cooperatives. 
 
The details of financial and technical assistance provided for deep -sea fishing trawlers, cold -
chains, processing units and development of other infrastructural facilities to fisheries cooperative 
societies, State-wise including Palghar district in Maharashtra and  the details of achievements and 
outcomes obtained so far through this convergence are attached as Annexure-B.

Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE कृ ͪष एवं ͩकसान कãयाण मंğी 
be pleased to state: 
 
(a)  whether the Government has issued any orders, circulars, guidelines or policy 
directives regarding grant and operation of Single Unified Licences for traders and 
commission agents in Agricultural Produce Market Committees (APMCs) across the 
country, if so, the details thereof, State/UT-wise; 
 
(b)  the details of States and Union Territories that have adopted or implemented the Single

(c) the details of MoUs, agreements or arrangements entered into among State 
Governments, APMCs or marketing boards for facilitating inter-State trading under such 
system;

THE MINISTER OF STATE FOR AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE  
 
कृ ͪष एवं ͩकसान कãयाण राÏय मंğी (SHRI RAMNATH THAKUR)  
 
(a) & (b): Agricultural marketing is a State subject. The State Governments undertake 
developmental policy measures for Agricultural Produce Market Committees (APMCs) in 
accordance with their respective Acts and Rules. The Government of India supplements 
the efforts of the States through appropriate policy initiatives, budgetary support and   
schemes/programmes. 26 States/UT (Andhra Pradesh, Arunachal Pradesh, Assam, 
Chandigarh, Chhattisgarh, Goa, Gujarat, Haryana, Himachal Pradesh, Jharkhand, 
Karnataka, Madhya Pradesh, Maharashtra, Manipur, Meghalaya, Nagaland, Odisha, 
Punjab, Rajasthan, Sikkim, Tamil Nadu, Telangana, Tripura, Uttar Pradesh, Uttarakhand 
and West Bengal) have the provision of single unified license in their respective APMC 
Acts.  
 

(c):     No State has entered into Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) or agreements 
with other State Agricultural Marketing Departments/Boards to facilitate inter-state trade on 
the basis of Single Unified License system. State APMC Act of Chhattisgarh enables inter-
state trade even without MoU, through National Agriculture Market (e-NAM). Similarly, 
Jammu & Kashmir, Bihar and Jharkhand support inter-state bids on e-NAM.    
 
(d):     The licenses are issued/ renewed by the respective APMCs at local level. Information 
of the Single Unified Licences issued is not maintained centrally. 
 
(e) & (f):  Value of inter-State agricultural trade conducted by license holders is not 
maintained centrally. State/UT-wise inter-State agricultural trade through National 
Agriculture Market (e-NAM) during the last five years is placed at Annexure. No specific 
evaluation of the effectiveness of Unified Licensing System has been undertaken by the

2600. SHRI SELVAGANAPATHI T.M.: 
Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE क ृ िष एवं िकसान कʞाण मंũी be 
pleased to state: 
(a)  whether it is a fact that despite the Government's concerted efforts, many Farmer Producer 
Organisations (FPOs) are struggling to achieve economic viability;  
(b)  whether it is also a fact that the National Academy of Agricultural Sciences has recommended 
that institutional buyers must prioritise (FPOs) in the procurement of both food and non-food 
commodities; 
(c)  whether it is also a fact that the Government has been maintaining that it will help in the 
formation of 10,000 FPOs; 
(d)  whether it is also a fact that many FPOs struggle to achieve the economies of scale required 
for profitability due to many factors; and  
(e)  if so, the details thereof? 
ANSWER 
 
THE MINISTER OF STATE FOR AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE  
 
क ृ िष एवं िकसान कʞाण राǛ मंũी   (SHRI RAMNATH THAKUR)  
 
(a): The Government is implementing the Central Sector Scheme for "Formation and Promotion of 
10,000 Farmer Producer Organizations (FPOs). 10,000 FPOs have been formed under the scheme 
since 2020-21. FPOs undertake a wide range of business activities including agri-input supply, 
aggregation and trading of agricultural produce, value addition and processing, seed production, 
digital commerce through e-market places, custom hiring services & export promotion. From the 
audited financial statements 2024-25 of the scheme FPOs, 6964 FPOs had a turnover of up to 
Rs.50 Lakh, 862 FPOs had a turnover of Rs.50 Lakh to Rs.1 Crore and 1135 FPOs had a turnover 
of over Rs.1 Crore.      
(b): The National Academy of Agricultural Sciences, in Policy Paper No. 144, covers all FPOs 
registered in the country. The recommendations in the Policy Paper No. 144 include promotion of 
FPOs - industry linkages, link institutional buyers with FPOs, strengthening linkage of FPOs with 
Research & Development etc.      
(c): Under the 10K FPO Scheme, financial assistance of up to ₹18 lakh per FPO is provided to 
meet management and handholding expenses during the initial 3 years. A matching Equity Grant 
of up to ₹15 lakh per FPO is  provided to strengthen the capital base of eligible FPOs and Credit 
Guarantee Facility for project loans of up to ₹2 crore per FPO to improve access to institutional 
credit.  In addition, each FPO is provided 5 years of handholding support through a Cluster-Based 
Business Organization (CBBO) for capacity building, business planning, market linkages, and 
overall institutional development.   Till date 827.81 crore has been released to the FPOs registered 
under the 10K FPO Scheme as management cost and Rs.631.98 crore as matching equity grant.  
(d) & (e):  So far, under the 10K FPO Scheme, more than 65 lakh shareholders (predominantly 
small and marginal farmers) have been collectivized to leverage economies of scale.  As on date, 
for greater bargaining for input supply, 6928 FPOs have seed licenses, 4987 have pesticide 
licenses and 6650 have fertilizer licenses.  5765 FPOs have their own processing units and 3083 
FPOs have availed credit guarantee.

2601.  Shri Ramasahayam Raghuram Reddy: 
           Shri K C Venugopal: 
 
Will the Minister of SOCIAL JUSTICE AND EMPOWERMENT be pleased to state: 
(a) the details of funds allocated, released and utilised for the implementation of the Sugamya 
Bharat Abhiyan from Financial Year 2015-16 to Financial Year 2024-25, year and State/UT-
wise; 
(b) the number of applications received, approved and pending under the Unique Disability ID 
(UDID) project from March 2016 to March 2026, year and State/UT-wise; 
(c) the number of Divyangjans linked to the UDID’s central database, State/UT-wise; 
(d) whether the Government intends to establish a disability registry to gather accurate data 
regarding Divyangjans and their status, if so, the details thereof; and  
(e )the policy measures being taken by the Government to address the increase in dropout  rates 
among Divyangjans children at the primary and higher secondary levels? 
 
  
ANSWER 
  
MINISTER OF STATE FOR SOCIAL JUSTICE AND EMPOWERMENT 
 (SHRI B L VERMA) 
 
(a) The Accessible India Campaign, also known as “Sugamya Bharat Abhiyan”, is a 
nationwide initiative to create a barrier-free environment for persons with disabilities (PwDs). 
The Details of the details of  State/UT-wise and year-wise funds released and utilised for the 
implementation of the Sugamya Bharat Abhiyan from Financial Year 2015-16 to Financial 
Year 2024-25 is Annexure -I. 
(b) Under the UDID sub-scheme, a centralized online platform, namely the UDID 
Portal(https://swavlambancard.gov.in/), has been developed for issuance of Disability 
Certificates and Unique Disability Identity (UDID) Cards to eligible persons with disabilities 
through hospitals authorized by the respective State/UT Governments. The year-wise and 
State/UT-wise details of applications received, approved and pending under the UDID Project 
from March, 2016 to March, 2026 are given at Annexure-II. 
(c and d) :  Government has established a centralized national database of persons with 
disabilities under the Unique Disability Identity (UDID) Project. UDID Portal serves as a 

national repository of certified persons with disabilities by integrating data received from 
hospitals authorized by the respective State/UT Governments for issuance of Disability 
Certificates and UDID Cards. The database is continuously updated as new applications are 
processed and disability certificates/UDID Cards are issued. State/UT-wise number of persons 
with disabilities linked to the UDID central database is given at Annexure-III. 
(e) :  The Department of School Education & Literacy is implementing the Samagra Shiksha 
Scheme wherein the following measures are taken to address dropout rates and enhance 
enrolment, retention and participation of CwSN at the primary and higher secondary levels: 
Under the Scheme, financial assistance of ₹3,500 per enrolled CwSN per annum is provided 
for identification and assessment, aids and assistive devices, transportation, escort and scribe 
allowance, Braille and large-print books, teaching-learning materials and other support 
services, including home-based education. In addition, a stipend of ₹2,000 per annum is 
provided through Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT) to Divyang girl students to encourage regular 
school attendance. 
To facilitate early identification and timely educational intervention, the Department has 
developed PRASHAST (Pre-Assessment Holistic Screening Tool) for screening school-going 
children aged 3–18 years for the identification of disabilities. The Government has also notified 
Pupil-Teacher Ratio (PTR) norms for Special Educators in general schools to strengthen 
inclusive education. 
Further, NCERT has developed accessible digital learning resources on the DIKSHA platform 
based on Universal Design for Learning (UDL), including Indian Sign Language (ISL)-based 
content and assistive learning materials

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE 
DEPARTMENT OF AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE 
 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 2602 
TO BE ANSWERED ON THE 04th August, 2026 
 
MSP FOR ALL CROPS 
 
2602.SHRI K C VENUGOPAL: 
Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE कृ ͪष एवं ͩकसान कãयाण 
मंğी be pleased to state:  
(a) the details of measures taken by the Government to provide remunerative price to 
farmersfor their produce during last five years; 
(b) whether the Government is aware of the fact that measures and policies adopted by 
Government have failed and it has compelled lakhs of farmers to leave their profession 
and seek job as labourer in cities; 
(c) if so, the reasons therefor; and 
(d) whether the Government would legalize Minimum Support Price (MSP) for all crops 
during current Monsoon session and if not, the reasons therefor? 
 
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE FOR AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE  
कृ ͪष एवं ͩकसान कãयाण राÏयमंğी    (SHRI RAMNATH THAKUR) 
(a) to (d): Every year, Government fixes Minimum Support Prices (MSPs) for 22 
mandated agricultural crops for the country as a whole, based on the recommendations 
of the Commission for Agricultural Costs & Prices (CACP), after considering the views of 
the State Governments and Central Ministries / Departments concerned. 
The Union Budget for  2018-19 had announced the pre-determined principle to 
keep MSPs at levels of at least one and half times of the cost of production. Accordingly, 
Government had increased MSPs for all mandated Kharif, Rabi and other commercial 
crops with a minimum margin of 50 percent over all India weighted average cost of 
production from year 2018-19 onwards. 
  

 
Out of the total production, only marketable surplus is available for procurement 
by Government agencies when market price of these produce fall below the MSP. 
Government procures cereals and coarse cereals through Food Corporation of India 
(FCI) and other designated State Agencies to provide price support to the farmers. 
Procurement of pulses, oilseeds and copra is done under Price Support Scheme under 
umbrella scheme of Pradhan Mantri Annadata Aay Sanrakshan Abhiyan (PM-AASHA), 
on the request of the concerned State Government as per the guidelines as and when 
market price of these produce fall below the MSP. Procurement agencies under PM-
AASHA Scheme are National Agricultural Cooperative Marketing Federation of India Ltd 
(NAFED) and National Co-operative Consumers' Federation of India Ltd. (NCCF). Cotton 
and Jute are also procured by Government at MSP through Cotton Corporation of India 
(CCI) and Jute Corporation of India (JCI), respectively. 
In addition, Adequate number of procurement centres are opened by respective 
State Government Agencies, taking into account the production, marketable surplus, 
convenience of farmers and availability of other logistics / infrastructure such as storage 
and transportation etc. Temporary purchase centres, in addition to the existing mandis 
and depots/godowns are also established at key points. The procurement operation is a 
continuously evolving process and during the last few years, procurement processes 
under MSP have improved to ensure payment of MSP to farmer’s bank account directly 
and linkage of Aadhaar and land records with the States’ procurement portals ensure that 
the farmers directly get the benefits of the MSP purchase.  
Government has launched Mission for Aatmanirbharta in Pulses till 2030-31, to 
reduce import dependence and achieve self-sufficiency in pulses. To encourage 
domestic production of  pulses, the Government is undertaking procurement of Tur, Urad 
and Masur under the PM-AASHA Scheme on the request of State Government from pre-
registered farmers as much as offered by them through Central Nodal Agencies, namely 
the National Agricultural Cooperative Marketing Federation of India Ltd. (NAFED) and the 
National Cooperative Consumers' Federation of India Limited (NCCF). 
Government also implements Market Intervention Scheme (MIS), a component 
under PM-AASHA, for procurement of agricultural and horticultural commodities, which 
are perishable in nature and are not covered under the Price Support Scheme (PSS). 
The objective of intervention is to protect the growers of these commodities from making 
distress sale in the event of a bumper crop during the peak arrival period when the prices 
tend to fall below economic levels and the cost of production. There should be at least a 
10 percent decrease in the ruling market prices over the previous normal year. The 
scheme is implemented at the request of a State/UT government. 
  

 
Government has introduced a new component of Price Differential 
Payment (PDP) under Market intervention scheme (MIS) from 2024-25 season for direct 
payment of the price difference between the Market Intervention Price (MIP) and the 
selling price to the farmers of perishable crops. States/UTs have an option to choose 
either to do physical procurement of the crop or to make the differential payment between 
the MIP & Sale Price to the farmers. 
 
Further, from 2024-25 season, Government added another component under 
Market intervention scheme (MIS) for reimbursing the Storage and Transportation cost 
of TOP crops (Tomato, Onion and Potato) to central nodal agencies & State designated 
agencies for transporting them from the producing State to consuming states in the 
interest of the farmers. 
 
Increased MSP has benefited farmers of the country which are evident from data 
of procurement and MSP amount paid to the farmers. The details of procurement and 
MSP amount paid to farmers during 2021-22 to 2025-26 (upto June, 2026) are given as 
under: 
 
Procurement and MSP amount paid to farmers during last five years 
2021-22 to 2025-26 
Total Procurement (In LMT) Total MSP Value (In lakh Crore) 
5781 14.58 
 
The total procurement of all 22 MSP crops has increased from 6,987 Lakh Metric 
Tonne (LMT) during 2004-14 to 12,819 LMT during 2014-26(upto June 2026). The MSP 
amount paid to farmers has increased from Rs. 7.41 Lakh Crores during 2004-14 to Rs. 
27.80 Lakh crores during 2014-26 (upto June 2026).    
The Government is implementing several policies, reforms, developmental 
programmes to increase agricultural productivity, reduce the cost of cultivation, promote 
crop diversification, ensure remunerative returns and provide income support to farmers. 
These various schemes / programmes cover the entire spectrum of agriculture including 
credit, insurance,income support, infrastructure, crops including horticulture, seeds, 
mechanization,marketing, organic and natural farming, farmer collectives, irrigation, 
extension activities,procurement of crops, digital agriculture etc.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA

DEPARTMENT OF COMMERCE

UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 2603 
ANSWERED ON 04/08/ 2026 
 
IMPORT RESTRICTIONS ON GOODS PRODUCED USING FORCED LABOUR 
 
2603.  PROF. SOUGATA RAY 
 SHRI KISHORI LAL 
 
Will the Minister of COMMERCE AND INDUSTRY ¼okf.kT; ,oa m|ksx ea=h½  be 
pleased to state:  
 
  
(a) whether the Government has any policy or legal framework to prohibit the import 
of goods produced wholly or partly through forced labour, including child labour 
and bonded labour, if so, the details thereof;    
(b) whether the Government has examined international practices, including 
import restrictions imposed by other countries on goods suspected to have 
been produced using forced labour; 
(c) whether the Government proposes to introduce legislation, amend the 
Customs Act, or frame rules to prohibit the import of goods manufactured using 
forced labour and to strengthen due diligence in supply chains; and 
(d) the steps taken by the Government to ensure that India's import policies are 
consistent with its commitments under the Constitution, International Labour 
Organization (ILO) conventions, and international human rights standards 
while safeguarding legitimate trade? 
 
 
ANSWER 
okf.kT; ,oa m|ksx ea=ky; esa jkT;ea=h ¼Jh ftfru izlkn½ 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF COMMERCE AND INDUSTRY 
(SHRI JITIN PRASADA) 
 
(a) to (d) Yes. Section 3 of the Foreign Trade (Development and Regulation) Act, 
1992 empowers the Central Government to make provisions for the development 
and regulation of foreign trade by facilitating imports and increasing exports and, in 
particular, to make provision for prohibiting, restricting or otherwise regulating the 
import or export of goods. In exercise of these powers, the Government has inserted 
Paragraph 2.20B in the Foreign Trade Policy (FTP), 2023, vide Notification No. 
23/2026-27 dated 13.07.2026, to prohibit the import of goods produced wholly or in 

2 
 
part using forced labour. The Government has also examined international 
practices, including import restrictions imposed by other countries on goods 
suspected to have been produced using forced labour. 
 
"Forced Labour" has been defined under Paragraph 11.64 of the FTP in accordance 
with the ILO Forced Labour Convention, 1930 (No. 29). The Central Government 
may notify specific goods for prohibition under this provision upon completion of due 
enquiry and satisfaction that such goods have been produced wholly or in part using 
forced labour. Bonded labour is addressed under the Bonded Labour System 
(Abolition) Act, 1976, and child labour under the Child and Adolescent Labour 
(Prohibition and Regulation) Act, 1986. 
The Government has also, through Public Notice No. 21/2026-27 dated 13.07.2026, 
inserted Paragraph 2.50A in the Handbook of Procedures, 2023, prescribing the 
procedure for determining whether imported goods were produced using forced 
labour. 
These measures provide a legal and policy framework to prohibit the import of goods 
produced wholly or in part using forced labour and are designed to ensure that India's 
import policy remains consistent with the Constitution of India, relevant International 
Labour Organization (ILO) conventions, and international human rights standards, 
while safeguarding legitimate trade.
