covered under the Mission. 
 
(b) to (d): Prior to the revision of the Operational Guidelines of MIDH in 2025, National

PANCHAYAT DEVELOPMENT INDEX 
 
2627.   SMT. BHARTI PARDHI: 
SHRI SHRIRANG APPA CHANDU BARNE: 
DR. SHRIKANT EKNATH SHINDE: 
SHRI RAVINDRA DATTARAM WAIKAR: 
SHRI NARESH GANPAT MHASKE: 
  
Will the Minister of PANCHAYATI RAJ be pleased to state: 
(a) whether the Ministry has successfully implemented the "Panchayat Development Index" 
(PDI) to rank all 2.5 lakh Gram Panchayats on their socio-economic performance, if so, the 
details thereof, State-wise; 
 
(b) whether a special incentive fund has been created in the 2026-27 Budget for "Frontrunner" 
Panchayats that achieve the status of 'Child-Friendly' or 'Water-Sufficient' villages, if so, the 
details thereof, State-wise; 
 
(c) whether the Ministry has completed the thematic training of over 30 lakh elected 
representatives to align local planning with the Sustainable Development Goals, if so, the details 
thereof, State-wise; 
 
(d) whether the "Gram Panchayat Development Plans" (GPDP) for the current fiscal year have 
successfully integrated climate-resilient farming techniques, if so, the details thereof, State-wise; 
(e) whether the Ministry is collaborating with international agencies like the UNDP, if so, the 
details thereof, State-wise; and 
 
(f) whether case India’s LSDG model as a global benchmark for rural governance, if so, the 
details thereof? 
 
ANSWER 
  
THE MINISTER OF PANCHAYATI RAJ 
(SHRI RAJIV RANJAN SINGH ALIAS LALAN SINGH) 
  
(a) Yes, Sir. The Ministry has developed the Panchayat Advancement Index (PAI), earlier known 
as Panchayat Development Index (PDI), as a composite assessment framework to measure the 
incremental performance of Gram Panchayats/Equivalent to Gram Panchayats across the themes 

2 
 
of localization of sustainable development goals. The PAI provides theme-wise and overall 
scores through scorecards and dashboards, enabling identification of performance gaps, relative 
strengths, and areas requiring focused attention at the Panchayat level. A total of 2.59 Lakh 
Gram Panchayats/Equivalent to GPs of 33 State/UTs have been onboarded in the exercise of PAI 
2.0 for FY 2023-24. State/UT wise numbers of GPs by overall PAI grades in 2.0 are placed at 
Annexure I. 
  
(b) No, Sir. Special incentive fund has not been created in the 2026-27 Budget for “Frontrunner” 
Panchayats in any themes of localization of sustainable development goals, including Theme 3: 
Child Friendly Village and Theme 4: Water Sufficient Panchayat. 
  
(c) The Ministry has been implementing a Centrally Sponsored Scheme of Revamped Rashtriya 
Gram Swaraj Abhiyan (RGSA) w.e.f. financial year 2022-23 with the major objective of 
Capacity Building & Training (CB&T) of Elected Representatives, Functionaries and other 
stakeholders of Panchayats across all States/UTs for enhancing the leadership skills and 
improving Panchayat Governance. Under the scheme of RGSA, the Ministry provides support 
for CB&T of elected representatives, functionaries and other stakeholders of Panchayats in 
different categories viz. basic orientation and refresher training, thematic training, specialized 
training, panchayat development plan training etc. A total of 36,81,750 elected representatives & 
other stakeholders of Panchayati Raj Institutions were trained on themes of localization of 
sustainable development goals (LSDGs) from FY 2022-23 to FY 2026-27 (as on 10th July 2026) 
under the scheme. State/UT wise details of Thematic Training from FY 2022-23 to 2026-27 is 
placed at Annexure II.  
  
(d) The Ministry of Panchayati Raj facilitates the preparation of Gram Panchayat Development 
Plans (GPDPs) through a thematic planning approach aligned with the nine themes of the 
Localization of Sustainable Development Goals (LSDGs). Gram Panchayats are advised to 
identify and prioritize key developmental sectors, referred to as “Sankalp”, before the 
preparation of their GPDPs. 
Sectors related to climate-resilient agricultural practices viz efficient water management through 
drip irrigation & sprinkler systems, watershed development, agroforestry, and other sustainable 
agricultural practices, are integrated under Theme 4: Water Sufficient Panchayat and Theme 5: 
Clean and Green Panchayat. 
For the Plan Year of FY 2026-27 (as on 29.07.2026), a total of 1,56,019 Gram Panchayats have 
taken Sankalp for the preparation of GPDP. Of these, 31,789 Gram Panchayats have selected 
Theme 4: Water Sufficient Panchayat and 32,806 Gram Panchayats have selected Theme 5: 
Clean and Green Panchayat as their respective focus areas. 
(e) No, Sir. No such collaboration has been established by the Ministry with the United Nations 
Development Programme (UNDP) under PAI. 
(f) The Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) provide a globally accepted framework for 
sustainable and inclusive development. The Ministry of Panchayati Raj has localized the SDGs 
for Panchayats by developing a framework of nine Localization of Sustainable Development 

3 
 
Goals (LSDG) themes, making the global development agenda more relevant and actionable at 
the grassroots level. The localization of SDGs through the nine LSDG themes, supported by the 
PAI framework, facilitates effective rural governance, improved service delivery, and outcome-
oriented Panchayat development.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF FISHERIES, ANIMAL HUSBANDRY AND DAIRYING 
DEPARTMENT OF FISHERIES 
 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION No. 2628 
ANSWERED ON 04/08/2026 
 
ILLEGAL FISHERIES 
2628. SHRI PUTTA MAHESH KUMAR:  
Will the Minister of FISHERIES, ANIMAL HUSBANDRY AND DAIRYING  be 
pleased to state: 
(a) whether the Government has conducted any study/surveys to identify and assess illegal 
fisheries in the country; 
(b) if so, the details regarding the number of illegal fisheries detected during the last five years, 
State-wise and district-wise in Andhra Pradesh and in Eluru District in Andhra Pradesh; 
(c) the details regarding the enforcement action taken against illegal fisheries during the last five 
years, including the number of units shut down across the country, State-wise and district wise 
in Andhra Pradesh and in Eluru District; and 
(d) the details regarding the measures undertaken by the Government to prevent and reduce 
illegal fisheries and undertake awareness programmes for fishers and coastal communities? 
 
ANSWER 
 THE MINISTER OF FISHERIES, ANIMAL HUSBANDRY AND DAIRYING 
(SHRI RAJIV RANJAN SINGH ALIAS LALAN SINGH) 
(a) to (c): ‘Fisheries’ is a state subject, and each Coastal State has enacted its Marine Fishing 
Regulation Act (MFRA) for governance of fishing activities within the territorial waters up to 
12 nautical miles from the baseline. The regulation of Fisheries in the Exclusive Economic Zone 
(EEZ) beyond territorial waters is governed by the Union Government through the Maritime 
Zones of India (Regulation of fishing by foreign vessels) Act, 1981 and the  Sustainable 
Harnessing of Fisheries in the Exclusive Economic Zone of India Rules, 2025. Government of 
Andhra Pradesh has informed that the Andhra Pradesh Marine Fishing Regulation  Act (AP-
MFRA) and AP-MFR Rules are implemented to curb the illegal fishing in the territorial waters 
of Andhra Pradesh and the details of district wise violations of the AP-MFRA across the state 
during the last 4 years are Annexed. It is further informed that Eluru district of Andhra Pradesh 
has no coastline.  
The Government of Andhra Pradesh has  also informed that there is a continuous intrusion of 
mechanized fishing boats from Tamil Nadu and Puducherry in the territorial waters of Andhra 
Pradesh near south coastal districts i.e., Tirupathi, SPSR Nellore, Prakasam and Bapatla and 
around 160 cases of i llegal fishing have been reported during last 5 years.  Government of 
Andhra Pradesh has informed that in 2022-23, a penalty amounting to Rs. 52,500 was collected 
and fish catch worth Rs.31000 was confiscated from 21 fishing boats from Srikakulam, Krishna, 
Bapatla and Prakasam Districts, in 2024-25, a penalty of Rs. 7500 was collected and fish catch 
worth Rs.5000 was confiscated from 3 fishing boats from Bapatla District and in 2025-26, Rs. 
2500 was collected and fish catch worth Rs.2500 was confiscated from  1 Fishing boat from  
Kakinada District for violation of fishing ban period.  

 
(d): The Department of Fisheries, Government of India (DoF, GoI) has issued advisories from 
time to time to all the coastal States/UTs for preventing juvenile fishing and ban on destructive 
fishing practices for ensuring sustainability. Paired bottom trawling or bull trawling and use of 
LED lights in fishing are banned in the EEZ of India. All the maritime States/UTs have also 
been advised to take necessary steps to prevent pair o r bull trawling and use of LED light for 
fishing within and beyond the territorial waters. Besides, the DoF, GoI has also advised to 
coastal states/UTs to review and amend their respective MFRAs to ensure mandatory use of 
Turtle Excluder Devices (TEDs) tow ards marine turtle conservation. The implementation of 
TED has been included and supported under the Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana 
(PMMSY) with 100% financial assistance (60% Central and 40% State).  The Sustainable 
Harnessing of Fisheries in the Exclusive Economic Zone Rules , 2025 are framed to promote 
sustainability of marine ecosystem with optimum utilization of untapped fishery resources. 
Emphasis is also given to promote ecosystem approach for sustainable harnessing of resources 
in the EEZ, and implementation of the conservation and management measures, such as uniform 
ban on fishing during monsoon or fish breeding season, minimum legal size of fish, bycatch 
reduction, best practices for reducing post -harvest losses, conservation of fish stocks or 
rejuvenation measures including sea ranching, installation of artificial reefs, etc. The Rules also 
prohibit destructive fishing and juvenile fishing in the EEZ to protect the marine biodiversity 
of our seas.  
The DoF, GoI issues advisory to coastal States and Union Territories (UTs) from time to time 
to sensitize the fishermen for prevention of crossing the International Maritime Boundary Line 
(IMBL). Besides, Indian Navy and Indian Coast Guard regularly cond uct Community 
Interaction Programmes (CIPs) for the fishermen in the coastal villages to sensitize them about 
IMBL among other safety and security measures. ICG ships and aircrafts, during regular patrol 
close to IMBL undertake shepherding of Indian fishing boats into Indian waters. Co-ordinated 
patrols with neighboring countries are also undertaken in order to sensitize the fishermen to 
avoid crossing of the IMBL. ICG also sensitizes Fisheries Departments of Coastal States/UTs 
and fisheries associations about the perils of fishing near/across IMBL. 
DoF, GoI has approved a project with total outlay of Rs. 364.0 Crores under the PMMSY for 
the National Rollout of Vessel Communication and Support System  (VCSS) including 
installation of transponders on 1,00,000 fishing vessels in all coastal States and UTs. The 
transponders are being  fitted in the fishing vessels with 100% government assistance. The 
transponders have geo-fencing features to give alerts to the fishermen  upon approaching to or 
crossing over the authorized areas of fishing and to prevent cross State borders or unauthorized 
fishing.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF HEAVY INDUSTRIES  
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 2629 
ANSWERED ON 04.08.2026 
 
REDUCING CARBON EMISSIONS 
 
2629. DR. PRABHA MALLIKARJUN:  
 
Will the Minister of HEAVY INDUSTRIES be pleased to state:  
 
(a) whether the Government has prepared any roadmap for reducing carbon emissions from energy -
intensive manufacturing and heavy industries sectors;  
 
(b) the details of schemes and programmes promoting adoption of green technologies, industrial 
energy efficiency and renewable energy integration during the last five years;  
 
(c) the details of amount of financial assistance, incentives and budgetary support provided for 
industrial decarbonisation projects, State-wise;  
 
(d) the details of expected contribution of such initiatives towards achieving India's climate 
commitments and industrial sustainability goals; and  
 
(e) whether industries located in Karnataka, including industrial units operating in and around 
Davanagere district, have benefited from such programmes and the details thereof? 
 
ANSWER 
THE MINISTER OF STATE FOR HEAVY INDUSTRIES 
(SHRI BHUPATHIRAJU SRINIVASA VARMA) 
 
(a) to (e): Ministry of Environment, Forests and Climate Change has informed that India’s 
Nationally Determined Contribution (NDC) under the Paris Agreement aims for a reduction in the 
emission intensity of its GDP and is not sector -specific. Accordingly, no sector-specific roadmap for 
reducing greenhouse gas emissions from energy -intensive manufacturing and heavy industries is 
prescribed under the NDC framework document.  
 
The Government promotes low -carbon development through the convergence of various 
schemes and programmes relating to energy efficiency, renewable energy, green hydrogen, and 
resource efficiency. The National Action Plan on Cl imate Change (NAPCC) and State Action Plans 
on Climate Change (SAPCC) provide the overarching framework for these actions. Eligible industries 
across states, including Karnataka, can avail of benefits under applicable schemes subject to respective 
guidelines.  
 
As a result of cumulative national measures, India successfully decoupled its economic growth 
from greenhouse gas emissions. As per India's First Biennial Transparency Report (BTR), the emission 
intensity of GDP declined by 37.38% in 2022 from the 20 05 level. Furthermore, India's non -fossil 
fuel-based cumulative installed electric power capacity has crossed 50%, achieving this milestone five 
years ahead of the 2030 target.  
 
Further, Bharat Heavy Electricals Limited (BHEL), a CPSE under Ministry of He avy 
Industries  continuously implements measures to reduce its carbon footprint. These include Improving 
energy efficiency across its manufacturing facilities; i ncreasing renewable energy adoption; 
generating nearly 276 million units of electricity from in-house solar installations over the last 9 years; 
creating carbon sinks by planting over 44,000 saplings in FY 2025 -26 alone; r educing waste and 
developing efficient, low-emission technologies for the power, industry, and transportation sectors.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE 
DEPARTMENT OF AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE 
 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 2630 
TO BE ANSWERED ON 4TH AUGUST, 2026 
 
OILSEED AND PALM OIL PRODUCTION 
 
2630. COM. SELVARAJ V:  
SHRI SUBBARAYAN K: 
 
Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE कृ ͪष एवं ͩकसान कãयाण मंğी 
be pleased to state:  
 
(a)  whether it is a fact that a national mission is launched in November 2024 aiming to 
boost primary oil seeds production from 39 MT in 2022-23 to 69.7 MT by 2030-31; 
(b)  if so, the details thereof and to what extent this target has been achieved so far; 
(c)  whether it is a fact that the palm oil shipments accounts for about 47% of the total 
imports of about 16 MT cooking oil in 2024-25 oil year; and 
(d)  the details of measures being taken to raise the palm oil production in the country? 
 
ANSWER 
 
THE MINISTER OF STATE FOR AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE 
कृ ͪष एवं ͩकसान कãयाण राÏय मंğी  (SHRI RAMNATH THAKUR) 
 
(a) & (b):  The National Mission on Edible Oils-Oilseeds (NMEO-OS) was approved on 
3rd October, 2024 to boost domestic oilseed production and to strive towards self-reliance 
(Atmanirbhar Bharat) in edible oils. The mission aims to increase primary oilseed 
production from 39 million tonnes (2022-23) to 69.7 million tonnes by 2030-31. 
 
The NMEO-OS is implemented through a cluster-based approach. Over 600 Value Chain 
Cluster have been identified across the country which is managed by Value Chain Partners 
such as Farmer Producer Organizations (FPOs), cooperatives and other agencies. Under 
these clusters, farmers are provided free high-quality seeds of latest high yielding varieties 
and training on good agricultural practices. The mission supports the establishment and 
upgradation of post-harvest infrastructure (oil mills) to improve oil recovery from primary 
and secondary sources. 
 
The mission strengthens availability of certified seeds through 100% support for purchase 
of breeder seeds, establishment of new seed hubs and specialised seed storage units in 
the public sector to enhance production and storage capacity. 

 
The mission focuses on improving productivity through Frontline Demonstrations (FLDs), 
Cluster Frontline Demonstrations (CFLDs) and Block-Level Demonstrations (BLDs) to help 
farmers adopt latest varieties and good agricultural practices. 
 
Oilseed production has increased from 39.67 million tonnes in 2023-24 to 43.06 million 
tonnes in 2025-26 (3rd Advance Estimate, DA&FW). Under the mission, 13.52 lakh hectares 
were covered under free seed distribution in Value Chain Clusters during 2025-26, against 
the annual target of 10.00 lakh hectares. 60 Seed Hubs & 50 specialized seed storage units 
have been sanctioned for production of Breeder Seed of recently released varieties.  
 
(c) & (d):  As reported by the Directorate of Sugar & Vegetable Oils, Department of Food 
and Public Distribution, India imported 160.72 lakh tonnes of edible oils during 2024–25. Of 
this, 75.17 lakh tonnes comprised palm oil, accounting for 46.77% of the total edible oil 
imports.  
 
The Government of India launched the National Mission on Edible Oils–Oil Palm (NMEO-
OP) in August 2021 to promote oil palm cultivation, with special focus on North Eastern 
States. The Mission is being implemented in 15 States. The mission provides 
comprehensive support to farmers, including assistance for high quality planting materials, 
inputs for intercropping and maintenance during the four year gestation period. There is 
also a provision for replanting of old and unproductive plantations. The mission supports 
farm machinery, irrigation facilities, seed gardens, nurseries and Custom Hiring Centres. 
The North Eastern States are provided financial assistance for setting up oil palm 
processing mills.  
 
From 2021-22 to 2025-26, 2.73 lakh hectares was brought under oil palm cultivation, taking 
the cumulative area to 6.40 lakh hectares as on 31.03.2026. During this period, 114.66 lakh 
tonnes of Fresh Fruit Bunches (FFBs) were harvested, resulting in the production of 20.10 
lakh tonnes of Crude Palm Oil (CPO). At present, 27 oil palm processing mills are 
operational across the country. The Mission provides Viability Gap Payment (VGP) to 
support oil palm growers. As on date, ₹18.90 crore has been disbursed to 9,244 oil palm 
farmers in Goa, Tamil Nadu, Gujarat, Karnataka, Odisha, Arunachal Pradesh, Assam, and 
Mizoram under this provision.

PROJECTS SANCTIONED TO ANDHRA PRADESH UNDER NHM 
 
2631. DR. D. PURANDESWARI: 
   
Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE                                              
क ृ िष एवं िकसान कʞाण मंũी be pleased to state: 
 
(a) whether the Government has implemented specific projects under the National 
Horticulture Mission (NHM) during 2025-2026 in Andhra Pradesh, with particular 
reference to the Rajahmundry Lok Sabha Constituency; 
(b) if so, the details of the total financial assistance provided for expanding the 
cultivation of high-value crops like oil palm, coconut and citrus fruits in the 
Rajahmundry region; 
(c) the number of integrated post-harvest management units and cold storage 
facilities set up in the East Godavari district under this scheme during the last one 
year; 
(d) whether the Ministry has received any proposals from horticulture growers in 
Rajahmundry regarding the establishment of specialized processing hubs for value 
addition; and 
(e) the details of the steps being taken by the Government to supply disease-
resistant planting materials to small farmers in Rajahmundry? 
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE FOR AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE 
 
क ृ िष एवं िकसान कʞाण राǛ मंũी (SHRI RAMNATH THAKUR) 
 
(a) & (b): The Department of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare is implementing Mission 
for Integrated Development of Horticulture (MIDH) throughout the country including 
in the State of Andhra Pradesh, under which financial assistance is provided for 
establishment of various horticulture activities such as Establishment of New 
Gardens, Creation of Water Resources, Protected Cultivation, Integrated Post-
Harvest Management, Centre of Excellence (CoE), Marketing, Beekeeping, and 
Horticulture Mechanization. 
 
 Further, Government is implementing various interventions through Coconut 
Development Board for the integrated development of coconut sector in the country 
wherein financial assistance is provided @ Rs. 56000 per hectare for new coconut 
plantation.  

 
In addition, National Mission on Edible-Oils-Oil Palm (NMEO-OP) is being 
implemented in 15 States including Rajahmundry region of Andhra Pradesh to 
promote oil palm cultivation and achieve Aatmanirbhar Bharat in edible oils. The 
Mission provides comprehensive support to farmers, including assistance for high-
quality planting material, inputs for intercropping, and maintenance during the four-
year gestation period, as well as replanting of old and unproductive plantations.  
Additional inputs such as farm machinery and irrigation facilities are also supported.  
Furthermore, the scheme promotes the establishment of seed gardens, nurseries, 
and custom hiring centres, while North-Eastern States receive additional support for 
setting up oil palm processing mills.  
 
     During 2025-26, an amount of Rs. 179.82 Lakhs was utilized in Andhra Pradesh 
under CDB scheme, out of which Rs. 2.94 Lakhs was utilized in Rajahmundry region 
covering 10.50 ha of coconut plantation. Under Oil Palm scheme, an amount of Rs. 
9.42 crore has been distributed for expanding oil palm cultivation in Rajahmundry 
region. Under MIDH, an amount of Rs. 13.31 Lakhs has been utilized for area 
expansion of citrus and dragon fruit in Rajahmundry region.  
 
(c): Under the Post Harvest Management (PHM) component of MIDH scheme, 
during 2025-26, two (02) Pack houses have been established in East Godavari 
District.  
 
    Further, Government is implementing Agriculture Infrastructure Fund (AIF) 
scheme across the country to mobilize a medium to long term debt financing facility 
for investment in viable projects relating to post harvest management infrastructure 
and community farming assets through incentives and financial support. Under AIF, 
there is provision for collateral free term loan upto Rs. 2.00 crore and interest 
subvention of 3% on the term loan availed for creation of post-harvest infrastructure, 
including establishment of cold storages. Under the Agriculture Infrastructure Fund 
(AIF), a total of 111 projects have been approved in East Godavari district, with a 
cumulative approved amount of ₹232.39 crore against a total project cost of ₹425.19 
crore. The projects include 44 Primary Processing Centres, 30 Warehouses, 11 
Sorting & Grading Units, 10 Assaying Units, 7 Silos, 7 Post-Harvest Management 
(PHM) Activities, 1 Integrated Primary and Secondary Processing Unit, and 1 
Packaging Unit.  
  

 
(d):  Under MIDH scheme, assistance is provided to horticulture growers @35% to 
50% of the maximum eligible cost for setting up of primary and secondary 
processing units which is entrepreneur based demand driven activity. Ministry of 
Agriculture and Farmers Welfare has not received any proposals from horticulture 
growers in Rajahmundry regarding the establishment of specialized processing hubs 
for value addition.  
 
(e): Under MIDH scheme, for ensuring availability of the disease-free planting 
material to the farmers, assistance is provided for production and distribution of good 
quality seeds and planting material of horticulture crops through setting up nurseries, 
and Tissue Culture (TC) units. Financial assistance is provided @ 40% of the eligible 
cost for private sector and 100% of eligible cost in case of public sector. Since 
inception of MIDH scheme i.e. from 2014-15 onwards, a total of 1184 nurseries have 
been established throughout the country.

COMPETITION IN SECTORS FOR LARGE BUSINESS GROUPS 
 
2632.  SHRI SANATAN PANDEY: 
 
Will the Minister of COMMERCE AND INDUSTRY be pleased to state: 
वाणिज्य  एवं उद्योग मंत्री 
(a)  whether the Government has assessed the level of competition in sectors 
where a few large business groups have significant market presence; 
 
(b)  if so, the details thereof; 
 
(c)  whether any measures have been taken to facilitate the participation of MSMEs 
and new entrants in Government tenders; and 
 
(d)  if so, the details thereof along with the outcome of such measures? 
 
ANSWER 
 
वाणिज्य  एवं उद्योग मंत्रालय में राज्य मंत्री (श्री णिणिन प्रसाद)   
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF COMMERCE & INDUSTRY 
(SHRI JITIN PRASADA) 
 
(a) & (b): The Competition Commission of India (CCI) under the Ministry of Corporate 
Aﬀairs conducts market studies from time to time to develop  a better 
understanding of competitive conditions within one or more sectors. These 
studies enable CCI to gauge market developments, track evolving competition 
dynamics, understand specific business practices and analyse implications for 
competition arising from structural features.  In the past, CCI has carried out 
market studies in various sectors/areas including e -Commerce, Telecom, Cab 
Aggregation and Artificial Intelligence. 
(c) & (d): The Government has taken following measures to facilitate the participation 
of MSMEs and new entrants in Government tenders: - 
 As per the  Public Procurement Policy Order, 2012, the target for 
procurement from Micro and Small Enterprises (MSEs) is 25%. As 
reported by  Central Public Sector Enterprises (CPSEs) on SAMBANDH 
portal, procurement by CPSEs from MSEs has been 49.05% in 2025-26. 
 GeM has implemented the following measures to facilitate the participation 
of MSMEs on GeM portal; 
 
i. GeM has integration with Udyam database to verify and update 
status of sellers as MSMEs. 
ii. In case of direct purchase from Marketplace, buyers are provided with 
the marketplace filters to identify the products offered by MSMEs. 
iii. In line with Public Procurement Policy for Micro and Small Enterprises 
(MSEs) order, 2012 functionality provided for reserving the bid for 
procurement from MSEs, giving purchase preference and relaxation in 
Earnest Money Deposit (EMD)/ prior experience/ turnover.

(d)  the details of the proactive steps taken and special saturation drives conducted by 
the Government to ensure 100% registration of eligible tribal and marginal farmers in the 
Dahod Lok Sabha Constituency; and  
(e)  the overall positive socio-economic impact of this continuous financial assistance 
with regard to agricultural productivity, procurement of agricultural inputs, and the livelihood 
of the farming community in the region? 
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE FOR AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE  
कृ ͪष एवं ͩकसान कãयाण राÏय मंğी  (SHRI RAMNATH THAKUR) 
 
(a) to (e):      The PM-KISAN scheme is a central sector scheme launched to supplement 
the financial needs of farmers with cultivable land-holding. Under the scheme, a financial 
benefit of ₹ 6,000/- per year is transferred in three equal instalments, into the Aadhaar 

seeded bank accounts of farmers through Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT) mode. Under the 
PM-KISAN Scheme, Government of India has disbursed over ₹ 4.47 lakh Cr. to the 
beneficiaries through 23 installments since inception of the Scheme.  
As per the impact evaluation study by the Development Monitoring and Evaluation 
Office (DMEO) of NITI Aayog, the scheme is successfully fulfilling its primary function of 
providing direct financial assistance to farmers holding agricultural land, thereby enhancing 
their economic stability and agricultural productivity. The study also shows that over 92 
percent of beneficiary farmers utilized the financial assistance for essential agricultural 
inputs such as seeds, fertilizers, and pesticides, which are particularly important in the face 
of rising input costs and weather-related uncertainties. 
  
Instalment-wise details of beneficiaries benefitted in Dahod and Mahisagar districts 
of Gujarat and amount released to them since inception is at Annexure. 
 
 In order to ensure that no eligible farmer,  including tribal and marginal farmers, is 
left out, the Government of India undertakes saturation drives in coordination with the 
States/UTs, including Gujarat. A major nationwide saturation drive was undertaken from 
15th November 2023 under the Viksit Bharat Sankalp Yatra (VBSY), during which, more 
than 1 Cr. farmers were included under PM-KISAN. Further, under the Government’s 100 
days initiative in 2024, over 25 lakh eligible farmers were added under the PM-KISAN 
scheme. A special drive was also conducted in September 2024 to clear the pending self-
registration cases, which resulted in the addition of over 30 lakh new farmers. Further, a 
nationwide saturation drive was undertaken in June, 2026 under PM-KISAN, alongwith the 
“Khet Bachao Abhiyaan” to expand the coverage of eligible farmers under the scheme, 
which resulted in the addition of about 17 lakh farmers in the country, including 1 lakh 
farmers in Gujarat, including Dahod.

GLOBALLY IMPORTANT AGRICULTURAL HERITAGE SYSTEMS 
2635. SHRI KODIKUNNIL SURESH: 
Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE क ृ िष एवं िकसान कʞाण मंũी 
be pleased to state: 
(a) the details of the financial, technical and institutional assistance provided by the 
Government to the Kuttanad Agricultural Heritage System, Kerala, after its recognition as a 
Globally Important Agricultural Heritage Systems (GIAHS) site by the Food and Agriculture 
Organization (FAO); 
(b) the details of the projects sanctioned, funds allocated and expenditure incurred for the 
conservation and sustainable development of the Kuttanad GIAHS site, year-wise; 
(c) whether the Government has formulated or proposes to formulate a dedicated action 
plan for the conservation, climate resilience, branding and promotion of the Kuttanad 
Agricultural Heritage System and if so, the details thereof; 
(d) whether consultations have been held with the Government of Kerala and other 
stakeholders for the long-term conservation and management of the site; and 
(e) the further steps proposed to strengthen and promote Kuttanad as a globally significant 
agricultural heritage landscape? 
ANSWER 
MINISTER OF STATE FOR AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE 
क ृ िष एवं िकसान कʞाण राǛ मंũी (SHRI RAM NATH THAKUR) 
(a) &  (b): As reported by the Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO), India, the Kuttanad 
Farming System in Kerala was recognized as a Globally Important Agricultural Heritage 
System (GIAHS) in 2013 under the FAO’s GIAHS Programme. 
As reported by the Government of Kerala, Kuttanad has been declared as a Special 
Agricultural Zone by the State Government. A comprehensive Kuttanad Package for 
mitigation of agrarian distress and restoration of the Kuttanad wetland ecosystem was 
implemented during 2008–2019 through more than 14 implementing agencies. Funding was 
mobilised through various Central Ministries and schemes, Government of Kerala Plan 
schemes and Finance Commission grants. As reported by the Kerala State Planning Board, 
expenditure of about ₹1,013.35 crore had been incurred under the Package up to 31 March 
2019. 
The International Research and Training Centre for Below Sea Level Farming 
(IRTCBSF) at Alappuzha undertakes research relating to climate change and salinity 
intrusion in Kuttanad and develops technologies for improving productivity and farmers’ 
income. Under the Pradhan Mantri Rashtriya Krishi Vikas Yojana (Detailed Project Report 
Component), a project titled “Ecological Utilization of Water Hyacinth (Eichhornia crassipes) 
in Kuttanad” was sanctioned during 2022-23 with a project cost of ₹1,513 lakh, against which 
₹107.52 lakh has been released. 

 
The Government of India also supports sustainable agriculture, conservation of agro-
biodiversity, climate resilience and farmers’ livelihoods through various Central Sector and 
Centrally Sponsored Schemes. Farmers and institutions in the Kuttanad region are eligible 
for assistance under these schemes, subject to the respective scheme guidelines and the 
priority proposed by the State Government in the Annual Action Plan of the State. Details of 
relevant projects and assistance reported in respect of the Kuttanad region are given in the 
Annexure. 
In addition, the Ministry of Jal Shakti implemented two flood mitigation projects for 
Padasekharams of the Kuttanad region during 2014-15 and 2017-18 at a total cost of ₹54.63 
crore. 
The Government of Kerala has further reported implementation of the following State 
Plan schemes in the Kuttanad region: 
(i) Development of Agriculture Sector in Kuttanad, with a budget provision of ₹7 crore during 
2025-26 for strengthening paddy field infrastructure. Since 2020-21, an expenditure of 
₹2,017.55 lakh has been incurred for replacement of traditional Petti and Para systems with 
Vertical Axial Flow (VAF) pump sets. 
(ii) Rebuild Kerala Initiative Project for sustainable development of the Kuttanad rice 
ecosystem and integrated farming, with an outlay of ₹203 lakh. 
(iii) Assistance to Paddy Cultivation in Kuttanad, under which financial assistance is 
provided to paddy farmers. 
(iv) Rural Infrastructure Development Fund (NABARD) General, under which two 
infrastructure projects with a total outlay of ₹1,800 lakh are under implementation. 
(c) to (e): The Government of India continues to support the Kuttanad region through various 
ongoing Central Sector and Centrally Sponsored Schemes, under which assistance is 
available for sustainable agriculture, climate resilience, farm mechanization, water 
management, infrastructure development and farmers’ livelihoods, subject to the provisions 
of the respective schemes and the priority proposed by the State Government in the Annual 
Action Plan of the State. 
Financial assistance is available under the Sub-Mission on Agricultural Mechanization 
(SMAM) for procurement of suitable farm machinery, including paddy transplanters, 
combine harvesters, power tillers and weeders, and for establishment of Custom Hiring 
Centres to improve access to farm machinery for small and marginal farmers. Infrastructure 
and water management interventions, including de-silting of canals, strengthening of bunds 
and modernization of pumping systems, are also supported under schemes such as PM-
RKVY, while drainage and flood mitigation infrastructure is supported under Rural 
Infrastructure Development Fund with NABARD assistance. These interventions contribute 
towards improving productivity, strengthening climate resilience and supporting sustainable 
agriculture in the Kuttanad region.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE 
DEPARTMENT OF AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE

AIMS AND OBJECTS OF AGRICULTURAL SCHEMES 
 
2638. Shri Balashowry Vallabhaneni: 
Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE कृͪष एवं ͩकसान कãयाण मंğी be 
pleased to state: 
(a) the aims and objectives of Krishonnati Yojana, National Mission on Natural Farming and 
National Bee and Honey Mission; 
(b) the status of implementation of above schemes across the country since their launch, year-
wise, State-wise and scheme-wise; 
(c) whether there are any plans to merge above schemes with PM-Krishi Vikas Yojana; and 
(d) if so, the details thereof and the reasons therefor 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE FOR AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE  
कृͪष एवं ͩकसान कãयाण राÏय मंğी (SHRI RAM NATH THAKUR) 
(a) & (b) Krishonnati Yojana (KY) is an umbrella Centrally Sponsored Scheme of the 
Department of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare comprising several flagship interventions, 
including the National Food Security & Nutrition Mission (NFSNM), Mission for Integrated 
Development of Horticulture (MIDH), Sub-Mission on Agricultural Extension (SMAE), National 
Mission on Edible Oil-Oilseeds (NMEO-OS), National Mission on Edible Oil-Oilpalm (NMEO-
OP), Sub-Mission on Seeds & Planting Material (SMSP), Digital Agriculture Mission, Mission 
for Atmanirbharta in Pulses, Mission Organic Value Chain Development for North Eastern 
Region (MOVCDNER) and  Integrated Scheme on Agricultural Marketing (ISAM). 
The overarching objective of Krishonnati Yojana is to promote holistic, sustainable and 
inclusive development of the agriculture sector by enhancing agricultural production and 
productivity, promoting quality seeds and planting materials, supporting crop diversification, 
horticulture and agroforestry, strengthening agricultural marketing and post-harvest 
infrastructure, facilitating digital agriculture and data-driven governance,  extension services 
and markets, ensuring food and nutritional security. The details of implementation of  
Krishonnati Yojana is placed at Annexure I. 
 
The Centrally Sponsored Scheme of National Mission on Natural Farming is being 
implemented since November, 2024 to promote natural farming across the country. Natural 
Farming (NF) is a chemical free farming, involving livestock (preferably local breed of cow) 
integrated natural farming methods and diversified crop systems rooted in the Indian traditional 
knowledge. It is aimed towards improving soil health and restoring ecosystems and reducing 
input cost to the farmer to achieve greater climate resilience. The objectives of the Mission 
are: - 

 
i. To promote nature based sustainable systems of farming, enhancing usage of on-farm 
made natural farming bio-inputs, to reduce dependency on externally purchased inputs 
and input cost reduction, to also improve soil health and have sustainable agriculture 
practices. 
ii. To popularize livestock (preferably local breed of cow) integrated agriculture-animal 
husbandry models. 
iii. To strengthen on-farm agroecological research and knowledge based extension 
capacities of ICAR institutions, KVKs, Agricultural Universities, etc. 
iv. To build upon the on-field experience of practicing Natural Farming farmers and scientific 
expertise to thereby evolve & improvise location specific NF package of practices for 
increased spread of NF. 
v. To establish scientifically supported common standards and easy farmer friendly 
certification procedures for naturally grown chemical-free produce. 
vi. To create and promote a single national brand for naturally grown chemical-free 
produce. 
The details of implementation of National Mission on Natural Farming is placed at Annexure 
II. 
The Government is implementing National Beekeeping and Honey Mission (NBHM) for 
promotion of scientific beekeeping and holistic development of beekeeping sector across the 
country.  The Mission aims to increase honey production and productivity, improve the quality 
and traceability of honey and other bee products, strengthen production and processing 
infrastructure, promote research, capacity building and entrepreneurship, create employment 
opportunities and augment farmers’ income by promoting beekeeping as a viable allied 
agricultural activity. NBHM is a demand-driven, project-based Central Sector Scheme under 
which financial assistance is provided to eligible implementing agencies as per the scheme 
guidelines. No State-wise allocation of funds is made under the Mission. The details of 
implementation of National Beekeeping and Honey Mission is placed at Annexure III. 
 
(c) & (d) Presently, the Centrally Sponsored Schemes of the Department of Agriculture & 
Farmers’ Welfare are implemented under two umbrella schemes, namely Pradhan Mantri-
Rashtriya Krishi Vikas Yojana (PM-RKVY) and Krishonnati Yojana (KY).

   Will the Minister of COMMERCE AND INDUSTRY  (वाणिज्य एवं उद्योग मंत्री)  be 
pleased to state: 
  
(a) the total number of trade delegations sent during the last six months to the 40

 along with the details of the total trade agreements achieved through such

(b) the details of the funds allocated during the current financial year for developing 
 modern infrastructure in other handicraft and One District One Product (ODOP) 
 clusters in Uttar Pradesh on the lines of the newly established B2B Cash and 
 Carry Centre and 3D Design Studio in Moradabad district in Uttar Pradesh; and 
(c) whether the Government has any proposals to formulate any special C entral 
 Scheme to impart training to traditional artisans in international quality standards,

 proposed for the next three years along with the total number of targeted

THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF COMMERCE AND INDUSTRY 
(SHRI JITIN PRASADA) 
  
(a) The Government promotes Indian products including handicrafts and one district 
one products through engagement with Indian Missions abroad and numerous 
participations in international exhibitions, Buyer-Seller Meets (BSMs), trade fairs under 
the Market Access Support intervention of Export Promotion Mission. The objective of 
Market Access Support intervention is to develop, expand, and sustain international 
markets, allowing for market diversification and international visibility. 
 
During the last six months, approval for 132 promotional activities (with financial support 
of ₹ 133.43 Cr) have been accorded to facilitate business linkages and enhance export 
opportunities in several countries. The details of events approved for Saudi Arabia and 
Australia are as below:

 (b) The implementation of One District One Product (ODOP) is primarily done through 
convergence with the schemes/programmes of the Central Ministries/Departments and 
the State Governments. No district-specific financial allocation is made under the ODOP 
initiative. However, several steps have been undertaken to promote and enhance the 
visibility of the ODOP products, which includes facilitating participation in domestic and 
international exhibitions, capacity building initiatives in collaboration with various 
agencies; e -commerce on boarding drives for Government e -Marketplace (GeM) - 
ODOP Bazaar. ODOP products have also been included as official gifts during various 
bilateral/multilateral meetings, thereby enhancing their visibility in international markets. 
 
Under the Scheme of Department of Expenditure for Special Assistance to States for 
Capital Investment (SASCI), States/UTs with legislatu res are provided financial 
assistance of up to ₹200 crores in the form of a 50 -year interest -free loan for 
establishing PM Ekta Malls (Unity Malls) to promote the sale of ODOP products, 
Geographical Indication (GI) products and other handicrafts across the country. 
 
Ministry of Textiles has sanctioned an amount of ₹6.27 crore  during FY 2025 –26 for 
infrastructure development projects in Uttar Pradesh State.  
 
(c) The ODOP initiative has previously collaborated with key institutions such as the 
Indian Institutes of Technology (IIT Bombay, Roorkee, Kharagpur, and Bhubaneswar), 
and National Institute of Design (NID Ahmedabad), along with the Directorate General 
of Foreign Trade (DGFT) and Press Information Bureau (PIB), to undertake capacity -
building initiatives focused on product innovation, diversification, quality enhancement, 
and market readiness. 
 
Ministry of Textiles provides  training support to traditional artisans under the existing 
schemes of the Office of Development Commissioner (Handicrafts). 
Under the Export Promotion Mission, the Government has also launched Trade 
Regulations, Accreditation & Compliance Enablement intervention to extend financial 
support to the exporters to meet International Testing, Inspection, Certification and other 
conformity requirements. 
 
The Export Promotion Mission also provides support to activities like Training / Capacity 
Building, District & Cluster Facilitation, Research, Innovation & Pilots with an objective 
to strengthen exporter preparedness and develop institutional support systems by 
addressing information asymmetries and capacity gaps.

DISPOSAL OF STEEL SCRAP 
 
2641.  SHRI KALI CHARAN SINGH:  
 
Will the Minister of STEEL be pleased to state:  
 
(a) the current status of implementation of the Steel Scrap Recycling Policy in the 
country;  
 
(b) the details of steel scrap presently lying at various Central Public Sector steel plants 
and other major integrated steel plants for disposal or recycling, plant-wise, indicating 
the estimated quantity, value and reasons for accumulation;  
 
(c) the details of steel scrap disposed of or recycled during each of the last three years 
and the current year, plant-wise, along with the revenue realised and whether disposal 
has been carried out through transparent auction or other approved mechanisms; and  
 
(d) the steps taken by the Government to ensure timely disposal of accumulated scrap, 
promote organized scrap collection and processing, increase the use of recycled scrap 
in steel production and strengthen the steel scrap recycling ecosystem to improve 
resource efficiency, reduce dependence on imported scrap and lower carbon 
emissions? 
 
ANSWER 
 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE          (SHRI BHUPATHIRAJU SRINIVASA VARMA) 
MINISTRY OF STEEL 
 
(a)&(d): The current status of implementation of Steel Scrap Recycling Policy in 
the country including the steps taken by the Government for steel scrap recycling to 
promote the circular economy in the sector is as under:-  
 
(i) The Steel Scrap Recycling Policy, 2019 provides a coordination framework with 
various Ministries to promote recycling of ferrous scrap generated from various 
sources. 
 
(ii) The Ministry of Road Transport and Highways (MoRTH) has formulated the 
Vehicle Scrapping Policy that includes a system of incentives/disincentives for 
creation of an ecosystem to phase out older, unfit polluting vehicles. Under the 
policy, MoRTH has issued rules for Registration and Functions of Vehicle 
Scrapping Facility (RVSF), which provides the procedures and infrastructure 
facilities required for de-pollution and dismantling of End-of-Life Vehicles (ELVs) 
for further recovery of metal and other materials under environmental regulations. 
As on 24.07.2026, 151 Registered Vehicle Scrapping Facilities (RVSFs) are 
operational across 23 States/UTs. 
 
Contd…..2/- 

::2:: 
 
(iii) The Government of India has notified the Hazardous and Other Wastes 
(Management and Transboundary Movement) Rules, 2016 to ensure safe 
handling, storage, recycling, utilisation, treatment and disposal of hazardous and 
other wastes in an environmentally safe manner. 
 
(iv) Ministry of Environment, Forest & Climate Change has introduced the 
Environment Protection (End-of-Life Vehicles) Rules, 2025, which establishes a 
framework for managing End-of-Life Vehicles (ELVs) in an environmentally sound 
manner and mandates Extended Producer Responsibility (EPR), requiring vehicle 
producers to meet annual scrapping targets based on the type of vehicle and 
materials recovered. 
 
(v) Recycling of Ships Act, 2019 has been notified by Ministry of Shipping, Ports 
and Waterways with aims to regulate and promote the safe and environmentally 
sound recycling of ships. 
 
(b)&(c): Steel is de-regulated sector and hence, the decision for recycling and 
utilization of ferrous scrap is taken by the steel plants based on their specific 
requirement and market dynamics. Scrap is continuously generated in steel plants 
during steel production and milling, which is continuously consumed and surplus scrap 
is disposed of as per market dynamics.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF COOPERATION  
 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 2642 
TO BE ANSWERED ON 4th AUGUST, 2026 
 
Computerization of Primary Agricultural Credit Societies 
†2642. Shri Imran Masood: 
Will the Minister of COOPERATION (सहकारिता मंत्री) be pleased to state: 
(a) whether the Government has reviewed the progress of the computerization and 
modernization of Primary Agricultural Credit Societies (PACS) during the period from 
January to June, 2026; 
(b) if so, the details of the computerized PACS, multipurpose PACS, and the number of 
PACS functioning as Jan Aushadhi Kendras and Bank Mitras, State-wise; 
(c) whether the Government has formulated any special action plan for the restructuring 
and financial strengthening of dormant or loss-making PACS; 
(d) whether any integrated national digital platform has been developed for the online  
monitoring of the functioning of PACS; and 
(e) if so, the details thereof and if not, the reasons therefor? 
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF COOPERATION 
सहकारिता मंत्री (SHRI AMIT SHAH) 
(a) Yes, Sir. Ministry of Cooperation, NABARD and Registrar of Cooperative Societies of 
all States/UTs are regularly reviewing the digitalisation progress of Primary Agricultural Credit 
Societies ( PACS) through  regular monitoring under national and state -level committees. A 
structured monitoring framework has been established for effective review of progress of this 
project in States/UTs, which comprises of the National Level Monitoring and Implementation 
Committee (NLMIC), State and District Level Impleme ntation and Monitoring Committees 
(SLIMC and DLIMC), State Cooperative Development Committee (SCDC) (under the Chief 
Secretary), and District Cooperative Development Committee (DCDC) (under the District 
Collector). These bodies ensure effective implementat ion, oversight, and coordination of all 
cooperative sector initiatives, including PACS computerization. During review meetings, the 
performance of PACS is closely monitored for timely completion of their online activities, 
which ensures transparency and accountability in financial transactions at the PACS level. 

Page 2 of 10 
 
The Government also continuously reviews the implementation of the Centrally 
Sponsored Project for Computerization of PACS  through periodic review meetings with 
States/UTs, NABARD, State Cooperative Banks (StCBs), District Central Cooperative Banks 
(DCCBs), System Integrators and other stakeholders. Progress is monitored through the ERP-
based National Software, Management Inf ormation System (MIS), project dashboards and 
periodic field reviews. 
 During the period from January to June, 2026, continued progress has been achieved 
in hardware deployment, ERP onboarding, Go -Live of PACS, digital transactions, statutory 
audit and convergence with various national digital platforms. The project also und ergoes 
continuous enhancement and customization based on feedback received from States/UTs to 
cater to State-specific business requirements and operational processes. 
(b) As on 30.06.2026, 63,686 PACS  have been onboarded on the ERP -based National 
Software under the Centrally Sponsored Project. The State/UT-wise details of approved PACS, 
hardware delivered and ERP onboarded PACS are given at Annexure-‘A’.  
The Government of India has approved the plan to establish new multipurpose 
PACS/dairy/fisheries cooperatives, aiming to cover all panchayats and villages in the country 
over the next five years. The details of the cooperative societies registered thereund er, State-
wise is at Annexure-‘B’. 
Under the Pradhan Mantri Bhartiya Janaushadhi Kendra (PMBJK) scheme, 4,275 
applications have been received from PACS, of which 4,255 have received initial approvals, 
900 have obtained drug licences, 846 have been allotted store codes and 645 centres have 
become operational as Jan Aushadhi Kendras. The State/UT wise list is at Annexure-‘C’. 
The list of Non- Credit Primary Cooperative Societies (Dairy etc.) working as Bank Mitras of 
District Central Cooperative Banks (DCCBs) under the Cooperation among Cooperatives 
campaign is attached as Annexure-‘D’.  
(c) The Government has adopted a multi -pronged strategy to restructure and financially 
strengthen Primary Agricultural Credit Societies (PACS), including those that are 
underperforming or at risk of closure. The central approach involves transforming these 
societies into economically vibrant, multipurpose entities to ensure their long -term financial 
sustainability. Key components of this action plan include: 
1. Formation of Multipurpose PACS (MPACS) :- The plan to establish new multipurpose 
PACS/dairy/fisheries cooperatives is implemented with the support of National Bank for 
Agriculture and Rural Development (NABARD), National Dairy Development Board (NDDB) 
and National Fisheries Development Board (NFDB), through convergence of various existing 
schemes of Govt. of India(GoI), such as National Programme for Dairy Development (NPDD), 
Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana (PMMSY), etc. 

Page 3 of 10 
 
The strategy envisages both formation of new MPACS and transformation of existing PACS 
into multipurpose entities capable of delivering credit and multiple non-credit services.  
2. Transformation into Multipurpose Societies: -  The Government prepared and circulated 
Model Bye-laws that enable PACS to diversify their income streams by undertaking more than 
25 business activities . By adopting these bye -laws, PACS can now function as Common 
Service Centres (CSCs), Jan Aushadhi Kendras, PM Kisan Samriddhi Kendras, and operate in 
sectors like LPG/petrol distribution and rural water supply. This diversification is designed to 
transform them from primarily credit-oriented societies into modern service hubs. The details 
of PACS involved in different activities is at Annexure-‘E’. 
 
3. Financial Strengthening and Capacity Building 
Under Section 63A of the Multi -State Cooperative Societies (Amendment) Act, 2023, a 
dedicated fund has been established for the revival of sick multi-State cooperative societies and 
to provide assistance for meeting their infrastructural requirements. 
To address "performance gaps" and strengthen functional capabilities, National Council for 
Cooperative Training (NCCT) has developed a comprehensive training module for the capacity 
building of one lakh PACS Secretaries. The objective of this initiative is to equip PACS 
Secretaries with the necessary managerial and administrative competencies to effectively 
discharge their responsibilities, promote diversification of business activities, and strengthen 
internal control systems. 
For this purpose, detailed training and study materials have been prepared. A national -level 
Training of Trainers (ToT ) programme was conducted on 24th –25th March 2026 at 
V AMNICOM, Pune, wherein 43 faculty members from various NCCT institutes were trained 
as Master Trainers. 
 
4. Operational Modernization and Transparency 
Computerization Project: A project with a financial outlay of ₹2,925.39 crore is bringing 
functional PACS onto a common ERP -based national software . This is intended to improve 
governance, reduce transaction costs, and ensure seamless accounting with cooperative banks. 
The Government utilizes the National Cooperative Database ( NCD) to identify gaps in 
geographical coverage and financial performance, allowing policymakers to target 
interventions toward underperforming societies 
 
5. Infrastructure Development 
i. Decentralized Grain Storage Plan: PACS are being strengthened through the creation 
of warehouses and primary processing units. 
ii. By converging various Central schemes, the Government is helping PACS improve 
their financial viability by providing them with infrastructure that generates steady 
rental income through hiring assurances from agencies like the Food Corporation of 
India (FCI) and National Agricultural Cooperative Marketing Federation of India Ltd.  
(NAFED).  

Page 4 of 10 
 
iii. Sahakar Innovation Scheme: Launched in FY 2025 -26, this scheme provides grant 
assistance of up to ₹25 lakh to cooperative societies for adopting new technologies and 
business models, specifically supporting those that lack adequate collateral 
Apart from these above mentioned initiatives, Ministry thorugh NABARD is implementing 
various initiatives for financial strengthening of dormant or loss making PACS which are as 
under:- 
I. Revival and Strengthening of Loss -making & Dormant PACS: - NABARD has 
prepared a structured programme for revival of approximately 59,000 -60,000 loss -
making and non -functional PACS through a Business Process Re -engineering (BPR) 
approach. P ACS are supported to undertake diagnostic assessments and prepare 
Turnaround Plans (TAPs) covering capital augmentation, business development, 
governance reforms and operational efficiency.  
II. PACS Accelerator Programme (PAP):- NABARD is scaling up the PACS Accelerator 
Programme (PAP) to diversify PACS businesses beyond credit operations.  Activities 
include identification of viable business opportunities, DPR preparation, financing 
support, standardisation of lending processes and handholding support.  
III. Capacity Building and Handholding: - Training programmes are conducted for PACS 
Boards, CEOs, Secretaries and staff,  Resource Support Agencies (RSAs) and Resource 
Persons (RPs) are being deployed for continuous guidance on business planning, 
governance and operational improvement.  
IV.  Technology Enablement and Computerisation: -  NABARD is supporting digital 
transformation through PACS computerisation and development of MIS, dashboards and 
monitoring portals. A proposed National Digital Dashboard (NDD) will monitor 
outcomes of PACS strengthening and revival initiatives.  
V. Governance and Institutional Strengthening: - Focus is placed on improving 
governance standards, audits, compliance systems and professional management of 
PACS. NABARD is promoting stronger linkages with DCCBs/StCBs  and supporting 
affiliation and financial sustainability plans.  
VI. Monitoring and Review Mechanism :- State-wise and district -wise targets have been 
prescribed. NABARD Regional Offices and DDMs are entrusted with monitoring 
implementation, business diversification, project sanction, disbursement and 
handholding support to PACS.  
 
 
(d) and (e) Under the Centrally Sponsored Project, a Common ERP -based National 
Software has been developed and implemented for computerization of PACS across the 
country. The software provides integrated modules for membership management, loan 
operations, deposits, fertilizer and seed distribution, inventory management, accounting, 
statutory audit, MIS and other business activities. Legacy data of PACS have been digitized 
and migrated to the ERP platform to facilitate digital record management, improve 
transparency and reduce dependence on manual record keeping.  
The ERP platform also facilitates integration with District Central Cooperative Banks 
(DCCBs), State Cooperative Banks (StCBs) and other digital platforms for seamless banking 

Page 5 of 10 
 
operations and digital service delivery. Further, the centralized MIS and project dashboard 
enable online monitoring of ERP onboarding, Go -Live status, digital transactions, statutory 
audit and other implementation milestones by the Ministry and other auth orized stakeholders. 
The ERP system also supports maintenance of digital records, generation of audit trails and 
standardized financial reporting, thereby enhancing transparency, accountability and efficiency 
in the functioning of PACS.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE 
DEPARTMENT OF AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE 
 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 2643 
TO BE ANSWERED ON THE 04th AUGUST, 2026 
 
IMPLEMENTATION OF DIGITAL AGRICULTURE MISSION IN TAMIL NADU 
 
2643.  SHRI MANI A: 
SHRI NAVASKANI K: 
Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE (कृ ͪष एवं ͩकसान कãयाण मंğी) 
be pleased to state: 
 
 (a) whether the Government has reviewed the implementation of the Digital Agriculture 
Mission in Tamil Nadu, and progress made in generation of Farmer IDs, digitisation of 
agricultural records and delivery of farmer-centric digital services across the State; 
(b) the initiatives undertaken to integrate Farmer IDs with digital land records, crop 
information, Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT), crop insurance, credit, soil health and other 
agricultural support services in Tamil Nadu; 
(c)  the measures taken to promote awareness, digital literacy and enrolment of farmers 
under the Digital Agriculture Mission through Common Service Centres, Farmer Producer 
Organisations & agricultural extension machinery in Tamil Nadu; 
(d)  the number of Farmer IDs generated in Dharmapuri district and the initiatives taken to 
facilitate registration of eligible farmers; and 
(e) whether Government proposes to further strengthen digital agriculture services in 
Dharmapuri district through technology-enabled advisory services, precision farming, 
digital crop monitoring and improved access to agricultural schemes and if so, the details 
thereof? 
                                               ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE FOR AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE 
कृ ͪष एवं ͩकसान कãयाण राÏय मंğी (SHRI RAMNATH THAKUR) 
 
(a) The Government closely monitors the implementation of AgriStack, the Farmers’ 
Registry, and the Crop Sowing Registry under the Digital Agriculture Mission in the States 
and Union Territories, including Tamil Nadu. Periodic review meetings with the States and 
Union Territories are being conducted to review and monitor the Mission's implementation, 
assess progress, address emerging challenges, and ensure timely generation of Farmer IDs, 
digitisation of agricultural records and delivery of farmer-centric digital services across the 
State including the State of Tamil Nadu. Further, to ensure effective and uniform 
implementation, National and Zonal Conferences are regularly organized to share best 
practices, address implementation issues, and provide strategic guidance to States/UTs. 

Further, Capacity-building and training programmes are being conducted regularly for State 
Government officials and field functionaries, with continuous technical assistance for 
onboarding the farmers on AgriStack, IT system integration, and the operationalisation of the 
digital platforms for AgriStack-enabled services to farmers. As of 30th July, 2026, in Tamil 
Nadu, more than 36.51 lakh farmers have been issued a Unique Farmer ID. 
(b) : As reported by Tamil Nadu, the Farmer Registry is being integrated with Digital land 
records to create a reliable digital database, which enables transparent and efficient delivery 
of government schemes and services to eligible farmers. This data is being utilized for the 
selection of beneficiaries of various schemes and services such as crop information, Direct 
Benefit Transfer (DBT), crop insurance, credit, soil health and other agricultural support 
services, since 2025-26. An exclusive portal "Tamil Man Valam" is developed for viewing soil 
fertility status and get crop with suitability/recommendations options.  
(c) & (d): A total number of 1,63,368 Farmer ID's have been generated in Dharmapuri 
district. Further, 1.31 crore land parcels have been integrated with farmer ID, including 4.95 
lakh land parcels in Dharmapuri Districts in Tamil Nadu. State Government has taken several 
measures to promote awareness, digital literacy and enrolment of farmers under the Digital 
Agriculture Mission in Tamil Nadu. Common Service Centre is one of the enrolment centres 
for Farmer Registry. Awareness campaigns are being conducted by the Department of 
Agriculture using the Agriculture Extension Centres (AEC) at the block level. Farmer Producer 
Organisations (FPOs), Common Resource Persons (CRPs) and other field functionaries have 
been actively engaged to facilitate farmer enrolment. Special enrolment camps are being 
organised in villages to assist farmers in Aadhaar authentication, generation of Farmer IDs 
and updating of land records. 379 Social Media group has been formed in Tamil Nadu to 
disseminate technology information to farmers and farmer groups. 
(e) The State Government proposes to further strengthen digital agriculture services in 
Dharmapuri district as part of the implementation of the Digital State-wide Agriculture Mission. 
The initiatives include expansion of the Farmer Registry by generating Unique Farmer IDs for 
all eligible farmers through the Farmer Sahayak and Farmer Registry TN applications. Efforts 
are also focused on strengthening the Digital Crop Survey using geo-tagged field data and 
AI-based validation for real-time crop monitoring. Farmers are provided with technology-
enabled advisories through the Uzhavar App on crop management, weather, disease control, 
and nutrient management. Authenticated digital records and Aadhaar-enabled service 
delivery are improving farmers' access to Government schemes and services. So far, 20.32 
lakh farmers have downloaded the Uzhavar App, which offers 24 digital services through a 
single platform. In addition, capacity-building and awareness programmes are being 

conducted through the agricultural extension machinery to enhance farmers' adoption of 
digital agriculture services. 
Further, the Government of India has initiated several digital agriculture services 
using Artificial Intelligence (AI) for technology-based advisories, such as BharatVistaar, 
National Pest Surveillance System (NPSS), and KISAN SARATHI for farmers across the 
country, including Tamil Nadu. Some of the key AI initiatives are as follows: 
I. BharatVistaar: A multilingual AI-powered Digital Public Infrastructure for 
agriculture has been developed that provides farmers with real-time, location-
specific advisories, government scheme information, weather forecasts, mandi 
prices, pest detection, and grievance support through a web portal, mobile app, 
and telephone. It has served over 5.9 lakh farmers and handled 93 lakh+ 
queries across the country. 
II. National Pest Surveillance System (NPSS): An AI and Machine Learning-based 
system has been developed to help farmers detect pest infestations by 
analyzing pest images, enabling timely action to reduce crop losses. It currently 
covers 73 crops and 436 pests across the country. 
III. KISAN SARATHI: An Information and Communication Technology (ICT) 
platform has been developed by ICAR and is used by Krishi Vigyan Kendras to 
provide crop-specific advisories to farmers. It has 2.97 crore+ registered 
farmers across the country.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE 
DEPARTMENT OF AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE 
 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO.  2644 
TO BE ANSWERED ON THE 04TH AUGUST, 2026 
 
PERFORMANCE OF PMFBY IN TAMIL NADU 
 
2644. SHRI MALAIYARASAN D: 
Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE क ृ िष एवं िकसान कʞाण मंũी 
be pleased to state :  
(a) the total number of farmers enrolled under the Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana 
(PMFBY) during the last five years in the country, State/UT-wise particularly in Kallakurichi 
constituency of Tamil Nadu; 
(b) the details of total premium collected from farmers and the share of Union and State 
Governments under the scheme during the last five financial years; 
(c) the number of claims reported, approved and settled under PMFBY along with average 
time taken for settlement of claims across States; 
(d) whether instances of delay in settlement of crop insurance claims and denial of eligible 
compensation have been reported under the scheme in Tamil Nadu, if so, the details 
thereof; and 
(e) the steps taken by the Government to improve transparency, grievance redressal and 
timely payment of claims under PMFBY along with measures proposed for strengthening 
the scheme further? 
ANSWER 
MINISTER OF STATE FOR AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE  
क ृ िष एवं िकसान कʞाण राǛ मंũी  (SHRI RAMNATH THAKUR) 
 
(a): State/UT-wise details of number of farmers enrolled during last five years under 
Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana (PMFBY) and Restructured Weather Based Crop 
Insurance Scheme (RWBCIS) are given in Annexure. 
 
 Further, 8,73,793 farmer applications were enrolled under the scheme in 
Kallakurichi district of Tamil Nadu  during 2021-22 to 2025-26.  
  
(b): The actuarial/bidded/tendered  premium rates are charged by implementing agencies 
under Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana (PMFBY).  However, extremely low premium 
rate across the country for the season is charged from the famers, which is maximum 2% 
of sum insured for Kharif crops, maximum 1.5% of sum insured for Rabi crops and 
maximum 5% of sum insured for commercial/horticultural crops.  Remaining part of 
actuarial premium is shared by the Central and State Government in the form of 
assistance to make the scheme affordable to farmers.    

From Kharif 2023, 3 Alternate Risk Transfer Models (ARTM) other than standard 
PMFBY namely, cup and cap model (80:110), cup and cap model (60:130) and profit and 
loss sharing model have been implemented under which in case of claims below certain 
threshold, portion of the premium paid by the Government as subsidy will go back to the 
Government and in case of claims above the threshold, Government are required to pay 
the additional claims.  Total liability of State and Central Government is dependent on the 
total claims generated in different clusters of a State and the ARTM model adopted by the 
State based on which excess premium becomes recoverable or claim liability becomes 
due. 
Total premium collected by insurance companies from farmers, States and Central 
Government during last five years i.e. 2021-22 to 2025-26 under the scheme is 
Rs.18,351.69 crore, Rs.66,177.87 crore and Rs.55,738.64 crore, respectively,   out of 
which Rs.15,552.29 crore have been refunded by the insurance companies to the States 
and Central Government under ARTM.   
(c) & (d): Total claims reported and claims paid during last 5 years under the scheme are 
Rs.91,318.21 crore and Rs.86,731.59 crore respectively.   
Majority of the claims  are settled within the stipulated timelines under the 
operational guidelines of the scheme by the insurance companies. However, some claims 
remained pending including in Tamil Nadu, mainly on account of unverified bank account 
details of enrolled farmers.  
 
As per timelines given in the Operational Guidelines of the scheme, insurance 
companies have to settle the claims within 21 Days from calculation of claims on National 
Crop Insurance Portal (NCIP) and receipt of premium subsidy by Insurance Companies. In 
case payment is not made as per timelines mentioned above penalty of 12% is auto-
calculated and levied through NCIP w.e.f. Kharif 2024 season. 
 
(e) : The following steps have been taken by the Government to bring transparency, to 
increase coverage,  grievance redressal and ensure timely settlement of claims:   
(i): For timely settlement of claims under the scheme: 
- Government has undertaken development of National Crop Insurance Portal (NCIP) 
as a single source of data for subsidy payment, dissemination of information,  
delivery of services including online enrollment of farmers, uploading/obtaining 
individual insured famer’s details and transfer of claim amount electronically to the 
individual farmer’s Bank Account.   
 
- In order to rigorously monitor claim disbursal process, a dedicated module namely 
‘Digiclaim Module’ has been operationalized for payment of claims from Kharif 
2022 onwards.  It involves integration of National Crop Insurance Portal (NCIP) with 
Public Finance Management System (PFMS) and accounting system of Insurance 
Companies to provide timely & transparent processing of all claims. 
 
- W.e.f. Kharif 2024, in case payment is not made timely by Insurance Company, 
penalty.of 12% is auto-calculated and levied through NCIP. 
    

- Delinking of Central Government share of premium subsidy from that of State 
Governments has been implemented so that farmers can get proportionate claims 
relating to the Central Government share.  
 
- 12% penalty is also levied from Kharif 2025 on State Government for delay in 
release of State share of subsidy. 
 
- Opening of ESCROW Account by the State Government concerned for deposit of 
their premium share in advance as per provisions of the scheme has been made 
mandatory w.e.f. Kharif 2025 season for bringing financial discipline. 
   
- Also, towards leveraging technology in implementation of the scheme, various 
steps like capturing of yield data/Crop Cutting Experiments (CCEs) data through 
CCE-Agri App & uploading it on the NCIP, allowing insurance companies to 
witness the conduct of CCEs, integration of State land records with NCIP and 
usage of remote sensing based yield estimation through YES-TECH have already 
been taken to improve timely settlement of the claims to farmers.  
  
- Crop Loss Assessment App (CLAP), developed as a digital mobile application to 
streamline and improve the efficiency of crop loss assessments for loacalised 
calamities/post harvest losses for individual farms and  land parcels under PMFBY.  
The use of CLAP has been made mandatory for all the States/UTs under the 
scheme.  
 
- YES-TECH (Yield Estimation System Based on Technology) for gradual migration 
to Remote-Sensing based yield estimation to help assess yields as well as fair and 
accurate Crop Yield Estimation. This initiative has been launched for paddy & 
wheat crops from Kharif 2023 wherein 30% weightage to yield estimation will 
mandatorily be assigned to YES-TECH derived yield. Soybean crop has been 
added from Kharif 2024 season.   
 
(ii)  With a view to improve Grievance Redressal:  
- Provision of Stratified Grievance Redressal Mechanism viz. District Level Grievance 
Redressal Committee (DGRC), State Level Grievance Redressal Committee 
(SGRC) has been made in the Revised Operational Guidelines of the Scheme.   
    
- Krishi Rakshak Portal and Helpline (KRPH) has been developed.  A single Pan-
India toll free number 14447 has been deployed and linked to the insurance 
companies’ database, where farmers can raise their grievances/issues.  Timelines 
to resolve these grievances/issues have also been fixed.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF HOME AFFAIRS 
 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 2645 
 
TO BE ANSWERED ON THE 4TH AUGUST, 2026/ SHRAVANA 13, 1948 (SAKA) 
 
PROVISIONS IN BNS TO DEAL CRIMES  
 
2645 # SHRI DILIP SAIKIA: 
 
Will the Minister of HOME AFFAIRS be pleased to state: 
 
(a) whether any provisions have been made under the Bharatiya Nyaya 
Sanhita (B.N.S.) 2023 to deal with crimes against women and children in 
stringent manner; and  
 
(b) if so, the details thereof? 
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HOME AFFAIRS 
(SHRI BANDI SANJAY KUMAR) 
 
(a) & (b): The Government is committed to prevention and countering of the 
crime against women and children. In the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, 
for the first time, the provisions relat ing to crime against woman and child 
have been given precedence and placed under one Chapter. Strict 
punishments up to death sentence have been provided for the offences 
against women. Punishment for gang rape of a woman below the age of 18 
years is life imprisonment till remainder of the convict’s natural life or death. 
A new offence for having sexual intercourse on false promise of marriage, 
employment, promotion or by concealing identity, etc. has also been 
incorporated in Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023. Main provisions related to 
protection of women and children in the new sanhitas are given in Annexure. 

 
-2- 
L.S.US.Q.NO. 2645 FOR 04.08.2026 
Annexure 
 
PROVISIONS FOR PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN   
 
i. Offences against woman and child have been given  precedence over 
all other offences in a new chapter-V of Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023. 
 
ii. In Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, the age differential for minor victims of 
gang rape has been done away with. Earlier different punishments 
were prescribed for gang rape on a girl below the age of 16 years and 
12 years. This provision has been modified and now gang rape on a 
woman below the age of eighteen years is punishable with 
imprisonment of life or death. 
 
iii. Women have been recognized as an adult member of family who can 
receive summons on behalf of the person summoned. The earlier 
reference to ‘some adult male member’ has been replaced with ‘some 
adult member’. 
 
iv. In order to provide more protection to the victim and enforce 
transparency in investigation r elated to an offence of rape, the 
statement of the victim shall be recorded through audio video means 
by police. 

 
-3- 
L.S.US.Q.NO. 2645 FOR 04.08.2026 
 
v. For certain offences against woman, statement of the victim is to be 
recorded, as far as practicable, by  a woman Magistrate and in her 
absence a male Magistrate in the presence of a woman to ensure 
sensitivity and fairness, creating a supportive environment for victims. 
 
vi. Medical practitioners are mandated  to send the medical report of a 
victim of rape to the investigating officer within 7 days. 
 
vii. It is provided that no male person under the age of fifteen years or 
above the age of 60 years (65 years earlier) or a woman or a mentally 
or physically disabled p erson or a person with acute illness shall be 
required to attend at any place other than the place in which such male 
person or woman resides. In cases where such a person is willing to 
attend the police station, they may be allowed to do so. 
 
viii. The new laws provide for free first-aid or medical treatment to victims 
of crimes against women and children at all hospitals. This provision 
ensures immediate access to essential medical care, prioritizing the 
well-being and recovery of victims during challenging times. 
 
 

 
-4- 
L.S.US.Q.NO. 2645 FOR 04.08.2026 
 
ix. The act of hiring, employing or engaging a child to commit an offence, 
is made a punishable offence under section 95 of Bharatiya Nyaya 
Sanhita 2023, which entails punishment of imprisonment of minimum 
seven years, extendable to ten years. This provision aims to deter 
gangs or groups from employing/hiring children for committing offence.
