GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF HEAVY INDUSTRIES  
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 2648 
ANSWERED ON 04.08.2026 
 
HIGH-SPEED EV CHARGING INFRASTRUCTURE ON NATIONAL HIGHWAYS 
 
2648. DR. BACHHAV SHOBHA DINESH:  
 
Will the Minister of HEAVY INDUSTRIES be pleased to state:  
 
(a) whether the Government has finalized the locations for the 2,000 high -speed charging stations 
sanctioned for major national highways by February 2026, if so, the details thereof;  
 
(b) whether the Government is providing a 100% capital grant for the installation of these chargers 
in public-private partnership (PPP) mode, if so, the details thereof;  
 
(c) whether these charging stations are being equipped with "Open Charging Point Protocol" (OCPP) 
to ensure compatibility across all EV brands;  
 
(d) whether the Government is collaborating with the Govt of Power to ensure dedicated green-energy 
feeders for these high-speed charging hubs, if so, the details thereof; and  
 
(e) whether this infrastructure rollout led to a measurable increase in the sales of long -range electric 
heavy vehicles and passenger cars, if so, the details thereof? 
 
ANSWER 
THE MINISTER OF STATE FOR HEAVY INDUSTRIES 
(SHRI BHUPATHIRAJU SRINIVASA VARMA) 
 
(a): There is an allocation of Rs.2,000 crore under the PM E-DRIVE scheme for deployment of adequate 
number of EV public charging stations (EVPCS) on pan India basis including major national highways. There 
is no target number of charging stations for national highways.  
 
(b): Under the PM E -DRIVE Scheme, 100% capital grant is provided only for “Category A" 
locations, comprising Central Government and State Government premises, including government 
offices, government residential complexes, and Central Public Se ctor Enterprises (CPSEs), subject 
to unrestricted public access for EV charging. 
 
(c): To ensure broad compatibility across all electric vehicle brands, EV charging stations funded 
by the PM E-DRIVE scheme are equipped with the Open Charge Point Protocol (OCPP). 
 
(d): No such proposal is under consideration.  
 
(e): Yes. EV sales have shown a consistent upward trend during the period 2019 –20 to 2025–26, 
and overall EV penetration has increased from 0.68% in 2019–20 to 8.26% in FY 2025–26.  However, 
no assessment has been carried out by MHI to establish a direct causal relationship between the rollout 
of the charging infrastructure and the increase in sales of EVs.

(c)  the details regarding the current status and physical progress of ongoing 
projects under NICDP, along with their timelines for completion and reasons for 
delay, if any; 
 
(d)  the details regarding the infrastructure components developed under these 
projects, including industrial nodes, logistics hubs, transport connectivity and 
utilities, State-wise; and 
 
(e)  the measures taken by the Government to expedite implementation and ensure 
timely completion of National Industrial Corridor projects? 
 
ANSWER 
 
वाणिज्य  एवं उद्योग मंत्रालय में राज्य मंत्री (श्री णिणिन प्रसाद)   
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF COMMERCE & INDUSTRY 
(SHRI JITIN PRASADA) 
 
(a): Government of India has undertaken development of industrial townships under the 
National Industrial Corridor Development Programme (NICDP), through Special 
Purpose Vehicles formed jointly with the State Government. The project 
development activities inclu de identification of industrial nodes as per the 
prioritisation of the State government, followed by preparation and approval of 
concept master plan and development plan, environmental clearance and detailed 
design plan by the State government, prior to co nsideration of the project for 
approval. The State Government contribution is in the form of land and Govt of 
India’s contribution is in the form of equity and/or debt. 
Government of India has approved a total of 20 industrial nodes under NICDP. Out 
of these, 12 projects were approved during the last 5 years. The State wise details 
of these projects is at Annexure I. 
 

 
(b): Department for Promotion of Industry and Interna l Trade (DPIIT) has sanctioned 
and released funds amounting to Rs.16,172.95 Crore to National Industrial Corridor 
Development and Implementation Trust (NICDIT) for development of Industrial 
Corridor Projects. NICDIT has further released funds to the extent of Rs.14,569.97 
Crore to the project SPVs to carry out project development for various industrial 
nodes/projects under NICDP. 
Details regarding the funds released to the project SPVs by NICDIT for the 
approved projects, State and project-wise is at Annexure II. 
(c): Out of the 20 projects approved under NICDP, four projects have been completed. 
The current status of ongoing projects (16 no.) under NICDP is at Annexure III. The 
total construction timeline for project completion is 36 -48 months from the actu al 
date of appointment of EPC contractor. 
(d): The internal trunk infrastructure, including roads, water supply, sewerage and 
power distribution within the industrial city/node, are executed through EPC

be pleased to state : 
 
(a) whether  the Government proposes to set up any special cluster or Mega Textile Park in 
Bhagalpur city of Bihar to promote the silk (Tussar silk) and handloom industry and if so, the 
details thereof;  
(b) the details of the funds allocated for this purpose;  
(c) th e details of efforts being made by the Government to connect the local weavers of 
Bhagalpur with the global market and to onboard them onto e-commerce platforms; and  
(d) the details of the financial assistance provided to the weavers of Bhagalpur under the 'Mudra 
Yojana' or other textile schemes, year-wise during the last three years? 
 
उत्तर 
ANSWER 
वस्त्र राज् य मंत्री (श्री पबित्र मार्घेररटा) 
THE MINISTER OF STATE FOR TEXTILES  
 (SHRI PABITRA MARGHERITA) 
 
(a) & (b):           The Ministry of Textiles is implementing National Handloom Development 
Programme (NHDP) all across the country for holistic development of handloom sector. Under 
Mega Clus ter Development Programme and Need based Special Infrastructure Projects, both 
components of NHDP, need based financial assistance upto Rs. 30.00 Crore (GoI) and Rs. 12.00 
Crore (GoI) respectively is provided for various interventions like upgraded looms &  
accessories, solar lighting units, worksheds, design & product development, development of pre -
loom, on-loom and post -loom facilities, promotion of natural/vegetable dyes, setting up of Dye 
house etc. on receipt of complete proposals from State Governments/UT/IA.” 
  
                However, under erstwhile Comprehensive Handloom Cluster Development Scheme 
(CHCDS), now subsumed and renamed as Mega Cluster Development Programme as one of 
component of NHDP (since 20.10.2021) 01 Mega Handloom Cluster at Bhagalpur (Bihar) was 
sanctioned during FY 2014 -15. The sanctioned interventions under the project included the 
establishment of 01 Dye House, 01 Design Studio & Product Development Centre, and 10 
Block-Level Clusters. The total amount of Rs. 5.28 crore was released for imp lementation of the 
project.  
  
  In addition, in the Union Budget 2026 –27, the Government has announced setting up of

The scheme is currently in its initial for mulation phase. Once the scheme guidelines and 
modalities are formulized, proposals from all states including Bihar will be invited.

2652.  Dr. Sambit Patra: 
Smt. Delkar Kalaben Mohanbhai: 
Dr. Shivaji Bandappa Kalge: 
  
Will the Minister of COOPERATION (सहकारिता मंत्री) be pleased to state: 
(a) the number of different crop seed varieties introduced in the market by the BBSSL for 
distribution in the country so far; 
(b) the manner in which the BBSSL proposes to distribute its seeds; 
(c) whether the BBSSL has established zonal or regional offices across the country for the 
effective implementation of its seed distribution programme; 
(d) if so, the details thereof in respect of Maharashtra and Dadar & Nagar Haveli; 
(e) whether the BBSSL also provides services such as seed selection, fertiliser advisory and

THE MINISTER OF COOPERATION 
सहकारिता मंत्री (SHRI AMIT SHAH) 
 
(a) Bhartiya Beej Sahakari Samiti Limited (BBSSL) has so far introduced seeds of 18 crops 
and 124 varieties in the market under the ‘Bharat Beej’ brand for distribution across the 
country.  
(b) BBSSL distributes its seeds through its nationwide network of member cooperative 
societies, private distributors and dealers, as well as through State Seed Federations and Seed 
Corporations under various government schemes. 
(c), (d) & (f) No, Sir. For the effective implementation of its seed distribution programme, 
BBSSL has designated region -wise Zonal Managers and Coordinators, including officials

responsible for Maharashtra and Dadra and Nagar Haveli, at its Head Office. In Maharashtra, 
seeds of fodder crops, cotton, sorghum and groundnut have been supplied by BBSSL through

distribution channels. In Dadra and Nagar Haveli, the Department of Agriculture has been 
designated as BBSSL’s Nodal Agency for coordinating seed distribution and related activities. 
(e) No, Sir. The BBSSL has been set up to act as an apex organization for production, 
procurement, processing, branding, labelling, packaging, storage, marketing and distribution 
of quality seeds; strategic research & development; and to develop a system f or preservation 
and promotion of indigenous natural seeds.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA  
MINISTRY OF AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE  
DEPARTMENT OF AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE  
 
LOK SABHA  
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 2653 
TO BE ANSWERED ON THE 04TH AUGUST, 2026  
 
SUGARCANE CULTIVATION 
 
2653. SHRI MADDILA GURUMOORTHY: 
 
Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE क ृ िष एवं िकसान कʞाण 
मंũी be pleased to state: 
 
(a) whether the Government has taken cognizance of the continuous decline in 
sugarcane cultivation in Tirupati district; 
(b) the district-wise area, production and productivity of sugarcane during the last five 
years, in State of Andhra Pradesh; 
(c) whether the Government has assessed the reasons for the decline, including 
inadequate irrigation, rising cultivation costs, delayed payments and labour shortages;  
(d) whether any special assistance is proposed for revival through improved varieties, 
mechanization, micro-irrigation and strengthening sugar mills; and  
(e) if so, the details thereof? 
 
ANSWER 
MINISTER OF STATE FOR AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE   
क ृ िष एवं िकसान कʞाण राǛ मंũी (SHRI RAMNATH THAKUR) 
 
 
(a) to (e): The district-wise area, production and productivity of sugarcane during the last 
five years, in the State of Andhra Pradesh, including Tirupati district, is given at Annexure. 
The Government of India is implementing various schemes for enhancing sugarcane 
production and revival through improved varieties, mechanization, micro-irrigation and 
strengthening sugar mills. The details of some major schemes are given below: 
 
 The Indian Council of Agricultural Research (ICAR) is developing high-yielding 
varieties of sugarcane for the state of Andhra Pradesh. ICAR-Sugarcane Breeding 
Institute (SBI) has recently identified an early maturing, high-yielding, and red-rot and 
smut resistant variety Co09004, which is ready for release. 
 
 The sugarcane development programme is being implemented under National Food 
Security and Nutrition Mission (NFSNM) (erstwhile NFSM) in 13 major sugarcane growing 
states, including Andhra Pradesh, from 2014-15 to enhance production and productivity 
of sugarcane wherein thrust has been given on transfer of technology through 
demonstrations and training in order to extend benefits to the farmers. 
 
 The Sub Mission on Agricultural Mechanization (SMAM) is being implemented w.e.f 
2014-15 through States/UTs Governments, including Andhra Pradesh, which involves the 
use of machinery and technology to carry out tasks that were traditionally performed 
manually. Key components of the crop production system including sugarcane—such as 
land preparation, sowing, irrigation, harvesting, and post-harvest operations—are now 
executed using   appropriate machines. This not only enhances operational efficiency but 
also significantly reduces the demand for manual labour. SMAM is now being 
implemented under the umbrella of the Centrally Sponsored Scheme of Rashtriya Krishi 
Vikas Yojana (RKVY). The scheme aims at 'reaching the unreached' by bringing the small 
and marginal farmers at the core, including women farmers, and giving the benefits of 
farm mechanization, by Promoting 'Custom Hiring Centers', creating hubs for hi-tech & 

high-value farm equipments, distribution of various agricultural equipments, creating 
awareness among stakeholders through demonstration and capacity building activities. 
Under this scheme, during the period from 2014-15 to 2026-27 (as on date), the central 
funds amounting to Rs. 955.28 Crores have been released to the State of Andhra 
Pradesh and 299815 number of machines have been distributed on subsidy to individual 
farmers, 7108 CHCs, 62 Hi-tech Hubs & 3428 FMBs have been established. 
 
 Per Drop More Crop )PDMC(, a Centrally Sponsored Scheme )CSS (is being 
implemented in the Country, including Andhra Pradesh, from the year 2015-16 .The 
PDMC Scheme focuses on enhancing water-use efficiency at farm-level through Micro 
Irrigation technologies; namely, Drip and Sprinkler irrigation systems .Micro Irrigation 
helps in water-saving as well as reduced fertilizer usage, labour expenses, other input 
costs and overall income enhancement of farmers .The Scheme emphasises to promote 
micro irrigation in water intensive/consuming crops, including sugarcane, to optimize 
water requirement. Under the PDMC Scheme, financial assistance is provided to farmers 
for installation of micro irrigation systems @ 55 %and 45 %of the unit cost to small & 
marginal farmers and other farmers, respectively .From 2015-16 to 2026-27 )so far(, an 
area of 11.75 lakh hectares has been covered under Micro Irrigation in the State of 
Andhra Pradesh under PDMC Scheme with total release of Central Assistance being Rs .
3424.35 crores  . 
 
 To encourage the farmers for cultivation of sugarcane, Fair and Remunerative 
Price (FRP) of sugarcane is fixed for every sugar season, based upon the 
recommendations of the Commission for Agricultural Costs and Prices (CACP) in 
consultation with all stake holders having regard to various factors. The FRP so fixed by 
the Central Government is the benchmark remunerative price, below which no sugar mill 
can purchase cane from the cane growers.  
 
Sugarcane is procured by the sugar mills at the FRP fixed by the Central 
Government. Power of Sugarcane (Control) Order, 1966 to regulate distribution and 
movement of sugarcane has been delegated to the State Governments. As per the 
provision of Sugarcane (Control) Order, 1966, the State Government may reserve area 
where sugarcane is grown for a sugar factory and direct a sugarcane grower or a 
sugarcane growers’ co-operative society, supplying sugarcane to a factory, and the 
factory concerned to enter into an agreement to supply or purchase, as the case may be, 
the quantity of sugarcane so fixed. 
 
To maintain uninterrupted crushing operations, sugar mills plan their daily crushing 
requirements in advance and coordinate with the farmers to ensure timely harvest and 
supply of sugarcane. 
 
Further, National Cooperative Development Corporation (NCDC), under the Ministry 
of Cooperation provides financial assistance for the revival and modernization of 
cooperative sugar mills. NCDC implemented “Grant in Aid to NCDC for strengthening of 
Cooperative Sugar Mills” from 2023-24 to 2024-25, under which ₹10005.00 Cr loans were 
provided to Cooperative sugar mills.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA

DEPARTMENT OF ANIMAL HUSBANDRY AND DAIRYING 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 2654 
ANSWERED ON 4TH AUGUST, 2026 
 
IMPLEMENTATION OF NLM-EDP 
2654. SHRI MOHMAD HANEEFA: 
Will the Minister of FISHERIES, ANIMAL HUSBANDRY AND DAIRYING 
मत्स्यपालन, पशुपालन और डेयरी मंत्री 
be pleased to state: 
 
(a) whether any projects have been sanctioned under the National Livestock Mission –Entrepreneurship 
Development Programme (NLM-EDP) in the Union Territory of Ladakh since the launch of the scheme; 
(b) the number of applications received from Ladakh, the number approved, rejected and pending, along 
with the amount of subsidy sought and sanctioned, year-wise; 
(c) the reasons for the poor implementation of the scheme in Ladakh despite a large section of  the 
population depending on livestock and allied activities for their livelihood, and whether the Government 
has conducted any assessment or enquiry to identify the factors responsible for the  low uptake of the 
scheme in the UT; and 
(d) whether the Government has any proposals to take any special measures to improve implementation 
of the scheme and promote poultry -based entrepreneurship and employment generation in Ladakh and 
if so, the details thereof? 
ANSWER 
THE MINISTER OF FISHERIES, ANIMAL HUSBANDRY AND DAIRYING  
                                                    (SHRI RAJIV RANJAN SINGH ALIAS LALAN SINGH)  
(a) and (b) A total of ten projects has been received in the National Livestock Mission – Entrepreneurship 
Development (NLM-EDP) Portal with a proposed subsidy of ₹1.30 crore for the Union Territory (UT) 
of Ladakh. None of the above projects have been recommended by the Union Territory Level Executive 
Committee. The approval of this committee is mandatory for consideration of these projects by the 
Project Approval Committee, Department of Animal Husbandry and Dairying (DAHD), Government of 
India. Hence, no project was approved by the DAHD, Government of India. 
(c) and (d) The National Livestock Mission (NLM) is a credit-linked demand driven scheme. The 
Department of Animal Husbandry and Dairying continuously interact with the Government officials and 
bankers to create awareness among the entrepreneurs and farmers.  The DAHD has requested the UT 
Administration to conduct awareness campaigns and provide necessary handholding support to promote 
livestock-based entrepreneurship, including poultry activities, under th is scheme. Further, the 
implementation of the scheme is regularly monitored through Regional Review Meetings, Project

2656.  Shri Jashubhai Bhilubhai Rathva:  
Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE कृिष एवं िकसान कÐयाण मंýी 
be pleased to state: 
(a) whether the Government has evaluated the progress achieved in 2025 under the Pradhan 
Mantri Dhan-Dhaanya Krishi Yojana (PMDDKY); 
(b) if so, the details thereof including the number of Agri Aspirational Districts covered, 
convergence achieved across Ministries and measurable impact on farmers’ incomes, 
productivity and crop diversification; 
(c) whether the Government has assessed the challenges faced in implementation, such as gaps 
in adoption of modern farming techniques, access to credit or market linkages, if so, the details 
thereof; 
(d) whether the Government has any plans to expand the scheme or introduce new interventions 
under the PMDDKY to further enhance farmers’ incomes, crop diversification, and climate-
resilient agriculture; and 
(e) if so, the details thereof? 
ANSWER 
MINISTER OF STATE FOR AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE 
कृिष एवं िकसान कÐयाण राºय मंýी (SHRI RAMNATH THAKUR) 
(a) & (b): The Union Cabinet approved Prime Minister Dhan Dhaanya Krishi Yojana (DDKY) 
on 16th July, 2025 to cover 100 districts and the scheme was formally launched on 11th October, 
2025.  
As DDKY is in 1st year of implementation, it is too early for an assessment on measurable 
impact on farmers’ incomes, productivity and crop diversification. However, to track progress 
of the scheme in each district, the scheme Dashboard captures Key Performance Indicators 
(KPIs) on monthly basis. Progress of DDKY Districts on all Indicators is available on the 
Dashboard (https://pmddky.niti.gov.in/). 

(c): District Action Plan (DAP) of DDKY districts are formulated by the District Dhan Dhaanya 
Krishi Yojana Samiti. On the basis of gap analysis, the plans are made in convergence of 36 
Central Schemes of 11 Departments, state schemes and private sector participation. While 
preparing DAPs, the factors such as soil fertility, rainfall & irrigation, mechanization, suitability 
of agro-ecological conditions for crop diversification, seed replacement rate, credit penetration, 
storage gap etc., have been taken into account by the DDKY Samiti. 
The DAPs have been reviewed by NITI Aayog and Central Ministries/Departments including 
Department of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare. The feedback for the same was provided to the 
DDKY districts, who have accordingly incorporated the same. 
(d) & (e): No further plan to expand the scheme, as the DDKY comprehensively covers the 
challenges faced by the farmers such as crop diversification, climate resilient agriculture etc 
through convergence of 36 schemes of 11 Departments, state schemes and private sector 
participation.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE 
DEPARTMENT OF AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE

 UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 2657 
TO BE ANSWERED ON THE 04TH AUGUST, 2026 
 
CHALLENGES IN TRADITIONAL FARMING 
 
2657.  SHRI EATALA RAJENDER: 
 
Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE कृ ͪष एवं ͩकसान कãयाण मंğी 
be pleased to state: 
 
(a)  whether the Bio-technology addresses challenges in traditional farming by enhancing 
crop resilience, improving yields and fostering sustainability through tools like genetically 
modified (GM) crops, bio-fertilizers and molecular breeding and these innovations help 
combat climate change, reduce reliance on synthetic pesticides and improve nutrient 
absorption; 
(b)  if so, the details of the steps taken and results yielded in this regard; 
(c)  whether the Bio-technology offers green growth prospects in agriculture industry and 
if so, the details thereof and views of experts in this regard; and 
(d)  whether it is also a fact that given the population growth and climate change, there 
are challenges to traditional farming practices and food security, which can be addressed 
with the application of biotechnology; and 
(e)  if so, the details of the steps taken and foreign assistance received, funds sanctioned 
and utilised therefor?  
ANSWER 
MINISTER OF STATE FOR AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE  
कृ ͪष एवं ͩकसान कãयाण राÏय मंğी (SHRI  RAMNATH THAKUR) 
 
(a) to (e): As reported by the Indian Council of Agricultural Research (ICAR), several 
research, development and capacity-building initiatives have been undertaken to harness 
biotechnology for enhancing agricultural productivity, resilience and sustainability. These 
initiatives include research on molecular breeding, genomics, marker-assisted selection, 
genome editing, molecular diagnostics and genetic resource characterization through ICAR 

Institutes, All India Coordinated Research Projects (AICRPs), All India Network Projects 
(AINPs) and Consortia Research Platform Projects (CRPs). The major outcomes of these 
initiatives include development and dissemination of bio-fertilizers such as Rhizobium, 
Azotobacter, Azospirillum, phosphate-solubilizing and potash-mobilizing microorganisms for 
improving nutrient-use efficiency and soil health. Further, microbial biopesticides and bio-
control agents such as Trichoderma, Pseudomonas fluorescens, Bacillus thuringiensis (Bt), 
Beauveria bassiana, Metarhizium anisopliae and nucleopolyhedrovirus (NPV) have been 
developed for eco-friendly pest management. Further, genome editing research has been 
initiated by ICAR in 24 field crops and 17 horticultural crops covering 41 crops across 34 
research institutions. The Government of India has allocated ₹500 crore for genome editing 
research at ICAR in March 2024. Two genome-edited rice varieties, namely DRR Dhan 100 
(Kamala) and Pusa DST Rice 1, have been developed by ICAR. 
Bio-technology offers significant green growth prospects by enabling sustainable 
intensification of agriculture. It facilitates the development of climate-resilient crops and 
improves resource-use efficiency. It also helps in reducing dependence on synthetic 
agrochemicals and promotes environmentally sustainable farming practices. These 
technologies, when integrated with conventional breeding, good agronomic practices and 
appropriate biosafety and regulatory frameworks, are expected to contribute towards 
enhanced productivity, conservation of natural resources, environmental sustainability, 
improvement in farmers’ income and long-term food and nutritional security.  
As reported by ICAR, to address the challenges posed by increasing population, 
climate change and declining natural resources, biotechnology, along with conventional 
breeding and improved crop management practices, provides opportunities for sustainable 
agricultural development. It enables the development of high-yielding and climate-resilient 
crop varieties. It also helps in improving nutrient and water-use efficiency and strengthening 
pest and disease management. Further, it promotes the use of bio-fertilizers and bio-control 
agents for sustainable agricultural production.

2658.  SHRI ESWARASAMY K: 
           SHRI K GOPINATH: 
 
Will the Minister of FISHERIES, ANIMAL HUSBANDRY AND DAIRYING  
मत्स्यपालन, पशुपालन और डेयरी मंत्री 
be pleased to state: 
 
 (a) the total amount of subsidy sanctioned and disbursed under the National Livestock Mission - 
Entrepreneurship Development Programme (NLM-EDP) during the last five years, State/UT-wise; 
(b) whether there are instances where approved beneficiaries under the said programme are yet to 
receive subsequent instalments of subsidy after release of the initial instalment, and if so, the 
details thereof along with the reasons for delay; 
(c) whether the Government is aware that out of 3,843 approved projects under the NLM - EDP, 
only 2,014 projects have received the first instalment of subsidy and merely 706 projects have 
received the second instalment, if so, the details thereof and if not , the reasons for the delay in 
release of the remaining instalments of subsidy to the eligible beneficiaries; 
(d) the mechanism in place to ensure timely verification, fund release and monitoring of projects 
sanctioned under NLM-EDP; 
(e) the number of farmers/entrepreneurs trained and the number of institutions, hatcheries, 
breeding farms or other infrastructure units established under the Mission during the last five years, 
State/UT-wise; and 
(f) the details of the National Livestock Mission including skill development and capacity 
building? 
ANSWER 
THE MINISTER OF FISHERIES, ANIMAL HUSBANDRY AND DAIRYING  
                                                    (SHRI RAJIV RANJAN SINGH ALIAS LALAN SINGH)  
 
(a) to (c) The total amount of subsidy sanctioned and disbursed under the National Livestock 
Mission-Entrepreneurship Development Programme (NLM -EDP) during the last five years, 
State/UT-wise is at Annexure I. 
 
 

Since inception 4291 projects have been approved. 2908 applicants  have received the first 
installment of subsidy to the tune of ₹478.67 Cr. till date, and 1364 projects have been completed 
for which ₹221.02 Cr of second Instalment subsidy has been released. The remaining 1544 projects 
are yet to receive the second instalment of subsidy  as these applicants have not completed the 
projects. Completion of projects is precondition for release of second installment subsidy. 
(d) The Department of Animal Husbandry and Dairying, Government of India regularly reviews 
the implementation of the Entrepreneurship Development Programme (EDP) through Project 
Approval Committee (PAC) meetings to monitor the pendency of applications for completion of 
projects. Regional Review Meetings  are also held at the level of higher officials wherein the 
monitoring of implementation and performance of the scheme is also undertaken. Field inspections 
by National Level Monitors and Departmental Officers from the Department of Animal Husbandry 
of State and Center are also in place to verify the projects. The Central Level Bankers Committee 
(CLBC) has been established in the Department of Animal Husbandry and Dairying, Government 
of India to coordinate with all the lending institution and to review the progress of implementation 
of the programme. 
(e) and (f) The re-aligned National Livestock Mission (NLM), launched in the year 2021-22. The 
scheme focuses on employment generation, entrepreneurship development and enhancing per -
animal productivity, thereby targeting increased production of meat, goat milk, eggs,  and wool. 
The scheme was further modified on 21st February 2024, adding the breed-upgradation of camels, 
horses, and donkeys, along with initiatives for fodder production utilizing wasteland, rangeland 
and degraded forest land.The scheme has following three Sub-Missions: 
(i) Sub-mission on Breed Development of Livestock and Poultry: The Sub-mission envisages 
entrepreneurship development for poultry, sheep, goat , pig, camel, horse and donkey . It also 
supports State Governments in establishing infrastructure for genetic improvement of sheep, goat, 
pig, camel, horse and donkey. 
(ii) Sub-mission on Feed and Fodder Development: This Sub-Mission focuses on enhancing 
production of quality fodder seed (breeder, foundation and certified) and its supply chain to ensure 
the availability of  quality breeder, foundation and certified  fodder seeds essential for fodder 
production. It also promotes entrepreneurship by supporting the establishment of Fodder Block, 
Hay Baling and Silage Making Units . Further, assistance is provided to the State and Union 
Territory Governments for fodder production in forest and non-forest and degraded land. 
(iii) Sub-mission on Innovation and Extension: This Sub-Mission assists institutes, universities 
and organizations engaged in research and development related to sheep, goats, pigs and the feed 
and fodder sector. It also supports extension activities , training and capacity building through , 
livestock insurance through various State and Union Territory Government.  
Under the National Livestock Mission – Entrepreneurship Development Programme (NLM-EDP) 
a total of 4,291 projects have been approved. These include 3,169 Sheep & Goat projects, 568 
Piggery projects, 339 Rural Poultry projects, 204 Feed and Fodder projects, 3 Fodder Seed  
Production projects, 6 Horse breeding projects, and one project each for Donkey and Camel 
breeding. State and Union Territory -wise list is at Annexure II 

Further, five regional semen stations for sheep and goat have been approved  in the State of West 
Bengal, Andhra Pradesh, Jammu and Kashmir, Assam and Rajasthan.  Six goat semen banks for 
goat have also been approved  for the State of Jammu and Kashmir , Meghalaya, West Bengal, 
Assam, Himachal Pradesh and  Rajasthan. In addition, 6,405 cattle and buffalo Artificial 
Insemination (AI) centers have been upgraded to provide AI services for goat in the State of Jammu 
and Kashmir, Chhattisgarh, West Bengal, Rajasthan, Himachal Pradesh and Meghalaya.  Further, 
nine pig semen collection and processing laboratories have been approved in the State of Sikkim, 
Meghalaya, Arunachal Pradesh, Manipur, Mizoram, Assam and Tamil Nadu. 
As regard to capacity building and skill development, 1,42,144 farmers have been trained under 
the National Livestock Mission during the last five years, from 2021–22 to 2025–26.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF FISHERIES, ANIMAL HUSBANDRY AND DAIRYING 
DEPARTMENT OF ANIMAL HUSBANDRY AND DAIRYING 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 2661     
ANSWERED ON 4TH AUGUST, 2026 
 
ILLEGAL TRADE AND CRUELTY TO BIRDS AND ANIMALS 
 
2661. MS SAYANI GHOSH: 
 
Will the Minister of FISHERIES, ANIMAL HUSBANDRY AND DAIRYING  
मत्स्यपालन, पशुपालन और डेयरी मंत्री 
be pleased to state: 
 
(a) whether the Government has taken note of the illegal sale, transport and caging of birds and 
other animals in open markets across the country, if so, the details thereof; 
 
(b) the number of inspections conducted, cases registered, prosecutions launched and convictions 
secured during the last five years, State-wise; 
 
(c) whether the Government has reviewed the adequacy of penalties under the existing laws, if 
so, the details thereof;  
 
(d) the measures taken by the Gov ernment in coordination with  State Governments to curb 
illegal wildlife and birds trade; and 
 
(e) whether any proposal i s under consideration of the Government to strengthen enforcement, 
surveillance and public awareness regarding animal cruelty? 
 
ANSWER 
THE MINISTER OF FISHERIES, ANIMAL HUSBANDRY AND DAIRYING 
SHRI RAJIV RANJAN SINGH ALIAS LALAN SINGH)  
(a) to (e) The Central Government has notified the Prevention of Cruelty to Animals (Pet Shop) 
Rules, 2018, the Prevention of Cruelty to Animals (Dog Breeding and Marketing) Rules, 2017, 
the Prevention of Cruelty to Animals (Regulation of Livestock Markets) Rules, 20 17, the 
Transport of Animals Rules, 1978 (as amended), and the Prevention of Cruelty to Animals (Egg 
Laying Hens) Rules, 2023, which prescribe welfare standards for the housing, sale, transport and 
handling of different categories of animals. Further, The Wild Life (Protection) Act, 1972  is 
enacted to provide protection of wild animals, birds and plants. Species specified in Schedules I 
and II of the Act are accorded a high degree of protection against hunting and other prohibited 
activities. Matters relating to illegal trade in wild animals and protected birds are dealt with under 
the provisions of the Wild Life (Protection) Act, 1972. 
The implementation and enforcement of the Prevention of Cruelty to Animals Act, 1960 and the 
above rules framed thereunder, as well as the Wild Life (Protection) Act, 1972, are primarily the 
responsibility of the respective State Governments/Union Territor y Administrations through 
their designated enforcement agencies. Accordingly, information relating to inspections 
conducted, cases registered, prosecutions launched and convictions secured in respect of illegal 
sale, transport and caging of birds and other  animals is maintained by the respective State 

Governments/Union Territory Administrations and the concerned enforcement agencies and is 
not maintained centrally by the Department of Animal Husbandry and Dairying. 
The Government of India has reviewed the existing penalties under  Prevention of Cruelty to 
Animals Act, 1960 which is very low and not having deterrent effect. 
As per the information received from Ministry of Environment, Forest & Climate Change 
(MoEF&CC), the important steps taken for protection and conservation of species include: 
a) The Wild Life (Protection) Act, 1972 provides for punishment for violation of its 
provisions. The Act also provides for forfeiture of any equipment, vehicle or weapon that 
is used for committing wildlife offence. 
 
b) A network of Protected Areas have been created in the country for protection of wildlife, 
including birds and their habitat. 
 
c) Financial assistance is provided to State Governments /UT Administrations for 
management of wildlife and development of its habitat under the Centrally sponsored 
schemes ‘Development of Wildlife Habitats’  and ‘Project Tiger & Elephant’  of 
MoEF&CC.  
 
d) A specific component of ‘Recovery programme for saving critically endangered species 
and habitats’ is provided under the Centrally Sponsored Scheme namely ‘Development 
of Wildlife Habitats’ of the MoEF&CC for focused conservation action on identified 25 
critically endangered species.  
 
e) Eco Development activities are undertaken by the States Governments /  UT 
administrations involving local communities in wildlife conservation.  
 
f) The Wildlife Crime Control Bureau (WCCB) has been set up under MoEF&CC to ensure 
co-ordination among various agencies and State Governments to combat organized 
wildlife crime. 
 
g) Advisories an d alerts are issued to State and Central agencies by the W CCB for  
preventive action on poaching and illegal wildlife trade.  
 
h) The law enforcement agencies like Border Security Force, Central Industrial Security 
Force, etc who assist in control of wildlife crime have been trained by the WCCB.  
 
i) India is a Party to Convention on International Trade in Endangered Species of wild fauna 
and flora (CITES), South Asian Wildlife Enforcement Network (SAWEN) and 
coordinates with international agencies in control of wildlife crime.  
 
j) Technology like c amera traps, drones, wireless, e -surveillance, etc. are used for 
monitoring of wild animals, detecting illegal intrusions, early warning system. 
 
Further, Department of Animal Husbandry and Dairying through Animal Welfare Board of India 
(AWBI) coordinates with the State Governments and State Animal Welfare Boards creates public 
awareness regarding animal cruelty through issuance of advisories. The Government of India 
also issues advisories to State Governments/UT Administrations for implementation of 
provisions of Acts and Rules.

Will the Minister of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare क ृ िष एवं िकसान कʞाण मंũी 
be pleased to state:  
(a) the details of the Pradhan Mantri Kisan Maan Dhan Yojana (PMKMDY) Scheme 
implemented by the Government across the country;  
(b) the total number of farmers benefitted under the said scheme in Maharashtra 
particularly in Latur, Ahilyanagar and Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar districts, Madhya 
Pradesh particularly in Khandwa district and Dadra and Nagar Haveli Parliamentary 
Constituency;  
(c) whether there are still many farmers in the rural and remote areas of the above

क ृ िष एवं िकसान कʞाण राǛ मंũी (SHRI RAMNATH THAKUR) 
 
(a):       Pradhan Mantri Kisan Maan Dhan Yojana (PM-KMY), a central sector scheme, 
is a voluntary and contributory pension scheme for the entry age group of 18 to 40 
years with a provision of minimum monthly assured pension of ₹3000/- on attaining the 
age of 60 years, subject to exclusion criteria. The Scheme aims to create a social 
security net for the small and marginal farmers, who own cultivable land upto 2 
hectares as per the land records of the concerned State/UT, during their old age. The 

amount of the monthly contribution ranges between ₹55 to ₹200 per month depending 
upon the entry age of the farmers into the Scheme. Govt. of India also provides 
matching contribution in the pension account of the farmers. The Life Insurance 
Corporation (LIC) of India is the fund manager for the Scheme. 
 
(b) to (d): Under PM-KMY, 80,981 farmers are enrolled from the State of 
Maharashtra including 1870 in Latur district, 2595 in Ahilyanagar district, and 2609 in 
Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar district. Further, 1,19,459 farmers are enrolled from the 
State of Madhya Pradesh, including 846 in Khandwa district, and 289 farmers are 
registered from The Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu. 
 
Various steps are taken to expand the coverage of PM-KMY Scheme in the rural 
and remote areas of all States/UTs including Maharashtra, Madhya Pradesh, and The 
Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu. As per the guidelines of the Scheme, 
the Common Service Centers (CSCs) are nominated for the enrollments of the farmers 
under the Scheme and a dedicated portal for PM-KMY Scheme has been created by 
the CSC to ensure smooth operations under the Scheme.  CSCs mobilize farmers, 
disseminate information and create awareness about the Pradhan Mantri Kisan 
Maandhan Yojana (PMKMY), and facilitate enrolment of eligible farmers. Further, 
States/Union Territories are advised from time to time to undertake outreach activities 
for wider awareness of Government schemes and to maximize enrolment of eligible 
farmers under PMKMY.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF COMMERCE & INDUSTRY 
DEPARTMENT FOR PROMOTION OF INDUSTRY AND INTERNAL TRADE 
 
LOK SABHA 
 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 2664. 
           TO BE ANSWERED ON TUESDAY, THE 04TH AUGUST, 2026. 
 
DEVELOPMENT OF INDUSTRIAL INFRASTRUCTURE 
 
2664.  DR. KIRSAN NAMDEO: 
 
Will the Minister of COMMERCE AND INDUSTRY be pleased to state: 
वाणिज्य  एवं उद्योग मंत्री 
(a)  whether the Government has taken various steps to promote industrial growth, 
attract investments and enhance export competitiveness in the country, 
particularly in backward and aspirational districts; 
 
(b)  if so, the details of the schemes and initiatives being implemented by the 
Ministry of Commerce and Industry for development of industrial infrastructure, 
promotion of manufacturing and strengthening of supply chains; 
 
(c)  whether the Government has identified districts having potential for export -
oriented industries and provided assistance under schemes such as Districts 
as Export Hubs (DEH); 
 
(d)  if so, the details of funds allocated and utilised under such initiatives during the 
last three years, State-wise; and 
 
(e)  the steps being taken by the Government to encourage MSMEs, startups and 
local producers to access domestic as well as international markets? 
 
ANSWER 
 
वाणिज्य  एवं उद्योग मंत्रालय में राज्य मंत्री (श्री णिणिन प्रसाद)   
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF COMMERCE & INDUSTRY 
(SHRI JITIN PRASADA) 
 
(a) & (b): Government of India launched the ‘Make in India’ initiative on 25th  September 
2014 to facilitate Investment, foster Innovation, build best in class Infrastructure, 
and make India a hub for manufacturing, design, and innovation. Presently, 
Make in India 2.0 focuses on 27 sectors including 15 manuf acturing sectors, 
implemented across various Ministries and Departments and State 
Governments. The list of sectors under Make in India 2.0 is at Annexure I. 
As part of Make in India initiative, the Production Linked Incentive (PLI) 
schemes have been implemented across 14 key sectors, namely Large -Scale 
Electronics Manufacturing (LSEM), IT Hardware, Pharmaceuticals, Bulk Drugs, 
Medical Devices, Automobiles and Auto Components, Advanced Chemistry 
Cell Batteries,  Solar PV modules, Telecom & Networking Products , Food 

Processing, Textiles, Specialty Steel, White Goods, Drones & Drone 
Components by incentivizing incremental production and sales. The PLI 
schemes have facilitated fresh investments in the identified sectors and 
supported the expansion of manufacturing capacities. 
The impact of PLI Schemes has been significant across various sectors in India 
as these schemes have incentivized domestic manufacturing, leading to 
increased production, job creation and a boost in exports. As of 31st  
March 2026, 892 applications have been approved across 14 sectors of the 
PLI schemes and has resulted in actual investments of over ₹2.40 lakh crore, 
production/sales exceeding ₹22.66 lakh crore, employment generation of over 
14.15 lakh persons (direct and indirect) across the country. These outcomes 
indicate the contribution of the schemes towards expanding manufacturing 
capacity, increasing production, strengthening industrial ecosystems, and 
improving the competitiveness of participating sectors. In addition, sector 
specific schemes by various Central Government Ministries/ Departments and 
schemes by State Government also incentivise industrial growth and 
investments. 
NITI Aayog launched the Aspirational Districts Programme (ADP) in January 
2018, wherein, 117 districts were identified as Aspirational Districts. ADP 
monitors the progress of these Districts based on the delta ranking method, 
which rewards Districts for their quarterly progress in the 49 Key Performance 
Indicators (KPIs) across sectors such as health & nutrition, education, 
agriculture & water resources, financial inclusion & skill development and basic 
infrastructure. The broad strategy of ADP rests on 3 Cs –Convergence 
(between Central and State Schemes), Collaboration (between Centre, State, 
District Administration, Development Partners and Citizens) and Competition 
(between Districts). 
The National Industrial Corridor Development Programme (NICDP) is driving  
India’s industrial transformation by developing 20 approved greenfield corridor 
projects and 306 operational plug -and-play industrial parks, with 20 more in 
progress. These projects, built in partnership with states and private players, 
aim to position India as a global manufacturing hub while fostering innovation, 
sustainability, and employment. AURIC in Maharashtra, one of India’s first 
Greenfield Industrial Smart Cities, exemplifies this vision with strong multimodal 
connectivity through highways, dry ports, airports, and railways, all aligned with 
PM GatiShakti to enhance logistics efficiency and competitiveness. 
Complementing NICDP, the Union Cabinet has launched the Bharat Audyogik 
Vikas Yojna (BHAVYA) with an outlay of ₹33,660 crore to establish 100 
worldclass industrial parks. Implemented by NICDC under DPIIT, BHAVYA will 
provide up to ₹1 crore per acre for parks spanning 100 –1000 acres, covering 
core infrastructure like roads, utilities, ICT systems, and value -added facilities 
such as factory sheds, labs, and warehousing, along with social amenities for 
workers. Following a challenge -based selection process and ensuring 
seamless connectivity under PM GatiShakti, BHAVYA aims to strengthen 

manufacturing, attract investments, generate large -scale employm ent, and 
promote sustainable, inclusive, globally competitive industrial growth. 
(c) & (d): The Government has taken measures to identify export potential and 
promote exports from the districts under this initiative. It includes identifying 
products and services with export potential in all districts of the country, in 
consultation with all stakeholders, including States/UTs. In order to facilitate 
grassroots export growth and resolve structural bottlenecks, the 
products/services (including GI products, agricultural clusters and toy clusters) 
with export potential in all districts of the country have been identified and 
institutional mechanism in the form of State Export Promotion Committees 
(SEPCs) at State/UT level and District Export Promotion Committees (DEPCs) 
at the district level has been created in all districts of the country to provide 
support for export promotion and address the bottlenecks for export growth in 
the Districts. 
The core operational mechanism of this initiative relies on the Distric t Export 
Action Plans (DEAPs), which are prepared and implemented by the DEPCs in 
collaboration with Central, State, and District stakeholders. These plans identify 
key products and services with export potential for each district, outline 
necessary interventions and identify support required by local industry from the 
production stage through to the exporting stage, detail specific supply chain 
bottlenecks and propose targeted mitigation strategies. 
As part of the DEH framework, export -potential products a nd services have 
been identified across 734 districts; SEPCs and DEPCs have been successfully 
constituted in all 36 States and Union Territories; and DEAPs have been 
prepared for 713 districts, out of which 249 have been formally deliberated and 
adopted by their respective DEPCs. 
With the advent of Foreign Trade Policy (FTP) 2023, the Directorate General of 
Foreign Trade (DGFT) has legitimized this cause through the inclusion of 
‘Districts as Export Hubs initiatives’ under Chapter 3 of FTP 2023. It aims to 
channelize the potential and diverse identity of each District of the country to 
make them Export Hubs. 
(e): The other major measures taken up under the “Make in India” initiative include 
National Single Window System, GIS enabled Land Bank, Foreign Direct  
Investment (FDI) policy reforms, PM Gati Shakti National Master Plan for 
integrated planning of multimodal infrastructure, Project Monitoring Group to 
remove bottlenecks in setting up of major infrastructure projects, setting up of 
industrial parks, interventions to improve ease of doing business, measures for 
reduction in comp liance burden, rationalization of labor laws, introduction of 
Goods and Services Tax, policy measures to boost domestic manufacturing 
through public procurement orders and Phased Manufacturing Programme 
(PMP). 
 

To support the development of Micro Small and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs), 
the Central Government supplements the eﬀorts of State/UT Governments 
through various  schemes, programmes and policy initiatives. This inter alia 
includes various schemes and programmes such as:- 
i. Prime Minister's Employment Gen eration Programme (PMEGP):  
PMEGP provides margin money subsidy up to 35%, for setting up of new 
micro enterprises, in the non -farm sector with project cost of ₹50 lakh for 
Manufacturing and ₹20 lakh for Service enterprises. 
ii. Credit Guarantee Scheme for Micro and Small Enterprises: The 
scheme is implemented through Credit Guarantee Fund Trust for Micro and 
Small Enterprises to provide credit guarantee for loans extended to MSEs. 
The ceiling for guarantee coverage under the scheme is ₹10 crore. 
iii. Self-Reliant India (SRI) Fund: The fund has been set up to infuse ₹50,000 
crore as equity funding in MSMEs with a provision of ₹10,000 crore from 
the Government of India and ₹40,000 crore through Private Equity/Venture 
Capital Funds. The Budget 2026 -27 has also annou nced a support of 
₹2000 crore to top up the Self-Reliant India Fund set up in 2021 to continue 
support to micro enterprises and maintain their access to risk capital. 
iv. Under the Digital India programme , the Ministry of Electronics and 
Information Technology (MeitY) oﬀers services on Digital Infrastructure as 
a Utility, Governance and Services on Demand, Digital Empowerment of 
Citizens and MSMEs. Digital payments are also done by MSMEs through 
different platforms. 
 
Startup India initiative was launched on 16 th January 2016, with an intent to 
build a strong  ecosystem for nurturing innovation, startups and encouraging 
investments in the startup ecosystem of the country. Under the Startup India 
initiative, the Government constantly undertakes various eﬀorts to su pport 
startups. The flagship Schemes namely, Fund of Funds for Startups (FFS), 
Startup India Seed Fund Scheme (SISFS) and Credit Guarantee Scheme for 
Startups (CGSS) support startups across sectors at various stages of their 
business cycle. 
FFS has been established with a corpus of ₹ 10,000 crore to catalyze venture 
capital investments and is operationalized by Small Industries Development 
Bank of India (SIDBI), which provides capital to Securities and Exchange Board 
of India (SEBI)  registered Alternative Investment Funds (AIFs) which in 
turn invest in startups. As on 30 th June 2026, supported AIFs under the 
Scheme have invested ₹ 27,902.70 crore in 1,460 selected startups. SISFS 
provides financial assistance to seed stage startups through incubators. SISFS 
is implemented from 1st April 2021. 
As on 30 th June 2026, selected incubators under the Scheme have approved 
funding of ₹ 706.33 crore to 4,245 startups. 
The Government is consistently working to boost exports and expand the 
country’s global footprint, com bining traditional strengths with emerging 
technology-driven sectors. Central to this ambition is the creation of a 
supportive ecosystem wherein, exporters, particularly MSMEs, can compete 
confidently in international markets. This eﬀort is reinforced by a dynamic policy 

framework, strong financial incentives, a growing digital infrastructure, 
improved trade facilitation, and a determined push to secure deeper market 
access through next-generation trade agreements. 
The RoDTEP scheme plays a central role by neutralizing embedded taxes on 
exports and enabling Indian goods to remain competitive worldwide. The 
recently launched Export Promotion Mission (EPM) further reinforces this eﬀort 
through two targeted pillars: expanding access to aﬀordable trade finance a nd 
upgrading quality, logistics, branding, and market -readiness across the export 
value chain. The Government has approved the EPM with a budgetary outlay 
of ₹ 25,060 crores (FY 2025–26 to FY 2030–31). It operates through Niryat 
Protsahan (focusing on trad e finance and credit enhancement)  and Niryat 
Disha (focusing on export logistics, warehousing, and market access), 
specifically targeting MSME competitiveness. 
India’s export strategy reflects a decisive whole -of-government approach, 
moving beyond transactional support to building a resilient, competitive, and 
future-ready ecosystem. By combining targeted financial incentives, 
technology-enabled trade facilitatio n, institutional reforms, and proactive 
market-access initiatives, the focus is on embedding digital governance, 
expanding global reach, and strengthening exporter capabilities across sectors 
and regions. This integrated approach positions India not just a s a participant, 
but as a trusted, technology-driven partner in global trade. 
Collectively, these initiatives are being implemented across all States and 
Union Territories to strengthen the regulatory ecosystem, facilitate investment, 
enhance competitiveness, and support sustained economic growth.

be pleased to state :

NMMS ATTENDANCE APP 
2666. Shri Sunil Bose: 
 
Will the Minister of RURAL DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state: 
 
(a)  the mechanism followed by the Government to assess the 
number of workers unable to register their attendance due to 
issues with the National Mobile Monitoring System (NMMS) 
attendance App; 
(b)  the details and total number of attendance discrepancies 
between the NMMS App and physical muster rolls since April 
2025 to till date, State-wise; 
(c)  the guidelines followed by the Government to ensure that no 
worker is denied wages due to issues with digital attendance 
recording on the NMMS App; and 
(d)  the details and total number of complaints filed regarding issues 
with the NMMS App alongwith the action taken thereon? 
 
ANSWER 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF RURAL DEVELOPMENT 
(SHRI KAMLESH PASWAN) 
  
(a) to (d): To ensure transparency and accountability in the 
implementation of Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment 
Guarantee Scheme (Mahatma Gandhi NREGS), it was decided that 
States/UTs shall ensure capturing of attendance at the worksite 
through National Mobile Monitoring System (NMMS) App with two-
time stamped, geo-tagged photographs of the workers in a day for all 
the works (except Individual Beneficiary Work) through NMMS w.e.f. 
1st January, 2023. A robust, face authentication based attendance 
capture mechanism using NMMS App has been adopted under Viksit 
Bharat- Guarantee for Rozgar and Ajivika Mission (Gramin) Act, which 
has come into force with effect from 01.07.2026.  
  
A comprehensive exemption mechanism has been put in place 
to ensure that no genuine worker faces difficulties due to technical 

Page 2 of 2 
 
issues in NMMS. Exemption mechanism ensures that in case of 
network connectivity issues at work site, attendance can be 
captured in offline mode, which can subsequently uploaded after 
moving into network connected area. Additionally exemptions are 
available in situations where the device or application is not 
functioning, eKYC of the workers has not been completed or the 
worker has a disability such as visual impairment. Any technical 
issues faced by States/UTs are taken up with the Ministry and are 
resolved on a real time basis. 
  
   The implementation of the NMMS application has significantly 
improved the attendance management system and the overall 
efficiency of the process. NMMS application also helps in timely 
payment of wages as wage lists and FTOs can be generated 
immediately after the closure of the muster roll. The States/UTs have 
clearly been advised to ensure that no eligible and willing workers be 
denied employment under above schemes due to any technical 
difficulties in NMMS.

2667. SHRI JAI PRAKASH: 
Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE कृ ͪष एवं ͩकसान कãयाण 
मंğी be pleased to state:  
(a)  whether the Government has undertaken any comprehensive review of the existing 
Minimum Support Price (MSP) system with regard to its coverage, effectiveness and 
regional disparities; 
(b)  the details of crops and States where procurement under MSP has remained 
significantly below production during the last three years, along with the reasons therefor; 
and 
(c)  the policy measures proposed to improve transparency, efficiency and timely 
payment under the MSP regime? 
 
ANSWER 
MINISTER OF STATE FOR AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE  
कृ ͪष एवं ͩकसान कãयाण राÏय मंğी  (SHRI RAMNATH THAKUR) 
(a) to (c):  Every year, Government fixes Minimum Support Prices (MSPs) for 22 
mandated agricultural crops for the country as a whole, based on the recommendations of 
the Commission for Agricultural Costs & Prices (CACP), after considering the views of the 
State Governments and Central Ministries/Departments concerned.  

The Union Budget for 2018-19 had announced the pre-determined principle to keep 
MSPs at levels of at least one and half times of the cost of production. Accordingly, 
Government had increased MSPs for all mandated Kharif, Rabi and other commercial crops 
with a minimum margin of 50 percent over all India weighted average cost of production 
from year 2018-19 onwards. 
Out of the total production, only marketable surplus is available for procurement by 
Government agencies when market price of these produce fall below the MSP. Government 
procures cereals and coarse cereals through Food Corporation of India (FCI) and other 
designated State Agencies to provide price support to the farmers. Procurement of pulses, 
oilseeds and copra is done under Price Support Scheme under umbrella scheme of 
Pradhan Mantri Annadata Aay Sanrakshan Abhiyan (PM-AASHA), on the request of the 
concerned State Government as per the guidelines as and when market price of these 
produce fall below the MSP. Procurement agencies under PM-AASHA Scheme are 
National Agricultural Cooperative Marketing Federation of India Ltd (NAFED) and National 
Co-operative Consumers' Federation of India Ltd. (NCCF). Cotton and Jute are also 
procured by Government at MSP through Cotton Corporation of India (CCI) and Jute 
Corporation of India (JCI), respectively. 
In addition, Adequate number of procurement centres are opened by respective 
State Government Agencies, taking into account the production, marketable surplus, 
convenience of farmers and availability of other logistics / infrastructure such as storage 
and transportation etc. Temporary purchase centres, in addition to the existing mandis and 
depots / godowns are also established at key points.  
The procurement operation is a continuously evolving process and during the last 
few years, procurement processes under MSP have improved to ensure payment of MSP 
to farmer’s bank account directly and linkage of Aadhaar and land records with the States’ 
procurement portals ensure that the farmers directly get the benefits of the MSP purchase.  
 National Institution for Transforming India (NITI) Aayog (erstwhile Planning 
Commission) has conducted a study entitled “Efficacy of minimum support prices on 
farmers”, 2016. The study covered 14 States, 36 Districts, 72 Blocks, 144 Villages and 
1440 Households. The study is based on both the primary and secondary data. The study 
has found among other things that MSP declared by the Government has encouraged 78 % 
of the farmers covered under the study for adopting improved methods of farming such as 

high yielding varieties of seeds, organic manure, chemical fertilizer, pesticides and 
improved methods of harvesting etc. 
Increased MSP has benefited farmers of the country which are evident from data of 
procurement and MSP amount paid to the farmers. The year wise details of procurement 
and MSP amount paid to farmers during 2023-24 to 2025-26 (upto June, 2026) are given as

Will the Minister of FISHERIES, ANIMAL HUSBANDRY AND DAIRYING be pleased to 
state: 
(a) the total amount of total funds released to West Bengal under Pradhan Mantri Matsya 
Sampada Yojana (PMMSY) since 2020 -21, year -wise, the number of utilisation certificates 
submitted, and the amount of Central funds lapsed or pending for utilisation and the reasons for 
pendency; 
 
(b) whether the West Bengal Government has submitted an Annual Action Plan for 2026 -27 
under PMMSY, constituted the State Level Approval Committee and appointed a Sta te Nodal 
Officer, and the funds provisionally allocated to West Bengal for the current financial year; 
 
(c) the targets set for West Bengal under PMMSY for 2026-27 covering pond aquaculture, cold 
chain infrastructure, motorisation of fishing boats, fisherm en insurance and PM -MKSSY 
formalisation district-wise; and 
 
(d) the steps being taken by the Ministry to assist the West Bengal Government in accelerating 
PMMSY implementation, particularly for Sundarbans fishermen, tiger widows and inland fish 
farmers across the State's 3.6 lakh hectares of water bodies?

THE MINISTER OF FISHERIES, ANIMAL HUSBANDRY AND DAIRYING 
(SHRI RAJIV RANJAN SINGH ALIAS LALAN SINGH) 
 
(a) The Department of Fisheries (DoF), Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and

(b) The PMMSY, originally approved for five years from 2020 -21 to 2024 -25, was

fishers, fish farmers, fish vendors, and other stakeholders in West Bengal have registered on

(d) The Department of Fisheries, Gov ernment of India, is extending technical and financial

livelihood enhancement of eligible beneficiaries such as marine and inland fishers, inland fish

various levels to monitor the progress of implementation of approved projects and the utilisation 
of Central funds.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF COMMERCE AND INDUSTRY 
DEPARTMENT OF COMMERCE 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 2669 
ANSWERED ON 04/08/2026  
  
REGULATORY FRAMEWORK FOR ORGANIC AGRICULTURAL PRODUCTS 
  
2669. SHRI PARSHOTTAMBHAI RUPALA: 
  
 Will the Minister of COMMERCE & INDUSTRY (वाणिज्य और उद्योग मंत्री) be 
pleased to state: 
 
 (a) whether the Government has examined the representation submitted by the 
 Governments of Australia and New Zealand regarding the regulation of the trade, 
 sale and import of organic agricultural products and the action taken thereon; 
(b) whether the Ministry, in coordination with FSSAI, the APEDA and other 
 concerned stakeholders, has reviewed the existing regulatory framework for 
 organic agricultural products; 
(c) whether the recommendations of the Parliamentary Committee for stringent 
 measures against counterfeit organic products have been considered; and 
(d) whether the Government proposes to strengthen the legal and regulatory 
 framework to curb counterfeit organic products and protect the credibility of 
 India's organic agricultural exports and domestic market and if so, the details 
 thereof? 
  
ANSWER 
  
वाणिज्य और उद्योग मंत्रालय में राज्य मंत्री (श्री णिणिन प्रसाद) 
 THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF COMMERCE AND INDUSTRY 
(SHRI JITIN PRASADA) 
 
(a) to (d) India’s export and import standard for Organic products is the National 
Programme for Organic Production (NPOP). India has a Mutual recognition 
Arrangement (MRA) on Organic standards with Australia, which is implemented with 
effect from 24.09.2025. With respect to New Zealand, an interim Mutual Recognition 
Arrangement (MRA) has been agreed, which shall come into effect, on the date of 
entry into force of the India-New Zealand FTA. 
  
The Government thr ough the Agricultural and Processed Food Products 
Development Authority(APEDA), which is the Secretariat for the NPOP, conducted 
detailed consultations with the key stakeholders including FSSAI for the revision of 
the NPOP Regulations, following which, the Eighth Edition of NPOP was notified on 
5th January 2025, which came into effect from 180 days from the issuance of this 
notification. 

2 
 
  
To strengthen the Organic legal and regulatory framework, so as to address non 
compliances including to curb counterfei t organic products and to protect the 
credibility of India's organic agricultural exports, stringent penalty provisions and 
sanctions have been introduced in the Eighth Edition of the NPOP, stipulating 
penalties for various forms of non -compliances by the certification bodies, certified 
operators etc. Penalty provisions have also been introduced against external service 
providers of Organic grower groups, as a further deterrent measure for various non-
compliances by them, including misrepresentation.  
  
Trade of organic products in the domestic market is covered under the Food Safety 
and Standards (Organic Food) Regulations, 2017 read with the Food Safety & 
Standards Act, 2006. The Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI), 
under the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, is the nodal agency for maintaining 
oversight over domestic organic trade, including enforcing compliance of standards, 
by the stakeholders.

COASTAL EROSION AND CLIMATE-RESILIENT FISHING VILLAGES 
 
2670.    SHRI SASIKANTH SENTHIL: 
             SHRI CAPTAIN BRIJESH CHOWTA: 
 
Will the Minister of FISHERIES, ANIMAL HUSBANDRY AND DAIRYING be pleased to state:  
 
(a) whether the Government has identified coastal fishing villages in Tamil Nadu under the Climate 
Resilient Coastal Fishermen Villages initiative, if so, the names of such villages and districts 
selected in Tamil Nadu; 
(b) the amount of funds allocated, released and utilised for Tamil Nadu under the said initiative; 
(c) whether coastal erosion and climate vulnerability mapping ha s been used for selection of 
villages in Tamil Nadu; 
(d) the livelihood, housing, safety and infrastructure support proposed for fisherfolk in such 
villages; and 
(e) whether the Government has reviewed support for deep -sea fishing transition mariculture and 
coastal pilots, if so, the details thereof and if not, the reasons therefor? 
 
ANSWER 
 
 THE MINISTER OF FISHERIES, ANIMAL HUSBANDRY AND DAIRYING: 
 
(SHRI RAJIV RANJAN SINGH ALIAS LALAN SINGH) 
 
(a) to (b): The Department of Fisheries, Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying, 
recognising the importance of strengthening coastal communities, has undertaken a transformative 
initiative under the Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana (PMMSY ) to develop 100 existing 
coastal fishermen villages, located close to the coastline across all coastal States and Union 
Territories, including Tamil Nadu, into Climate Resilient Coastal Fishermen Villages (CRCFVs). 
This initiative aims to upgrade these vi llages into economically vibrant and climate‑resilient 
fishermen villages. Under PMMSY, ₹200 crore has been earmarked for the development of 
CRCFVs, with a unit cost of ₹2 crore per village, with 100% funding by the Government of India. 
In Tamil Nadu, 16 coastal villages have been approved for development as CRCFVs at a total cost 
of ₹32 crore, and the first and second installments amounting to ₹16 crore have already been 
released to the State Government. The district‑wise details of the coastal villages identified in Tamil 
Nadu are furnished at Annexure‑I.  
 

(c) Villages for development as CRCFV across all coastal States/UTs, including Tamil Nadu, have 
been jointly identified with the respective State/UT Governments in accordance with the prescribed 
Guidelines. The selection of villages under CRCFV prioritized those situated on the seashore and 
close to the shoreline (0–5 km, then 0–10 km, then 0–20 km). Preference was given to villages with 
a higher proportion of fishermen (100%, then 90–100%, then 80–90%), greater numbers of fishing 
boats, fish landings, and allied fisheries activities. Alignment with the villages covered under the 
National Innovations in Climate Resilient Agriculture (NICRA) Scheme of ICAR was also 
considered wherever available. 
(d) The De partment of Fisheries, Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry & Dairying has 
approved the need -based activities proposed by the State Government in the DPR submitted for 
each village. The activities include infrastructure components like multipurpose halls, fish auction 
and processing units, drying yards, net‑mending sheds, storage rooms, RCC roads with street 
lighting, desalination plants and rest sheds. The livelihood and economic interventions include 
marine and brackish‑water cage culture, bivalve and crab fattening units, bio‑fertilizer production, 
artificial reefs, ice boxes, fishing‑implement shops and mobile fish‑food outlets, green‑fuel boats, 
life buoys, life jackets and towing equipment, collectively aimed at strengthening resilience, 
enhancing productivity and improving welfare across coastal fishing communities.  
(e) The Department of Fisheries, Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying has 
supported the transition from trawling to deep-sea fishing and towards mariculture to promote 
sustainable fishing practices under the Blue Revolution and PMMSY schemes. The Government of 
Tamil Nadu has reported that, under the Blue Revolution Scheme (2017 –18), the State undertook 
the “Diversification of trawl fishing boats from Palk Bay into deep‑s ea fishing boats”. Approval 
was accorded for replacing 750 trawlers with deep‑sea fishing vessels at a unit cost of ₹80 lakh, 
with a financial support comprising 50% central subsidy, 20% State subsidy, 10% beneficiary 
contribution, and 20% institutional financing, amounting to ₹281.50 crore.  
For mariculture, financial assistance has been extended under the PMMSY Scheme for activities 
such as seaweed culture (raft and monoline methods) and open sea cage farming across multiple 
districts of Tamil Nadu . These  efforts have benefited over 2000 fisherfolks and supported the 
establishment of nearly 10,000 seaweed raft/monoline units and over 179 open sea cages.

GRIEVANCE REDRESSAL MECHANISM UNDER PMFBY 
 
2671.  MS IQRA CHOUDHARY: 
SHRI BABU SINGH KUSHWAHA: 
SHRI NEERAJ MAURYA: 
SHRI LALJI VERMA: 
MRS RUCHI VIRA: 
 
Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE कृ ͪष एवं ͩकसान कãयाण मंğी 
be pleased to state:  
 
(a)  whether the Government has taken cognizance of recent reports that it is not 
possible for farmers to report crop loss within 72 hours due to technical glitches in the Crop 
Insurance App and lack of network connectivity in rural areas and if so, the steps taken to 
resolve this problem during the last three years including Jaunpur Lok Sabha Constituency; 
(b)  whether despite the announcement to include 'wild animal attacks' from Kharif 
season 2026, there is any proposal/plan to provide interim relief to farmers for crops 
destroyed by nilgai and stray cattle at present, if so, the number of farmers benefited during 
the last three years including Jaunpur; 
(c)  whether any centralized grievance redressal mechanism has been established, if 
any, against insurance companies that reject insurance claims regarding 'paddy 
submergence' on technical grounds in the flood-affected areas of Uttar Pradesh; 
(d)  the number of insurance claims relating to paddy crop losses due to waterlogging in 
the flood-affected areas of Jaunpur rejected by insurance companies, along with the 
number of complaints received against them; and 
(e)  whether the Government proposes to prescribe a ceiling on the profits of private 
insurance companies and reduce the premium contribution payable by farmers, if so, the 
details thereof ? 
ANSWER 
MINISTER OF STATE FOR AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE  
कृ ͪष एवं ͩकसान कãयाण राÏय मंğी   (SHRI RAMNATH THAKUR) 
 
(a):   As per provisions of the Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana (PMFBY), in case of 
localised calamities and post-harvest losses where claims are settled on individual 
farm/farmer basis,  farmers have to intimate the loss within 72 hours of the happening of 
even by calling on the toll-free number i.e. 14447. In addition to the same, intimation can 
also be given on crop insurance app, to the State Government, insurance company, 
concerned bank/financial institutions, etc.  Keeping in view these options available, there is 
no proposal regarding extension of time limit from 72 hours.  

(b):   Losses to crops due to wild animals, being preventable in nature, were not covered 
earlier.  However, at the request of Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change 
and State Governments, States have been allowed to notify the losses by wild animals on 
individual assessment as add on cover at the cost of State Government.  Detailed protocol 
for such coverage has been given in the Operational Guidelines of the scheme.  Crop loss 
by wild animals under PMFBY is not notified by the State Government of Uttar Pradesh. 
 
     Considering requests from various stakeholders for inclusion of this peril under 
localized calamities in PMFBY, a Committee was constituted for “Defining Modalities of 
Crop Loss by Wild Animal Attack and Inundation for Paddy Crop Under Localised Risk”.  
The Committee has submitted its report alongwith recommendations and Standard 
Operating Procedures (SOPs) for coverage of these risks. 
 
(c) & (d):  To improve the grievance redressal mechanism under PMFBY, Krishi 
Rakshak Portal and Helpline (KRPH) has been developed under which, a single pan-India 
toll free number 14447 has been deployed and linked to the insurance companies’ 
database, where farmers can raise their grievances/issues.  Timelines to resolve these 
grievances/issues has also been fixed.

UTILISATION OF FIFTEENTH FINANCE COMMISSION TIED GRANTS 
  
2672. SHRI G M HARISH BALAYOGI: 
  
Will the Minister of PANCHAYATI RAJ be pleased to state: 
  
(a) the details of Tied Grants allocated under the Fifteenth Finance Commission from 2020-21 to 
2025-26, year, State and UT-wise; 
  
(b) the details of Tied Grants allocated, released and utilised under the Fifteenth Finance 
Commission during said period, State, year and district-wise, Mandal-wise and Gram Panchayat-
wise in Andhra Pradesh; 
  
(c) the component-wise details of expenditure incurred under the Drinking Water and 
Sanitation/Solid Waste Management components out of the Tied Grants during the said period, 
State and district-wise, Mandal-wise, Gram Panchayat-wise in Andhra Pradesh; 
  
(d) the details of works undertaken and completed under the said components during the said 
period, State and district-wise, Mandal-wise and Gram Panchayat-wise in Andhra Pradesh; 
  
(e) whether any unutilised funds, delays in utilisation/implementation gaps have been reported 
under the Tied Grants in Andhra Pradesh, if so, the details thereof, district-wise; and 
  
(f) the steps taken/proposed to ensure timely utilisation and effective monitoring of Tied Grants 
under the Fifteenth Finance Commission in Andhra Pradesh? 
  
ANSWER 
  
THE MINISTER OF PANCHAYATI RAJ 
 
(SHRI RAJIV RANJAN SINGH ALIAS LALAN SINGH) 
  
(a) to (f) The Department of Drinking Water & Sanitation, Ministry of Jal Shakti is the nodal 
Department for the implementation of the Fifteenth Finance Commission Tied Grants.  
  
As reported by the Department of Drinking Water & Sanitation, the Fifteenth Finance 
Commission submitted its report in two phases, the first, an Interim Report for the financial year 
2020-21 and Final Report for the award period 2021-26.  
  

2 
 
The Fifteenth Finance Commission (FC-XV) recommended Rs.2.36 lakh crore to RLBs in 28 
States including Andhra Pradesh for the period 2021-22 to 2025-26 including for those areas 
which are not required to have panchayats (Fifth and Sixth Scheduled areas and excluded areas), 
out of which 60% i.e. Rs. 1.42 lakh crore is tied grant to be utilized for (i) supply of drinking 
water, rainwater harvesting and water recycling; and, (ii) sanitation and maintenance of ODF 
status equally i.e. Rs. 0.71 Lakh crore for each component. 
  
The release of tied grant allocated to all states is based on the fulfilment of stipulated criteria 
mentioned in the operational guideline for the implementation of XV-FC recommendation on 
RLB grants. Department of Expenditure further release funds to states and state government 
transferred the same to RLBs/ Excluded areas. The tied grant has to be utilized specifically for 
Water and Sanitation related activities as mentioned in the manual for utilization for tied grant. 
  
Based on the interim report (2020-21) of the 15th Finance Commission, the entire recommended 
amount i.e. Rs. 1312.50 Crore was released to the State of Andhra Pradesh. Further, as
