2673. Shri Raja A: 
 
Will the Minister of RURAL DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state: 
 
(a)  the details of major rural development schemes implemented in 
the State of Tamil Nadu during the last five years; 
(b)  the number of villages and households that have benefited under 
programmes such as Pradhan Mantri Gram Sadak Yojana 
(PMGSY), Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment 
Guarantee Scheme (MGNREGS), Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana-
Gramin (PMAY-G) and Watershed Development Schemes; 
(c)  the measures taken to ensure timely fund release and effective 
monitoring of the projects; and 
(d)  measures taken to deal with regional disparities, improve rural 
infrastructure, create sustainable employment and enhance the 
overall quality of life in rural areas in the State? 
 
ANSWER 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF RURAL DEVELOPMENT 
(SHRI KAMLESH PASWAN) 
  
(a): Ministry of Rural Development (MoRD) has been implementing 
number of welfare schemes/programmes, such as, Mahatma Gandhi 
National Rural Employment Guarantee Scheme (MGNREGS), Pradhan 
Mantri Awaas Yojana-Gramin (PMAY-G), Pradhan Mantri Gram Sadak 
Yojana (PMGSY), Deendayal Antyodaya Yojana – National Rural 
Livelihoods Mission (DAY-NRLM), Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Grameen 
Kaushalya Yojana (DDU-GKY), Rural Self Employment Training 
Institutes (RSETIs), National Social Assistance Programme (NSAP) 
and Watershed Development Component of PMKSY (WDC-PMKSY), 
during last five years across the country including in the State of 
Tamil Nadu. The Viksit Bharat Guarantee for Rozgar and Ajeevika 
Mission (Gramin) Act, 2025 (VB- GRAM G) has come into force across 
all rural areas of the country with effect from 1st July, 2026 replacing 

Page 2 of 3 
 
the previous rural employment framework Mahatma Gandhi National 
Rural Employment Guarantee Act (MGNREGA), 2005. 
  
(b): The benefits accrued under PMGSY, MGNREGS, PMAY-G and 
WDC-PMKSY in Tamil Nadu are given below:- 
  
Programme Benefits accrued 
PMGSY Since April 2021 till 30.07.2026, a total of 1190 roads 
with 4791 km length and 66 bridges have been 
completed. 
MGNREGS As per NREGASoft, the total number of 15705.21lakh 
households in Tamil Nadu availed employment during the 
last five financial years. Further, the scheme is being 
implemented in 12,481 Gram Panchayats in the State. 
PMAY-G 14,510 villages are targeted under the scheme. During 
the last five years, a total of 3,81,710 houses were 
constructed in the State. 
WDC-
PMKSY 
A total of 5445 Water Harvesting Structures (WHS) have 
been created / rejuvenated, 19.42 Hectare (ha) area 
covered with soil and moisture conservation activities; 
11248.89 ha area brought under plantation, 3201.61 ha 
have been brought under protective irrigation, 1,44,183 
number of farmers benefitted and 10,93,878 man days 
have been generated. 
 
(c): Release of funds under the programmes is based on achieving 
defined physical milestones in terms of scheme guidelines and 
utilization of already released funds. In order to streamline the fund 
disbursal process, a new fund flow mechanism namely, SNA-SPARSH 
for Centrally Sponsored Schemes (CSS) has been introduced, with the 
principle of 'just in time release' to bring about more efficiency in 
cash management at both Centre and States level, through an 
integrated framework of PFMS, State IFMIS and e-kuber platform of 
Reserve Bank of India (RBI) in a progressive manner. 
 
Ministry of Rural Development has evolved a comprehensive 
multi-level and multi format system of monitoring and evaluation of 
the implementation of rural development schemes, through 
Performance Review Committee Meetings, National Level Monitors 
(NLMs), Area Officers Schemes, Common Review Mission, Mid-Term 
Review, Labour Budget meetings, Labour Budget Revision meetings, 
Programme Review meetings, Concurrent Evaluation and Impact 
Assessment Studies. Specific reviews of States/UTs are also 
undertaken from time to time and action is taken on the basis of their 

Page 3 of 3 
 
findings. Further, end-to-end digital solutions have also been 
operationalized under the programmes to ensure ease of 
implementation, better targeting, effective delivery and improved 
transparency besides enabling concurrent monitoring /assessment of 
progress and effectiveness by the stakeholders concerned on real 
time basis. 
 
(d): All schemes/programmes are implemented with the active 
cooperation of the States/UTs and in accordance with defined 
schematic guidelines. As per implementation framework of the 
programmes, respective State Governments are responsible for 
identification of beneficiary, conceiving of project proposals for 
infrastructure including roads and sustainable assets, generation of 
demand for employment etc. keeping in view the actual requirement 
of interventions for addressing the rural poverty and improving the 
quality of life of rural population. These measures collectively 
contributing towards creating sustainable employment, 
strengthening rural infrastructure and improving the overall quality of 
life in the State of Tamil Nadu.

INTERSTATE NARCOTICS TRAFFICKING 
 
2674.      SHRI DEEPENDER SINGH HOODA: 
 
Will the Minister of HOME AFFAIRS be pleased to state: 
 
(a) whether the Government has taken cognizance of reports identifying 
Haryana as a key  transit route for interstate narcotics trafficking between 
Punjab, Delhi, Rajasthan and hilly States; 
 
(b) the  quantity of narcotic drugs, including heroin, synthetic drugs and 
psychotropic substances, seized in Haryana during the last ten years, 
district-wise; 
 
(c) the number of NDPS cases registered, persons arrested and amount of 
drugs seized in Haryana during the said period, district-wise; 
 
(d) whether the Narcotics Control Bureau has identified any major trafficking 
corridors, highway routes or organized interstate drug networks operating 
through Haryana; and 
 
(e) the steps taken by the Government to strength en anti -narcotics 
surveillance, interstate coordination and monitoring along major transport 
corridors in Haryana? 
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HOME AFFAIRS 
(SHRI NITYANAND RAI) 
 
(a) The issue of interstate narcotics trafficking is continuously monitored 
through  intelligence  gathering,  operational  surveillance  and  inter-agency  

-2- 
L.S.US.Q.NO. 2674 FOR 04.08.2026  
coordination by Narcotics Control Bureau (NCB), Haryana State Narcotics 
Control Bureau and other Central and State enforcement agencies. The 
evolving trends of illicit narcotic drug trafficking, including the use of various 
interstate routes passing through Haryana, are regularly assessed. However, 
no State can be categorized as a permanent transit route, as trafficking 
patterns remain dynamic and are continuously evaluated based on 
intelligence inputs and enforcement actions. The issue is also reviewed 
through the Narco-Coordination Centre (NCORD) mechanism and actionable 
intelligence is shared with the concerned enforcement agencies for 
coordinated action under the Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances 
(NDPS) Act. 
 
(b)&(c) National Crime Records Bureau (NCRB) has  started collecting 
detailed data of drug-wise seizure since 2017. However, the Bureau does not 
collect district-wise data on the seizure of drugs and persons arrested. As 
per latest data published by NCRB pertaining to the year 2024; quantity of 
narcotic drugs, including heroin, synthetic drugs and psychotropic 
substances, seized in Haryana during 2017 to 2024 is at Annexure -I and 
district-wise cases registered under NDPS Act in Haryana during 2015 to 
2024 is at Annexure-II. 
 
 

-3- 
L.S.US.Q.NO. 2674 FOR 04.08.2026  
(d) NCB continuously analys es intelligence inputs to identify and 
dismantle organized drug trafficking networks. Traffickers frequently change 
their routes and modus operandi to evade detection. Actionable intelligence 
is regularly shared with th e concerned State Anti -Narcotics Task Forces 
(ANTFs) for coordinated enforcement action. Further, on 23.02.2026, a 
meeting under the chairmanship of the Deputy Director General (NWR), NCB 
was held with representatives of the ANTFs/ State Crime Record Burea u 
(SCRBs) of Haryana, Himachal Pradesh, Punjab, Chandigarh and Jammu & 
Kashmir along with concerned Central agencies, to identify narco -hotspots, 
entry/exit points, trafficking routes and drug trafficking groups/gangs. During 
the meeting, emphasis was laid  on district-wise mapping of narco -hotspots 
and trafficking routes, identification of organized drug trafficking networks 
and strengthening intelligence-based surveillance.  
 
(e) Government has taken various steps to strengthen anti -narcotics 
surveillance, interstate coordination and monitoring in the Country including 
State of Haryana, some of which are as under: - 
 
(i) Established a 4 -tier (Apex and Executive Committee at Central level 
and State and District level Committee at the State level) Narco-Coordination 
Centre  (NCORD)   mechanism  for   ensuring   better  coordination  between  
 

-4- 
L.S.US.Q.NO. 2674 FOR 04.08.2026  
Central & State Drug Law Enforcement Agencies and other stakeholders in 
the field of controlling drug trafficking and drug abuse in India. During the 
year 2025, 2 State Level NCORD Meetings and in 2026 (till 31.05.2026), 1 
State Level NCORD meetings were held in the State of Haryana. During the 
year 2025, a total of 234 District Level NCORD Meetings were conducted in 
the districts of Haryana and 103 District Level NCORD Meetings have been 
conducted during the year 2026 (till 24.07.2026).   
 
(ii) The NCORD Portal, developed by NCB, serves as a comprehensive 
gateway and Knowledge Management System for all stakeholders from 
district to central levels.  
 
(iii) National Integrated Database on Arrested Narco -Offenders (NIDAAN), 
hosted at the Inter-operable Criminal Justice System (ICJS) platform, offers 
an integrated database of all arrested NDPS offenders for use by NCB, 
National Investigation Agency (NIA), State Police, and other agencies to aid 
proactive policing and investigations.  
 
(iv) Joint Coordination Committee (JCC) meetings are held regularly in 
which all relevant Central and State agencies participate, to discuss 
investigation of important narcotics cases in the State. Till date 04 State 
Level Joint  Coordination Sub  Committee meetings  for the State of Haryana  

-5- 
L.S.US.Q.NO. 2674 FOR 04.08.2026  
& other adjoining States /UT’s have been held by NCB for better Inter-Agency 
Coordination.  
 
(v) Regular intelligence is being shared  among NCB, Haryana Police and 
other Drug Law Enforcement Agencies (DLEAs) through the NCORD and 
Multi-Agency Centre (MAC/SMAC) mechanisms. Further, joint operations are 
conducted by the Haryana State Narcotics Control Bureau, Haryana and NCB 
for effective enforcement action against drug trafficking. 
 
(vi) Financial investigations conducted by all DLEAs led to freezing/seizure 
of assets worth Rs. 14.33 crore in 98 cases in Haryana during 2025 and 
assets worth Rs. 6.54 crore in 40 cases during 2026 (till May). 
 
(vii) NCB, shared a list of habitual narcotics offenders operating in Haryana 
with the Haryana State Narcotics Control Bureau. The DLEAs have 
effectively utilized the provisions of the Prevention of Illicit Traffic in 
Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Su bstances (PITNDPS) Act and invoked 
detention orders against 75 habitual drug offenders in Haryana during 2025 
and 10 during 2026 (till June).

(d)  whether any impact assessment study has been conducted and if so, the details 
thereof? 
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE FOR AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE 
    
कृ ͪष एवं ͩकसान कãयाण राÏय मंğी    (SHRI RAMNATH THAKUR)  
 
 
(a) & (b):  Agriculture Infrastructure Fund (AIF) Scheme facilitates medium - to  - long 
term debt  financing  for creation of post harvest management infrastructure and viable 
farming assets.  The Scheme provide 3% interest subvention and credit guarantee support  
on loans up to  ₹ 2 crore for eligible borrowers, subject to a maximum lending rate of 9% 
per annum. Under Agriculture Infrastructure Fund (AIF) Scheme, as on 30th June, 2026, 
6850 projects have been sanctioned in the State of Andhra Pradesh, with a total loan 
amount of ₹ 3,635.57 crore.  Out of these, loan for 4272 projects has been fully disbursed. 
 
(c):  The district-wise detail of funds sanctioned and utilized for projects in the State of 
Andhra Pradesh as on 30th June, 2026 is placed at Annexure. 
 
(d):  Yes, in November 2025, an Impact Assessment Study of the Agriculture 
Infrastructure Fund (AIF) has conducted by the Indian Institute of Management (IIM). 
Ahmadabad. As per the study, the scheme has improved access to finance for agricultural 

enterprises, including small and marginal farmers, entrepreneurs, and established agri-
businesses. It has resulted in improved price realization and an upward shift of the 
beneficiaries in the Agri-value chain. According to the study, each AIF unit on an average 
supports a minimum of 12-13 direct jobs during peak season, 6 during lean months and 19 
indirect jobs through backward and forward linkage such as logistics, marketing, repairs, 
packaging and ancillary input services. Interventions under the AIF have resulted in an 
average reduction of 5-15% in post-harvest losses driven by improved storage, processing 
and mechanization systems that enhance efficiency and reduce spoilage across 
commodities. The beneficiaries surveyed reported income gains ranging from 11-15 %.  
Further as per the study, the Agriculture Infrastructure Fund (AIF) has strengthened farm-
gate infrastructure and improved mechanisation. It has addressed gaps in storage, 
processing, logistics, and market linkages by supporting a wide range of infrastructure 
projects for different types of beneficiaries.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF COMMERCE & INDUSTRY 
DEPARTMENT FOR PROMOTION OF INDUSTRY AND INTERNAL TRADE 
 
LOK SABHA 
 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 2677. 
           TO BE ANSWERED ON TUESDAY, THE 04TH AUGUST, 2026. 
 
INDUSTRIAL AND ECONOMIC DEVELOPMENT PACKAGE 
 
2677.  SHRI GURJEET SINGH AUJLA: 
 
Will the Minister of COMMERCE AND INDUSTRY be pleased to state: 
वाणिज्य  एवं उद्योग मंत्री 
(a)  whether Government recognizes that Amritsar, a historic and religious city 
attracting millions of domestic and international tourists annually, remains 
economically underdeveloped  despite its strategic location on international 
border, with no major industrial base and limited avenues for employment, if so, 
the details thereof; 
 
(b)  whether Government intends to formulate a spe cial industrial and trade 
promotion package for Amritsar, given that cross-border trade via Attari-Wagah 
border remains suspended, leaving  border farmers and youth with few 
opportunities, if so, the details thereof; 
 
(c)  whether the Ministry consider esta blishing border area industrial corridors, 
tourism-linked manufacturing units, and agro -based industries in region to 
boost employment, strengthen local  economy, provide economic security in a 
region frequently impacted by tensions due to its  proximity to international 
border, if so, the details thereof; and 
 
(d)  whether the Amritsar should be included by the Government in a special 
economic vision  plan for border districts to ensure balanced regional 
development? 
 
ANSWER 
 
वाणिज्य  एवं उद्योग मंत्रालय में राज्य मंत्री (श्री णिणिन प्रसाद)   
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF COMMERCE & INDUSTRY 
(SHRI JITIN PRASADA) 
 
(a) to (d): State Governments adopt different policy measures to promote industrial 
development. The Union Government supplements the efforts of the State/UT 
Governments through various schemes, programmes, and policy initiatives for 
the overall development and promotion of industry across the Country, 
including Punjab. 
During the last 4 years, Amritsar district has received investments amounting 
to ₹8,706 crore through the Fast Track Single Window Portal with potential 
employment generation of 32,069 persons. These investments span various 
sectors including Agri & Food Processi ng, Agro -based Industries (including 
Processing of Agro-waste), Tourism & Hospitality. 

Amritsar qualifies as a Border District under Punjab Industrial & Business 
Development Policy, 2026. The Policy provides an enhanced fiscal incentive 
framework for indus trial units established therein. The incentives available 
under this framework include Capital Investment Incentive, Interest Subsidy, 
Net SGST reimbursement, Employment Generation Subsidy, Stamp Duty 
exemption/reimbursement, Change of Land Use (CLU) fee e xemption, and 
Electricity Duty exemption, among others, subject to the terms and conditions 
prescribed under the Policy. Eligible units in Amritsar may avail an overall fiscal 
incentive ceiling of up to 125% (which is higher than the ceilings of incentives  
available in other districts) of the eligible Fixed Capital Investment (FCI), subject 
to a maximum of ₹500 crore, along with a flexible eligibility period of 10 to 15 
years. 
The Government of India has approved development of Integrated 
Manufacturing Cluster (IMC) at Rajpura-Patiala with an area of 1,098.85 acres 
under the Amritsar-Kolkata Industrial Corridor (AKIC) in August 2024 for total 
project cost of Rs. 1,367.72 crore. Project Manager for New Cities (PMNC) and 
EPC Contractor have been appointed for implementation of internal trunk 
infrastructure works. As per DPR, Integrated Manufacturing Cluster (IMC) at 
Rajpura-Patiala under the Amritsar -Kolkata Industrial Corridor (AKIC) has an 
estimated employment generation potential of approximately 64,200 jobs. 
The Punjab Industrial & Business Development Policy, 2026 identifies Agri & 
Food Processing Industries and Processing of Agro -waste into 
Energy/Bioenergy/Manure as Priority Sectors, with enhanced fiscal support 
available to eligible units established in Border Districts, including Amritsar. 
In addition, the Punjab Food Processing Policy, 2026 provides sector -specific 
incentives such as 100% exemption of Mandi  Fee/Market Fee/Rural 
Development Fee and other State taxes on the purchase of raw material for 
eligible food processing units for a period of five years, along with 100% Net 
SGST reimbursement, subject to prescribed conditions. 
The Punjab Tourism & Hospit ality Policy, 2026 has also been notified to  
promote tourism-linked economic activity in the region. These measures are 
aimed at leveraging Amritsar's tourism potential to generate allied 
manufacturing and service-sector employment in the border region.

Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE कृͪष एवं ͩकसान

(a) the details of area under cultivation, production and productivity (yield per

(c) whether the data on area, production and productivity of Arecanut in Karnataka is

(d) the details of financial assistance provided by the Union Government for

ANSWER 
 
THE MINISTER OF STATE FOR AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE 
 
कृͪष एवं ͩकसान कãयाण राÏय मंğी  (SHRI RAMNATH THAKUR) 
 
(a): The details of area under cultivation, production and productivity (yield per 
hectare) of Arecanut during each of the last five years i.e. from 2021-22 to 2025-26 
(Second Advance Estimates) in the country, State/UT- wise, are given  
at Annexure-I. 
 
(b): During the last five years, Karnataka accounted for 71.56% of the country's 
total area and 75.47% of the country’s total production under Arecanut. 

(c): The Department of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare (DA&FW) releases area 
and production estimates of horticulture crops, including Arecanut, at the State/UT 
level and All-India level, sourced from the Directorate of Arecanut and Spices 
Development (DASD). The district-level data of area, production and productivity of 
Arecanut for each of the last five years in Karnataka is given at Annexure-II.  
 
(d): Under the Mission for Integrated Development of Horticulture (MIDH), a 
centrally sponsored scheme, there is no specific provision for providing assistance 
for Arecanut development through area expansion to the States/UTs. However, 
financial assistance is provided to the Directorate of Arecanut and Spices 
Development (DASD) under MIDH, for implementing, coordinating and monitoring 
the activities on development of Arecanut, Spices and Aromatic plants. The details 
of funds allocated and released to DASD under MIDH during the last five years is as 
under:

(e): The overall development of Arecanut at the National level is coordinated by 
the Directorate of Arecanut and Spices Development (DASD), Calicut. DASD has 
implemented the following technical programmes and technology-dissemination 
schemes: 
 Arecanut based Multispecies Cropping Systems: To enhance farmer’s 
income from the existing unit area, the Directorate promotes and 
popularizes multispecies cropping systems in existing Arecanut gardens. 
Front Line Demonstrations (FLDs) are held in the fields of progressive 
farmers, along with the organization of awareness and training  
programmes to disseminate this technology and adoption of this practice. 
 Management of Fruitrot/ Mahali disease through effective fungicides: 
Establishes FLDs to demonstrate the effect of the new fungicide 
Mandipropamid in management of fruit rot disease in Arecanut in selected 
areas of Kerala and Karnataka. 
 Management of Arecanut rootgrub infestation through the use of 
Entomopathogenic Nematode (EPN):  Establishes FLDs to popularize 
the use of EPN in management of root grubs in Arecanut. 
 Promotion of Hybrid Dwarf varieties: Demonstrated dwarf hybrid 
varieties of Arecanut in selected farmers’ fields to encourage easier 
harvesting operations and optimize plant density.  

 Yellow Leaf Disease (YLD) management through plastic mulch: FLDs 
are established in farmers’ field to demonstrate the effect of plastic 
mulching in YLD management in Arecanut. 
 Initiative for disease prediction: A Temperature and Relative Humidity 
Controller Unit has been given to the Indian Council of Agricultural 
Research (ICAR)- Central Plantation Crops Research Institute (CPCRI) for 
studying the  relationship between weather and Leaf Spot Disease (LSD) 
of Arecanut to help in disease prediction. 
 Community-Based Leaf Spot Disease (LSD) management: DASD has 
established large-scale demonstration on community-based management 
of LSD in Arecanut across 10 LSD affected Arecanut growing taluks in 
Karnataka from 2025-26 in the selected farmers’ fields of the affected 
area. This programme covers 50 hectare, with 5 hectare in each taluk, 
aiming to popularize the recommended scientific management measures 
for control of LSD. An amount of Rs. 6.32 crores has been sanctioned for 
this programme for a period of three years. 
 Evidence based Health Research: To address the knowledge gap and 
provide conclusive evidence on the health effects of Arecanut, DASD, in 
collaboration with ICAR-CPCRI, is implementing a project titled "Evidence-
Based Research on Arecanut and Human Health”. This project brings 
together around 12 National and State-level agencies dealing with medical 
research, including All India Institute of Medical Sciences (AIIMS), New 
Delhi; Centre for Cellular & Molecular Biology (CCMB), Hyderabad; and 
others to conduct detailed research on the effects of Arecanut on human 
health. An advisory Committee has been setup for monitoring this 
research. The project has been started in 2025-26 and an amount of Rs 
9.99 crores has been sanctioned for a period of three years. 
 Value Chain Study on Arecanut: The DASD in association with ICAR-
CPCRI, is conducting a pilot study on value chain of Arecanut to 
understand the existing value chains in the sector and to analyse the 
consumption patterns and distribution channels of Arecanut and its 
products.

PESTS CONTROL IN SUGARCANE 
 
†2680. SHRI CHANDAN CHAUHAN: 
Will the Minister of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare/ कृͪष एवं ͩकसान कãयाण मंğी 
be pleased to state: 
(a) whether the Government is aware that the productivity of farmers is being 
adversely affected due to top borer, smut disease and other pests and diseases in 
various sugarcane-producing regions, including Bijnor in Uttar Pradesh; 
(b) the names of the research, trials and projects undertaken for the prevention of 
various pests and diseases affecting the sugarcane crop, development of disease-
resistant varieties during the last five years and modern control techniques, along 
with the major outcomes thereof; 
(c) whether the Government is making any arrangements to provide timely scientific 
advisory, quality seeds, pest and disease management and financial 
assistance/compensation through crop insurance or other schemes to the affected 
farmers in case of crop damage; and 
(d) the future action plan of the Government to permanently mitigate the losses 
caused by pests and diseases in sugarcane-producing regions, including Bijnor? 
 
ANSWER 
MINISTER OF STATE FOR AGRICULTURE & FARMERS WELFARE 
कृͪष एवं ͩकसान कãयाण राÏय मंğी (SHRI RAMNATH THAKUR) 
 
(a):  The production of Sugarcane has increased from 2158.10 Lakh Metric tonnes 
(MT) during 2023-24 to 2296.99 Lakh MT during 2025-26 (3rd Advance Estimates) in 
the State of Uttar Pradesh. Similarly, the yield has increased from 81.34 MT/Ha during 
2023 -2024 to 81.97 MT/Ha during 2025-26 in UP (Year-wise statement at  
(Annexure I).  
   
  

(b):  The ICAR-Indian Sugarcane Research Institute (ICAR-ISRI), Lucknow, is 
actively engaged in research, field trials and technology development for the 
prevention and management of major insect pests and diseases affecting sugarcane 
across the country. At present, the institute is executing 15 Institute funded research 
projects, 4 externally funded research projects and 9 contract research projects 
(details at Annexure II) covering various aspects of sugarcane insect pest and 
disease management including disease diagnosis, host resistance, integrated pest 
and disease management, biological control and climate-resilient crop protection 
strategies   
The Institute also promotes environmentally sustainable crop protection 
through the development and dissemination of biological control technologies.  Timely 
application of the recommended bio-control agents in conjunction with other 
recommended crop management practices substantially reduces the incidence of 
insect pests and diseases, enhances crop health and productivity, minimizes 
dependence on chemical pesticides and contributes to environmentally sustainable 
sugarcane cultivation. 
As informed by State Government, during the last five years, several 
sugarcane varieties have been released/adopted for the state of U.P. Among these, 
early-maturing sugarcane varieties such as CoSh-19231, CoSh-17451, CoSh-18231, 
CoLk-16202, CoLk-15466, and Co-15023, as well as mid and late-maturing sugarcane 
varieties including CoSh-16233, CoSh-15233, CoLk-16470, CoLk-15206, CoLk-
14204, and CoLk-15207 have been released/ adopted, and are being utilized by the 
farmers of the State for sugarcane cultivation.  
(c): As informed by State Government, scientific advisories are issued in a timely 
manner by the State Government through the Sugarcane Development Department, 
U.P., and the Uttar Pradesh Sugarcane Research Council, Shahjahanpur. 
Additionally, the availability of healthy and high-quality seeds to farmers is ensured 
through a three-tier seed production system. Under the direction and supervision of 
the Uttar Pradesh Sugarcane Research Council, Shahjahanpur, breeder seeds are 
produced at various research centres, institutions, and sugar mill farms. These seeds 
are distributed to various districts in accordance with the allocation orders of the 
Sugarcane Commissioner, U.P. 
  

ICAR-ISRI are regularly conducting field surveys and surveillance in farmers' 
fields as well as in the command areas of sugar mills to monitor the incidence and 
severity of insect pests and diseases in sugarcane. Bio-control agents are being 
distributed to farmers under the Scheduled Caste Sub Plan (SCSP) programme to 
promote eco-friendly disease and pest management practices. Farmers are regularly 
advised on the timely and need-based application of recommended insecticides and 
fungicides for effective management of insect pests and diseases. In addition, 
technical training programmes, farmer awareness sessions, distribution of extension 
literature (leaflets and technical bulletins), scientific advisories, quality seed 
distribution programmes, and farmer–scientist interactions are being conducted on a 
regular basis. Information regarding various Government schemes related to 
agriculture is also disseminated to the farming community. These extension activities 
aim to enhance farmers' awareness, strengthen their knowledge of integrated pest 
and disease management, and improve the productivity and sustainability of 
sugarcane cultivation. 
Further, Department of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare (DA&FW), through its 
Regional Central Integrated Pest Management Centre (RCIPMC) in Lucknow and 
three Central Integrated Pest Management Centres (CIPMCs) at Gorakhpur, Agra and 
Varanasi in Uttar Pradesh, regularly conducts pest surveillance and disseminates 
Integrated Pest Management (IPM) knowledge through training programmes like 
Farmers Field Schools, Season Long Training Programme and Orientation 
Programme. A total of 35 surveys covering 4906 hectare of area, have been 
conducted in Uttar Pradesh including Bijnor for the period from September 2023 to 
March 2026 for sugarcane crop. Further, 105 advisories have been issued during 
September 2024 to March 2026 for management of pests and diseases in Sugarcane 
crop, and 26 number of training programs have been conducted for creating 
awareness for pests and diseases in Sugarcane crop in Western Uttar Pradesh 
including Bijnor, in which 517 farmers, State Department Officials and Agro-input 
Dealers were trained. 
  

The State of Uttar Pradesh has been implementing Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima 
Yojana (PMFBY) and Restructured Weather Based Crop Insurance Scheme 
(RWBCIS) since Kharif 2016. Notification of crop under the scheme is prerogative of 
the State Government. While Sugarcane is eligible for coverage under the Scheme, 
at present the Government of Uttar Pradesh has not notified sugarcane under 
PMFBY/RWBCIS. 
(d):  ICAR-ISRI is implementing and strengthening an integrated strategy for the 
sustainable management of insect pests and diseases in sugarcane. The future action 
plan includes continuous surveillance and early warning systems for the timely 
detection of emerging pest and disease outbreaks, development, evaluation and 
promotion of resistant and high-yielding sugarcane varieties, production and 
dissemination of quality disease free planting seed through seed multiplication 
programmes; promotion of Integrated Pest and Disease Management practices 
integrating cultural, biological, mechanical and need-based chemical control 
measures; large-scale production and field application of bio-control agents and other 
bio-inputs; strengthening of diagnostic and advisory services through digital platforms 
and field-based extension systems; organization of regular farmer training 
programmes, frontline demonstrations, and awareness campaigns; capacity building 
of extension personnel and sugar mill field staff; and promotion of climate-resilient crop 
management practices. These interventions are being implemented across the 
sugarcane-growing regions of the country, including Bijnor district of Uttar Pradesh, 
with the objective of minimizing crop losses, improving sugarcane productivity, 
enhancing farmers' income and ensuring sustainable sugarcane cultivation. 
 The State Government of Uttar Pradesh reported that currently, no severe 
impact of diseases or pests has been reported in any sugarcane-growing region in the 
state, including Bijnor. 
Further, DA&FW is providing assistance to sugarcane crop under National 
Food Security and Nutrition Mission (NFSNM) since 2014-15. Under the scheme, 
thrust is being given on transfer of technology through demonstration and training.

Will the Minister of COMMERCE AND INDUSTRY be pleased to state:

(a)  whether the Government has assessed the impact of various Production Linked 
Incentive (PLI) Schemes on industrial development in Tier-II and Tier-III regions 
in the country including Lok Sabha Constituency Dewas –Shajapur of Madhya 
Pradesh; 
 
(b)  the details of investment, production, exports and employment generated under 
PLI Schemes in these regions, sector-wise including Madhya Pradesh; 
 
(c)  whether industries in Dewas, Shajapur and nearby industrial clusters have 
benefited from the PLI framework, if so, the details thereof; 
 
(d)  whether the Government has any proposals to extend, modify or introduce 
additional incentives to attract manufacturing investments in industrial areas of 
Dewas–Shajapur and other emerging districts of Madhya Pradesh; and 
 
(e)  the steps being taken by the Government to promote MSMEs, manufacturing, 
exports and  the vision of Atmanirbhar Bharat by encouraging greater 
participation of industries from Lok  Sabha Constituency Dewas –Shajapur 
under the PLI Schemes?

वाणिज्य  एवं उद्योग मंत्रालय में राज्य मंत्री (श्री णिणिन प्रसाद)   
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF COMMERCE & INDUSTRY 
(SHRI JITIN PRASADA) 
 
(a): The Government has approved 14 Production Linked Incentive (PLI) Schemes 
across key manufacturing sectors with a total approved outlay of  ₹1.91 lakh 
crore to boost domestic manufacturing, attract investments, enhance exports, 
generate employment and strengthen India's integration with global value 
chains. 
The PLI Schemes are implemented as  pan-India initiatives, and eligible 
companies are selected through a transpare nt application process based on 
the criteria prescribed under the respective Scheme Guidelines. The location of 
manufacturing units is determined by the applicant companies based on 

commercial and operational considerations. The Government regularly 
reviews the progress and outcomes of the PLI Schemes through the respective 
implementing Ministries/Departments. 
(b): The PLI Schemes have recorded significant cumulative achievements across 
the country, including manufacturing units established in the State of Madhya 
Pradesh. As on 31.03.2026, the cumulative achievements under the PLI 
Schemes are as follows: 
Parameter Achievement 
Investment Over ₹2.40 lakh crore 
Production/Sales Over ₹22.66 lakh crore 
Exports Over ₹15.2 lakh crore 
Employment More than 14.15 lakh (direct and indirect) 
 
(c): The PLI Schemes are open to eligible manufacturers across the country and 
are implemented through a transparent application -based process. Forty-five 
manufacturing units in the State of Madhya Pradesh have been approved under 
various PLI Schemes. The Scheme also indirectly benefits suppliers and 
vendors to the manufacturing units incentivized through the PLI Schemes. 
District wise details of manufacturi ng units are not maintained in the Ministry. 
The sector -wise details of the approved manufacturing units in Madhya 
Pradesh are provided at Annexure-I. 
(d): The Production Linked Incentive (PLI) Schemes are implemented as pan-India, 
wherein eligible applica nts from across the country, including emerging 
industrial regions, may participate subject to fulfillment of the eligibility criteria 
prescribed under  the respective Scheme Guidelines. The Schemes provide 
adequate flexibility within the approved framework to enable eligible companies 
to establish manufacturing facilities at locations based on their commercial and 
operational considerations. 
The Government continuously reviews the implementation of the PLI Schemes 
in consultation with the respective implementing Ministries/Departments and 
industry stakeholders. Based on sectoral requirements and emerging needs, 
proposals for modification or extension of individual PLI Schemes are 
considered by the Government in accord ance with the prescribed approval 
process. 
(e): The Government has undertaken several initiatives to promote manufacturing, 
exports and the vision of Aatmanirbhar Bharat. The PLI Schemes provide 
performance-linked incentives to eligible manufacturers to en hance domestic 
production, value addition, exports and employment across strategic sectors. 
In addition, the Government has launched complementary initiatives such as 
Make in India, PM GatiShakti National Master Plan, National Logistics Policy, 
Districts as Export Hubs, Startup India, Ease of Doing Business reforms, and 
various programmes for the promotion of MSMEs. These initiatives provide an 
enabling ecosystem  for industries across the country, including those in 

Madhya Pradesh, to strengthen their manufacturing capabilities and participate 
in domestic and global value chains. Eligible industries from Dewas –Shajapur 
may also participate in the respective  PLI Schemes, subject to fulfillment of 
the eligibility criteria prescribed under the applicable Scheme Guidelines.

 (xiv) Employment generation and skill development continue to remain a priority

(SHRI KAMLESH PASWAN) 
  
(a) to (c): Consequent upon commencement of the Viksit Bharat– 
Guarantee for Rozgar and Aajeevika Mission (Gramin) (VB-G RAM G) 
Act, 2025, the scheme has successfully been implemented in rural 
areas of the entire country w.e.f 01.07.2026. The VB-G RAM G 
provides for a statutory guarantee of one hundred and twenty five 
days of wage employment in a financial year to every rural household 
whose adult members volunteer to undertake unskilled manual work 
against one hundred day of guaranteed wage employment available 
under Mahatma Gandhi NREGS. The new scheme has been 
successfully implemented in the State of Maharashtra and Madhya 
Pradesh also w.e.f 0.1.07.2026. In case of Maharashtra n interim 

Page 2 of 2 
 
allocation Rs.4420.32 crore has been made for the State. 
Subsequently, Mother Sanctions amounting to Rs.1459.92 Crore have 
been issued to the State of Maharashtra as first installment of Central 
Share under various components based on the proposal received from 
the State. Further in case of Madhya Pradesh an interim allocation 
Rs.6252.03 crore has been made for the State. Subsequently, Mother 
Sanctions amounting to Rs.630.76 Crore have been issued to the 
State of Madhya Pradesh as first installment of Central Share under 
various components based on the proposal received from the State.  
It is also stated that under Section 5(4) of the Act, the State 
Governments may make provision for providing additional days of 
employment beyond the period guaranteed under the Act from their 
own resources. The Act also aims to strengthen sustainable rural 
livelihoods through the creation of durable assets and 
implementation of the permissible works specified in Schedule I of 
the Act, namely Water-related Works, Core Rural Infrastructure, 
Livelihood-related Infrastructure and Special Works to Mitigate 
Extreme Weather Events. These provisions are intended to enhance 
livelihood security, strengthen rural infrastructure and promote 
sustainable rural development.  
(d): Deendayal Antyodaya Yojana–National Rural Livelihoods 
Mission (DAY-NRLM), a flagship poverty alleviation programme of the 
Ministry of Rural Development, is being implemented through the 
State Rural Livelihoods Missions (SRLMs) across 760 districts and 
7,246 blocks in 34 States and Union Territories including Maharashtra 
and Madhya Pradesh. As of June 2026, the Mission has mobilized 
about 10.08 crore rural households into nearly 92 lakh Self Help 
Groups (SHGs). Under the existing provisions of DAY-NRLM, 
capitalization support is provided to eligible SHGs in the form of 
Revolving Fund (RF) of ₹20,000–₹30,000 per SHG and Community 
Investment Fund (CIF) of up to ₹2.50 lakh per SHG to support income-
generating and livelihood activities, including entrepreneurial 
ventures. 
  In addition, interest subvention is available on bank loans to 
eligible SHGs. For loans up to ₹3 lakh, banks provide credit at a 
concessional interest rate of 7% per annum. For loans above ₹3 lakh 
and up to ₹5 lakh, banks extend credit at an interest rate equivalent 
to their one-year MCLR or any other external benchmark-based 
lending rate or 10% per annum, whichever is lower. Cumulatively, 
loans amounting to ₹13.41 lakh crore have been disbursed to SHGs 
under the Mission. These benefits are available to eligible SHGs, 
including those in Maharashtra and Madhya Pradesh, in accordance 
with the scheme guidelines.

SCHEME TO PROMOTE MANUFACTURING OF ELECTRIC PASSENGER CARS 
 
2686. SHRI P C MOHAN:  
 
Will the Minister of HEAVY INDUSTRIES be pleased to state:  
 
(a) whether any company approved or applying under the Scheme to Promote Manufacturing of 
Electric Passenger Cars in India has proposed to set up or expand manufacturing facilities in 
Karnataka, including Bengaluru and if so, the details thereof including investment committed;  
 
(b) the details of domestic value addition and technology transfer commitments applicable to any 
such facility proposed in Karnataka, and the timeline for achieving the prescribed localisation levels;  
 
(c) the details of m anufacturing capacity and employment generation expected to be created in 
Karnataka under the Scheme; and  
 
(d) the role envisaged for the State Government of Karnataka in facilitating land, infrastructure and 
other support for such investment under the Scheme's implementation framework? 
 
ANSWER 
THE MINISTER OF STATE FOR HEAVY INDUSTRIES 
(SHRI BHUPATHIRAJU SRINIVASA VARMA) 
 
(a) to (c): Scheme to Promote Manufacturing of Electric Passenger Cars in India (SPMEPCI) 
was notified on 15.03.2024 to attract investments from global electric passenger car manufacturers 
and promote India as a manufacturing destination for electric passenger cars. T o avail benefit under 
SPMEPCI, approved applicants have to setup manufacturing facilities in India with a minimum 
investment of Rs. 4,150 cr, for manufacturing of e -4W and made operational within a period of 3 
years from the date of issuance of approval le tter by MHI and achieve minimum Domestic Value 
Addition (DVA) of 25% within 3 year & 50% within 5 year.  
 
Application window for SPMEPCI was open for 120 days till 21.10.2025, however, no 
applications were received. 
 
(d): For implementation of SPMEPCI, det ailed guidelines supplementary to the provisions 
specified in SPMEPCI notification dated 15.03.2024 were issued on 02.06.2025 and State 
Government has no role w.r.t duty foregone benefit under SPMEPCI. However, State Governments 
can facilitate setting up o f manufacturing facilities along with other initiatives for ease of doing 
business to attract foreign investment.

2688. MR PATHAN YUSUF:  
 Will the Minister of COMMERCE AND INDUSTRY (वाणिज्य एवं उद्योग मंत्री) be 
pleased to state: 
 
(a) the status of implementation of recently concluded Free Trade Agreements and 
 ongoing trade negotiations; 
(b) the expected impact of these agreements on India's exports, manufacturing 
 sector and employment; 
(c) the steps taken by the Government to enhance the competitiveness of Indian 
 exporters, particularly for Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises 
 (MSMEs); and  
(d) the projections of export growth arising from these agreements, sector-wise? 
  
ANSWER 
 
वाणिज्य और उद्योग मंत्रालय में राज्यमंत्री (श्री णिणिन प्रसाद) 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF COMMERCE AND INDUSTRY  
(SHRI JITIN PRASADA) 
(a)        The status of implementation of recently concluded Free Trade Agreements 
(FTAs) and ongoing trade negotiations is at Annexure. 
(b)      FTAs are economic instruments aimed at expanding trade, enhancing 
competitiveness and deepening economic integration. FTAs provide calibrated market 
access through tariff elimination at Entry into Force (EIF), ph ased tariff 
reductions/elimination, and sensitive/exclusion lists across sectors. The details of 
sectors covered, tariffs structure and salient features of the implemented FTAs may be 
sourced at https://www.commerce.gov.in/#/international-trade/trade-agreements   
Assessment of the impact of Free Trade Agreements (FTAs) is an ongoing exercise . 
India's recently concluded Free Trade Agreements (FTAs) with Australia, the UAE, 
EFTA, Oman, the UK and New Zealand are expected to provide opportunities for 
enhanced trade and growth of domestic industries. These agreements include 
provisions relating to investment and market access, which is expected to support 
domestic producti on, facilitate investment flows, and create opportunities for 
employment across labour intensive sectors including manufacturing, agriculture, 
MSMEs and allied sectors 

2 
 
Further, before entering into new FTA negotiations, Government ensures that sector -
specific stakeholder consultations are held at all stages of the negotiations. FTAs are 
negotiated with the endeavour to deliver comprehensive, balanced, fair and mutually 
beneficial outcomes. It also enables a preferential, stable and predictable trade 
ecosystem for Indian exporters in the trading partner countries. In addition to this 
structured approach, post -implementation, the Government is continuously engaged 
with all stakeholders to ensure effective FTA utilization through trade promotion, trade 
facilitation and addressing challenges if any. Strategic safeguards for sensitive sectors 
ensure export growth while protecting domestic priorities. 
 (c)      Government has taken several initiatives and measures, from time to time, 
towards enhancing domestic capacities and boosting exports from the country including 
for MSMEs, small exporters and regional industries as under: 
(i) The Foreign Trade Policy, effective from 1st April, 2023, designed to integrate India 
more effectively into the global market, improve t rade competitiveness, and establish 
the country as a reliable and trusted trade partner; 
(ii) Export Promotion Mission: The Government has approved the Scheme for Export 
Promotion Mission (EPM) for the period FY 2025 –26 to FY 2030 –31, aimed at 
strengthening India’s export competitiveness - particularly for MSMEs. The EPM shall 
operate through two integrated sub-schemes: 
o Niryat Prothsahan, focused on improving access to trade finance through 
instruments such as interest subvention, export factoring, collater al 
guarantees for export credit, credit guarantee for e -commerce exporters, 
and credit enhancement support; and 
o Niryat Disha, focused on other trade enablers such as export quality and 
compliance support, international branding and packaging, market access 
initiatives, export logistics & warehousing, and trade intelligence. 
  
(iii)       Bharat Trade Net (BTN): Bharat Trade Net (BTN), announced in the Union 
Budget 2025 is a flagship digital public infrastructure initiative to enhances MSME 
competitiveness by enabling simpler, paperless documentation, reducing compliance 
burdens, and facilitating faster, secure trade transactions recognized globally. 
  
(iv)       The introduction of grassroots programs such as Districts as Export Hubs 
(DEHs) and E -Commerce Ex port Hubs enables MSMEs, start -ups, and artisans to 
access international markets at lower costs and with simplified export processes. 
  
(v)        Strengthening infrastructure through the National Logistics Policy and PM Gati  
Shakti enhances multimodal connectivity and reduces logistics costs, directly benefiting 
MSME exporters by easing supply chain bottlenecks. 
  

3 
 
(vi)       Launch of a Common Digital Platform for Certificate of Origin, to facilitate trade 
and increase FTA utilisation by exporters. 
  
(vii)      Government is continuously engaged with industry associations and concerned 
stakeholders, including Indian Missions abroad, Export Promotion Councils, trade 
associations and concerned Ministries/Departments, to advance trade through trade 
promotion, trade facilitation and remedial measures related to import and export. 
  
(viii)     The Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises has established 65 Export 
Facilitation Centers (EFCs) in its field offices across the country to provide requisite 
mentoring and hand holding support to MSMEs in exporting their products and services. 
Further, International Cooperation (IC) Scheme of Ministry of MSME facilitates 
participation of MSMEs  in international exhibitions/fairs/conferences/seminar/buyer -
seller meets abroad.   
  
(d)       The operationalization of Free Trade Agreements (FTAs) has strengthened 
India's trade engagement with key partner countries by providing unprecedented market 
access, reducing trade barriers, enhancing supply chain linkages and creating new 
opportunities for Indian exporters across sectors. Despite persistent global challenges, 
including geopolitical tensions and supply chain disruptions, India's exports increase d 
from US$ 776.4 billion in FY 2022-23 to US$ 863.1 billion in FY 2025-26. Merchandise 
exports to major FTA partner countries and trade blocs have been substantial at US$ 
179.1 billion in FY 2025-26, accounting for 40.5% of India's total merchandise exports. 
Merchandise export to recent FTA partners also indicated significant export growth. For 
example, exports to the UAE increased from US$ 16.7 billion in FY 2021 -22 (prior to 
CEPA implementation) to US$ 37.4 billion in FY 2025-26, while exports to Australia rose 
from US$ 4.0 billion in FY 2021 -22 to US$ 7.3 billion in FY 2025 -26 following the 
implementation of ECTA. Similarly, exports to EFTA countries increased from US$ 1.64 
billion in FY 2019-20 to US$ 1.76 billion in FY 2025-26. 
  
Further, trade trends, including for exports and imports, continue to be shaped 
by a multitude of global and domestic factors, including economic growth, geopolitical 
developments, industry demand, domestic needs, commodity price movements and 
evolving supply chains.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF HEAVY INDUSTRIES  
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 2689 
ANSWERED ON 04.08.2026 
 
MANUFACTURING OF FLEX-FUEL AND ELECTRIC VEHICLES 
 
†2689. SHRI BRIJENDRA SINGH OLA:  
SHRI RAHUL KASWAN:  
SHRI SUKHJINDER SINGH RANDHAWA:  
 
Will the Minister of HEAVY INDUSTRIES be pleased to state:  
 
(a) the details of the projects approved, investment received, production capacity, employment 
generation and technology development achieved so far for the manufacturing of flex -fuel vehicles, 
electric vehicles and related automobile components under the Production Linked Incentive (PLI) 
Scheme, category-wise and State-wise;  
 
(b) whether the Government has formulated any phased national policy to incentivize flex -fuel 
vehicles operating on fuel blended with more than twenty per cent ethanol and if so, the details 
thereof;  
 
(c) whether the Government has conducted any independent cost -benefit study regarding the 
incentivization of flex-fuel and electric vehicles and if so, the details thereof; and  
 
(d) whether the Government has conducted any integrated scientific study on the impact of ethanol 
production on water consumption, agricultural land use, food security, carbon emissions, biofuel 
supply chain and the domestic automobile industry and if so, the details thereof? 
 
ANSWER 
THE MINISTER OF STATE FOR HEAVY INDUSTRIES 
(SHRI BHUPATHIRAJU SRINIVASA VARMA) 
 
(a):   Production Linked Incentive scheme for Automobile & Auto Components (PLI-Auto scheme) 
is implemented on an all-India basis. The current status of implementation of PLI-Auto scheme is as 
below:-  
 
Parameter Cumulative till 31.03.2026 
Investment (Rs. cr) 44,326 
Incremental Sales (Base Year FY2019-20) (Rs. cr) 52,414 
Employment generated (Nos.) 67,820 
Incentive disbursed (Rs. cr)  2,386.36 
 
To boost domestic manufacturing and localisation of AAT products, PLI -Auto scheme 
mandates minimum Domestic Value Addition (DVA) of 50% for availing incentives. As on 
28.07.2026, 18 applicants have received DVA certificates for 155 AAT products/variants.  
 
(b): Ministry of Heavy Industries (MHI) has not formulated any separate phased national policy 
to incentivize flex-fuel vehicles operating on fuel blended with more than 20% ethanol.  
 
(c): MHI has not conducted any study regarding incentivization of flex-fuel and electric vehicles. 
 
 

 
-2- 
 
(d): Government has adopted a balanced approach to the Ethanol Blended Petrol (EBP) 
Programme, ensuring that water sustainability, food security and farmers' interests remain paramount. 
Under the National Policy on Biofuels, ethanol is produced from multiple ap proved feedstocks, 
including sugarcane-based feedstocks, maize, damaged foodgrains, broken rice, foodgrains unfit for 
human consumption, surplus foodgrains approved by the National Biofuel Coordination Committee 
(NBCC) and other approved agricultural feedstocks. 
Government is also promoting crop diversification towards comparatively less water -
intensive feedstocks such as maize. An Expert Committee constituted by Ministry of Agriculture & 
Farmers Welfare in 2024 examined the water requirement of various eth anol feedstock crops & its 
recommendations are being considered while implementing the programme. 
 
Water-use efficiency is also being enhanced through micro-irrigation, drip irrigation and other 
water conservation measures under the Per Drop More Crop component of the Pradhan Mantri Krishi 
Sinchayee Yojana. Many sugar mills are also encouraging farmers to adopt water-efficient cultivation 
practices.  
 
Molasses-based distilleries with incineration boilers and grain -based distilleries are required 
to operate as Zero Liquid Discharge (ZLD) units, enabling recycling and reuse of process water while 
eliminating liquid effluent discharge.

(b) the total number of posts lying vacant out of the said posts at present; 
(c) the number of backlog vacancies for persons belonging to SCs, STs, and OBCs; 
 and 
(d) the action being taken by the Government to fill up the said vacancies and 
 backlog posts? 
  
  
ANSWER 
 
वाणिज्य और उद्योग मंत्रालय में राज्यमंत्री (श्री णिणिन प्रसाद) 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF COMMERCE AND INDUSTRY 
(SHRI JITIN PRASADA) 
 
(a) to (d) The Ministry of Commerce and Industry comprises of two Departments namely 
Department of Commerce (DoC) and Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal 
Trade (DPIIT) which have officers belonging to All India Service, Central Secretariat 
Service, Indian Economic Services, Indian Statistics Service, Central Secretariat 
Stenographers Service, Indian Trade Service and other organized services. The 
guidelines of Government of India regarding reservation to Scheduled Caste (SCs), 
Scheduled Tribes (ST s) and Other Backward Classes (OBCs) are followed by the 
respective Cadre Controlling Authorities. However, for the posts which are filled by 
Department/ Subordinate Offices /Autonomous Bodies itself, the reservation to 
SC/ST/OBC categories is ensured by maintaining appropriate reservation roster. In this 
regard, Liaison Officers have been appointed by both the Departments to monitor proper 
implementation of reservation in their respective organizations including Subordinate 
Offices Organizations and Autonomous Bodies. 
  
Occurrence and filling up of vacancies, along with backlog reserved vacancies, 
is a continuous process. By the time, vacant posts are filled up, new vacancies arise 
due to retirement, resignation, death, promotion etc. These vacancies are fi lled up by 
various recruiting agencies viz. Union Public Service Commission (UPSC), Staff 
Selection Commission (SSC) and by the Department/Organisations in accordance with 
the reservations norms/guidelines of Government of India for providing reservations to 
SC/ST/OBC categories.

2694. Shri Arun Govil: 
 Dr. Rajeev Bharadwaj: 
 
Will the Minister of RURAL DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state: 
 
(a)  whether the Government has decided that Self Help Groups will  
now be formed only for needy women, if so, the details thereof 
and the scheme formulated to strengthening the current 
functioning of SHGs; 
(b)  the total number of SHGs formed so far under the Deendayal 
Antyodaya Yojana-National Rural Livelihoods Mission (DAY-
NRLM) along with the total amount of bank loans disbursed to 
them, State and district-wise including Dewas- Shajapur, Kangra 
and Chamba Lok Sabha Constituencies of Madhya Pradesh and 
Himachal Pradesh; 
(c)  the number of loan accounts categorized as Non-Performing 
Assets (NPAs) out of the said loans along with the total NPA 
amount; 
(d)  whether the Government is aware that the income of Self Help 
Groups can be significantly enhanced through dairy activities, if 
so, the details thereof; 
(e)  the steps taken by the Government to link such groups with 
dairy business, milk collection, processing and marketing; 
(f)  whether the Government are undertaking any specific initiative 
to integrate them with schemes like 'Lakhpati Didi', if so, the 
details thereof along with the efforts made in this regard in 
Meerut-Hapur Lok Sabha Constituencies; and 
(g)  the details of the schemes formulated by the Government to 
strengthen the currently functioning SHGs? 
 
  

Page 2 of 10 
 
ANSWER 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF RURAL DEVELOPMENT 
(DR. CHANDRA SEKHAR PEMMASANI) 
  
(a): The Deendayal Antyodaya Yojana–National Rural Livelihoods 
Mission (DAY-NRLM) schemes adheres to the principle of universal 
social mobilization, which aims to organize all identified rural poor 
households by mobilizing at least one-woman member from each 
household into a Self-Help Group (SHG), ensuring that no poor 
household is left behind. The identification of poor households is 
undertaken through the Socio-Economic and Caste Census (SECC) 
2011 and the Participatory Identification of Poor (PIP) process. 
Recognizing that poverty and social exclusion are multidimensional, 
the Mission places special emphasis on reaching the most vulnerable 
and marginalized groups, including Scheduled Castes (SCs), 
Scheduled Tribes (STs), Particularly Vulnerable Tribal Groups 
(PVTGs), minorities, persons with disabilities (PwDs), elderly 
persons, transgender persons, single women, women-headed 
households, migrant families, and other socially excluded 
communities.  
 
The Deendayal Antyodaya Yojana–National Rural Livelihoods 
Mission (DAY-NRLM) is being implemented to strengthen the 
functioning of Self-Help Groups (SHGs) through continuous capacity 
building in group management, financial literacy, bookkeeping, and 
livelihoods. Funds are provided to SHGs in the form of Revolving Fund 
(RF) and Community Investment Fund (CIF) to strengthen their 
financial base, along with facilitating savings, bank credit, interest 
subvention, and other financial services. The Mission also promotes 
sustainable farm and non-farm livelihoods, enterprise development, 
skill enhancement, and market linkages, while strengthening Village 
Organisations (VOs) and Cluster Level Federations (CLFs) for 
institutional support. Further, community cadres such as Bank 
Sakhis, Krishi Sakhis, and Pashu Sakhis provide last-mile services.  
 
(b): The total number of SHGs formed under DAY-NRLM scheme is 
given at Annexure -I and total amount of bank loan disbursed to 
states/UTs is placed at Annexure-II. Bank loan disbursed to Dewas- 
Shajapur, Kangra and Chamba Lok Sabha Constituencies of Madhya 
Pradesh and Himachal Pradesh are given at Annexure - III & IV 
respectively.  
 
(c): The NPA data is not maintained district wise, however, the NPA 
account & amount in respect of Madhya Pradesh is 14308 and 

Page 3 of 10 
 
Rs.13,305 lakh respectively and as far as Himachal Pradesh 
concerned NPA Accounts is 478 and amount is Rs.638.56 lakh.  
  
(d) & (e): In order to enhance the income of SHGs through dairy 
activities following measures are undertaken by the Government. 
i. The Department of Animal Husbandry & Dairying (DAHD) is 
implementing schemes such as National Programme for Dairy 
Development (NPDD), Supporting Dairy Cooperatives & Farmer 
Producer Organisations engaged in dairy activities (SDCFPO), 
Animal Husbandry Infrastructure Development Fund (AHIDF) 
across the country to complement and supplement the efforts 
of State Governments in strengthening dairy infrastructure. 
These schemes aim to expand the network of dairy 
cooperatives, strengthen dairy infrastructure, meet working 
capital needs. These measures help to strengthen 
cooperatives, expand the organised dairy sector, and ensure 
that milk producers receive the maximum share of the 
consumer price. The SHGs are eligible to avail assistance under 
the schemes as per the norms of the scheme.  
ii. Under DAY-NRLM, special attention has been given to promote 
women owned dairy based collectives who are into 
aggregation, value addition and marketing of milk. These 
collectives have also been provided support for milk collection, 
processing and marketing.  
iii. Besides, the SHGs members are mobilised by the States to 
aggregate and supply milk to local dairy cooperatives and 
companies. 
  
(f): The Lakhpati Didi initiative is an outcome of DAY-NRLM. The 
objective of the initiative is to enable SHG member earn an income 
of at least Rs.1.00 lakh as on sustainable basis (for 4 agricultural / 
business cycles). The mission is facilitating SHG members through 
structural approach of identifying potential Lakhpati Didi, training & 
facilitating them to have income generating activities. So far, 3.46 
crore Lakhpati Didis have been enabled across the country, including 
24,000 in Meerut and 13,000 in Hapur, Uttar Pradesh.

2695. SHRI PARIMAL SUKLABAIDYA:  
 
Will the Minister of HEAVY INDUSTRIES be pleased to state:  
 
(a) the progress made in the implementation of the PM E -DRIVE Scheme in Assam, particularly in 
Cachar district, including the number of electric vehicles registered and reimbursement claims 
processed;  
 
(b) the details of public EV charging stations sanctioned, installed and operational in Cachar district 
and along the Guwahati–Silchar highway and other major corridors in Assam;  
 
(c) whether the Government has assessed the fuel savings and reduction in carbon dioxide emissions 
achieved through electric vehicle adoption in Assam, particularly in Cachar district; and  
 
(d) the steps taken to promote electric mobility, strengthen charging infrastructure and encourage the 
adoption of electric public t ransport and commercial vehicles in Cachar district and other parts of 
Assam? 
 
ANSWER 
THE MINISTER OF STATE FOR HEAVY INDUSTRIES 
(SHRI BHUPATHIRAJU SRINIVASA VARMA) 
 
(a): The PM E -DRIVE Scheme is being implemented on a pan -India basis, and no State -wise 
allocation of funds has been made. As on 22.07.2026, a total of 42,035 EVs have been sold in Assam, 
under this Scheme which includes 8,003 EVs sold in Cachar district. Furth er, a total of 40,009 EVs 
have been incentivised in Assam with a total reimbursement of  ₹ 99.10 crore to OEMs.  
 
(b): An allocation of ₹2,000 crore has been made under the PM E-DRIVE Scheme for deployment 
of Electric Vehicle Public Charging Stations (EVPCS) on pan India basis including the state of Assam.  
Assam has not yet submitted any proposal for deployment of EVPCS under the PM E -DRIVE 
scheme.    
 
(c): No such assessment has been done by the Ministry of Heavy Industries (MHI)  for Cachar 
district of Assam. 
 
(d): The MHI is implementing following schemes to promote electric mobility, strengthen 
charging infrastructure and encourage the adoption of electric public transport  and commercial 
vehicles across the country including Cachar district and other parts of Assam: 
 
i. Faster Adoption and Manufacturing of (Hybrid &) Electric Vehicles in India (FAME India) 
Scheme Phase-II: The Government implemented this scheme for a period of five years from 
01.04.2019 to 31.03.2024 with a total budgetary support of ₹11,500 crore. The scheme provided 
demand incentive for e -2Ws, e-3Ws, e-4Ws and grant for e -buses and setting up of EV public 
charging stations (EV PCS). FAME-II has supported the sale of approximately 16.72 lakh electric 
vehicles, including e-2Ws, e-3Ws, and e -4Ws. In addition, 5, 297 electric buses (e -buses) have 
been deployed under the Scheme as on 30.06.2026. Further, an amount of ₹912.50 crore was 
allocated under the Scheme for the establishment of EVPCS across the country. 

 
ii. Production Linked Incentive (PLI) Scheme for Automobile and Auto Component Industry 
in India (PLI -Auto): The Government notified this scheme for Automobile and Auto 
Component Industry in India, on 23.09.2021, for enhancing India's manufacturing capabilities for 
Advanced Automotive Technology (AAT) products, including EVs, with a budgetary outlay of 
₹25,938 crore.  
 
iii. Production Linked Incentive (PLI) Scheme for National Programme on Advanced 
Chemistry Cell (ACC) Battery Storage :  The Government on 09.06.2021  notified the PLI  
Scheme for manufacturing of ACC in the country with a budgetary outlay of ₹18,100 crore. The 
scheme aims to establish a competitive domestic manufacturing ecosystem for 50 GWh of ACC 
batteries. 
 
iv. PM Electric Drive Revolution in Innovative Vehicle Enhancement (PM EDRIVE) Scheme: 
This scheme with an outlay of ₹10,900 crore is implemented from 01.04.2024 . This scheme 
supports incentivization of approximately 28.30 lakh electric vehicles (EVs) including e -2W, e-
3W, e-Trucks, e-buses and e -Ambulances. Further, grant for EV public charging stations (EV 
PCS) and upgradation of testing agencies is also available under this scheme. An allocation of 
₹4,391 crore has been made under the scheme for deployment of 14,028 e -buses out of which 
13,800 e-buses have been allocated in seven cities having four million plus population viz. Delhi, 
Bengaluru, Hyderabad, Mumbai, Ahmedabad, Pune and Surat. Further, 200 e -buses have been 
approved for Union Territory of Jammu & Kashmir. ₹2,000 crore has been allocated for 
deployment of EV Public Charging Stations on pan India basis.   
 
v. PM e -Bus Sewa -Payment Security Mechanism (PSM) Scheme : This Scheme notified on 
28.10.2024, has an outlay of ₹3,435.33 crore and aims to support deployment of more than 38,000 
electric buses. The objective of this scheme is to provide payment security to e -bus operators in 
case of default by Public Transport Authorities (PTAs). 
 
 Following initiatives have also been taken up by the Government of India to increase the 
use  of electric vehicles in the country: – 
i.  GST on electric vehicles and chargers/ charging stations for electric vehicles has been 
reduced to 5%. 
ii.  Ministry of Road Transport & Highways (MoRTH) announced that battery -operated 
vehicles will be given green license plates and be exempted from permit requirements. 
iii. MoRTH issued advisory to states to waive road tax on EVs, which in turn will help reduce 
the initial cost of EVs.

(b) to (d): Gross FDI inflows have increased from over USD 34 billion in 2012 -13 to over 
USD 94.84 billion in 2025 -26. The 2025 -26 gross inflo ws represent a 17 % 
increase compared to 2024 -25 (USD 80.62 billion). It is the highest ever FDI 
inflow reported in the FY. The recent trend in net FDI inflows is associated with 
increased FDI by India as well as greater repatriation. The increase in ODI 
outflow underscores the growing global aspirations and capabilities of Indian 
enterprises as they venture abroad to acquire strategic assets, access new 
markets and tap into advanced technologies. The repatriations/ disinvestments 
indicate a maturing invest ment ecosystem where foreign investors are 
monetising investments after successfully scaling up Indian enterprises, 
transfer of ownership to domestic investors reflecting strengthening of domestic 
capital and entrepreneurial capacity. 
The Government has ta ken various steps/initiatives for promotion and 
facilitation of industries such as Make in India, Ease of Doing Business, Startup 
India, Production Linked Incentives (PLI) Schemes for various sectors, Focus 
Sub Sectors, Phased Manufacturing Programme (PMP) , One District One 
Product (ODOP), Industrial Information System (IIS) which provides GIS -
enabled database of industrial areas including clusters, parks, nodes, zones 
etc., and a comprehensive Single Window System (Investment Clearance Cell). 
To promote FD I, the Government has put in place an investor friendly policy, 
wherein most sectors, except certain strategically important sectors, are open 
for 100% FDI under the automatic route. More than 90% of the FDI inflow is 
received under the automatic route. Na tional Single Window System (NSWS) 
has also been launched as the online single point interface of the Government 
of India for investors to start any industry in India and take requisite 
permissions. FDI policy provisions have been progressively liberalised  and 
simplified across various sectors such as Pension, Other Financial Services, 
Asset reconstruction Companies, Broadcasting, Pharmaceuticals, Single Brand 
Retail Trading, Construction & Development, Power Exchanges, e -commerce 
activities, Coal Mining, Contract Manufacturing, Digital Media, Civil Aviation etc. 
In the recent past,  reforms in the FDI Policy have been undertaken in sectors 
such as Defence, Insurance, Petroleum & Natural Gas, Telecom and Space.  
 

To complement the reforms, eﬀorts have been un dertaken to ensure a 
seamless business regulatory framework across the country and nudge states 
to promote healthy competition to attract investments. The Government of India 
released Business Reforms Action Plan (BRAP) 2024 rankings and Logistics 
Ease Across Diﬀerent States (LEADS) 2024 report to inter-alia communicate to 
potential investors examples of positive business ecosystem as well as logistics 
performance undertaken by various States and UTs. Under the Regulatory 
Compliance Burden (RCB) excercise, 47,865 compliances reduced since 2020 
out of which 16,136 simplified, 22,289 digitised, 5,170 decriminalised, 4,270 
redundancies removed. Through the Jan Vishwas (Amendment of Provisions) 
Act, 2023, the Government has decriminalised 183 provisions across 4 2 
Central Acts from 19 Ministries/Departments. Building upon the Jan Vishwas 
Act, 2023, the Government undertook a comprehensive review of central laws 
and introduced the Jan Vishwas (Amendment of Provisions) Act, 2026, which 
amends 784 provisions across 7 9 Central Acts administered by 23 Ministries. 
Of these, 717 provisions have been decriminalized to promote Ease of Doing 
Business, while 67 provisions have been amended to facilitate Ease of Living. 
 
Furthermore, to ensure that India remains an attractive and investor friendly 
destination, the Government reviews FDI policy on an ongoing basis and makes 
changes from time to time.
