GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE 
DEPARTMENT OF AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE 
 
LOK SABHA 
UN-STARRED QUESTION NO. 2697 
TO BE ANSWERED ON 4th AUGUST, 2026 
 
TECHNICAL TRAINING FOR SMALL AND MARGINAL FARMERS 
 
2697 SHRI MANICKAM TAGORE B: 
 
Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE कृ ͪष और ͩकसान 
कãयाण मंğी be pleased to state: 
(a) Whether the Government is aware that small and marginal farmers are facing 
difficulties in improving crop productivity due to lack of technical training and 
exposure to modern agricultural practices, if so, the details thereof; 
(b) Whether the Government has conducted any nationwide assessment on the 
impact of limited technical knowledge on crop yields of small landholders, if so, 
details  and key findings thereof; 
(c) Whether the existing agricultural extension services are adequately reaching 
small farmers with updated scientific practices, if so, the details  and gaps identified; 
(d) Whether the Government proposes to strengthen farmer training programs 
through Krishi Vigyan Kendras under Indian Council of Agricultural Research, if so, 
the details thereof and coverage achieved; and 
(e) Whether the lack of exposure to agro-industrial practices is affecting income 
potential of small farmers, if so, the details thereof and steps taken to bridge this 
gap? 
 
ANSWER 
 
THE MINISTER OF STATE FOR AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE 
कृ ͪष एवं ͩकसान कãयाण राÏय मंğी (SHRI RAMNATH THAKUR) 
(a) to (c): The Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare, Government of India 
continuously undertakes nationwide campaigns and awareness programmes in 
collaboration with the State Governments and with active involvement of Agriculture 
Technology Management Agency (ATMA), Indian Council of Agricultural Research 
and Krishi Vigyan Kendras to educate farmers on modern agricultural practices and 
enhance crop productivity, production and farmers income.  
  

 
 
       Under Sub-Mission on Agriculture Extension (SMAE), a Centrally Sponsored 
Scheme “Support to State Extension Programs for Extension Reforms” (Agricultural 
Technology Management Agency-ATMA) is being implemented by the Government 
of India in 734 districts of 28 states & 5 UTs for promoting decentralized and farmer-
friendly extension system in the country since 2005-06. The Scheme supports State 
Government’s efforts and to make available latest agricultural technologies and good 
agricultural practices in different thematic areas of agriculture and allied areas 
(Including improving crop productivity and exposure to modern agricultural practices) 
to farmers to modernize agriculture through different extension activities viz; Farmers 
Training, Demonstrations, Exposure Visits, Kisan Mela, Mobilization of Farmers 
Groups and organizing Farm Schools etc. Under this Scheme, it has been 
provisioned that at least 50% beneficiaries must be selected from Small & Marginal 
farmer category. 
 
   During the financial year 2025-26, 50.92 lakh farmers have been benefitted 
through different extension activities under the ATMA Scheme.  
 
      The Mass Media Support to Agriculture Extension Scheme creates awareness 
among farming communities and other stakeholders through the dissemination of 
information on DA&FW schemes, crop advisories, weather and market information, 
and region-specific modern agricultural technologies. The scheme leverages 
Doordarshan, All India Radio and digital and social media platforms to ensure wider 
outreach, timely access to knowledge and effective dissemination of farmer-centric 
information. 
      To educate farmers, the Ministry supports and organizes national/regional-level 
exhibitions/fairs to create awareness about various schemes, missions and new 
initiatives, while promoting appropriate technologies, improved agronomic practices 
and best practices among farmers and other stakeholders in the agriculture and 
allied sectors.  
     In addition, the Department operates Kisan Helpline Centres to provide a single-
window platform for farmers’ on agricultural advisories, information on Government 
schemes/programmes and grievance redressal.  
  

 
  
     Bharat-VISTAAR (Virtually Integrated System to Access Agricultural Resources) 
is a multilingual AI-powered Digital Public Infrastructure platform designed to provide 
farmers with reliable, real-time and location-specific agricultural advisories and 
access to various farmer support services. The platform integrates information on 
Government schemes, benefit status tracking, grievance redressal, weather updates, 
mandi prices, ICAR advisories and other agricultural services to enable informed 
decision-making and better crop management.  
     The Department of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare is implementing various 
flagship Schemes/Missions on crop diversification, organic farming and value 
addition, including Mission for Integrated Development of Horticulture (MIDH),  
Mission on Atmanirbharta in Pulses, National Mission on Edible Oils–Oilseeds 
(NMEO-OS), National Mission on Edible Oils–Oil Palm (NMEO-OP), National 
Mission on Natural Farming (NMNF), Paramparagat Krishi Vikas Yojana (PKVY), 
National Food Security and Nutrition Mission (NFSNM), National Bamboo Mission 
(NBM), Sub-Mission on Agricultural Mechanization (SMAM), Per Drop More Crop 
(PDMC), Farmer Producer Organizations (FPOs), Mission for Cotton Productivity 
(KAPAS KANTI), Central Integrated Pest Management Centres (CIPMCs), Crop 
Diversification Programme (CDP) and  National Bee Keeping and Honey Mission 
(NBHM).  
      Creation of awareness amongst farmers about the above Schemes and Missions 
are being implemented by the Department and is undertaken in collaboration with 
State Governments. In addition, awareness is created amongst farmers on modern 
agricultural practices and technical trainings are conducted across the country 
through the extensive network of 113 ICAR Institutes, 731 Krishi Vigyan Kendras 
and Agriculture Technology Management Agency (ATMA) across 734 districts of the 
country. 
   The impact and effectiveness of the Sub Mission on Agricultural Extension has 
been evaluated by NITI Aayog. The study indicates that agricultural extension 
services have significantly contributed in enhancing farmers’ awareness, adoption of 
new agricultural practices and improved farming decisions.  
  

 
 
     The study revealed that 92.33% of respondents reported that the training enabled 
them to adopt new agricultural interventions and practices. More than 70% of the 
beneficiaries rated the quality of training positively. Further, the assessment 
indicated that Mass Media interventions through television, radio and mobile 
applications were effective in disseminating agricultural information, with 90.5% of 
respondents stating that these information sources improved their farming decisions, 
particularly in the areas of crop planning, pest and disease management and market 
timing. 
(d):  Krishi Vigyan Kendras (KVKs) are using innovative training methodologies, 
modern tools, and experiential learning approaches to make capacity-building 
programmes more practical, participatory and outcome-oriented. Hands-on training 
is being emphasized in frontier areas such as precision agriculture, agri-drones, 
digital agriculture, and other climate-smart technologies to enhance farmers' practical 
skills. In addition, KVKs are using the concept of ‘Model Demonstration Farms’ to 
build farmers' confidence, facilitate peer learning, and develop Communities of 
Practice. Innovative farmers are being nurtured as Professors of Practice and 
engaged as Master Trainers to strengthen farmer-to-farmer knowledge 
dissemination and local capacity building. KVKs also organise training of the farmers 
who have been trained earlier for re-skilling and upskilling to reinforce knowledge, 
introduce emerging technologies, and obtain real-time feedback for continuous 
improvement. During 2025-26, the KVKs trained 22.22 lakh farmers for their 
knowledge and skill upgradation on latest agricultural technologies.  
(e):  Agriculture Infrastructure Fund (AIF) Scheme facilitates medium- to long-term 
debt financing for creation of post-harvest management infrastructure and viable 
farming assets. The Scheme provides 3% interest subvention and credit guarantee 
support on loans up to ₹2 crore for eligible borrowers, subject to a maximum lending 
rate of 9% per annum. The implementation of the scheme is reviewed through the 
monitoring mechanism prescribed in the Scheme Guidelines at the National, State 
and District levels by the National Level Monitoring Committee (NLMC), State Level 
Monitoring Committees (SLMCs) and District Level Monitoring Committees (DLMCs). 
The progress of the Scheme is also monitored through the digital AIF Portal.  
As on 15.07.2026, a total of 2,08,828 projects has been sanctioned under the AIF, 
involving loans amounting to ₹93,374.36 crore.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF FISHERIES, ANIMAL HUSBANDRY AND DAIRYING 
DEPARTMENT OF ANIMAL HUSBANDRY AND DAIRYING 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION No. 2699 
ANSWERED ON 04TH AUGUST 2026 
 
RASHTRIYA GOKUL MISSION 
 
2699. SHRI THARANIVENTHAN M S:  
SHRI ANURAG SHARMA:  
  
Will the Minister of FISHERIES, ANIMAL HUSBANDRY AND DAIRYING 
मत्स्यपालन, पशुपालन और डेयरी मंत्री 
be pleased to State: 
 
(a)  whether the Government will furnish the year -wise details of implementation of the 
Rashtriya Gokul Mission (RGM) since its inception, including number of indigenous breed 
development centres, semen stations, bulls inducted and artificial insemination cover age 
achieved, State-wise, including Lok Sabha Constituency, Arani of Tamil Nadu;  
(b)  the details of funds allocated, released and utilised and the number of farmers benefited 
under the Mission during the last five years, State-wise including Tamil Nadu;  
(c)  whether any assessment has been conducted on improvement in milk productivity, 
genetic upgradation and conservation of indigenous bovine breeds, if so, the details thereof;  
(d)  whether challenges such as uneven breed coverage, infrastructure gaps and shortage of 
trained personnel have been reported and corrective steps taken by the Government thereon;  
(e)  the steps taken by the Government to strengthen indigenous cattle conservation, expand 
artificial insemination and advance breeding technologies, expand AI network and improve 
dairy farmer income and enhance the productivity and sustainability of dairy sec tor in the 
country including particularly in Tamil Nadu and allied sector support;  
(f)  the progress made under the Mission including the number of Gokul Grams, semen 
stations, In-Vitro Fertilization (IVF) laboratories and other breeding infrastructure established, 
State/UT-wise; and  
(g)  the details of indigenous cattle breed conserved and genetically improved under the 
Mission, along with the increase in milk productivity achieved? 
 
ANSWER 
THE MINISTER OF FISHERIES, ANIMAL HUSBANDRY AND DAIRYING 
(SHRI RAJIV RANJAN SINGH ALIAS LALAN SINGH) 
 
(a) to (g) In order to supplement the efforts of the States and Union Territories, Department of 
Animal Husbandry and Dairying (DAHD), Government of India is implementing Rashtriya 
Gokul Mission (RGM) since December 2014 for development and conservation of indigenous 
breeds, genetic upgradation of bovine population and enhancement of milk production and 
productivity. All indigenous bovine breeds as notified by National Bureau of Animal Genetic 
Resources are covered and promoted under the scheme.  The RGM scheme is demand driven 
and the proposals received from the States/UTs are considered as per guidelines. 

During the last five years, an amount of Rs . 12,748.69 lakh have been released and 
utilized in Tamil Nadu under National Programme for Dairy Development (NPDD) scheme for 
the creation and strengthening of dairy infrastructure in the State. 
The implementation of the Rashtriya Gokul Mission (RGM) and other measures 
undertaken by the Department of Animal Husbandry and Dairying and State Government, the 
milk production in the country has increased from 146 Million Tonnes in 2014 -15 to 248 
Million Tonnes in 2024 -25 that is by 70%. The productivity of indigenous and non -descript 
cattle in the country has improved from 2.54 kilograms per animal per day in 2014–15 to 3.86 
kilograms per animal per day in 2024 –25. Similarly, the total milk production in  Tamil Nadu 
has grown from 7.13 million tonnes in 2014-15 to 11.44 million tonnes in 2024–25, reflecting 
an impressive 60% increase and the productivity of indigenous and non-descript cattle in Tamil 
Nadu has improved from 2.65 kilograms per animal per day in 2014–15 to 3.28 kilograms per

MISAPPROPRIATION OF FUNDS UNDER PMFBY 
 
2701. SHRI NEERAJ MAURYA: 
 
Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE क ृ िष एवं िकसान कʞाण मंũी  
be pleased to state :   
 
(a) whether the attention of the Government has been drawn to the crop insurance scam 
exposed in Uttar Pradesh, where compensation worth crores of rupees was 
misappropriated on the basis of fake land records (Khatauni) without actual agricultural 
land; 
(b) whether insurance claims were distributed to four times the number of actual farmers 
in several villages and 90% of the fraudulent activities were carried out in the names of 
non-loanee farmers; 
(c) the role played by the collusion of bank officials and insurance companies in this 
matter, and whether the Government will conduct a technical investigation into the portals 
that automatically approved fake data numbers; and 
(d) whether the Government proposes a comprehensive action plan to ensure the data 
security of farmers in the future? 
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE FOR AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE  
क ृ िष एवं िकसान कʞाण राǛ मंũी  (SHRI RAMNATH THAKUR) 
(a)   State Government of Uttar Pradesh has informed that the instances of fraudulent 
insurance obtained through forged means by certain persons under the Pradhan Mantri 
Fasal Bima Yojana (PMFBY) in certain districts of the State have come to the notice of 
the Government. The cases were immediately investigated and necessary action, as per 
rules, has been taken against the persons found guilty. The details are as under:  
 
 In district Mahoba, a total of 06 First Information Reports (FIRs) have been registered, 
60 persons have been named and 50 persons have been arrested.  
 
 In district Jhansi, 02 FIRs have been registered, 11 persons have been named, and 01 
person is in judicial custody. Recovery process of the compensation amount obtained 
through wrongful means has also been effected in respect of 10 persons pertaining to 
Simardha Gram Panchayat and in Naya Gaon.  
 
 In district Hamirpur, 1,145 insurance policies pertaining to 391 non-loanee farmers for 
Kharif 2025 season were found to be incorrect during investigation and have since been 
cancelled.  
 
 In district Farrukhabad, during Rabi 2024-25, 35 persons from 03 villages of the district 
wrongfully obtained compensation.  During investigation, 02 FIRs have been registered 
against 03 Tehsil Coordinators of insurance companies, 06 Bank Branch Managers and 
21 farmers among others.  

 
 In district Mathura, upon detection of cases of duplicate insurance during Rabi 2021-22, 
investigation revealed that compensation had been obtained through 267 applications 
submitted by 152 persons. Recovery amounting to ₹27,52,123.13 relating to 22 
applications of 17 persons has been made. Further, compensation amounting to 
₹14,34,382.55 received against 15 applications relating to 06 other persons has been 
refunded. Thus, a total amount of ₹41,86,505.68 has been recovered in the district.  
 
 In the State, following investigation under PMFBY, 1,19,531 insurance applications for 
Kharif 2025 season and 36,247 insurance applications for Rabi 2025-26 season have 
been cancelled. 
 
 
(b) :    No, Sir.  State Govt. of Uttar Pradesh has informed that no such case has come to 
the notice of the State Government so far.  
 
(c) & (d) :  During investigation by the State Government, the involvement of personnel of 
banks/insurance companies has been found in the districts of Jhansi, Mahoba and 
Farrukhabad. 
 
The Government of India has also taken cognizance of the matter and has issued 
necessary directions to all insurance companies implementing the Scheme, CSC e-
Governance India Limited, and all participating banks to strengthen scrutiny of enrolment 
proposals and ensure strict compliance with the Operational Guidelines of PMFBY. 
 
Land records data of Uttar Pradesh has already been integrated with National Crop 
Insurance Portal (NCIP).  Further, from the ensuing crop season, a provision has been 
made under the NCIP whereby all applications pertaining to consolidation 
(Chakbandi)/non-digitized villages shall be accepted by the concerned insurance 
company only after verification and approval by the District Level Monitoring Committee 
(DLMC) headed by the District Magistrate. 
 
Necessary instructions have already been issued to the insurance companies and 
the States/Union Territories in respect of localised crop loss assessment. As per these 
instructions, crop loss assessment is required to be conducted in the presence of the 
designated Government field functionary, keeping transparency while recording the 
assessment and a copy of the survey report is mandatory to be handover to the 
concerned farmer. Further, the process of localised crop loss assessment is done through 
the Crop Loss Assessment Process (CLAP) module under PMFBY. 
 
In order to prevent fraudulent applications under the scheme, various verification 
and validation protocols have been implemented at the stage of enrolment of farmers 
under the scheme in National Crop Insurance Portal (NCIP) such as Aadhar validation of 
farmers, bank account validation through PFMS, land record validation through ROR of 
the States/UTs, AgriStack farmer ID validation and insured Crop validation with Digital 
Crop Survey, etc.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE 
DEPARTMENT OF AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE 
 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION No. 2702 
TO BE ANSWERED ON 04th August, 2026 
 
FARMER WELFARE INITIATIVES 
 
2702. SHRI VIJAYAKUMAR ALIAS VIJAY VASANTH: 
 
Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE कृ ͪष एवं ͩकसान 
कãयाण मंğी be pleased to state: 
 
(a) whether the Government has initiated collaborations between farmers and 
agri-industries for skill development and market linkage, if so, the details thereof and 
outcomes achieved so far; 
(b) whether soil degradation and declining fertility are major contributors to 
reduced crop productivity among small landholders, if so, the details thereof and 
studies conducted ; 
(c) whether the Government has implemented soil health management programs 
such as Soil Health Card Scheme effectively, if so, the details of coverage and 
impact assessment in this regard; 
(d) whether climate change and erratic weather patterns are further compounding 
challenges faced by small farmers, if so, the details thereof and mitigation measures 
taken; and  
(e) whether the Government proposes to provide financial assistance or 
subsidies for adoption of modern technologies like precision farming and micro-
irrigation and if so, the details thereof ? 
 
ANSWER 
 
THE MINISTER OF STATE FOR AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE  
कृ ͪष एवं ͩकसान कãयाण राÏय मंğी  (SHRI RAMNATH THAKUR)  
 
(a): The Government has initiated collaborations between farmers and agri 
industries for skill development and market linkage. The details are given below. 
 
(i) A Centrally Sponsored Scheme “Support to State Extension Programs for 
Extension Reforms” (ATMA) is being implemented in 734 districts of 28 states & 5 
UTs in the country. The scheme promotes decentralized and farmer-friendly 
extension system in the country. The objective of the Scheme is to support State 
Government’s efforts and to make available latest agricultural technologies and good 
agricultural practices in different thematic areas of agriculture and allied areas to 
farmers through different extension activities viz; Farmers Training, Demonstrations, 
Exposure Visits, Kisan Mela, Mobilization of Farmers Groups and organizing Farm 
Schools etc. Skill training is also one among the components under the ATMA 
cafeteria. A total of 17,366 farmers have been trained during 2025-26 through 
DA&FW skill training programme under ATMA. 
 

(ii) Agriculture Skill Council of India (ASCI) through Centres of Excellence for 
Agriculture Skills in India (CEASI)  has collaborated with multiple agri-industry 
partners for the skill development and capacity building of farmers, Wage workers, 
Farmer Producer Organizations (FPOs), and rural youth through CSR-funded and 
Industry-funded initiatives with industry partners. The training covers governance of 
FPOs, farm mechanization, financial management, business planning, price risk 
management, and market linkages, thereby strengthening the institutional capacity of 
FPOs and enhancing their preparedness for market engagement. These capacity – 
building programmes are aimed at strengthening the capacities of farmers, FPOs 
and Rural Youth through Industry-aligned skilling on business planning, financial 
management, price risk management, and market oriented practices.  
  
(b) & (c):      Crop productivity is reduced due to several factors like seeds, package 
of practices, climate change, soil degradation, etc. Ministry of Agriculture and 
Farmers Welfare addresses these challenges through soil test-based balanced and 
integrated nutrient management, Soil Test Crop Response (STCR)-based district 
general fertilizer recommendations, conservation agriculture, organic resource 
recycling, biofertilizers and reclamation of degraded lands. These technologies 
improve soil health, enhance nutrient use efficiency and sustain crop productivity. 
During the Khet Bachao Abhiyan, farmers training were organized under Agricultural 
Technology Management Agency Scheme (ATMA).  
 
      Government promotes judicious use of fertilizer through Soil Health & Fertility 
scheme. The scheme is being implemented since 2014-15 to provide Soil Health 
Cards (SHCs) for all farm holdings, to promote balanced and integrated nutrient 
management for improving productivity and soil fertility. Soil samples are processed 
as per standard procedures and analysed for parameters such as pH, Electrical 
Conductivity, Organic Carbon, available Nitrogen, Phosphorus, Potassium, Sulphur, 
and micronutrients (Zinc, Copper, Iron, Manganese & Boron). The diagnostic soil 
health assessment of farmer fields is taken up periodically so as to issue SHCs at 
least once in 3 years.  
 
       Since 2014-15, 26.10 crore Soil Health Cards have been generated/ distributed 
as on date across the country. Total 8313 Soil Testing Labs (1267 Static Soil Testing 
Labs, 168 Mobile Soil Testing Labs, 6197 Mini Soil Testing Labs and 681 Village 
Level Soil Testing Labs) have been established across the country. In addition to 
state soil labs above, 1020 school mini soil labs are also established in the country 
under school soil health programme. 93781 farmer’s trainings, 6.80 lakh 
demonstrations, 7425 farmer’s melas/campaigns on soil health card 
recommendations have been organized across the country. 1351166 ha area also 
covered under Promotion & Distribution of Micronutrients in the scheme. 

     The National Food Security & Nutrition Mission (NFSNM) (formerly NFSM) helps 
reduce soil degradation by promoting sustainable crop and nutrient management 
rather than focusing only on increasing production. The mission explicitly supports 
integrated nutrient management, conservation of land resources, and improved 
farming practices. 
 
      The National Mission on Natural Farming (NMNF) was launched as a Centrally 
Sponsored Scheme in November 2024 to promote chemical-free, nature-based 
farming. One of its core objectives is to improve soil health and reverse soil 
degradation by reducing dependence on synthetic fertilizers and pesticides. 
 
      Paramparagat Krishi Vikas Yojana (PKVY) is a Government of India scheme 
launched in 2015 to promote organic farming. It was initially a component of Soil 
Health Management (SHM) under the National Mission for Sustainable Agriculture 
(NMSA) and is now implemented under Pradhan Mantri Rashtriya Krishi Vikas 
Yojana (PM-RKVY). Its primary objective is to improve soil health, conserve natural 
resources, and reduce dependence on chemical inputs. 
 
      National Productivity Council (NPC), New Delhi carried out a study 'Soil Testing 
Infrastructure for Faster Delivery of SHC in India' in 76 districts of 19 States covering 
170 soil testing labs and 1700 farmers. As a result of application of fertilizer and 
micronutrients as per SHC recommendations, there has been a decrease of use of 
chemical fertilizer application in the range of 8-10% was found. Overall 5-6% 
increase in the yield of crops was reported, due to application of fertilizer and 
micronutrients as per SHC. An impact study of Soil Health & Fertility Scheme 
was conducted by National Institute of Agricultural Extension Management 
(MANAGE), Hyderabad. As per report, about 62.8% of the farmers use fertilizers 
according to the recommendations on the SHC.  The cost per acre reduced by 4 to 
10 % due to low fertilizer use. Crop yields increased for majority of the crops, 
although moderately. Overall, paddy farmers reduced use of urea by 9%, 
Diammonium Phosphate (DAP)/Single Super Phosphate by 7%. There was 
substantial decline in fertilizer use especially urea and DAP in paddy and cotton 
resulted in decreased cost of cultivation per unit area. 

(d): Indian Council of Agricultural Research (ICAR) is implementing a project- 
National Innovations in Climate Resilient Agriculture (NICRA) that studies the impact 
of climate change on agriculture, conducts district level risk and vulnerability 
assessment of agriculture to future climate change and integrated simulation 
modelling studies for estimating the future projections of climate change. Under the 
project, risk and vulnerability assessment of agriculture to climate change has been 
carried out at district-level for 651 predominantly agricultural districts as per 
Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC) protocols. 310 districts were 
identified as vulnerable out of which 109 districts have been categorized as ‘very 
high’ and 201 districts as ‘highly’ vulnerable. District Agriculture Contingency Plans 
(DACPs) for these 651 districts have also been prepared to address weather 
aberrations and recommending location specific climate resilient crops and varieties 
and management practices. To enhance resilience to climate variability, location-
specific climate-resilient technologies, including the System of Rice Intensification 
(SRI), aerobic rice, direct-seeded rice, zero-till wheat, climate-resilient crop varieties, 
and in-situ crop residue management, are being demonstrated for adoption by 
farmers. Under NICRA, climate-resilient technologies are being demonstrated in 448 
Climate Resilient Villages across 151 vulnerable districts in 28 States/UTs, 
supported by village-level seed banks and community nurseries to enhance farmers' 
resilience and ensure timely availability of quality seeds. 
 
     Climate change and erratic weather patterns impact agriculture. Government is 
promoting resilience in agriculture through sustainable agricultural practices under 
various schemes, such as Per Drop More Crop (PDMC) for improving water-use 
efficiency through micro-irrigation; Rainfed Area Development (RAD) for promoting 
Integrated Farming Systems; Paramparagat Krishi Vikas Yojana (PKVY) for organic 
farming; National Mission on Natural Farming (NMNF) for natural farming; Mission 
for Aatmanirbharta in Pulses, National Mission on Edible Oils–Oilseeds (NMEO-OS) 
and National Food Security & Nutrition Mission (NFSNM) that also promote crop 
diversification; Mission for Integrated Development of Horticulture (MIDH) for 
horticulture development; Agroforestry for farmland ecology etc. 
  
         DA&FW is leveraging satellite-based monitoring and Artificial Intelligence (Al)-
based analytical systems for forecasting agricultural risks and supporting timely crop 
management interventions across the country. The Krishi Decision Support System 
(DSS) that integrates and standardizes geospatial and non-geospatial data, including 
satellite, weather, soil, crop signatures, reservoir and ground water data, enables 
monitoring of drought conditions, adverse weather events and flood inundation to 
provide near real-time risk alerts and support crop management interventions to 
reduce risk of crop loss across States/UTs.  

    The India Meteorological Department (IMD) provides Al-based monsoon and 
weather advisories across the country to support informed agricultural decision-
making. The advisories enable farmers to plan agricultural operations based on 
timely and location-specific weather forecasts. 
 
    The Government has also introduced yield-based Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima 
Yojana (PMFBY) and weather index based Restructured Weather Based Crop 
Insurance Scheme (RWBCIS) from Kharif 2016 to provide financial support to the 
farmers opting for crop insurance against crop loss/damage arising out of natural 
calamities, adverse weather incidence and to stabilize the income of farmers etc. 
Comprehensive risk insurance is provided under the scheme from pre-sowing to 
post- harvest losses. Further, with effect from Kharif 2023, Government has rolled 
out Yield Estimation System based on Technology (YES-TECH) wherein yield 
estimation is done using satellite imagery and remote sensing data. 
 
 
(e): Support for micro-irrigations provided under the Pradhan Mantri Krishi 
Sinchayee Yojana–Per Drop More Crop (PMKSY-PDMC) in accordance with the 
prescribed scheme norms. The Government provides financial assistance @ 55% for 
small and marginal farmers and @ 45% for other farmers for installation of Drip and 
Sprinkler systems under the PDMC. The Assistance for installation of Micro Irrigation 
systems is limited to 5 hectares per beneficiary.  
 
     Under the Mission for Integrated Development of Horticulture (MIDH), 
government provides financial assistance for adoption of modern technologies in 
horticulture, including precision farming, protected cultivation and efficient water 
management practices. Under the scheme, assistance is available for establishment 
of Protected Cultivation structures such as Poly houses, Shade-net Houses and 
Plastic Tunnels, which facilitate precision cultivation through controlled growing 
conditions. Financial assistance is generally provided at 50% for these structures, 
subject to the norms and ceilings prescribed under the MIDH guidelines. Support is 
provided for add-on components under protected cultivation, including hydroponics, 
aeroponics, circulation fans (in polyhouses), sensor-based automation systems for 
fertigation, and support systems for vegetable crops, as per the approved norms 
under the scheme. The scheme also supports the establishment of Hi-tech 
Nurseries.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF FISHERIES, ANIMAL HUSBANDRY AND DAIRYING 
DEPARTMENT OF ANIMAL HUSBANDRY AND DAIRYING 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO 2703 
ANSWERD ON 4TH AUGUST, 2026 
PASHUJANYA YUDH ABHYAS 
 
2703. SHRI KARTI P CHIDAMBARAM: 
 
Will the Minister of FISHERIES, ANIMAL HUSBANDRY AND DAIRYING  
मत्स्यपालन, पशुपालन और डेयरी मंत्री 
be pleased to state: 
 
(a) whether the Government has finalised the evaluation report of the national mock exercise, 
Pashujanya Yudh Abhyas, conducted under the National One Health Mission, if so, the details 
thereof;  
 
(b) whether the evaluation identified any gaps in disease surveillance, inter -agency coordination 
or emergency response mechanisms, if so, the details thereof;  
 
(c) whether any time-bound action plan has been prepared by the Government to address the gaps 
identified during the exercise, if so, the details thereof; and  
 
(d) the details of the measures taken or proposed to be taken by the Government to strengthen 
preparedness for future zoonotic disease outbreaks? 
 
ANSWER 
THE MINISTER OF FISHERIES, ANIMAL HUSBANDRY & DAIRYING 
(SHRI RAJIV RANJAN SINGH ALIAS LALAN SINGH) 
 
a) The Department of Animal Husbandry & Dairying  (DAHD), Government of India  has 
successfully conducted Pashujanya Yudh Abhyas (PYA), on animal health emergencies, at Khari 
village, Vidisha District, Madhya Pradesh, from 29th June 2026 to 3rd July 2026. The evaluation 
report for the mock drill is finalized capturing observations on bio safety and biosecurity, 
preparedness, coordination and communication mechanisms, and emergency response capabilities 
for managing zoonotic disease outbreaks. 
(b) and (c) The exercise provided an opportunity to identify the gaps in outbreak preparedness and 
response. Accordingly, it helped in strengthening the areas like timely communication, 
coordination, sampling and testing protocols, infection prevention and control, waste disposal, 
capacity building of response teams, documentation and information sharing across stakeholders. 
The exercise also highlighted the importance of continued capacity building and adherence to 
standard operating procedures.  

(d) The measures taken by the department to strengthen preparedness for future zoonotic disease 
outbreaks include: 
i. Under Livestock Health and Disease Control Programme (LHDCP) financial assistance is 
provided to States/UTs for training and awareness on Good Animal Husbandry Practices, 
Biosecurity/Sanitary measures, vaccination against animal diseases, disease surveillance a nd 
monitoring and capacity building which supports preparedness and response for disease 
management and outbreaks. 
ii. Department under the component of Assistance to States for Control of Animal Disease 
(ASCAD) of LHDCP supports States/UTs on sharing basis for State prioritised activities  such as 
capacity building, surveillance and monitoring of livestock diseases, training, prevention and 
control of zoonotic diseases including emergent and re-emergent diseases etc.  
iii. Formulated National Action Plan for Prevention, Control and Containment of Avian Influenza 
for preparedness and response including surveillance, biosecurity, culling operation, movement 
control, and post-operation monitoring. 
iv. The ‘Standard Veterinary Treatment Guidelines (SVTGs) has been developed for Livestock 
and Poultry’ for best practices in veterinary care to enhance livestock health and disease control 
while ensuring the responsible use of drugs including antimicrobials.  
v. Formulated the Crisis Management Plan (CMP) for Livestock Diseases’ for managing and 
responding to animal disease outbreaks, ensuring swift containment, mitigation and handling of 
animal health crises and reducing pandemic risks through prevention and control measures. 
vi. Advisories related to emergent infectious and zoonotic diseases issued to all States/UTs from 
time to time.  
vii. Formulated the National Action Plan for Control and Eradication for Glanders for prevention 
and control and containment of disease in definite time line.   
viii. The Department supports five designated Regional Disease Diagnostic Laboratories (RDDLs) 
and one Central Disease Diagnostic Laboratory (CDDL) for specialized and referral diagnostic 
services for livestock diseases. Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) for laboratory 
investigations, including sample collection, preservation and dispatch, are in place to promote 
uniformity and quality in laboratory diagnostics. 
ix. The Indian Council of Agricultural Research Research – National Institute of High Security 
Animal Diseases (ICAR -NIHSAD), Bhopal, functions as the national reference laboratory for 
emerging and exotic livestock and poultry diseases. 
x. One of the member of National Joint Outbreak Response Team is from DAHD.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF HOME AFFAIRS 
 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 2704 
 
TO BE ANSWERED ON THE 4TH AUGUST, 2026/ SHRAVANA 13, 1948 (SAKA) 
 
MANAGEMENT OF BORDERS 
 
†2704.   SHRI ANIL YESHWANT DESAI 
 
Will the Minister of HOME AFFAIRS be pleased to state: 
 
(a) whether it is the responsibility of the Government to see that no person 
should cross our border without proper authorization; 
 
(b) if so, the role of Para-military forces in this task; 
 
(c) whether the presence of large number of illegal people in the country 
shows negligence on the part of our authorities responsible for management 
of our borders; and 
 
(d) if so, the action taken by Government on the above and if not, the reasons 
therefor? 
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HOME AFFAIRS 
(SHRI NITYANAND RAI) 
 
 
(a) to (d) : The Government of India has undertaken several measures to curb 
cross-border infiltration along international borders. The Government of 
India, through its border guarding forces (BGFs), has adopted a multi-pronged 
approach to curb cross-border infiltration such as: 
 
 

-2- 
L.S.US.Q.NO. 2704 FOR 04.08.2026  
• Enhanced Border Surveillance : Deployment of advanced surveillance 
equipment such as CCTV, drones, automatic number plate recognition 
systems. 
• Strengthening Border Infrastructure : Development of fencing, border 
outposts, roads, and helipads to enhance vigilance and mobility of security 
forces. 
• Regular Patrolling & Checkpoints: Intensified area domination through 
patrolling, Naka points, and mobile teams to monitor illegal activities. 
• Intelligence & Coordination: Close collaboration between intelligence 
agencies and other organizations for real -time information sharing through 
established platforms. 
• Regulated Cross-Border Movement: Identification and management of 
designated entry/exit points to ensure controlled movement of people and 
goods. 
• Community Engagement & Awareness : Programs to educate border 
residents and discourage them from aiding illegal activities. 
• Cross-Border Cooperation : Coordination with neighbouring countries 
through meetings and joint initiatives to strengthen enforcement measures.

scheme in Madhya Pradesh, district-wise including Ratlam, Jhabua and Aliraipur districts;

fish production and marketing; and  
(d) if so, the details thereof and the future action plan of the Government in this regard?

Dairying, Government of India has been implementing the Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada 
Yojana (PMMSY) with a t otal outlay of Rs. 20,750 crore, with effect from the financial year

Territories including Madhya Pradesh. Under the PMMSY, the Department of Fisheries, 
Government of India has accorded approval to various fisheries developmental activities at a cost 
tune of Rs. 910.80 crore with central share of Rs. 305.50 crore, to the Government of Madhya

training and capacity building on modern equipment and best Aquaculture practices in 
collaboration with States/UTs and Central/State academic, training & research Institutions, 
including Indian Council of Agricultural Research (ICAR) institutes, Universities/Colleges, 
Fisheries Research Stations, Krishi Vigyan Kendras (KVKs), and empaneled firms/agencies.   The 
PMMSY inter-alia provides social security measure to fishers, fish workers through group 
accidental insurance coverage to both marine and inland fishers and allied fish workers wherein 
the entire insurance premium amount is shared between the Centre and State in the ratio of 60:40

the State governments on various interventions such as seed production of newly 
released varieties, distribution of certified seeds of high yielding & climate resilient 
varieties, seedkit distribution, demonstration of latest crop production technologies, 
capacity building and strengthening post-harvest infrastructure. In addition, 100% central 
assistance is given on purchase of breeder seeds to the States/UTs. The Mission also 
supports assured procurement of Masoor from willing and registered farmers through

Mantri Annadata Aay Sanrakshan Abhiyan (PM-AASHA), as per the requisition made by

2030-31.

(ICAR) is undertaking basic and strategic research on lentils at the ICAR-Indian Institute 
of Pulses Research (IIPR), Kanpur. In addition, applied research is being carried out 
through the All India Coordinated Research Project (AICRP) on Rabi Pulses in 
collaboration with the State Agricultural Universities and research institutes to develop 
location-specific, high-yielding varieties and appropriate production technology packages 
for enhancing the productivity and production of lentil in Uttar Pradesh, including 
Bahraich. As a result of these efforts, 20 high-yielding, climate-resilient lentil varieties 
have been notified for cultivation in Uttar Pradesh, including Bahraich, since 2018. 
To facilitate the adoption of newly released lentil varieties, about 368 quintals of 
breeder seed were produced during the last three years and supplied to the seed-
producing agencies for multiplication into certified seed for use by farmers across Uttar 
Pradesh, including Bahraich. Further, to enhance the availability of quality certified seeds 
of improved lentil varieties, about 4,996 quintals of certified seeds were produced during 
the last three years and made available through 14 Seed Hub on Pulses-centres 
established in the State under the aegis of ICAR. Additionally, to promote improved lentil 
varieties and production technologies, scientists associated with the AICRP at State 
Agricultural Universities conducted 421 Frontline Demonstrations (FLDs) on farmers' 
fields across Uttar Pradesh, including Bahraich, during the last three years. 
  

As reported by the State, the requirement and availability of certified/quality seeds 
of Lentils in Uttar Pradesh during the years 2023-24 to 2025-26 is as under: 
(Quantity of Seeds in lakh Qtls.)

1 2023-24 2.34 2.49

In addition, the Food Safety and Quality Assurance Infrastructure (FSQAI) is a 
demand-driven component scheme under the Pradhan Mantri Kisan SAMPADA Yojana 
(PMKSY), being implemented by the Ministry of Food Processing Industries (MoFPI). 
Under this scheme, the Ministry provides financial assistance for setting up Food Testing 
Laboratories. Proposals are invited from across the country through Expressions of 
Interest (EOIs) issued from time to time on the MoFPI Ministry's SAMPADA Portal. 
Presently, no proposal for the establishment of a Food Testing Laboratory in Bahraich is 
pending with the Ministry of Food Processing Industries.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF COOPERATION 
 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 2708 
TO BE ANSWERED ON 04th August, 2026 
 
Strengthening Cooperative Societies 
 
†2708. Shri Darshan Singh Choudhary: 
 
Will the Minister of COOPERATION (सहकारिता मंत्री) be pleased to state: 
 
(a) whether any special scheme or action plan is being implemented by the Government to set up 
new dairy cooperative societies in the country and to make the existing dairy cooperative societies 
more efficient, self-reliant and competitive; 
(b) the details of new dairy cooperative societies set up, societies funds strengthened, number of 
member farmers, funds allocated, utilized and achievements made during the last three years, 
State-wise; 
(c) whether the Government is taking any special initiative to provide financial and technical 
assistance to dairy cooperative societies for milk collection, cold societies chain, processing, value 
addition, quality testing, marketing, digitization and working capital; 
(d) if so, the details thereof; and  
(e) if not, the reasons therefor?  
 
 
ANSWER 
 
THE MINISTER OF COOPERATION 
(सहकारिता मंत्री) (SHRI AMIT SHAH) 
 
(a) and (b): As part of the National Plan for formation of new Multipurpose PACS, Dairy and 
Fishery Cooperative Societies to achieve cooperative coverage in every uncovered 
Panchayat/village over a period of five years, 25,552 new Dairy Cooperative Societi es (DCSs) 
have been registered across the country, so far. The State -wise details of newly formed Dairy 
Cooperative Societies and the member farmers associated with them are given at Annexure-I. 
 
Further, the Ministry of Cooperation, in convergence with the Department of Animal Husbandry 
& Dairying (DAHD), is implementing the National Programme for Dairy Development 

Page 2 of 10 
 
(NPDD) across the country to strengthen dairy cooperatives. The scheme comprises the following 
two components:  
Component A,  implemented across the country, supports creation and strengthening of 
infrastructure for milk testing, procurement, chilling, processing and value addition, including 
organization of new Dairy Cooperative Societies and strengthening of existing societies. 
Under Component A, during the last three years (2023 -24 to 2025 -26), 77 projects  have been 
sanctioned in 29 States/Union Territories, involving funds released of ₹353.71 crore. The details 
of projects sanctioned and funds released during the last three years are given at Annexure-II. 
 
From 2025–26, financial assistance has also been extended under Component A for organization 
of new Dairy Cooperative Societies. Accordingly, 25 projects have been approved in 25 States for 
formation of 11,689 new Dairy Cooperative Societies, with a total outlay of ₹193.03 crore, 
including a Central share of ₹103.23 crore. An amount of ₹68.44 crore has been released, of which 
₹38.89 crore has been utilized. State-wise details are given at Annexure-III. 
 
For strengthening existing Dairy Cooperative Societies, against a target of 46,422 societies during 
2024–25 to 2028 –29, 11,871 societies were strengthened during 2024 –25 and 19,526 societies 
during 2025–26. State-wise details are given at Annexure-IV. 
 
Under NPDD Component A, assistance is provided for milk collection, quality testing, chilling, 
processing and value addition. As on date, 6,580 Bulk Milk Coolers with a capacity of 159.45 lakh 
litres, 47,578 Automatic Milk Collection Units and 9,810 Electr onic Milk Adulteration Testing 
Units have been installed. 
 
Component B – Dairying through Cooperatives, implemented in nine States (Andhra Pradesh, 
Bihar, Madhya Pradesh, Punjab, Rajasthan, Telangana, Uttar Pradesh, Uttarakhand and West 
Bengal), supports modernization of dairy processing and marketing infrastructure and enhanc es 
farmers' access to organized markets. 
 
(c) and (d): Yes, Sir. The Government is providing financial and technical assistance to Dairy 
Cooperative Societies across the dairy value chain. In addition to the details mentioned above, 
under Component B of NPDD, 42 projects have been approved in the nine participating States. 
Financial assistance comprising ₹895.59 crore as loan and ₹381.43 crore as grant has been 
sanctioned, against which ₹787.96 crore as loan and ₹315.55 crore as grant have been released. 
State-wise details are given at Annexure-V. 
 
Financial assistance for modernization and expansion of dairy infrastructure is also 
provided under the Animal Husbandry Infrastructure Development Fund (AHIDF) and the Dairy 
Sahakar Scheme of the National Cooperative Development Corporation (NCDC). Working capital 
support is available through NCDC and interest subvention schemes, while RuPay Kisan Credit 

Page 3 of 10 
 
Cards, Micro -ATMs and digital banking facilities are being extended to dairy cooperative 
members. 
To strengthen marketing and value realization, cooperative dairy products are being promoted 
through the National Cooperative Exports Limited (NCEL) and digital marketing platforms. Under 
sustainability initiatives, Cooperative Inputs and Services Delivery  Multi-State Cooperative 
Society Ltd. and Gomay Sahkari Samiti Multi -State Cooperative Society Ltd. were registered on 
31.12.2025 to improve dairy productivity, input supply, manure management and farmers' income. 
 
(e): Does not arise in view of replies to parts (c) and (d) above.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF STEEL 
 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 2709 
FOR ANSWER ON 04.08.2026  
 
 
FUNDS FOR PLI SCHEME FOR SPECIALTY STEEL 
 
2709.  SHRI RADHAKRISHNA:  
 
Will the Minister of STEEL be pleased to state:  
 
(a) the committed investment, actual investment realised and incentive disbursed to 
date under the Production-Linked Incentive (PLI) scheme for Specialty Steel, 
company-wise;  
 
(b) the number of approved applicants at risk of deselection for missing the annual 
incremental production/investment threshold in two consecutive years;  
 
(c) the funds allocated, sanctioned, released and utilised under the scheme since its 
2023-24 launch; and  
 
(d) the progress in import substitution of specialty steel grades achieved so far against 
the scheme's stated targets? 
 
ANSWER 
 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE          (SHRI BHUPATHIRAJU SRINIVASA VARMA) 
MINISTRY OF STEEL 
 
(a)to(d): The Production Linked Incentive (PLI) Scheme for Specialty Steel has 
been approved with a financial outlay of ₹6,322 crore. The participating companies 
have committed investments of ₹56,106 crore. As on 30 June, 2026, actual investment 
of about ₹26,320 crore has been made by the participating companies and cumulative 
incremental production and import substitution of about 3.7 million tonnes has been 
achieved under the Scheme. Incentives amounting to ₹235.7 crore have been 
disbursed to eligible companies. The projects are reviewed periodically vis-à-vis the 
investment and production commitments, incentive claims and other provisions of the 
Scheme guidelines.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF PANCHAYATI RAJ 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 2710 
ANSWERED ON 04/08/2026 
  
RASHTRIYA GRAM SWARAJ ABHIYAN 
  
2710.   SHRI G LAKSHMINARAYANA: 
  
Will the Minister of PANCHAYATI RAJ be pleased to state: 
  
(a) the number of agencies, institutions or vendors penalised, de-empanelled or blacklisted under 
RGSA during the last three years, State-wise; 
(b) the mechanisms adopted for verification of attendance and utilisation of funds under RGSA 
training programmes; 
(c) the particularly Andhra Pradesh district-wise, Gram Panchayats generating Own Source 
Revenue (OSR) exceeding the prescribed threshold during the last three years, State-wise; 
(d) whether any assessment has been conducted regarding the effectiveness of RGSA capacity-
building programmes, if so, the details thereof; and 
  
(e) the measures taken to ensure authenticity of geo-tagged monitoring of Gram Panchayat assets 
and infrastructure projects? 
  
ANSWER 
  
THE MINISTER OF PANCHAYATI RAJ 
(SHRI RAJIV RANJAN SINGH ALIAS LALAN SINGH) 
  
(a) Panchayat, being “Local Self Government”, is a State subject. However, the Ministry of 
Panchayati Raj has been implementing the Centrally Sponsored Scheme of Rashtriya Gram 
Swaraj Abhiyan (RGSA) since the financial year 2022-23 in States/UTs. No agencies, 
institutions or vendors have been penalised, de-empanelled or blacklisted under Rashtriya Gram 
Swaraj Abhiyan during the last three years. 
(b) To ensure transparency, accountability, and accuracy in capacity-building activities under the 
Revamped RGSA, the Ministry has developed a dedicated Training Management Portal (TMP) 
for real-time monitoring of training programmes across States and Union Territories. The system 
incorporates Aadhaar-authenticated/biometric attendance, real-time upload of geo-tagged and 
time-stamped training photographs, and unique participant ID mapping to monitor training 
participation and prevent duplicate or proxy attendance. 

2 
 
Further, the utilization of funds under the RGSA Scheme is strictly governed by the Ministry of 
Finance guidelines through a robust financial monitoring framework. Funds are released and 
tracked in real time via the Public Financial Management System (PFMS) under the Single 
Nodal Agency (SNA/SNA-SPARSH) model, ensuring that further releases are made only after 
proper accounting of unspent balances. Additionally, the release of subsequent installments is 
contingent upon the submission of Utilization Certificates (UCs), audited accounts, and 
Quarterly/Annual Progress Reports (QPRs/APRs). 
(c) As per Article 243H of the Constitution of India, legislature of the State may, by law, 
authorize a Panchayat to levy, collect and appropriate such taxes, duties, tolls and fees in 
accordance with such procedure and subject to such limits and assign to the Panchayats such 
taxes, duties, tolls and fees levied and collected by the State Government for such purposes and 
subject to such conditions and limits as may be specified in the law. As such, this Ministry does 
not maintain or monitor the district-wise status of Own Source Revenue (OSR) mobilization by 
Gram Panchayats (GPs) in States, including the State of Andhra Pradesh. However, as reported 
by the State of Andhra Pradesh, the district-wise details of OSR generated from FY 2023-24 to 
2025-26 is at Annexure-I. 
(d) Yes, Sir. To assess the effectiveness of RGSA capacity-building programmes and to propose 
corrective measures to strengthen Panchayati Raj Institutions, an external evaluation of the 
Revamped RGSA has been undertaken through the Institute of Rural Management, Anand 
(IRMA). In addition, NITI Aayog has commissioned an independent assessment of RGSA to 
provide complementary evidence on outcomes. The evaluations indicate that the scheme’s 
structured, multi-layered capacity-building, combining classroom/thematic modules, exposure 
visits, and digital learning, has enhanced PRI capacities in Panchayat operations, planning, and 
implementation (including GPDP), digital governance, citizen engagement, and financial 
management. Post-training assessments record measurable gains in knowledge and practice, 
supporting more effective local governance and the localisation of SDGs.  
  
(e) The Ministry of Panchayati Raj ensures the authenticity of geo-tagged monitoring of Gram 
Panchayat assets and infrastructure projects through the mActionSoft mobile application. The 
application allows only live, real-time photo capture and does not allow uploading of pre-
existing gallery images. It automatically captures tamper-proof GPS coordinates and time stamps 
with each photograph and facilitates geo-tagging of assets at three stages of execution, namely 
before commencement, during progress, and upon completion. Geo-tagged photographs are 
linked with the corresponding asset/work in eGramSwaraj, enabling effective monitoring and 
verification.

VB-GRAM-G SCHEME FOR ASSAM 
 
2711. Shri Joyanta Basumatary: 
 
Will the Minister of RURAL DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state: 
 
(a)  the details and total number of person-days generated under 
Viksit Bharat Guarantee for Rojgar and Aajeevika Mission-
Gramin (VB-GRAM-G) scheme in Assam since 2025 with a 
special category for flood-affected and remote districts in 
Assam, district-wise; 
(b)  the details of funds allocated, released and utilised under VB-
GRAM-G in Assam since 2025, year-wise; 
(c)  whether the transition to the VB-GRAM-G will address issues 
such as declining person days, wage delays, and seasonal 
disruptions in flood-prone regions like Assam, if so, the details 
thereof; 
(d)  the manner in which such issues will be addressed, if not, the 
reasons therefor; and 
(e)  whether any region-specific reforms or flood-resilient works are 
being planned to ensure sustained rural employment generation 
in the States of the North-Eastern Region, if so, the details 
thereof? 
 
ANSWER 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF RURAL DEVELOPMENT 
(SHRI KAMLESH PASWAN) 
  
(a) & (b): Consequent upon enactment of Viksit Bharat–Guarantee 
for Rozgar and Aajeevika Mission (Gramin) (VB-G RAM G), Act 2025, 
the scheme has been operationalized in rural areas of the entire 
country with effect from 1st July, 2026 including Assam. District-wise 
details of persondays generated under Mahatma Gandhi NREGS and 
VB–G RAM G Scheme in the State of Assam, during the last financial 
years and current financial year 2026-27 (as on 30.07.2026) are at 
Annexure. 
  

Page 2 of 3 
 
With regard to fund allocation under VB- G RAM G, which came 
into force w.e.f 01.07.2026, it is stated that for FY 2026-27, an interim 
allocation Rs.1929.70 crore has been made for the State. 
Subsequently, Mother Sanctions amounting to Rs.630.96 Crore have 
been issued to the State as first installment of Central Share under 
various components based on the proposal received, out of which the 
State has so far utilised an amount of Rs.18.58 Crore. 
  
(c) to (e): The Viksit Bharat–Guarantee for Rozgar and Aajeevika 
Mission (Gramin) (VB-G RAM G) Act, 2025 provides for a statutory 
guarantee of one hundred and twenty five days of wage employment 
in a financial year to every rural household whose adult members 
volunteer to undertake unskilled manual work, as against one 
hundred days under the erstwhile Mahatma Gandhi NREGS. The Act 
also provides for technology-enabled implementation, timely 
payment of wages in accordance with the prescribed timelines, 
payment of delay compensation wherever applicable, and a time-
bound grievance redressal mechanism. 
Under VB–G RAM G Scheme, climate resilience, adaptation, and 
mitigation of extreme weather risks form an integral part of the 
statutory rural employment and asset creation framework. Within the 
planning framework, climate resilience and adaptation are embedded 
as core priorities under the Scheme. Permissible and priority 
categories of works include water conservation, watershed 
development, groundwater recharge, afforestation, source 
sustainability, flood and drought mitigation measures, and 
restoration and strengthening of natural resource assets. The 
Schedule to the Act further provides a dedicated thematic areas of 
works related to “Special works to mitigate Extreme Weather Events 
and Disaster Preparedness,” with an explicit thematic focus on 
disaster risk reduction, climate adaptation, and protection of rural 
communities and assets from floods, cyclones, storms, droughts, 
landslides, forest fires, and other extreme weather events. 
Illustrative works under this category include construction of 
cyclone shelters, flood shelters, and multipurpose disaster-resilient 
structures; diversion channels, embankments, and other disaster-
mitigation works; stabilising ponds and water structures for flood 
management; post-disaster rehabilitation and restoration of rural 
roads and community assets windbreak and shelter-belt plantations; 
and forest fire management works such as fire breaks and fuel buffer 
zones. The intended outcome of these provisions is the creation of 
climate-resilient villages capable of withstanding extreme weather 
conditions.

 Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE कृिष एवं िकसान कÐयाण 
मंýी  be pleased to state:  
(a) whether the Government has conducted any evaluation of the impact of the Minimum 
Support Price (MSP) declared during the last three years on farmers' income, agricultural 
production, crop diversification and profitability, if so, the major findings thereof; 
(b) the details of the Minimum Support Price declared for major crops, actual Government 
procurement, number of farmers benefited and the procured yield compared to total 
production, State-wise and crop-wise; 
(c) whether the Government has identified such States and crops where Government 
procurement remained limited despite the declaration of the Minimum Support Price, 
forcingfarmers to sell their produce at lower prices, if so, the details thereof; and 
(d) the steps being taken by the Government to make the Minimum Support Price mechanism 
more effective and comprehensive? 
ANSWER 
MINISTER OF STATE FOR AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE  
क ृ िष एवं िकसान कʞाण राǛमंũी (SHRI RAM NATH THAKUR) 
(a) to (d): Every year, Government fixes Minimum Support Prices (MSPs) for 22 mandated 
agricultural crops for the country as a whole, based on the recommendations of the 
Commission for Agricultural Costs & Prices (CACP), after considering the views of the State 
Governments and Central Ministries/Departments concerned. 
The Union Budget for 2018-19 had announced the pre-determined principle to keep 
MSPs at levels of at least one and half times of the cost of production. Accordingly, 
Government had increased MSPs for all mandated Kharif, Rabi and other commercial crops 
with a minimum return of 50 percent over all India weighted average cost of production from 
year 2018-19 onwards. 
Out of the total production, only marketable surplus is available for procurement by 
Government agencies when market price of these produce fall below the MSP. Government 
procures cereals and coarse cereals through Food Corporation of India (FCI) and other 
designated State Agencies to provide price support to the farmers. Procurement of pulses, 
oilseeds and copra is done under Price Support Scheme under umbrella scheme of Pradhan 
Mantri Annadata Aay Sanrakshan Abhiyan (PM-AASHA), on the request of the concerned 
State Government as per the guidelines as and when market price of these produce fall below 

the MSP. Procurement agencies under PM-AASHA Scheme are National Agricultural 
Cooperative Marketing Federation of India Ltd (NAFED) and National Co-operative 
Consumers' Federation of India Ltd. (NCCF). Cotton and Jute are also procured by 
Government at MSP through Cotton Corporation of India (CCI) and Jute Corporation of India 
(JCI), respectively. 
In addition, Adequate number of procurement centres are opened by respective State 
Government Agencies, taking into account the production, marketable surplus, convenience 
of farmers and availability of other logistics / infrastructure such as storage and transportation 
etc. Temporary purchase centres, in addition to the existing mandis and depots / godowns are 
also established at key points. The procurement operation is a continuously evolving process 
and during the last few years, procurement processes under MSP have improved to ensure 
payment of MSP to farmer’s bank account directly and linkage of Aadhaar and land records 
with the States’ procurement portals ensure that the farmers directly get the benefits of the 
MSP purchase.  
Government has launched Mission for Aatmanirbharta in Pulses till 2030-31, to reduce 
import dependence and achieve self-sufficiency in pulses. To encourage domestic production 
of pulses, the Government is undertaking procurement of Tur, Urad and Masur under the PM-
AASHA Scheme on the request of State Government from pre-registered farmers as much as 
offered by them through Central Nodal Agencies, namely the National Agricultural Cooperative 
Marketing Federation of India Ltd. (NAFED) and the National Cooperative Consumers' 
Federation of India Limited (NCCF). 
Increased MSP has benefited farmers of the country which are evident from data of 
procurement and MSP amount paid to the farmers. The year wise details of total food grains 
produced, crops procured, MSP amount paid to farmers and farmers benefitted during 2023-
24 to 2025-26 (upto June, 2026) for all the States are given as under:

The Government is implementing several policies, reforms, developmental

various schemes / programmes cover the entire spectrum of agriculture including credit, 
insurance,income support, infrastructure, crops including horticulture, seeds,

  The Government is also implementing the Crop Diversification Programme (CDP), which 
is a centrally sponsored scheme under the Pradhan Mantri- Rashtriya Krishi VikasYojana 
(PM-RKVY) in the Original Green Revolution States viz; Haryana, Punjab & Uttar Pradesh 
since 2013-14 to divert the area of water guzzling paddy crop to alternative crops like pulses, 
oilseeds, coarse cereals, nutri cereals, etc. The primary objective of the scheme is to 
demonstrate and promote improved production technologies of alternate crops for diversion 
of paddy cultivation as well as to restore soil fertility through cultivation of leguminous crops 
that generate heavy biomass and consume lesser nutrients. 
The Government of India is further encouraging crop diversification among farmers 
through the state governments to grow crops such as coarse cereals, nutri cereals (Shree 
Anna) under the National Food Security & Nutrition Mission (NFSNM), pulses under Mission 
for Aatmanirbharata on Pulses, oilseeds under the National Mission on Edible Oil (NMEO)-

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF STEEL 
 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 2715 
FOR ANSWER ON 04.08.2026  
 
 
STEEL SCRAP RECYCLING UNITS IN TELANGANA  
 
 
2715. SHRI ARVIND DHARMAPURI:  
 
Will the Minister of STEEL be pleased to state:  
 
(a) the details of steel scrap recycling capacity created and quantity of steel scrap 
recycled in the country, State/UT-wise including Telangana;  
 
(b) the steps taken to promote organised scrap collection, processing and use of scrap 
in steelmaking;  
 
(c) whether any organised vehicle scrapping, steel recycling or downstream scrap-
based units have been established or proposed in Telangana; and  
 
(d) if so, the strategy adopted to reduce emissions, improve resource efficiency and 
build a circular economy in the steel sector? 
 
ANSWER 
 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE          (SHRI BHUPATHIRAJU SRINIVASA VARMA) 
MINISTRY OF STEEL 
 
(a)&(c): During Financial Year 2025-26, about 36 million tonnes ferrous scrap 
was used for production of steel, of which approximately 28 million tonnes scrap 
generated domestically.  The details of Registered Vehicle Scrapping Facilities 
(RVSFs) across the country including Telangana is available on the Ministry of Road 
Transport and Highways’ parivahan portal at the URL given below:  
 
‘https://vscrap.parivahan.gov.in/vehiclescrap/vahan/rvsfdetails.xhtml’. 
 
(b)&(d): The steps taken by the Government to promote organized scrap 
collection, processing and use in steelmaking to promote circular economy in the steel 
sector as well as the strategy adopted to reduce emissions and improve energy 
efficiency in the sector are as under: - 
 
(i)   The Steel Scrap Recycling Policy, 2019 provides a coordination 
framework with various Ministries to promote recycling of ferrous scrap generated 
from various sources. 
Contd…..2/- 

::2:: 
 
(ii)  The Ministry of Road Transport and Highways (MoRTH) has formulated 
the Vehicle Scrapping Policy that includes a system of incentives/disincentives for 
creation of an ecosystem to phase out older, unfit polluting vehicles. Under the 
policy, MoRTH has issued rules for Registration and Functions of Vehicle 
Scrapping Facility (RVSF), which provides the procedures and infrastructure 
facilities required for de-pollution and dismantling of End-of-Life Vehicles (ELVs) 
for further recovery of metal and other materials under environmental regulations.  
 
(iii)  The Government of India has notified the Hazardous and Other Wastes 
(Management and Transboundary Movement) Rules, 2016 to ensure safe 
handling, storage, recycling, utilisation, treatment and disposal of hazardous and 
other wastes in an environmentally safe manner. 
 
(iv)  Ministry of Environment, Forest & Climate Change has introduced the 
Environment Protection (End-of-Life Vehicles) Rules, 2025, which establishes a 
framework for managing End-of-Life Vehicles (ELVs) in an environmentally sound 
manner and mandates Extended Producer Responsibility (EPR), requiring vehicle 
producers to meet annual scrapping targets based on the type of vehicle and 
materials recovered. 
 
(v)  Recycling of Ships Act, 2019 has been notified by Ministry of Shipping, 
Ports and Waterways with aims to regulate and promote the safe and 
environmentally sound recycling of ships. 
 
(vi) Ministry of Steel has released the Taxonomy for Green Steel for defining 
and categorizing the low emission steel. 
 
(vii) Ministry of Steel released a report titled "Greening the Steel Sector in 
India: Roadmap and Action Plan" on the basis of the recommendations of the 14 
Task Forces constituted by this Ministry for this purpose which provides the 
roadmap for green steel and sustainability, towards net-zero target by 2070. The 
report is available on Ministry of Steel's website. 
 
(viii) Four pilot projects have been awarded for implementation of pilot 
projects for use of hydrogen in steel sector under National Green Hydrogen 
Mission launched by Ministry of New & Renewable Energy. 
 
(ix) National Solar Mission launched by Ministry of New and Renewable 
Energy in January, 2010 promotes the use of solar energy and also helps to 
reduce the emission of steel industry.  
 
(x)  Ministry of Power has notified Carbon Credit Trading Scheme (CCTS) 
on 28.06.2023 for regulating Indian Carbon Market across various industrial 
sectors, which is also applicable to steel plants.

(b) if so, the details thereof, including the number of artisans, weaver s, trainees and Self -Help 
Groups covered, along with the financial assistance provided during the last five years in 
Chhattisgarh, district-wise;  
(c) whether the Government has established or proposes to establish dedicated design, skill 
development and common facility centres for traditional Kosa weaving clusters in the State and, 
if so, the details thereof;  
(d) the  details of measures taken to improve branding, Geographical Indication (GI) -based 
promotion, digital marketing and export opportunities for Chhattisgarh Kosa silk; and  
(e) the  details of steps taken to ensure that traditional weaving skills are preserved through 
institutional training, artisan support and market -linked livelihood opportunities for rural and 
tribal youth? 
उत्तर 
ANSWER 
वस्त्र राज् य मंत्री (श्री पबित्र मार्घेररटा) 
THE MINISTER OF STATE FOR TEXTILES  
 (SHRI PABITRA MARGHERITA) 
 
(a) to (e):  The Ministry of Textiles is administering following schemes for the overall 
development of handloom sector and welfare of handloom workers across the country including 
Chhattisgarh: 
1. National Handloom Development Programme(NHDP); 
2. Raw Material Supply Scheme(RMSS); 
  
Under the above schemes, financial assistance is provided to eligible handloom agencies/workers 
for raw materials, procurement of upgraded looms & accessories,  solar lighting units,

common infrastructure, publicity and brand development through India Handloom Brand (IHB), 
Handloom Mark (HLM) and GI tag , e-commerce facilities, marketing of handloom products in 

domestic/overseas markets, concessional loans under weavers’ MUDRA scheme and social 
security etc.  
The Government has undertaken various measures to safeguard Chhattisgarh's Kosa silk weaving 
heritage through skil l development, sericulture promotion, artisan welfare, and market support. 
Schemes such as Samarth, state -level artisan training programmes, sericulture development 
initiatives, and the ODOP programme collectively contribute to preserving the traditional craft 
while encouraging the younger generation to view Kosa silk weaving as a viable cultural and 
economic profession.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF RURAL DEVELOPMENT 
DEPARTMENT OF RURAL DEVELOPMENT 
 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 2718 
  ANSWERED ON 04/08/2026 
 
EXCLUSION OF HOUSEHOLDS FROM PMAY-G IN ANDHRA PRADESH 
 
2718. Shri Sribharat Mathukumilli: 
 
Will the Minister of RURAL DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state: 
 
(a)  whether the Government has assessed the number of eligible 
rural households in Andhra Pradesh excluded from Pradhan 
Mantri  Awas Yojana- Gramin (PMAY-G) despite the revised 
eligibility criteria, if so, the details thereof; 
(b)  whether the Government has examined cases where landless 
eligible beneficiaries in Andhra Pradesh were sanctioned 
houses but could not commence construction due to non-
availability of land, if so, the details and the action taken 
thereon; 
(c)  whether the Ministry has conducted any independent audits to 
assess the quality, durability and occupancy of PMAY-G houses 
constructed in Andhra Pradesh, if so, the findings and action 
taken on deficiencies; and 
(d)  whether the Government maintains data on PMAY-G 
beneficiaries who have migrated after receiving houses due to 
lack of livelihood opportunities, affecting the objective of 
sustainable rural habitation, if so, the details thereof? 
 
ANSWER 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF RURAL DEVELOPMENT 
(DR. CHANDRA SEKHAR PEMMASANI) 
  
(a): Under PMAY-G, the universe of eligible beneficiaries includes 
all the houseless and households living in zero, one or two rooms with 
kutcha wall and kutcha roof (kutcha houses) as per Socio -Economic 
Caste Census (SECC) 2011 and Awaas+ 2018 survey data. The 
beneficiaries are identified on the basis of housing deprivation 
parameters and exclusion criteria prescribed under SECC 2011. 
These parameters/criteria are applied both on SECC 2011 and 
Awaas+ 2018 survey databases and then they are further subjected 
to due verification by Gram Sabha and an appellate process 

Page 2 of 3 
 
thereafter to arrive at the final list of eligible beneficiaries. In 
addition, the Government of India has provided approval for updating 
the Awaas + list for identifying additional eligible rural households 
using modified exclusion criteria under the scheme. In line with the 
decision of the Government of India, Awaas + 2024 Mobile App was 
launched for conducting the survey. To ensure that no eligible 
beneficiary is left behind, the Ministry of Rural Development has 
introduced Self Survey option also in the Awaas + 2024 Mobile App.  
  
(b): Providing land to the landless PMAY-G beneficiaries for the 
construction of houses is accorded top priority since they are among 
the most deserving beneficiaries in the Permanent Wait List (PWL) of 
PMAY-G. The responsibility to ensure that such beneficiaries are 
provided land vests with the state. The state can give land from the 
government pool of land or any other land, including public land 
(Panchayat common land, community land or land belonging to other 
local authorities).  
  
As informed by the Government of Andhra Pradesh, some 
landless beneficiaries have been identified during the Awaas + 2024 
survey. Once Permanent Wait List on the basis of Awaas + 2024 
survey is finalised and enabled on AwaasSoft, the system will 
prioritise the beneficiaries as per the approved scheme guidelines. 
  
(c): Under PMAY-G, the house is constructed by the beneficiary 
himself/herself or under his/her supervision. Further, as per the 
guidelines of PMAY-G, the States/UTs provide the beneficiaries a 
bouquet of options of house designs according to the local climatic 
conditions, using appropriate local material and technology suitable 
to the region of their residence. The State/UT Government can also 
facilitate supply of construction material at competitive rates.  
 
The Ministry of Rural Development has also published a 
compendium of rural housing typologies “PAHAL” which is available 
on the program website of PMAY-G. This can also be accessed 
through AwaasApp. 
 
Further, to ensure good quality construction of houses under 
PMAY-G, the Government of India has rolled out the Rural Mason 
Training (RMT) Program with the target to train adequate number of 
masons for house construction in rural areas.  
 
(d): Data on PMAY-G beneficiaries who have migrated after 
receiving houses due to lack of livelihood opportunities is not 
maintained by the Ministry of Rural Development. However, as per the 

Page 3 of 3 
 
findings of an evaluation study of PMAY-G conducted by the Indian 
Institute of Management (IIM), Ahmedabad, the incidence of 
migration among PMAY-G beneficiaries has declined by 
approximately 6%. The proportion of respondents citing “lack of 
housing” as a reason for migration has come down from 36% to 18%, 
and seasonal displacement has declined from 13.8% to 4.2%.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE 
DEPARTMENT OF AGRICULTURAL RESEARCH & EDUCATION
